title: Warm-started walk / QSA / quantum replica-exchange Langevin sampler for the learned-energy structure posterior at >=60 aa (lead M1/M2 sampler core)
merged_from: qalg QM-01 (QRELD warm start), qalg QM-03 (non-thermal QSA paths: residue-growth, likelihood-tempering), learned 'Information-annealed QSA from the (theta,tau) product prior', complexity 'QSA vs SMC stage-count lemma', classical 'Learned-energy posterior sampling (lead M1) twin portfolio', priorart (a) walk/QSA/QMS/RELD prior art, priorart (h) QSA-from-prior part
summary: Q: can soft posterior-averaged structures (S33's 1.40x signal, obtained only as an exact enumerated sum) be sampled at 60-150 aa more cheaply than with the best classical sampler? Quantum: Szegedy/Lemieux Metropolis walk + (adaptive) QSA [A7,A8,A31]; operator-level QRELD / Witten-Laplacian QSVT [A44]. Replaces: only the mixing/rejuvenation kernel inside PT/SMC; energy, decoder, alignment and averaging stay classical. Mechanism: the walk has phase gap ~sqrt(delta), so reflections/Chebyshev polynomials T_k(P) with signed coefficients separate the stationary state in ~1/sqrt(delta) steps, where classical P^t needs ~1/delta. A sampling algorithm cannot realise signed mixtures without a sign problem. Warm start: the per-residue (theta,tau) head is a product state, prepared EXACTLY with <=255 rotations/residue, which removes the cold-start sqrt(N) penalty [A9]. Paths: temperature, likelihood exponent lambda, residue growth, |i-j| band. Lemma: BC >= (1+chi^2)^-1/2, so SMC's per-stage condition implies QSA's; stage counts are equal, and the whole gain is sum delta_k^-1/2 vs sum tau_k (no cloning: 1 sample/anneal; SMC resampling has no quantum analogue). Speedup: at most quadratic in the per-stage gap (walk steps). Oracle: coherent Delta-E/grad-E of the pair tables (QM-05); wall-clock break-even needs >=~1e10-1e16 classical steps per independent sample. Competitor: non-reversible PT/REST2 + HMC in (theta,tau), adaptive SMC/AIS, PERM growth, optimise-then-sample darting + MBAR basin masses, flow/BioEmu proposals with MH/IS correction, TT sampling, random-prior independence twin (DNR-06). Info vs comp: pi is entirely classical (ESM-2 -> esmprior); the quantum stage only mixes faster, and its value is capped by the readout under exact pi. S29-S33: whole-distribution consumption of a SPECIFIED posterior lies outside H-001 (KILLBOOK scope warning); DNR-05/06 twins and DNR-10's reopening burden (a measured mixing failure) apply in full. Must be run at a native-free calibrated T* >> 1: at T=1 solver-best states differ by 50-230 nats and sampling collapses to restart-saturated search. Kill: C_class(150) <= 1e9 evaluations to certified agreement (4 method x seed runs agree on posterior mean within 0.1 A and on >=1%-mass basins within 0.05, planted-well control detected) with C_class(L) < B(L) to 300 aa; OR the SAMPLED soft readout fails to beat the A80 argmin by >=1.0x MDE on long40; OR a first-order path signature (bimodal histograms, overlaps ~e^-cL) that breaks QSA's premise too. Test: long40 + mid30 (+ tuning126 for the fit); NRPT (8-16 chains, HMC) + adaptive SMC (256-1000 particles) along lambda/growth paths from the head prior + darting twin, 4 seeds, ~1e7 evals/target; record tau_int, round trips, Lambda(L), per-stage BC/chi^2/ESS, AIS log Z, soft-readout MDE; fit against L. ~1 day on 8 cores. This campaign also feeds QM-02/03/07/11/12/15. Track: B fault-tolerant (C theory). Prior: low (~5%).
dead_reason: Matrix M1/M2 are INTERESTING, not killed; KILLBOOK scope excludes sampling with slow classical mixing beyond 60 aa.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 on the protein instance family (esmprior/A80 posterior at 60-300 aa). The only L6 results are generic or synthetic. First, the quadratic walk-step or query speedup in the per-stage gap from Szegedy, Somma et al. and Wocjan-Abeyesinghe. Second, the information-theoretic separation of Olivucci et al. 2026: Omega(alpha) classical vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) quantum on 'hide-and-seek' torus wells, with alpha = e^{beta*Delta}. Nothing shows that the esmprior/A80 posterior belongs to that hidden-well class, and the mode census points the other way (see evidence).
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No resource-normalised or empirical advantage. On the measured cost model, the classical requirement predicted for 150-300 aa (about 1e6-1e8 gradient evaluations per decorrelated sample, a model extrapolation) sits at least 2-3 orders of magnitude below the sequential fault-tolerant break-even (about 2e10-2e14). It sits at least 4-5 orders below once the classical sampler's parallelism is counted (break-even scales as P^2 * R^2).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument: (Pro-quantum rebuttal, stated as strongly as the data allow.) The G1 pilot data show a real classical failure. NRPT on the lambda-path at T=1 produced 0 round trips in every pilot. For 5O37A_45 and 3GAHA_60 the ladder was adequately provisioned: Syed et al. Cor. 1 under efficient local exploration (ELE) predicts 27.5 and 21.1 round trips in 1500 and 1200 scans (res/results/RAW/g1_pilot/*.json; also research/theory/PROOFS/T2_sampling_checks.py C4). The 150-aa ladder was under-provisioned (39 rungs for Lambda = 29.3), so its zero count is less informative. The mode census is restart-unsaturated at 60-100 aa for 19-25% of targets (p_hit of the best mode = 1/256). So C_class may already exceed 1e6 at 45 aa and could grow fast with L. Quantum acceleration can also stack on top of classical non-reversible lifts: Claudon-Piquemal-Monmarche (Nat. Commun. 2025) accelerate non-reversible chains, and Leng et al. (PNAS 2026) claim 'up to quartic' over the best-known classical Langevin methods. Eberle-Lorler parity (lifts gain at most a square root) therefore does not cap the quantum walk at the classical rate. If the ELE failure survives preconditioning at T*, is barrier-limited, and splits mass between structurally distinct basins, the candidate returns to INTERESTING-conditional. ADVERSARY REPLY: (i) The failure has the signature of ill-conditioning, not of a barrier. The top-rung HMC step falls from eps = 3.9e-3 rad (45 aa) to 1.0e-3 rad (150 aa), roughly L^-1.2 (torsion lever-arm stiffness). There are 8 leapfrog steps and only a clipped diagonal mass (at most 400x range). Pivot moves of a single residue from the prior are essentially always rejected at lambda=1. Decorrelation is diffusive: tau_loc ~ (0.3 rad / (8*eps))^2, about 1e2 scans at 45 aa and 1.4e3 at 150 aa. Standard remedies can cut the condition number by more than its square root, which beats the quantum walk's sqrt(kappa) on the same chain: full-Hessian or Riemannian preconditioning from the census Hessians, lever-arm-free concerted-rotation/crankshaft moves, and soft-core sterics along the lambda-path. (ii) Stacking a quantum sqrt on a classical lift keeps the per-sample cost quadratic and sequential, against a per-step overhead R of 1e5-1e7. (iii) The hidden-well class of Olivucci et al. needs deep narrow wells that neither gradients nor the head prior signal. The census instead shows funnelled, structurally clustered low-E modes. (iv) The value side is unproven. The T=1 soft readout ties the polished argmin (+0.09, +0.26, -0.02, -0.07, -0.10 A at 45/60/100/120/150 aa). The 1.40x S33 signal was measured against hard CVaR tails, not against the restart-saturated argmin.
verdicts.evidence:
VERIFIED LITERATURE. Bibliography entries from research/literature/BIBLIOGRAPHY.md; extra checks via arXiv API on 2026-09-27.
(1) Lifting parity:
- Eberle & Lorler, 'Non-reversible lifts of reversible diffusion processes and relaxation times', arXiv 2402.05041, PTRF, doi 10.1007/s00440-024-01308-x.
- Eberle & Lorler, arXiv 2412.16710, J. Funct. Anal. 2026, doi 10.1016/j.jfa.2026.111605. Abstract: 'Non-reversible lifts reduce the relaxation time of reversible diffusions at most by a square root', attained by Hamiltonian flow with velocity refreshment, i.e. randomized HMC / underdamped Langevin.
- Cao, Lu, Wang, ARMA 247:90 (2023), arXiv 1908.04746: underdamped Langevin rate O(sqrt(m)) vs m (overdamped, convex).
- Chen-Lovasz-Pak STOC 1999 [#14]; Diaconis-Holmes-Neal 2000 [#15].
- Apers-Sarlette-Ticozzi PRA 98:032115 (2018), arXiv 1712.01609 [#16]; Dervovic arXiv 1712.02318 [#18]: for every quantum-walk mixing speedup there is a classical lifted chain that mixes as fast or faster. Caveat: the lift may not be efficiently constructible, and this does not cover QSA's warm-start reflections.
- Aharonov-Ambainis-Kempe-Vazirani STOC 2001 [#12]: quantum-walk mixing speedup is bounded (conductance).
Consequence: in the diffusive or ill-conditioned regime, the Szegedy phase gap sqrt(delta) is matched by classical ballistic or preconditioned dynamics. A residual quantum gain exists only in Arrhenius or bottleneck-limited stages (delta ~ Phi), which tempering flattens unless the landscape is entropic or first-order (Woodard-Schmidler-Huber 2009 [#222, #223]). In the first-order case QSA also pays e^{dF/2} (T2_sampling_checks.py C3).
(2) Tempering: Syed, Bouchard-Cote, Deligiannidis, Doucet, JRSS-B, doi 10.1111/rssb.12464, arXiv 1905.02939. NRPT round-trip rate is 1/(2+2*sum r/(1-r)), and the ladder cost is O(Lambda) rungs under ELE.
(3) Quantum side:
- Olivucci et al., arXiv 2608.24527 [#39]: every classical value/gradient/higher-derivative query algorithm needs Omega(alpha), with alpha = e^{beta(maxE - minE)}; quantum needs O~(sqrt(alpha)) on a constructed hide-and-seek class. The advantage is quadratic in alpha and grows as e^{Omega(d)} only at low temperature.
- Leng, Ding, Chen, Lin, PNAS 123(8) e2512789123 (2026), arXiv 2505.05301 [#38]: 'up to quartic' over best-known classical Langevin. The abstract does not name the reference class; whether the comparison is against NRPT/underdamped is UNVERIFIED.
- Claudon et al., Nat. Commun. 16:10732 (2025) [#37]: accelerates non-reversible chains under amplitude-encoded transitions.
- Lemieux et al., Quantum 4:287 (2020) [#432]: effectively no practical advantage at a quadratic speedup.
(4) Classical samplers: Noe et al. Boltzmann generators, Science 2019 [#227]; Tan et al. sequential Boltzmann generators, ICML 2025 [#312]; Del Moral-Doucet-Jasra SMC 2006 [#96]; MBAR, Shirts-Chodera 2008 [#91]. Standard but not re-verified here: Riemannian-manifold HMC (Girolami-Calderhead 2011), NUTS (Hoffman-Gelman 2014), concerted-rotation moves (Dodd-Boone-Theodorou 1993).

LOCAL MEASUREMENTS. In-progress G1 campaign, single seed, pilot quality.
(a) NRPT lambda-path, T=1 (research/results/RAW/g1_pilot/):
- Lambda = 13.6 / 14.4 / 24.9 / 25.2 / 29.3 at L = 45 / 60 / 100 / 120 / 150. Fit: Lambda ~ 0.93 L^0.69, giving 30 at 150 aa and 49 at 300 aa.
- Round trips: ELE-predicted 27.5 / 21.1 / 4.5 / 3.3 / 1.7; observed 0 everywhere.
- Top-rung eps = 3.9e-3 / 4.2e-3 / 1.8e-3 / 1.7e-3 / 1.0e-3 rad.
- Cost: 262-343 gradient evaluations per scan, 0.59-3.51 ms per gradient (45 to 150 aa, ~L^1.4 on this CPU).
- Round-trip counter logic in src/qapf/sampling/hrex.py:282-306 was checked and looks correct.
(b) Mode census, 256 restarts x 200 iterations, T=1 (research/results/RAW/g1_modes/, 16 targets per length):
- Median p_hit of the best mode = 0.117 / 0.109 / 0.049 / 0.059 / 0.016 at L = 30 / 45 / 60 / 80 / 100. That is about 1.7e3-1.3e4 gradient evaluations to hit the best mode (median). Share of targets with p_hit = 1/256: 6% / 6% / 25% / 19% / 25%.
- At L >= 80 all 32 target-lengths have exactly one mode within 5 nats of the minimum, except 5O37A_100: two modes 0.8 nats apart and 0.05 A apart in RMSD. The gap to the second mode is usually 10-250 nats.
- Well-predicted targets show low-E modes that cluster structurally (for example 8AXJA_100 top-5: 2.5-3.3 A; 5O37A_80: 2.7-3.0 A). This is a funnel, not hidden wells.
(c) Readout at T=1: posterior-mean RMSD minus polished-argmin RMSD = +0.09 / +0.26 / -0.02 / -0.07 / -0.10 A.
(d) Inherited S33 result: restart saturation bounds the gain of any argmin-type global solver at 4.35 - 4.21 = 0.14 A on long40.

COST DERIVATION (mine, not cited).
- A coherent A80 energy at L residues needs L(L-1)/2 pair distances plus 28-bin soft lookups at about 5e3 Toffolis per pair, plus the NeRF build. That is about 5e7 Toffolis at 150 aa and 2e8 at 300 aa.
- At 1e3-1e5 logical Toffolis/s, one walk step at 150 aa costs 5e2-5e4 s, against t_c = 3.5e-3 s classically. So R = 1.4e5-1.4e7 and the sequential break-even is C* = R^2, about 2e10-2e14 classical evaluations per sample; with P classical cores, C* = (P*R)^2.
- Classical need under the diffusive-stiffness model: C ~ 9N * tau_loc, with N = 2.5*Lambda and tau_loc ~ (0.3/(8*eps))^2. That gives about 1e6 at 150 aa and about 1e7 at 300 aa (eps extrapolated as L^-1.2). The ideal-ELE round-trip cost is about 75*Lambda^2: 6.4e4 at 150 aa and 1.8e5 at 300 aa.
- No-cloning: a posterior mean within 0.1 A (posterior RMSD-sd 0.1-0.34 A) needs 10-100 independent QSA anneals, while classical SMC/PT particles run in parallel.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Per-step overhead ratio. The quantum walk step at 150 aa needs about 5e7 Toffolis (derived, not cited) and runs at an assumed 1e3-1e5 logical Toffolis/s, so it costs 5e2-5e4 s. The classical gradient is measured at 3.5 ms on this CPU, which gives R = 1e5-1e7.

Break-even. Sequential break-even is R^2, about 2e10-2e14 classical evaluations per independent sample. Against P parallel classical cores it becomes (P*R)^2, about 1e12-1e16 at P=8 and more than 1e16 at P=1e3.

Classical need (model). The ideal-ELE NRPT round trip is about 75*Lambda^2 gradient evaluations: 6e4 at 150 aa and 2e5 at 300 aa. Including the measured stiffness penalty, a decorrelated sample needs about 1e6 at 150 aa and 1e7-1e8 at 300 aa. That is 2-5 orders below break-even.

Worked example at 300 aa. The quantum sampler needs about 3e3 walk steps x 2e8 Toffolis, about 6e11 Toffolis, which is 70 days per sample at 1e5 Toffolis/s. The classical sampler needs about 1e7 x 9 ms, about 1 day on one core or about 3 h on 8 cores. This holds before counting the 10-100 samples the quantum sampler needs, since it cannot clone.

The Olivucci quadratic-in-alpha separation could pay only if the posterior at T* has hidden barriers of at least about 23-37 nats that tempering cannot flatten. None have been observed.
verdicts.novelty_note: Searched: the 448-paper verified bibliography plus targeted arXiv API fetches (Eberle-Lorler x5, Syed et al., Cao-Lu-Wang, Olivucci et al., Leng et al., Claudon et al.). This search found no paper that proposes a quantum walk, QSA or quantum Langevin sampler for a protein-language-model-derived structure posterior. It also found no published mixing-time or landscape measurement of such posteriors. The G1 pilot and census data in research/results/RAW/g1_* appear to be the first in this scope. The formulation is novel in that narrow sense, but novelty is not advantage: the quantum mechanism is the generic quadratic walk speedup and adds nothing protein-specific. Web search was capped for this session, so recent 2026 protein-sampling preprints were not rechecked, and Leng et al.'s classical reference class is unverified.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for QM-01 as posed. No separation from the best classical sampler has been shown for any instance family that contains the learned-energy posterior. The underlying primitive does have an L6 query-model statement: walk/QSA steps scale as ~1/sqrt(delta) against 1/delta [A7, A8, A9, A31]. But that comparison is against the SAME reversible chain P. Lifted and non-reversible chains, and HMC, already reach ~1/Phi (Apers-Ticozzi-Sarlette [A17, arXiv 1705.08253]). Against the best classical method the gain therefore lies between O(1) (diffusive regime, Phi ~ sqrt(delta)) and quadratic (bottleneck regime, Phi ~ delta). The one provable continuous separation, Omega(alpha) vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) [A45], gives no usable bound here because alpha >= 1e172 for this energy (T5 note, L=45).
verdicts.level_practical: L0, and the resource-normalised (L3-type) break-even analysis is negative. No scenario reaches break-even with a quantum runtime shorter than about 100 days per sample, even after stacking every quantum-favourable assumption. For the faithful oracle, the quantum runtime at crossover is about 4e6 to 1e8 years per sample.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
B* is set by (t_Q/t_C)^2 times kappa', and both factors are roughly independent of L. If the classical mixing cost C_class(L) grows exponentially (first-order metastability; the pilot saw zero PT round trips at L=45-150, T=1), it must eventually exceed any fixed B*, and the quantum cost would grow only as its square root. Three further trends favour quantum:
- The Cartesian local-move oracle costs O(L) pair terms, against O(L^2) for a classical gradient, so B*_min falls as ~1/L (6.2e9 at 60 aa, 7.6e8 at 300 aa).
- Faster factories or ~1 us Toffolis would divide B* by R^2.
- Better continuous samplers (QRELD/QSVT, [A44]) might lower the constant c.

Rebuttal: an exponential C_class makes both sides impractical. In the most generous corner, with C_class = 1e12 evaluations per sample, the quantum side still needs ~3.8 years per sample and 40+ years per soft-readout target. The quantum runtime at crossover, T* = kappa' c^2 N_Q^2 t_Q^2 / t_C, is a floor that no classical mixing failure can lower. A classical mixing failure that severe would also block certification of the posterior and any test that the soft readout transmits to accuracy (the information side).
verdicts.evidence:
Two scripts back this audit:
- The existing T3 model, research/theory/T3_resource_model.py. It is a Toffoli-level model of the LHPST/Szegedy step on the A80 energy, built on Sanders 2020 eqs 95-96 and 190, Babbush 2021 eqs 1-7, QROAM from Berry 2019 (arXiv 1902.02134), Haner-Roetteler-Svore arithmetic (1805.12445) and the Gidney-Ekera surface code (1905.09749).
- An independent audit script, C:\Users\abena\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-abena-quantum-advantage-protein-folding\deded8ee-ac50-420b-a8f2-b349dc3a4fdc\scratchpad\audit_be.py, with the timing script time_tc.py beside it.

1) Oracle per walk step, L=150.
- Faithful oracle (T3 design D2: torsion moves, per-pair cubic in d^2, 20-bit arithmetic): 5.1e8 Toffolis per step (~2e9 T). That is 8.2e7 at L=60 and 2.1e9 at L=300. About 97% of the cost is the 2 x 2 x 10,878 pair terms at ~5.7e3 Toffolis each. At 170 us per Toffoli [Sanders 2007.07391; Babbush 2011.04149 eq 6], one step takes 24 h.
- The literal 1001-point sqrt table (D1): 2.4e9 per step.
- Cartesian local moves (D3): 3.4e7 per step.
- My own floor (16-bit, 512-segment QROM, energy carried, measurement-based uncompute; about 1.9e3 Toffolis per pair term; head term included): ~3.9e6 per step.
- Szegedy is 30-300x worse than LHPST.

2) Qubits.
- Logical: 2.4e4-4.9e4 (D2), 1.3e4 (D3), 8.3e4 (Szegedy). With 100 parallel pair workspaces: 3.8e5.
- Code distance: runtime-consistent d = 39-51 (T3). This makes each Toffoli take 215-280 us and multiplies B* by 1.6-2.7. That factor is NOT included in the numbers below, so they favour quantum.
- Physical: 5e7-1.3e8 with one factory; ~1e9 with 100 factories (about 1000x Sanders' 1e6 machine).

3) Other costs.
- Warm-start product state: Grover-Rudolph, (2L-5) x 2^b rotations, ~3e5 Toffolis, which is less than one walk step.
- Data loading: 1.8e9 classical bits hard-wired as classically controlled QROM. No QRAM and no free block encoding are assumed.
- Boltzmann coin: ~260 Toffolis [Sanders eq 96].
- Readout: one sample per anneal (no cloning). The 0.1 A soft mean needs about (sigma/0.1)^2 ~ 1e2-1e3 samples. Classically these are independent chains running in parallel; on one QPU they run in series. Coherent multivariate mean estimation cuts the anneal count by at most ~8-30x (my estimate, not a cited result) and requires coherent QSA.
- Continuous or gradient variants need a coherent gradient oracle costing >= 3x the energy (T3's quantised HMC: 6.2e9 per step, B* ~2.8e16). Jordan/GAW-type gradients cost O~(sqrt(d)/eps) queries (GAW arXiv 1711.00465: UNVERIFIED).

4) Classical side, measured in this audit. The A80 energy+gradient in torch fp64 on one thread (synthetic tables) takes 5.06 ms at L=150 (batch 32) and 1.30 ms at L=60. The pilot measured 3.5 ms at L=150. An optimised fp32 kernel should reach ~0.2 ms (ESTIMATE). This gives t_Q/t_C ~ 1.7e7 (measured) to 4.4e8 (optimised), against 6.3e7 for Sanders' SK example.

5) kappa' correction (DERIVED; T3 set kappa' = 1). The quadratic speedup is relative to the walked chain P. So B* = kappa' (c N_Q t_Q / t_C)^2, where:
- kappa' = tau_P / B_best, the number of P steps per best-classical gradient evaluation.
- Rigorous lower bound from cost: kappa' >= t_C / t_P, i.e. >= 9 for torsion pivots and >= 0.75L (113 at L=150) for local Cartesian moves.
- Diffusive-regime estimate: kappa' ~ d^{3/4} kappa_c^{1/2} ~ 1e3 (INFERENCE).

6) Break-even per independent sample, L=150 (B* in evaluations, T* = quantum runtime at crossover).

| Scenario | B* | T* |
|---|---|---|
| Faithful D2, R=1, kappa'=9, c=3, one sample | 2.4e16 (measured t_C) to 1.5e19 (optimised) | 3.9e6 to 9.8e7 yr |
| Faithful D2, Babbush floor kappa'=c=S=1 | 3e14 | 4.8e4 yr |
| Faithful D2, central soft readout (kappa' 1e3, c=10, 100 samples) | >= 3e23 | — |
| Most generous stacked corner, one sample | 1.7e9 | 102 days |
| Same corner, optimised classical t_C | 1.1e12 | 7 yr |
| Same corner, soft readout (N_Q=12) | 2.5e11 to 1.6e14 | 40 to 1000 yr per target |

The most generous stacked corner means: floor Cartesian oracle, R=100 factories (~1e9 physical qubits), unoptimised single-core classical code, kappa' at its lower bound, c=3.

Across L, that corner gives B*_min(L) = 6.2e9 (60 aa), 3.0e9 (100 aa), 1.7e9 (150 aa), 7.6e8 (300 aa). QM-01's own kill line (C_class(150) <= 1e9) therefore sits at the single most generous corner.

These numbers are consistent with Sanders et al. ('a day and a million physical qubits' vs 'four CPU-minutes'; ~1 yr crossover for SK-512), Babbush et al. (quadratic, S=1e3: 100 d to 880 yr), Lemieux et al. (a quadratic speedup needs ~1 ns logical gates to match Janus; arXiv 1910.01659), and T5 (9e9 to 9e19).

Pilot at L=150, T=1: 3.7e5 gradient evaluations, zero round trips. The classical cost at T* has not been measured. Chen-Lovasz-Pak lifting bound: UNVERIFIED citation.
verdicts.decisive_test:
A paper derivation settles the practical question, and one CPU run settles the conditional window. The derivation is done; the CPU measurement has not been run.

Step 1 (done in this audit). The quantum runtime at crossover is T*(L) = kappa' c^2 N_Q^2 t_Q^2 / t_C. It does not depend on any classical mixing measurement. Its minimum over all stacked quantum-favourable choices is 102 days per sample and >= 40 years per soft-readout target. For the faithful oracle it is 4e6 years or more. Optimising the classical code only increases T*. On paper, no practical advantage exists.

Step 2 (8-core CPU, about 1 day; closes the theoretical-conditional window). Two pieces:
- Write a fused fp32 A80 energy+gradient kernel and measure t_C at L=150. If t_C <= 1 ms, B*_min rises from 1.7e9 to >= 4e10.
- Run the planned G1 NRPT+HMC and adaptive-SMC portfolio at a calibrated T* on 5O37A_150 and long40 (4 seeds). Record evaluations per independent sample to certified agreement.

If that per-sample cost is <= 1.7e9 (<= 2.5e11 for the 100-sample readout), QM-01 is dead in every corner, including its own stated kill criterion.

Optional ~1e7-evaluation check on one 60-aa crop: measure tau_P/B for single-residue Cartesian Metropolis against NRPT-HMC. This confirms kappa' >= 0.75L.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Break-even B* is the number of classical energy+gradient evaluations per independent sample above which quantum wins:
- Faithful learned-energy walk (5.1e8 Toffolis per step at 150 aa; 24 h per step on one factory; 2.4e4-4.9e4 logical and ~1e8 physical qubits): B* ~ 2.4e16 to 1.5e19 per sample. Quantum runtime at crossover is 4e6 to 1e8 years.
- Absolute floor, stacking a Cartesian local-move oracle (~3.9e6 Toffolis per step), 100 CCZ factories (~1e9 physical qubits), a single-core unoptimised classical code at 5.1 ms, kappa' at its derived lower bound and c=3: B* ~ 1.7e9 per sample (7.6e8 at 300 aa), with 102 days of quantum runtime per sample.
- The soft-readout target needs 1e2-1e3 samples, which run in parallel classically and in series on one QPU. That pushes B* to 2.5e11-1.6e14 and the runtime to 40-1000 years per target.
- Toffolis per sample at crossover: ~5e12 (floor) to ~7e17 (faithful).

The code-distance correction for these long runs (d = 39-51) adds another 1.6-2.7x against quantum. The oracle does not erase the asymptotic quadratic gap; the constant factor t_Q/t_C ~ 1e7 to 4e8, squared, puts the crossover out of reach.
verdicts.novelty_note:
The search found no evidence of a published Toffoli-level resource estimate for a coherent walk or QSA operator on a learned or off-lattice protein energy. Scope: the 448-paper literature set (commit 86ff140), the T3/T5 notes, and the domain notes, which flag this as an open gap. The repo's T3 model plus this audit appear to be the only such accounting within that scope.

The kappa' correction is new relative to T3, which assumed kappa' = 1. It says the quadratic gain is measured against the walked reversible chain, not against HMC or lifted chains, with kappa' >= 0.75L for local Cartesian moves. The underlying principle is standard (Apers-Ticozzi-Sarlette, arXiv 1705.08253). The search found no evidence that it has been applied to protein break-even analyses in the scanned literature.

The measured t_C figures were taken with synthetic pair tables; they time the arithmetic but do not stand in for real esmprior outputs.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for this protein instance: it is a formulation only. No separation has been shown for the esmprior/A80 posterior, and none has been shown against lifted, non-reversible, PT or HMC samplers. Generic support exists for the primitive only. (1) L6-quadratic walk-step speedup against REVERSIBLE chains in an oracle model (Szegedy 2004; Somma et al. 2008; Wocjan-Abeyesinghe 2008; Harrow-Wei 2020; warm start per Orsucci et al. 2018). (2) Provable Omega(alpha) vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) continuous separation, but only on hide-and-seek wells on the torus (Olivucci et al., arXiv 2608.24527). Nobody has shown that such wells occur in this landscape. Against the best classical local sampler the gain is quadratic only when the gap is conductance-limited (delta ~ Phi, i.e. metastable). When the gap is diffusive (delta ~ Phi^2), a lifted chain already reaches ~1/Phi ~ 1/sqrt(delta) (Chen-Lovasz-Pak 1999; Apers-Sarlette-Ticozzi PRA 98, 032115; Dervovic arXiv 1712.02318). So the premise that "signed mixtures cannot be realised classically" does not by itself give an advantage over non-reversible or HMC samplers.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No classical mixing failure has been measured on the target, so the reopening burden of DNR-10/K-007 is not met. Prior evidence runs against the value premise. The break-even point is at least 1e9 to 1e10 gradient evaluations per independent sample at 150 aa. On this 8-core box that is roughly 40 CPU-days or more per sample (measured 3.5 ms per batched gradient evaluation at 150 aa), so the proposed ~1-day campaign can only KILL. It cannot certify C_class >= B(L).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The problem is information-limited and verification-limited, not computation-limited.

(1) VALUE: the premise is weaker than stated. The S33 1.40x MDE soft-readout signal was measured against HARD CVaR TAILS, a readout already killed (K-004). Against the ARGMIN, the exact 262,144-state Gibbs posterior mean gave only -0.170 A (0.33x MDE) on mid30 and -0.159 A (0.47x) on long40, and H-Q1 ('posterior-mean readout beats argmin') was FALSIFIED. The S33 authors wrote that the cloud gain "is mostly contraction, which the canonical projection removes" (+0.20 A projection penalty vs +0.01 for the argmin). Condition C fails on the relaxed prior: E901/E903 show that 'the prior cannot tell which relaxed structure is closer to the native'. The program's own uncommitted G1 pilot at T=1 is single-seed, has 0 round trips and is not at equilibrium, so it is indicative only. In it, the posterior-expected RMSD is within 0.03-0.38 A of the lowest-energy sample. Posterior spread is 1.0-3.7 A pairwise RMSD. The posterior sits 5.5-11.6 A from native at 60-150 aa (3GAHA_60 11.58 A, 4LPQA_120 10.89 A, 5O37A_150 6.30 A). A faster sampler of a posterior whose mass is on the wrong fold cannot deliver structure accuracy.

(2) COST: NRPT communication barrier Lambda grows only ~L^0.64 (13.6 at 45 aa to 29.3 at 150 aa; 7.05 at T=8 for 45 aa). The path cost is therefore polynomial, and any gap must come from within-rung metastability. QSA and SMC stage counts are equal by the BC >= (1+chi^2)^-1/2 lemma, so the whole gain is at most a per-stage square root. With a quantum walk step of >=1e6 Toffolis at ~1e3-1e4 Toffolis/s (assumption) against 1.5-3.5 ms per classical gradient evaluation, R = 3e4-7e7 and break-even is tau* ~ R^2 ~ 1e9-5e15 steps per sample. QSA also yields one sample per anneal (no cloning), while PT/SMC are embarrassingly parallel.

(3) VERIFICATION PARADOX: in the only regime where quantum could pay (C_class >= B(L)), the classical baseline cannot be run to certify either the posterior or its transmission to accuracy. The claim would rest entirely on extrapolation from L <= 100 aa.

(4) RELEVANCE: real 60-150 aa structures and ensembles come from amortised generators (AF2, ESMFold, BioEmu with reweighting) in seconds. esmprior_v1 (510k parameters, trained on 600 crops <= 72 aa) has no demonstrated native information at >= 60 aa, so sampling its posterior is a self-constructed proxy bottleneck, not a protein-science computation anyone needs at 1e10 steps.

verdicts.decisive_test:
TRANSMISSION-FIRST KILL TEST (about 4-8 CPU-hours on 8 cores), run before any mixing-time campaign. A faster sampler has no value if the sampled soft readout does not beat the argmin.

1. On long40 (45 targets, 44-60 aa) plus the g1 ladder (16 targets at 60/80/100 aa), rerun the existing 256-restart A80 mode census.
2. Polish every mode to a positive-definite Hessian (L-BFGS to gradient norm <1e-4; the current census has n_nonpos ~107).
3. Form the classical darting/Laplace mixture over basins: w_k ∝ exp(-E_k/T) det(H_k/T)^{-1/2}. Use a native-free T* ladder (T = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64), choosing T* by a pre-registered rule (e.g. posterior ESS or held-out log-likelihood on tuning126/mid30, not native RMSD).
4. Compute the aligned, projected soft structure and compare it with the A80 argmin by paired MDE.

KILL QM-01 if the best pre-registered T* gives < 1.0x MDE against the argmin on long40, as the exact-enumeration precedent did (0.47x). Note this test sets the classical darting twin as the bar a quantum sampler must beat, not only the argmin.

Only if it PASSES: run the stated G1 NRPT+HMC / adaptive SMC campaign at T* to measure C_class(L) at 45-100 aa (4 seeds, 1e7 gradient evaluations per target). Then compute on paper B(L) = (c R)^2 using the measured t_C = 0.6-3.5 ms and a costed walk step (H-008). Kill if the extrapolated C_class(150) < B(150), or if the landscape census shows diffusive rather than conductance-limited gaps (delta ~ Phi^2; Lambda sublinear), in which case lifted, non-reversible or HMC samplers already capture the square root.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Measured classical cost on this box (G1 pilot, batched torch): 0.59 / 0.78 / 1.46 / 2.39 / 3.51 ms per gradient evaluation at 45 / 60 / 100 / 120 / 150 aa.

Assumed quantum walk step: 1e6-1e8 Toffolis (H-008; this is the program's own I(agent) estimate, not published) at ~1e3-1e4 Toffolis/s (Babbush et al. 2021-type assumption). That gives 1e2-1e5 s per step, so R = 3e4-7e7. For a pure quadratic speedup, break-even is ~R^2 = 1e9-5e15 classical gradient evaluations per independent sample, before the extra costs listed below. At 150 aa, 1e9 evaluations take about 3.5e6 s (~40 days) on 8 cores. The proposed ~1e7 evaluations per target (about 10 h at 150 aa) can therefore only certify C_class <= 1e7 (kill), never C_class >= B(L).

Extra costs on the quantum side:
- QSA stage count (equal to SMC's by the BC lemma), with phase-estimation and log overheads;
- no cloning, so one sample per anneal, and the readout needs ~1e2-1e3 independent samples;
- no parallel-chain amortisation, which PT/SMC get for free.

The rough candidate estimate (>= ~1e10-1e16 steps per sample) is consistent with this.

title: Hide-and-seek narrow wells: provable continuous-Gibbs separation vs white-box discovery, calibration and the DMDGP ceiling
merged_from: qalg QM-02 (PT + quantum narrow-well discovery), complexity 'Hide-and-seek on the backbone torus (DMDGP ceiling)', learned 'Composite-likelihood overconfidence as source of hide-and-seek wells', classical 'Continuous quantum Langevin (lead M2) vs white-box mode discovery'
summary: Q: does the learned-energy posterior at T* contain narrow, deep basins that carry mass (persistence / hide-and-seek) yet are almost never reached by prior-initialised descents or PT? Quantum: Olivucci et al. [A45] continuous Gibbs sampler, Omega(alpha) classical vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) quantum queries, alpha = e^{beta*Delta}; minimal form is fixed-point AA of the product head prior onto a native-free sublevel set {E < E_thr}. Replaces: rare-mode discovery only; masses, polishing and averaging stay classical. Mechanism: amplitudes add under the Grover iterate (k*sqrt(p)) while classical trials add probabilities. The lower bound covers value/gradient/any-derivative QUERIES in the black-box model. Caveats: (i) classical restarts target the basin of attraction p_att >> the sublevel-set volume p, so quantum wins only if 1/sqrt(p) < 1/p_att; (ii) the energy is WHITE-BOX, a sum of 1-D pair tables. Case A (unimodal tables, rigid sharp-pair graph): DG/EDM locates wells from table minima in poly(L), which dequantises the separation. Case B (k-modal tables, register ambiguity): locating wells is a DMDGP instance (NP-hard) and quantum backtracking is again quadratic in the tree. Claimed ceiling: max(quadratic in alpha, quadratic in T_BP). Likely origin: E_pair is an unadjusted pairwise composite likelihood (Varin-Reid-Firth), so clusters of confidently wrong bins (1,168 ESM false-positive contacts, 57% within +-2 register) create narrow, overconfident, artefactual wells that native-free recalibration can delete. Speedup: quadratic in alpha (query). Oracle: threshold/gradient oracle (QM-05); pays only if p_att < ~1e-10 per mass-carrying basin. Competitor: table-cluster enumeration + cluster-seeded L-BFGS, darting/mode-jumping MH, lambda-tempering of long-range pair terms, nested sampling, NRPT. Info vs comp: wells are properties of the model's calibration; if calibration removes them there was never a computational problem. S29-S33: E800b restart saturation (7.08 -> 4.35 A by 32-64 restarts, floor 4.21 A) is direct evidence of case A at 44-60 aa; M9/DNR-07 bound restart gains at <=0.14 A. Open only at >=100 aa. Kill: min p_hit >= 1e-4 for every >=1%-mass basin at 60-150 aa; OR >=90% of high-mass narrow modes are seeded by top-k table clusters; OR at calibrated T* narrow modes hold <5% mass or are not >=3x narrower (funnel). Test: calibrate T* on held-out prots/ by posterior-predictive coverage (never long40 RMSD); on 12 long40 targets run 1,000 prior-initialised descents + 24-replica PT; cluster; record basin mass, Hessian log-volume, p_hit, Woodard persistence, DG coverage of PT modes, planted-well control; repeat at T=1. ~1 day. Track: C theory/query, then B. Prior: low (3-5%).
dead_reason: Matrix M2 is INTERESTING (top theory line); restart saturation bounds it only at <=60 aa.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 on the protein instance family. The Omega(alpha) vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) separation of Olivucci et al. [A45, arXiv:2608.24527, verified] is L6, but only for its information-local, black-box hide-and-seek family, and it provably does not transfer to this energy. DERIVED (proof sketch): E(x) is linear in its pair-table grid values plus a small, known local head. The parameter count is P ~ 2*(L-3)(L-2)/2*1001, i.e. 9.5e6 at L=100 and 2.2e7 at L=150 (about 5e4 gradient queries at L=100). So a classical algorithm can identify the whole energy with at most P+1 generic value queries and then sample offline with no further queries. The classical query complexity of sampling is therefore at most poly(L)*G. The Omega(alpha) bound cannot hold once alpha > P, while the measured alpha is at least 1e172 (T5 note, L=45). On this family the Õ(sqrt(alpha)) quantum algorithm needs at least 1e86 queries, about 79 orders of magnitude more than classical identification. What remains is an offline computational problem: locating wells in known tables is distance geometry, or DMDGP in the k-modal case. The best known quantum speedup there is quadratic in the search-tree size (Montanaro backtracking), and classical branch-and-prune is polynomial under protein-like pruning assumptions (Liberti-Lavor-Masson-Mucherino, arXiv:1103.1264). The claimed ceiling max(quadratic in alpha, quadratic in T_BP) therefore collapses to "quadratic in T_BP", and T_BP is empirically about 1 (see practical).
verdicts.level_practical:
L0. I measured this directly this session on the vendored A80/esmprior_v1 energy at T=1, using the same 200-iteration batched L-BFGS as scripts/g1_mode_census.py. A deterministic white-box construction finds the deep basins that prior-initialised restarts and PT miss. The construction is: expected distances from the distograms, then classical MDS plus weighted SMACOF, then both chiralities, then L-BFGS. That is 2 descents, about 400 gradient evaluations.
(a) This expected-distance pair gave the lowest DG basin in 61/64 crop runs (L=80: 15/16; L=100: 15/16; L=120: 15/16; L=150: 16/16), out of 16-64 DG seeds per crop.
(b) Against 256 prior restarts (about 55k gradient evaluations, i.e. 18x the DG budget), DG found lower energy in 8/16 targets at L=80, 12/16 at L=100 (by 129-403 nats) and 6/7 at L=120 (by 219-638 nats).
(c) Against the PT pilots (375k-478k gradient evaluations, over 100x the DG budget), DG was 33 nats lower at 5O37A_100, 70 at 4LPQA_120 and 80 at 5O37A_150.
So the rare, deep basins that look hide-and-seek to a proposal that ignores the tables (census p_hit about 1/256 to 0.05 at L=100-120) are read straight off the tables. That is Case A dequantisation, with p_att of order 1.
Deeper does not mean more native-like (condition C). At 5O37A_120 the DG basin is 276 nats deeper than the census best but has RMSD 8.77 vs 4.98 A. The glassy targets (6/16 at each of L=120 and L=150, every seed in a separate basin) are the low-information ones: median RMSD 10.3 A at L=120 and 7.5 A at L=150, vs 3.6 and 4.4 A for the funnel targets. The problem is information-limited, not computation-limited.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
1) Unknown unknowns. No classical method certifies that no deeper basin exists. An adversarial well could be spread as many weak pair biases, each below its table's modal bin, so the expected-distance seed would not see it (class O). Answer: the family is still linear in the tables, so it is query-identifiable, and the hardness becomes offline and spin-glass-like, where known quantum gains are Grover or backtracking (quadratic) and are killed by the break-even. Such wells would also be the artefacts of a mis-calibrated composite likelihood that the candidate itself predicts.
2) Everything here was measured at T=1. At a coverage-calibrated T* (Varin-Reid-Firth / Ribatet-Cooley-Davison magnitude adjustment, arXiv:0911.5357) mass spreads over many basins and the task becomes ensemble sampling. Answer: temperature makes narrow wells lose mass entropically. The PT communication barrier falls with T (tscan 5O37A_45 in progress: Lambda about 11.4, 10.1, 9.2, 7.1 at T=1, 2, 4, 8). Warm-start mode-jumping samplers mix in polynomial time given one start per mode (Re-ALPS, arXiv:2512.17977), and the 64 distogram-draw DG seeds supply those starts.
3) Outside this scope (non-pairwise neural energies with nonlinear parameterisation, or L > 150), the identification argument fails and a hide-and-seek structure could exist. That would be a different candidate.
4) Caveat on my data: all endpoints are truncated 200-iteration descents. E-comparisons between methods use the same protocol, but absolute basin counts are inflated.

There is no window: the quantum run is faster only when 1/p_att > 3e9, and finishes within a day only when 1/p_att < (86400/t_Q)^2, about 6.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for the protein task. The Olivucci et al. [A45] Omega(alpha) vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) separation is a provable (L6-type) query result only for the constructed hide-and-seek family. T5 (research/theory/NO_GO_RESULTS/T5_quadratic_ceiling.md, Theorem A) shows it is exactly quadratic, and in practice it is Grover applied to rejection sampling. The A80 learned energy is not a member of that family, for two reasons. (1) It is white-box and pair-additive: every 1-D pair table exposes the location of a well through its minima, so the energy is not information-local and Lemma 1 does not apply. (2) Its alpha is vacuous: beta*Delta >= 2.05e4 nats at L=100 (E_pair falls from a prior mean of 41,134 to a posterior mean of 20,614), so alpha >= 10^8900 and sqrt(alpha) >= 10^4450. What survives is a conditional L1 statement: IF a funnel-free (golf-hole) well carrying >= 1% of the mass exists with a best-classical hit probability p, THEN amplitude amplification saves a factor of about 1/(1.38 sqrt(p)) in calls. No such well has been shown to exist.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. The minimal form of the idea (amplitude amplification of the product head prior onto a sublevel set) is dead by 30 to 200 orders of magnitude, whatever the hardware. Even the idealised golf-hole case needs a best-classical hit probability p_C < ~1e-15 per mass-carrying basin at 170 us per Toffoli (S=1), and it breaks even only after T* = 1.3e3 to 1.7e5 years. Against 1e3 cores the requirement becomes p* ~ 1e-21 with T* ~ 1e6 to 2e8 years. Every census basin measured so far has p_hit >= 1/256, and parallel tempering (PT) reached lower-energy states than restarts on 3 of 3 crops.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
(1) The KL values below come from thermodynamic integration over non-round-tripping NRPT chains (0 round trips), so the averages <E_pair>_lambda may be biased. The exponent could be wrong by a factor of about 2. Even a factor-of-10 error leaves p_sub <= 1e-6.6 at lambda=0.1 for L=100, and the minimal form is killed by the p_att argument regardless (point 3 of the evidence).
(2) The census is censored at 1/256. At L=100, 5 of 13 crops hit the best mode at most 3 times in 256 restarts, and PT found states 4, 31 and 357 nats below the best restart at L=45, 60 and 100. So restarts do miss deep states and a hard tail exists. A golf-hole basin with p_C < 1e-15 is not experimentally excluded at L >= 100.
(3) Under a hypothetical 1 us Toffoli, the golf-hole break-even is T* = 16 days to 2.2 years at S=1. That is not astronomical in that idealisation.
(4) Amplitude amplification could start from a better coherent proposal than the product prior. The two such proposals are costed elsewhere and both fail. A coherent relaxation map (T4) has p* ~ 3e-18 and T* ~ 1e9 years. A coherent tempered-posterior qsample needs walk operators, which returns the question to the T2/T3 sampling-mixing break-even B(L) >= 1.5e15 energy+gradient evaluations per independent sample (D2 central, S=1). Rebuttal to (2) and (3): a pair-additive energy rewards partial satisfaction, which makes a funnel, and its 1-D tables leak where the well is. Table-cluster seeding and distance-geometry/EDM seeding then dequantise the problem (Case A). Case B, the DMDGP backtracking case, is again only quadratic.
verdicts.evidence:
All derivations are in this audit. The pilot numbers come from research/results/RAW/g1_pilot/*.npz (pair_trace, lams) and research/results/RAW/g1_modes/*_R256_s0.json.

(A) Oracle and resource count for the minimal form (one Grover iterate = A (prep of the product head prior), then compute E(x), compare with the threshold, uncompute, then A^dagger, then the reflection). Costs come from the T3 cost model (research/theory/T3_resource_model.py, D2 per-pair cubic splines in d^2, QROAM, u=2):
- C_E = 2.1e7 / 5.7e7 / 1.3e8 Toffolis at L = 60 / 100 / 150 (central).
- Prior prep is 1.6 to 4.2e6 Toffolis (Grover-Rudolph over 256 head bins plus jitter).
- One iterate costs G = 4.4e7 / 1.2e8 / 2.7e8 Toffolis (generous parameters: 2.0e7 / 5.2e7 / 1.1e8).
- At 170 us per Toffoli (one CCZ factory; Sanders 2020 arXiv:2007.07391, Babbush 2021 arXiv:2011.04149) that is 2.1 h / 5.7 h / 12.5 h per iterate.
- Logical qubits: 2.0e4 / 3.3e4 / 4.9e4, dominated by stored frames.
- The pair tables are about 1.6 Gbit of classical data compiled into QROM at L=100. This affects compile cost, not qubit count.
- The self-consistent code distance at break-even run lengths is d = 47 to 57, which gives 0.7 to 3.3e8 physical qubits.
- The Olivucci variant needs gradient queries, about 3x C_E each.
- Fixed-point amplitude amplification (Yoder-Low-Chuang style) or Durr-Hoyer with an unknown threshold multiplies the query count by about 1.6 to 2.2.

(B) Prior mass of the sublevel set, DERIVED. The tempering path pi_lambda ∝ pi_0 exp(-lambda E_pair) is exactly the exponential tilt of E_pair under the prior. The Chernoff bound gives P0(E_pair <= t) <= exp(lambda t + log Z(lambda)). At t = <E_pair>_lambda this equals exp(-KL(pi_lambda||pi_0)). A narrow basin can carry mass only if its energy is below the mean, so every narrow, deep, mass-carrying well has prior mass p_sub <= e^{-KL}. Thermodynamic integration on the 5 pilot NRPT traces (PILOT) gives:

| crop | KL at lambda=1 | KL at lambda~0.1 | KL at lambda~0.01 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5O37A_45 | 113 nats (p <= 1e-49) | 35 nats | 8 nats |
| 3GAHA_60 | 142 nats (1e-61) | 35 nats (1e-15) | 9.5 nats |
| 5O37A_100 | 457 nats (1e-198) | 154 nats (1e-67) | 36 nats (1e-16) |
| 4LPQA_120 | 504 nats (1e-219) | 140 nats | 43 nats |
| 5O37A_150 | 960 nats (1e-417) | 227 nats (1e-98) | 68 nats (1e-30) |

At L=100 this means 1/sqrt(p_sub) >= 1e8 Grover iterates (lambda=0.01), 1e33 (lambda=0.1) and 1e99 (lambda=1). The quantum wall-clock is then >= 7e4 years, 7e28 years and 1e95 years, and that is only 1e8 x 5.7 h at the easiest temperature.

(C) Caveat (i) made quantitative. Classical L-BFGS restarts from the same prior hit the best census mode with p_att = 4e-3 to 0.14 at L=100 (median about 0.01 to 0.03). Each restart costs t_C = 1.3 s (216 gradient evaluations, measured). The ratio r = p_sub/p_att is therefore <= 1e-63. Quantum can win only if sqrt(p_sub) > c S t_Q p_att / t_C. With p_att = 1/256 the right-hand side is 85 > 1, so the minimal form cannot win for any p_sub <= 1. Even to be feasible it needs p_att < 4.6e-5 (S=1, 170 us).

(D) Golf-hole idealisation (r ≈ 1, p_att = p_sub = p). The classical side uses rejection sampling with measured single-thread batched energy evaluations of 0.53 / 0.87 ms at L = 60 / 100 (1.96 ms extrapolated at L=150). The break-even is p* = (t_C/(1.38 S t_Q))^2 and T* = 1.9 S t_Q^2 / t_C:

| t_Toffoli | S | L=60 | L=100 | L=150 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 170 us | 1 | p* = 2.6e-15, T* = 6.5e3 yr (1.5e4 yr after correcting d) | p* = 9.6e-16, T* = 2.9e4 yr (7.2e4 yr) | p* = 9.9e-16, T* = 6.3e4 yr (1.7e5 yr) |
| 170 us | 1e3 | p* ~ 1e-21, T* = 6e6 to 6e7 yr | same range | same range |
| 1 us | 1 | T* = 16 to 82 days | T* = 68 to 364 days | T* up to 2.2 yr |
| 1 us | 1e3 | T* = 45 to 2,200 yr | same range | same range |

Any quantum win takes wall-clock >= T*.

(E) The other forms are already costed:
- T4 coherent-relaxation amplitude amplification: p* ~ 3e-18, T* ~ 1e9 yr (research/theory/PROOFS/T4_amplified_mode_finding.md).
- T3 walk sampling: B(L) ~ 1.5e15 (S=1, R=1) and 1.5e17 (S=1e3, R=100).

(F) The classical adversary is already stronger than restarts. The NRPT posterior mean E_pair (20,614) sits below the best census restart (21,168 total) on 5O37A_100, and polished PT states beat 256 restarts on all 3 crops compared.

Citations: [A45] Olivucci et al. arXiv:2608.24527 (preprint); Sanders et al. PRX Quantum 1, 020312 (2020); Babbush et al. PRX Quantum 2, 010103 (2021), both verified in research/literature/BIBLIOGRAPHY.md. Chernoff/KL and thermodynamic integration are standard. Yoder-Low-Chuang fixed-point search is cited from memory and was not re-verified in this session.
verdicts.decisive_test:
A paper-level kill of the minimal form is already done here (thermodynamic-integration KL on the existing traces). The one cheap experiment left targets the golf-hole residue: run nested sampling on the learned energy for 5O37A_100, 4LPQA_120 and 5O37A_150, plus 3 long40 crops.
- Setup: n_live = 500, constrained-prior moves by prior-reflected slice or HMC. This takes about 2.5e5 NS iterations x 20 to 40 energy evaluations, roughly 5e6 to 1e7 evaluations, or 2 to 3 CPU-hours per crop at 0.87 ms per batched evaluation on 1 thread, well inside the 8-core / 95% ceiling.
- Readout: NS measures ln X(t) = ln P0(E <= t) directly.
- (a) Confirm ln X(<E>_{lambda*}) <= -30 nats at L >= 100. This independently validates the KL bound without relying on the non-mixing chains, and it fixes the Grover exponent.
- (b) Test ln X(E) against 1/T for a convex intruder (a first-order / golf-hole signature) and for bimodal energy histograms of the live points.
- (c) For any intruder found, take the basin's classical hit probability under the best portfolio (PT, cluster-seeded L-BFGS, NS itself) and compare it with p*(L) ~ 1e-15 (S=1, 170 us).
- KILL is final if ln X(E) is concave (funnel) on all crops, OR if every basin with >= 1% of the mass is hit with p_C >= 1e-4 by PT, NS or cluster seeding. That second condition is already met on every crop measured so far.
- The only outcome that reopens the candidate is a convex intruder carrying >= 1% of the mass with p_C < 1e-12 by every classical method. Even then, the practical case needs sub-microsecond Toffolis.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Per Grover iterate, where the iterate is one value oracle compute plus uncompute, prior prep and its inverse, and the reflections:

| L | Toffolis (central, generous) | logical qubits | physical qubits (d = 47 to 57) | wall-clock at 170 us |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 | 4.4e7, 2.0e7 | 2.0e4 | 0.7 to 3.3e8 across L | 2.1 h |
| 100 | 1.2e8, 5.2e7 | 3.3e4 | (as above) | 5.7 h |
| 150 | 2.7e8, 1.1e8 | 4.9e4 | (as above) | 12.5 h |

Pair-table lookups are 92 to 97% of the cost. A gradient oracle (for the Olivucci sampler) costs about 3x more. Fixed-point or unknown-threshold search costs 1.6 to 2.2x more in queries.

1. **Minimal form (product-prior amplitude amplification onto {E < E_thr}).** The required iterate count 1/sqrt(p_sub) >= e^{KL/2} is 1e8 to 1e99 at L=100 (lambda from 0.01 to 1). Restarts need 1/p_att ~ 1e2 to 1e2.4. The quantum side loses by at least 1e30 at any physically meaningful temperature. It cannot win for ANY p_sub while p_att >= t_C/(c S t_Q) = 4.6e-5 (S=1, 170 us). KILL independent of hardware.
2. **Golf-hole idealisation.** Break-even needs p* ≈ 1e-15 at 170 us and S=1, with T* = 6.5e3 to 6.3e4 years (1.5e4 to 1.7e5 years once d is corrected). At S=1e3: p* ≈ 1e-21, T* ≈ 1e7 to 1e8 years. At a hypothetical 1 us Toffoli: p* ≈ 3e-11 to 4e-10, T* ≈ 16 days to 2.2 years (S=1).
3. **Scaling with L.** The iterate cost and t_C both grow as L^2, so p* is flat in L and T* grows as L^2 (the same shape as T4).
4. **Other forms.** Coherent-relaxation amplitude amplification (T4): p* ~ 3e-18, T* ~ 1e9 years. Walk-based sampling (T3): B(L) ≥ 1.5e15 evaluations per independent sample.

The crossover sits at least 11 orders of magnitude below every measured hit probability (p_hit >= 1/256).
verdicts.novelty_note: The search found no evidence, within the program's 448-paper literature map and theory notes T2 to T5, of a fault-tolerant resource estimate for amplitude amplification onto a sublevel set of a learned protein energy, nor of a large-deviation bound on the sublevel-set prior mass for such an energy. The bound p_sub <= exp(-KL(pi_lambda||pi_0)) is Chernoff applied to the tempering path. It is standard mathematics, and its use here to rule out Grover or hide-and-seek on learned-energy posteriors is new to this program but trivial. It generalises: on any tempering-path sampler, KL(pi_T*||pi_0) sets the exponent of every prior-initialised quantum search. There is no novel quantum mechanism. The candidate reduces to Grover with an expensive oracle.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for the protein instance. The L6 result (Olivucci et al., arXiv 2608.24527, verified: Omega(alpha) classical vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) quantum gradient queries) holds only for its own black-box class: a smooth bump on a torus whose log-density is constant outside a small patch, so every value and derivative query there returns the same flat answer (the paper's Sec. III.1). The learned energy is not in that class. It is white-box, and it is a sum of O(L^2) soft-binned (sigma = 0.5 A) -log p pair tables plus theta/tau and steric terms (src/qapf/protein/energy.py), so gradients carry information almost everywhere. The only flat pieces are single pair terms inside one bin or beyond the open >40 A last bin; there is no global plateau. The mapping 'protein posterior contains A45-type instances' is therefore unproven (L0), and the candidate's Case-A dequantisation argument is itself only L0/L1. The Case-B ceiling (quadratic in the backtracking tree size T_BP) is prior art in substance: Montanaro 2018 (bibliography C57) plus Lavor et al. 2022 (below).
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No quantum or classical evidence shows that a mass-carrying narrow basin exists that prior-initialised descents or PT miss while it matters for structure. The in-progress G1 data (raw, uncommitted, preliminary, I(agent)) point the other way. At L=100, PT at T=1 finds minima far below the 256-restart best, but at the same RMSD: 5O37A_100 is 358 energy units lower at 5.54 vs 5.56 A; 3GAHA_60 is 31 units lower at 11.31 vs 12.14 A. Condition C reappears: deeper wells do not transmit to structure accuracy.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
(1) Wrong instance class. The A45 lower bound is purely informational, a hide-and-seek adversary over a derivative-free plateau. The learned pair energy gives informative gradients everywhere and is white-box, so the basin of attraction p_att is much larger than the sublevel-set volume p, and table-cluster seeding or distance geometry can locate wells directly. Nothing in A45 transfers to a white-box sum of 1-D tables.

(2) The minimal quantum form is already killed. Fixed-point amplitude amplification of the product prior onto {E < E_thr} is Grover over prior-seeded descents, i.e. AA-2/M9 amplitude-amplified restarts and QA-2 Grover, both KILLED in the literature phase (OPPORTUNITY_MATRIX M9: at most ~8x fewer calls, and quadratic fails the fault-tolerant test [C64, C65]). The output is consumed as an energy-ordered cut, so it sits in H-001 class (b), and DNR-07 applies at <=60 aa (E800b restart saturation; M9 bound <=0.14 A).

(3) Protein relevance is circular. The candidate's own origin story is that narrow wells are composite-likelihood overconfidence artefacts. If so, the quantum sampler finds artefacts faster, and the correct fix is classical recalibration, which is information, not computation. Also, esmprior_v1 was trained on crops <=72 aa, but the claim is 'open only at >=100 aa', so any wells there are out-of-distribution extrapolations of a 510k-parameter head, not physical metastable states.

(4) Existing data (preliminary, I(agent), from research/results/RAW/g1_modes/*.json, 80 runs, 16 targets x L in {30,45,60,80,100}, 256 restarts x 200 L-BFGS iterations, T=1) show a funnel/glass dichotomy, not persistence. The hit probability of the best-found mode correlates with accuracy (Spearman p_hit vs best-mode RMSD = -0.57, p = 3e-8, n = 80). The gap between the best and second mode also correlates (Spearman -0.55, p = 1e-7). Confident targets form funnels: 2AB0A, 8AXJA, 5O37A and 9PGXA at 60–80 aa hit the best mode 12–40% of the time, with gaps of 100–250 units and RMSD 2–3 A. Rarely hit best modes (p_hit = 1/256) occur on information-poor targets with RMSD 7–12.7 A, e.g. 3GAHA_60, 7B4RA_60, 9IXCA_60, 3TE4A_60. Hard-to-find deep modes coincide with wrong folds, which is the opposite of useful hide-and-seek.

(5) T=1 is grossly overconfident. PT pilots at L=100–150 show 0 round trips, NRPT Lambda of 25–29 and posterior RMSD SD of 0.07–0.34 A. Energy gaps of 40–250 units put essentially all mass (weights of order e^-40 to e^-250 for competing modes) on one mode. At a calibrated T* the barriers alpha = e^{Delta/T*} shrink, so any query advantage collapses toward the classical regime.

Caveat on this evidence: 200 L-BFGS iterations do not converge. Median non-positive Hessian eigenvalues are 104 of 195 dimensions at L=100, so the census 'modes' and Laplace masses are unreliable, and unfound modes are unmeasured by construction. This keeps the verdict at WEAK rather than KILL.

title: Gates on what any faster sampler can buy: readout-visible slow modes (delta_f, H(B)), walk-vs-lift ratio sqrt(delta)/Phi, and learned-transport preconditioning
merged_from: complexity 'Readout-specific mixing gate (delta_f, H(B))', complexity 'Quantum walk vs every classical lift: ratio Theta(sqrt(delta)/Phi)', learned 'Learned transport maps shrink what quantum Langevin accelerates (C_PI in latent coordinates)'
summary: Q: after the strongest classical adversaries are applied, how much of QM-01's quadratic gain is left, and does it touch the built chain? Quantum: walk-based mean estimation / QRELD (as QM-01). Mechanism, three proven or derivable gates (I(prog)): (1) Readout gate: expand the soft-readout functional f = sum c_k phi_k. The classical cost is O~(1/delta_f + tau_f sigma^2/eps^2), with delta_f the gap of the slow modes f actually overlaps, while walk estimation pays the GLOBAL gap. If delta_f >> delta (e.g. a mirror-swap slow mode with identical aligned mean), classical wins regardless. The accuracy value of any sampler is bounded by H(B) = RMSD(readout at classical budget B) - RMSD(readout under exact pi). (2) Lift gate: a lift cannot raise conductance, so t_mix(lift) >= 1/(4 Phi), while the walk costs ~1/sqrt(delta); by Cheeger, T_lift/T_QW = Omega(sqrt(delta)/Phi). Diffusive regime (delta ~ Phi^2): lifts/NRPT match the walk. Metastable regime (delta ~ Phi): the full quadratic survives against every lift of that chain. (3) Transport gate: compare sqrt(C_PI(x)) * C_grad^Q against C_PI(z) * C_grad^C in NeuTra/flow latents or prior-quantile coordinates u = F_q(theta,tau). If C_PI(z) <= sqrt(C_PI(x)), quantum loses before overhead. Only barriers flows cannot remove survive (plausibly QM-02's narrow wells). Speedup: none of its own; bounds QM-01/12/15. Oracle: none (classical measurements). Competitor: NRPT, lifted chains, NeuTra-HMC, u-space HMC, MSM estimates. Info vs comp: H(infinity) is set by esmprior information; only H(B) - H(infinity) is computational headroom. S29-S33: sharpens DNR-10's reopening condition from 'mixing failure' to 'mixing failure visible to the readout functional'. Kill (quantum relevance): soft readout at <=1e7 evals within 0.3x MDE of a 1e9 / exact-register reference; OR delta_f/delta >= 100; OR delta/Phi^2 <= 10 at all L in 44-120; OR latent tau_int <= sqrt(raw tau_int). Test: 10 mid30 + 10 long40 targets, PT at 1e5-1e8 evals for the H(B) curve, TICA+MSM (200-500 states) for delta, Phi (PCCA+) and projections onto the 5 slowest modes; HMC raw vs u-space vs small-IAF NeuTra, 25->60 aa. 10-20 CPU-hours, reusing the QM-01 runs. Track: C theory/query. Prior: low for a surviving gain; high decision value.
