- State the information-locus-inversion lemma: when the non-diagonal term is instance-independent and the diagonal has poly description, adjacency-oracle lower bounds are vacuous.
- KILL QM-09 as an experimental lane if A80 has poly Lipschitz and poly description (expected), leaving only T5 G5/G10 as a pure-complexity open problem.

Drop the proposed CTQW-vs-PERM runs. At L <= 16 exact enumeration is the baseline, and localisation under disorder is already established (Keating 2007; Jackson 2012; Muthukrishnan 2019), so the outcome is foregone.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
No instance exists, so there is no break-even to compute.

Cost if QHD were run on A80 at L = 60 (d = 115, INFERENCE):
- Queries: LZW's Otilde(d^3) scaling, which is NOT established for A80, gives about 1.5e6 coherent energy queries.
- Cost per query: about 1e8 Toffolis per coherent A80 evaluation (T4 S7: C_step about 1.6e8 per reversible gradient step at L = 60; T3 about 4.6e4 Toffolis per pair x 1,770 pairs).
- Total: about 1e14 Toffolis. That is about 5 years at 1 us per Toffoli, or centuries at T3's 170 us single-factory rate.
- Classical side: the full 256-restart L-BFGS census at L = 60 costs 52,363 gradient evaluations in about 80 CPU-s (g1_summary, 2AB0A_60).

A quadratic-only gain would need >= 1e12 classical steps per sample (T5 section 4.5: 2.1e12 at L = 45). Only a genuinely (sub)exponential white-box separation could pay, and none is known for any non-cryptographic, non-algebraic explicit energy.
verdicts.novelty_note:
The arXiv-API search found no paper that tests whether GHV, LWWZ, welded-tree or hierarchical-graph super-polynomial separations transfer to protein energies or conformational graphs (scope: arXiv abstracts 2002-2026; web search engines unavailable this session).

Each component of the proposed no-go is prior art:
- (i) The explicit-naming lemma is folklore in the welded-tree literature: random labels are essential (from memory, unverified quote).
- (ii) The description-complexity barrier is largely already in this repo (T5 Proposition C1 caveat; gaps G5 and G10).
- (iii) Disorder-induced localisation on glued trees is published (Keating et al. 2007; Jackson et al. 2012; Muthukrishnan et al. 2019).

Two things are new:
- The information-locus-inversion framing: the instance sits off-diagonal in the separations but on-diagonal in proteins. As a result DNR-11's reopening condition is not met in substance.
- The correction that A80 is O(L)-body in torsion coordinates, which invalidates the 'bounded body order' phrasing of no-go (ii).

Both belong as a short theory note closing T1 G-12/B5. They do not justify a new research lane.

Add to BIBLIOGRAPHY: Lu & Li 2019 (the nearest protein CTQW paper, weak baseline), Ramos et al. 2025, Hamoudi et al. 2026, LWWZ 2025, BLH 2023, Chakrabarti et al. 2025, Liu et al. 2026, Muthukrishnan et al. 2019, Keating et al. 2007.

title: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent / coherent tunnelling through tall thin barriers (argmin search and barrier-crossing variants)
merged_from: qalg QM-11 (QHD global minimisation at >=80 aa), complexity 'Tunnelling through tall thin barriers vs soft-core HREX and PIMC', priorart (c) QHD / continuous-space quantum optimisation
summary: Q: beyond the restart-saturated regime, do learned energies have tall-thin barriers (e.g. chain crossing through soft sterics) that coherent Schrodinger dynamics crosses faster than thermal activation, and do lower minima or crossings improve the chain? Quantum: QHD H(t) = e^{phi_t}(-Laplacian/2) + e^{chi_t} f(x) on a d = 2L-5 grid (QFT kinetic term, phase oracle); Riemannian QHD on the torsion torus; quantum Langevin. Replaces: multi-restart L-BFGS / basin hopping (argmin variant) or local-MCMC barrier crossing (sampling variant). Mechanism: early kinetic phase delocalises (coherent smoothing), late phase concentrates amplitude; WKB tunnelling ~exp(-c w sqrt(Delta)) beats activation exp(-beta Delta) when barriers are thin and tall. Separations exist only on constructed instances (Leng-Zheng-Wu, empirical classical hardness); no speedup for convex problems (Chakrabarti et al. 2025). Classical adversaries that copy the EFFECT: Gaussian homotopy/DEM continuation (Piela-Scheraga 1989), soft-core Hamiltonian replica exchange (lambda-softened sterics; target unchanged at lambda=1), pivot/crankshaft moves, SQA/PIMC. Tunnelling keeps room only for thin barriers generated by the pair-distance terms themselves (not softenable without changing pi). Speedup: none known for this landscape. Oracle: phase oracle per Trotter step 1e6-1e8 Toffolis, ~700-1000 grid qubits at 60 aa, thousands of steps; potential synthesis dominates for tabulated energies (arXiv 2607.16996). Info vs comp: argmin is information-limited at <=60 aa (decoder 4.35 vs floor 4.21 A; condition C rho -0.08). S29-S33: the argmin variant falls under K-002/DNR-02, K-006 and DNR-07 restart saturation at <=60 aa; it reopens only if QM-02/C-2 finds a growing search gap at >=80 aa AND condition C passes. The sampling variant (barrier census) is not covered by those kills. Kill: best energy saturates within ~1e3 restarts and |rho(E,RMSD)| <= 0.1 at every length tested; OR thin tall barriers appear only in steric terms and soft-core HREX gives polynomial round trips; OR barriers are broad (w sqrt(Delta) >= beta Delta). Test: long40 + 70-120-aa native-free crops (OOD-flagged): restarts R = 1..1024, Gaussian homotopy, within-target Spearman(E,RMSD) over the top 100 minima; NEB paths between PT basins with Delta, width and steric vs pair decomposition; 8-replica soft-core HREX vs PT round trips. <= 1 day. Track: C theory/query (B if pursued). Prior: low.
dead_reason: Argmin variant is covered by K-002/DNR-02/DNR-07 at <=60 aa, but the >=80 aa regime and the barrier-crossing sampling variant fall outside existing kills.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for the protein / learned-energy family: no separation statement exists for A80-type energies, and no barrier-shape theorem applies to them. The only rigorous QHD advantage result is Leng–Zheng–Wu (arXiv:2311.00811). It proves a QHD upper bound of O~(d^3) queries plus O~(d^4) gates on a constructed family; the classical hardness side was only EMPIRICAL. This session dequantised that family in practice. Gaussian homotopy (DEM, 1989) solved 100% of instances at d = 16 to 2048 with 2,100 gradient queries per run, a count that does not depend on d. Isotropic Langevin annealing solved it in poly(d). So the constructed separation does not survive as a super-polynomial one (PILOT numerics plus an elementary rotation-covariance derivation; not peer-reviewed). The convex case gives no speedup with exact oracles (Chakrabarti et al., arXiv:2503.24332). Their super-quadratic gain needs noisy evaluations, and the A80 energy is exact. The theoretical level of QM-10 on the protein family is therefore L0.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No simulation, resource-normalised comparison or hardware result exists for QHD, tunnelling or QLD on any protein or learned energy. The fault-tolerant cost per QHD run is 1e4–1e6 times the measured classical time-to-best-basin at 60–80 aa (see the break-even note).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The actual landscape does show real classical hardness, and nobody has measured barrier shapes on it.
(1) G1 pilot: λ-path NRPT with HMC plus prior-proposal pivot moves made 0 round trips at L = 45–150. Λ grew from 13.6 to 29.3, so nonlocal classical moves do not yet mix at T = 1.
(2) Unconverged census (200 L-BFGS iterations): median p_hit is 0.016 at 100 aa and hits the 1/256 floor at 100–120 aa. Within-target Spearman(E, mode RMSD) is 0.20, 0.36 and 0.31 on three 120-aa crops, so condition C may pass beyond 60 aa. That would reopen the argmin variant's relevance.
(3) Real-time coherent QHD is not stoquastic ground-state dynamics, so the PIMC-equivalence results (Isakov 2016; Crosson–Harrow 2016; Jiang 2016) do not formally cover it.
(4) QMC can be exponentially slower than incoherent tunnelling when there are many homotopy-inequivalent tunnelling paths (Andriyash–Amin, arXiv:1703.09277). A chain-topology landscape might produce such paths. Stoquastic adiabatic separations exist (Hastings–Freedman, arXiv:1302.5733; Gilyén–Vazirani, arXiv:2011.09495).
(5) Gaussian homotopy is not a universal adversary. DEM underperformed basin hopping on non-separable Lennard-Jones and peptide landscapes, and it wins on the Leng–Zheng–Wu family only because that family is rotated-separable.
(6) My MEP pilot on the A80 energy did not converge. Pair-term-generated thin barriers are therefore not excluded by measurement.

Why this does not rescue QM-10:
(a) The measured bottleneck is collective, either first-order-like along λ or glassy. Adiabatic and tunnelling gaps also close exponentially at first-order transitions (Bapst–Semerjian, arXiv:1203.6003; Jörg et al., EPL 89, 40004), and the WKB action of an M-residue rearrangement grows with M.
(b) Pair features are Gaussian-softened (σ = 0.5 Å) over bins at least 1 Å wide, and the per-pair NLL range is at most ln(1e6) = 13.8 nats. The barrier-top and well curvatures are both of order ΔNLL/σ², which makes pair-term barriers broad by construction.
(c) Pivot MH moves make any single-torsion barrier irrelevant, whatever its height.
(d) Even if a thin-barrier class exists, the cost gap per run is 4–6 orders of magnitude.

LITERATURE (verified this session via the arXiv API or Crossref):

- Leng, Zheng, Wu, arXiv:2311.00811 (PDF read). The instance is F_U(x) = Σ_k w((Ux)_k) with w(y) = y^4 − (y − 1/32)^2 − c and U a random rotation hiding separability. The classical baselines tested were scipy dual annealing, basin-hopping, Ipopt, SQP, SGD and Gurobi. No Gaussian homotopy, PT or PIMC was tested. The authors say their study "does not exclude the possibility of efficient classical algorithms".

With K = 400 steps and M = 4 antithetic samples, it succeeded in 100% of runs at d = 16, 64 and 256 (50 runs each) and at d = 1024 and 2048 (10 runs each), at 2,100 queries per run. IN-REPO PILOT:
- t4_converge: relaxations of up to 5000 iterations raise p_hit at 80 aa to 0.21–0.32 (2AB0A_80, 5O37A_80) and lower the best energies by 127–151 nats. The 200-iteration mode explosion is therefore partly under-convergence.

DERIVATIONS:
- Equal-resolution criterion: the quantum ground-state spread equals the thermal spread when ħ = 2T/ω_w. Tunnelling over a parabolic top then beats activation only if T_c = ħω_b/2π > T, i.e. |E''_top| > π²·E''_well. The pair terms give a ratio of order 1.
- A steric relu² crossing at a bond midpoint (d = 1.9 Å) has Δ ≈ 88 nats plus table floors and |E''_top| ≈ 44 nats/Å² against 5–20 nats/Å² in the wells, giving ω_b/ω_w ≈ 1.5–3, below π. Soft-core HREX can soften it and leaves π unchanged at λ = 1.
- QLD's stationary state is the quantum Boltzmann state, not π. Recovering π needs ħ → 0, which removes tunnelling. At ħ > 0 that state can be sampled exactly by classical PIMD.
verdicts.decisive_test:
A native-free barrier census plus a nonlocal-crossing test. Pre-register it; it runs in about 1 day or less on 8 cores within the 95% ceiling, and any L above 72 aa is flagged OOD.

Protocol, on 4 ladder crops each at L = 80, 100 and 120:
1. Relax 256 prior restarts to real convergence (at most 5000 L-BFGS iterations, |g| < 1). Record the converged p_hit(L) and the top 20 minima.
2. For pairs among the top 10 minima, build converged pathways using NEB or a string with at least 64 images, climbing image and FIRE/L-BFGS (|g⊥| < 1 at every top). Alternatively, use discrete-path-sampling chains of intermediate minima.
3. For each elementary step, record Δ, the tangent curvature ratio ω_b/ω_w = sqrt(|E''_top|/E''_well), and the steric versus pair share of Δ.
4. Measure the per-step crossing rate at T = 1 of three classical move types: pivot (single torsion drawn from the head prior), crankshaft (two torsions), and 8-replica λ-softened soft-core HREX on the relu² sterics and the d < 4 Å table floor.

KILL permanently if both of these hold:
- at least 90% of elementary steps have ω_b/ω_w < π, or are crossed at a rate of at least 1e-4 per MC step by pivot, crankshaft or soft-core HREX;
- converged p_hit(120) ≥ 1e-3.

REOPEN only as a Track-C theory note, and only if a class of pair-term steps turns up that is not steric, has ω_b/ω_w > π and Δ > 30 nats, is not crossed by the classical nonlocal moves, and grows in frequency with L.

Already done (under 10 min, E1–E2): the only published QHD separation family is solved classically in poly(d), and by homotopy with a query count that does not depend on d.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
QHD at L = 60 (d = 115 torsions):
- Data register: 7 bits per coordinate gives about 805 logical data qubits (1365 at L = 100), plus fixed-point workspace.
- Phase oracle: about 1e7–6e7 Toffolis per call including compute and uncompute. About 3.5e6 of that is the table lookup (1653 pairs × 2 tables × 1001 grid entries); the rest is building coordinates from torsions (NeRF-style chain build) and pair-distance arithmetic. The T4 estimate for a reversible gradient step is about 1.6e8.
- Trotter steps: 1e3–1e4 as a heuristic. The proven count on the Leng–Zheng–Wu family is O~(d^3), about 1.5e6 at d = 115.
- Total: 1e10–6e11 Toffolis per run. That is 20 days to 3 years per run at the repo's 170 µs/Toffoli baseline, or 3 hours to 7 days at an optimistic 1 µs.

Classical, measured in-repo:
- A converged L-BFGS restart takes 0.95 s at L = 60 and 1.36 s at L = 80 on one core.
- Converged p_hit is 0.19–0.32, so the time to reach the best basin with 99% confidence is about 23–30 s single-core, or about 4 s on 8 cores.

Break-even:
- Even if every QHD run succeeded, a QHD run would have to replace 1e4 (1 µs) to 1e6 (170 µs) classical restarts. So classical p_hit per restart would need to be at most about 1e-4 to 1e-6.
- The T4 pilot slope (d ln p/dL ≈ −0.03 per residue) puts that at roughly L ≳ 300–500 aa, before crediting basin hopping, CSA, homotopy or soft-core HREX, which all raise p.
- The QHD success probability on this landscape is unknown; no theory exists.
- The sampling variant has no break-even at all: no QHD or QLD primitive samples π(T = 1) exactly, and its ħ > 0 target can be sampled classically with PIMD.
verdicts.novelty_note: Search scope was arXiv API title/abstract queries on "quantum Hamiltonian descent" combined with {classical, Langevin, homotopy, smoothing, basin hopping, simulated annealing}. Within that scope I found no published classical rebuttal of arXiv:2311.00811, and no application of QHD or tunnelling to protein or learned-energy landscapes. The dequantisation here uses an elementary rotation-covariance lemma: isotropic smoothing, ULA or PIMD on F_U split exactly into d independent 1D problems. It is new as far as this scope shows, but the method itself dates to 1989 (DEM). The web-search budget ran out in this session and papers citing 2311.00811 from 2024–2026 were not enumerated. Run a fuller citation search before claiming priority.

verdicts.level_theoretical:
L0 for the A80 learned-energy task: no separation is known or derivable for this landscape, in either the argmin variant or the barrier-crossing variant. The per-run gate cost derived below is an L3-type cost with no speedup statement to attach it to. Stronger levels exist only elsewhere:
- **Constructed families, L6:** a provable (sub)exponential QHD/QAA separation via Gilyén–Vazirani (arXiv 2504.14841 building on 2011.09495). Leng–Zheng–Wu (arXiv 2311.00811) prove Õ(d³) queries for QHD, but the classical super-polynomial hardness there is only empirical.
- **Convex or local basin refinement, with exact oracles (which is the regime here):** "QHD does not offer a speedup over classical zeroth order methods" (Chakrabarti et al., arXiv 2503.24332). Its super-quadratic gain needs noisy evaluations, which A80 does not have.

Nothing transfers to A80 unless a barrier census finds tall, thin, non-steric barriers that the classical twin cannot remove.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. One QHD Trotter step on the A80 energy costs 3.5e7 Toffolis at L=45 and 2.6e8 at L=120 (central assumptions). At 170 µs per Toffoli with 100 factories, one run of 1e3 steps takes 0.7–5 days (L=45–120). The same step costs about 1–2e7 classical energy+gradient evaluations. At L=100, a single Trotter step at R=100 (5.1 min) takes longer than the whole median classical multistart argmin on one core (~19 s). A perfect one-shot QHD global optimiser breaks even only if the classical restart hit probability is at most ~1e-6 (and as low as ~1e-10 in other scenarios). PILOT measurements give ≥ 1.6e-2 at the median and a censoring floor of 3.9e-3.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
QHD is not bound by the quadratic ceiling:
- WKB tunnelling costs about e^{S_WKB} against thermal activation at e^{βΔ}.
- Provable (sub)exponential separations exist (arXiv 2504.14841), and so does an Õ(d³)-query result against empirically super-polynomial classical solvers (arXiv 2311.00811).
- The per-step overhead is "only" a factor r·S/R ≈ e^{11.5–19}.
- A80 pair channels can contribute up to 13.8 nats each (the −log 1e-6 floor), so up to ~27.6 nats per residue pair from CA+CB. Barriers built from several pairs can be taller still.
- So in principle a thin non-steric barrier with βΔ − S_WKB ≳ 20–30 nats would pay back the overhead per crossing. Nobody has measured the landscape of a learned energy.

Rebuttal (why this does not rescue the candidate):
1. No such barrier has been measured.
2. The only tall, thin barriers in A80 are the steric relu² walls (w_s = 10, up to 160 nats per CA pair). Soft-core HREX removes them classically and leaves the target unchanged at λ=1.
3. The pair terms are Gaussian-smoothed bins (σ = 0.5 Å), so a σ-homotopy (σ 0.5→2 Å) is available classically in closed form. It is a same-cost classical copy of QHD's "coherent smoothing" in distance space.
4. QHD outputs |ψ(T)|², not π. The only positive signal so far (the 1.40× soft average) needs π-exact samples. Wrapping tunnelling in π-preserving machinery (a QeMCMC proposal or a quantum Gibbs walk/Langevin sampler) turns this candidate back into QM-02, with T3's break-even of B ≥ 1e11–1e17 evaluations.
5. The argmin output is information-limited (headroom ≤ 0.14 Å; within-target ρ = −0.08).
6. The G1 pilot's reported bottleneck is a collective, first-order-like λ-path transition, not a thin barrier. Adiabatic/QHD gaps are also expected to be small at first-order transitions (INFERENCE).
verdicts.evidence:
**Resource derivation.** DERIVED here, reusing the T3 oracle model (`research/theory/RESOURCE_MODELS.md`, `T3_resource_model.py` v2 parameters). Scratch scripts: `C:\Users\abena\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-abena-quantum-advantage-protein-folding\deded8ee-ac50-420b-a8f2-b349dc3a4fdc\scratchpad\qhd_cost.py` and `qhd_be.py`.

- Cutoffs and incremental ΔE are unavailable because the whole x changes every step. Nothing carries over between steps: every step recomputes all (L−2)(L−3)/2 CA and CB pairs.
- Riemannian QHD (Abe–Nagai, arXiv 2603.28624) needs a dense chain metric G(x) and its inverse computed coherently, which makes it costlier per step (INFERENCE).

verdicts.decisive_test:
A paper check against existing RAW data, taking minutes on one core, plus one bounded extension.

1. **Argmin variant.** For every crop in `research/results/RAW/g1_modes/*_R256_s0.json` (DEP, native-free):
   - compute the classical time-to-best-known-energy TTT_C = (1/p_hit)·K_C·t_C;
   - compare it with one perfect-QHD run, T_Q(L) = N_T·G_QHD(L)·t_T/R, which is ≥ 0.7 d (L=45) to 5 d (L=120) at N_T = 1e3 and R = 100;
   - kill if TTT_C·S < T_Q on every crop. The pilot median TTT_C ≈ 2–80 s already implies this.
   - For crops censored at p ≤ 1/256, extend to 2^14 restarts, about 1.4 h per L=100 crop on 8 cores under the 95% governor. That certifies p_hit ≥ ~6e-5, still at least 60× above p* ≈ 1e-6, the most generous QHD break-even.
   - To guard against multistart missing the global minimum, run NRPT and basin hopping for a 1-core-day budget of ≈ 4e7 evaluations, which is below one QHD run. Confirm the best energy stops improving over the last 90% of that budget.
   - Record within-target Spearman(E, RMSD) over the top 100 minima as an ORACLE diagnostic only.
2. **Sampling variant (same day).** Run NEB between PT basins on 80–120-aa OOD crops and split each barrier into steric, pair and head parts.
   - Keep the lane alive only if some non-steric barrier has βΔ − S_WKB ≥ ~20 nats (ln(r·S/R) at S = 1e3, R = 100, plus ln(A_Q/A_C)).
   - The same barrier must also survive both classical twins: 8-replica soft-core-steric HREX and an analytic σ-homotopy (σ 0.5→2 Å) replica ladder, judged by round trips at matched evaluation budget.
   - Even if it survives, it goes to QM-02 (a π-exact walk or Langevin sampler), not to QHD.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
**Per step.** Every QHD Trotter step needs 2·C_E: a full coherent A80 energy, computed then uncomputed. That is ≈ 2.3e4·L² Toffolis central and ≈ 1.2e4·L² generous. The kinetic/QFT part is under 0.05%, so QHD encoding optimisations aimed at the kinetic term (arXiv 2607.16996) buy nothing here.

**Per run.** A run of N_T = 1e3–1e4 steps costs 6e10–2.6e12 Toffolis at L = 60–120.
- Wall-clock: 0.7–51 days with 100 factories, and 69 days to 14 years with one factory.
- Qubits: 3–7e4 logical, 1–2.3e8 physical.

**One step versus classical.** One step at R=1 equals 1.0–2.1e7 classical energy+gradient evaluations. The ratio is roughly L-independent because both sides scale as L².

**Argmin break-even.** Even if QHD were a perfect one-shot global optimiser, classical multistart would need p_hit ≤ 1e-6 (R=100, S=1) to 1e-10 (S=1e3, N_T=1e4). The measured value is ≥ 1.6e-2 at the median up to L=100. The gap is ≥ 4e3× in the single most generous case and ~1e7–1e8× under Babbush-style adversaries.

**Barrier-crossing break-even.** Tunnelling must beat thermal activation by a net βΔ − S_WKB ≥ 11.5–26 nats per crossing. That is only possible for thin barriers that are either steric (removable classically, target unchanged) or Gaussian-bin pair barriers (σ-smoothable classically in closed form).

**Classical twins, prior kills and output.** The quantum side has no known speedup mechanism on this landscape. The classical twins copy the smoothing and tunnelling effects at the same per-evaluation cost. The argmin variant is also already covered by K-002/DNR-02, K-006 and DNR-07, plus T4's p* ≈ 1e-18 amplitude-amplification kill. QHD cannot supply the π-exact samples that the only positive signal needs.

**Disposition.** Record in KILLBOOK. Fold the barrier census into G1 as a landscape diagnostic, not as a quantum lane.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for protein energies. There is a formulation only. No evidence shows that the A80/esmprior landscape contains the engineered structure behind any QHD separation. Generic QHD separations exist only on constructed instances. arXiv:2311.00811 solves each instance with Õ(d^3) queries, and its classical hardness is only empirical. arXiv:2504.14841 (Leng, Wu, Wu, Zheng 2025) proves a (sub)exponential oracle separation by compiling the Gilyén-Hastings-Vazirani construction into an objective function. That construction is far from a sum of smooth, bounded pair negative-log-likelihoods. The candidate text omits it; add it. arXiv:2503.24332 shows no QHD speedup for convex problems beyond what discretisation allows. T1 already lists structured continuous OPT as the open route B5/G-12, with no theorem for this energy.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. Nothing has been measured, and there is no fault-tolerant break-even. The project's own T3 cost model (research/theory/T3_resource_model.py, driven by scratchpad qhd_cost.py) gives one QHD Trotter step as 3.3e7 to 6.3e7 Toffolis at 60 aa and 1.3e8 to 2.6e8 at 120 aa. Logical qubits including arithmetic workspace are 1.6e4 to 3.2e4 at 60 aa and 2.9e4 to 6.6e4 at 120 aa. The candidate's 700 to 1000 qubits count the grid data register only. Taking 1e3 steps at 170 µs per Toffoli, one run lasts 65 days (60 aa) to 1.4 years (120 aa).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
Each barrier class this learned energy can contain is either already handled classically or is a regime where QHD does not help.
(i) Tall barriers come only from sterics. In src/qapf/protein/energy.py each pair term is -log(p~+1e-6), which is at most 13.8 per pair, and the soft bins smooth it with σ = 0.5 Å. The only unbounded term is sterics: w_s·relu(4-d)^2 with w_s = 10, up to 160 per overlapping pair. Chain crossing is steric, broad (4 Å range) and exactly softenable. Ramped-repulsion or soft-core homotopy removes it, and argmin needs no fidelity to λ < 1.
(ii) Pair terms can look thin in torsion space because of lever arms: σ/r ≈ 0.01 to 0.05 rad for r = 10 to 50 Å. A pivot or Metropolis jump with a step larger than that width crosses such a barrier at no activation cost, since acceptance depends only on the endpoints. WKB tunnelling therefore beats only local gradient or Langevin dynamics, which is the wrong adversary; this is the lesson of Denchev 2016 and Isakov 2016. The G1 sampler already uses pivot moves.
(iii) The "coherent smoothing" of the early phase has an explicit classical twin: Feynman-Hibbs / DEM Gaussian smoothing of the potential. QHD has no physical ħ, so the comparison of exp(-c·w·√Δ) with exp(-βΔ) contains a free schedule parameter that a classical smoothing width can match.
(iv) The only measured classical hardness is the G1 pilot NRPT λ-path: 0 round trips and a first-order-like bottleneck at λ ≈ 0.4 to 0.5, with Λ ≈ 14 at 45 to 60 aa and 25 to 29 at 100 to 150 aa. That is a mass/entropy (folding-collapse) transition. Adiabatic and QHD-type dynamics show exponentially small gaps at first-order transitions (Jörg et al. EPL 89, 40004 (2010), DOI 10.1209/0295-5075/89/40004; Altshuler, Krovi, Roland PNAS 107, 12446 (2010), DOI 10.1073/pnas.1002116107).
(v) Lower minima buy little structure. In the G1 pilot at 120 aa (3 crops), the lowest-energy restart has RMSD 3.79, 4.17 and 7.35 Å against 3.67, 3.99 and 7.12 Å for the oracle-best of 256 modes. The gap is only 0.12 to 0.23 Å, below the pre-registered K-G1d threshold of 0.3 Å. Spearman(E, RMSD) over modes is 0.20, 0.31 and 0.36.
Also, real chains cannot pass through themselves, so a "crossing" is an optimisation shortcut with no physical meaning. QHD's real-time dynamics are not a Gibbs sampler and carry no transition-path meaning. The sampling variant's quantum-Langevin part duplicates the project's existing M1/M2 walk/QSA lane.

verdicts.decisive_test:
Step 1, on paper (about 1 hour; the structural half is essentially done above). Bound the barrier sources of the A80 energy.
- Pair NLL is at most 13.8 per pair, smoothed at σ = 0.5 Å.
- The only tall, unbounded term is sterics, 10·relu(4-d)^2.
- Pair features that are thin in torsion space have width σ/r ≈ 0.01 to 0.05 rad, below a 0.1-rad pivot step, so a classical jump can hop them.

Step 2, one CPU run (at most about 8 hours on 8 cores, reusing scripts/g1_mode_census.py and qapf.protein.energy).
- Crops: the 8 pre-registered G1 2048-restart crops (L = 60, 100, 150) plus L = 80 and 120 ladder crops. All runs are native-free (DEP); RMSD is used for evaluation only.
- Budget: equal gradient-evaluation budget, about 4.5e5 per crop.
- Arms:
  - (a) plain L-BFGS multistart, R = 1 to 2048 (already pre-registered);
  - (b) ramped-steric homotopy multistart, w_s 0 → 2.5 → 5 → 10;
  - (c) Gaussian / Feynman-Hibbs-smoothed homotopy, σ 2.0 → 0.5 Å.
- Record: best energy per arm; RMSD of the lowest-energy structure against the oracle-best mode; Spearman(E, RMSD) over the top 100 minima.
- NEB/string (16 images) between the 10 lowest-energy mode pairs. At each saddle, split Δ into steric and pair parts and measure the torsion-space width.

KILL the argmin variant if (b) or (c) matches or beats (a)'s best energy, and the lowest-energy structure lies within 0.3 Å of the oracle-best mode at every L. The pilot already shows 0.12 to 0.23 Å at 120 aa.

KILL the barrier variant if either holds at every L:
- more than 50% of Δ at every saddle is steric; or
- the pair-dominated saddles are hoppable (width below the pivot step), or broad (w·√Δ ≥ βΔ).

If a pair-dominated, thin, tall saddle does survive, there is a known classical control: the pivot step can be widened until it covers that saddle's width.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Classical side, measured in the G1 census: at 120 aa, 256 L-BFGS restarts take 5.6e4 gradient evaluations in about 280 s on 8 CPUs, about 5 ms per gradient evaluation and about 218 per restart.

Quantum side, from the project T3 model (central): 2.6e8 Toffolis per QHD Trotter step at 120 aa, taking 1e3 steps as the lower end of 'thousands'.
- At 170 µs per Toffoli (Sanders/Babbush single-factory assumption): about 4.4e7 s per run, equal to about 9e9 classical gradient evaluations, or about 4e7 restarts.
- At 1 µs per Toffoli (very optimistic, many factories): about 2.6e5 s, equal to about 5e7 gradient evaluations, or about 2.4e5 restarts.

A single QHD run therefore has to beat about 1e5 to 1e7 classical restarts, and also the soft-core and Gaussian homotopy adversaries. At 120 aa, perfect selection among classical minima buys only 0.12 to 0.23 Å.

Simulator runtime is not physical runtime; none has been measured.
verdicts.novelty_note:
What was searched: arXiv API abstract searches for 'Hamiltonian descent' (16 records up to 2026-07-18), 'quantum tunneling' AND protein AND folding, 'quantum annealing' AND 'off-lattice', and 'Hamiltonian descent' AND molecular; plus Crossref lookups for the classical precedents. General web search was unavailable (the session's search budget was exhausted), so coverage is not exhaustive.

Under that scope, the search found no evidence of QHD or coherent-tunnelling optimisation applied to protein or peptide conformational energies, learned or physical, in 2019 to 2026. The nearest non-protein work is QHD on quadratic programs, Ackley-type benchmarks, constrained NLPs and community detection, plus the 2607.16996 resource estimates.

Novelty differs by part:
- Application: moderate to low.
- Mechanism: none. Schrödinger-dynamics, quantum-annealing and DEM global optimisation of peptides and clusters were simulated classically between 1989 and 2003 (Piela/Scheraga, Amara/Hsu/Straub, Finnila, Lee/Berne, Liu/Berne). The 'tunnelling' metaphor was classicalised as STUN for protein folding (Schug 2003). My inference, not verified here: none of these established a decisive advantage over basin hopping or REMC.
- Riemannian QHD: exists (arXiv 2603.28624).
- Barrier census: novel as a measurement. The literature phase found that learned energies have never been landscape-characterised. It should be folded into G1 as a diagnostic, not opened as a separate quantum lane.

title: Prior-to-posterior amplitude amplification (quantum rejection sampling / independence walk): product head prior, coherently simulated flow generator, and distogram-native realizability conditioning
merged_from: qalg QM-04 (quantum rejection from coherent product prior), learned 'One-shot quantum conditioning killed by KL-total-correlation identity', learned 'Coherently simulated learned generator (BioEmu-class) + amplitude-amplified reweighting', learned 'Distogram-native state space conditioned on 3D realizability', classical 'Exact reweightable Boltzmann sampling (flow + importance weights) vs quantum rejection', priorart (h) rejection/Bayesian-network part
summary: Q: can a cheap coherent prior be turned directly into posterior samples by amplitude amplification, skipping annealing? Quantum: quantum rejection sampling [A36,A37]; independence-Metropolis Szegedy walk; coherent flow simulation (Layden et al. 'Wavefunction Flows', abstract only). Replaces: classical rejection / importance correction from the prior or generator. Mechanism: accept amplitude sqrt(w/w_max); AA needs O(sqrt(M)) prior preps vs O(M) classically, M = w_max/E_q[w] = e^Phi (independence-sampler gap = 1/M exactly, Liu 1996). KILL IDENTITY (learned lane): D_KL(pi||q) <= Phi and, for product q, D_KL = sum_i KL(pi_i||q_i) + TC(pi), so one-shot conditioning costs >= exp([sum KL + TC]/2): exponential in exactly the information the pair terms add beyond the per-residue head, which S33's lever-arm law and tt-only ablation (rho 0.32) imply is extensive. Plain IS decays as exp(-Var log w) ~ exp(-cd); AA halves the exponent but SMC tempering is stable with O(d) stages (Beskos-Crisan-Jasra), and against SMC the quantum analogue is QSA = QM-01. Variants: (a) product head prior (exact, cheap prep); (b) coherent flow/BioEmu generator: ~1e11-1e13 Toffolis per qsample plus a non-coherent log-density divergence; generators already give independent samples, break-even needs 1 + chi^2 >~ 1e16; (c) distogram-native pair bins (5 qubits x L^2/2 pairs) conditioned on Euclidean realizability: realizable assignments have dimension 3L-6 in an L^2/2 space (the S29-S33 a = mu counting), so P(F) = exp(-Theta(L^2)); sparse-graph interval realizability is strongly NP-hard (Saxe). Coordinates satisfy realizability for free. Speedup: quadratic in M; absolute cost exp(Theta(L)) or exp(Theta(L^2)). Competitor: adaptive SMC/AIS from the prior; sequential/transferable Boltzmann generators; BioEmu proposals + SMC; flow-augmented MCMC; random-prior + L-BFGS (QX-25). Info vs comp: the more informative the learned pair model, the more expensive one-shot quantum conditioning becomes. S29-S33: product prior = the random-prior twin that beat VQE (K-006, DNR-06); M6 is WEAK because of coherent decoders, removed in (a) but replaced by the Phi exponent. Kill: measured Phi(T*,L) grows linearly and exceeds ~40 nats by L~60 (quantum needs >= 5e8 coherent full-energy evaluations per sample vs ~1e5 for SMC); SMC cost <= L^3 and <= 1e8 evals at 60 aa; log P(F) slope <= -0.5 nat per included pair on mid30. Test: free byproduct of QM-01's SMC (log Z ratios, 64-restart w_max, SMC marginals, Phi/L at T in {1,3,10,30}); small IAF log-weight chi^2/ESS; interval-DG realizability rate vs k confident pairs. Hours. Track: C theory (kill) / B. Prior: very low (<1%).
dead_reason: Matrix M6 is WEAK, not KILLED; the KL/TC identity and dimension-counting arguments are new kills to record (KILLBOOK Section B candidates), not prior evidence.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for the protein-relevant claim. The only provable statement is L6 in a black-box query model, and it holds only against a strawman comparator: classical rejection or independence-Metropolis from the same proposal. Quantum rejection sampling and amplitude amplification need Theta(sqrt(M)) queries against Theta(M) classically, with M = e^Phi (Ozols-Roetteler-Roland, tight). The independence sampler's gap is exactly 1/M, so a Szegedy walk also gives sqrt(M), not more. Against the relevant classical twin (tempered SMC, which uses the structure w = e^{-lambda U}) there is no separation. On the measured instances the mechanism is exponentially worse: its cost is exp(Theta(L)) against SMC's polynomial cost.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No regime was found in which QM-11 is useful under matched conditions. At every measured (L, T), SMC started from the same exact product prior needs about 150-1500 pair-energy evaluations per particle. QM-11 needs at least e^{Phi/2} coherent iterations, each costing two or more full coherent energies. Its best case is 3GAHA_60 at T=30: e^{14.3} ≈ 1.6e6 iterations for exact sampling, and possibly about 1e2-1e4 for the eps-approximate version (sigma was not measured at T>1). That is before the fault-tolerant cost ratio R ≈ 3e4-2e7 per evaluation is applied. Variant (c) is exponentially dominated (e^{-Theta(L^2)}). Variant (b) needs 1+chi^2 > R_gen^2 ≈ 1e10-1e20.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
Amplitude amplification from the prior is exact and immune to metastability. Its cost e^{Phi/2} does not depend on barriers or mixing. The classical side's correctness at T=1 is not established:
- my SMC is pivot-only with N=128, and lineages collapse to 54-67 of 128 at T=1;
- its KL disagrees with NRPT thermodynamic integration (TI) by 1.7x at L=45 (67 vs 117 nats), and the NRPT pilot had zero round trips.

If the learned posterior has a persistence or first-order bottleneck along every classical path, the exact classical cost could grow exponentially while QM-11 stays at e^{Phi/2}. The literal pre-registered threshold "Phi > 40 nats at L~60" is also NOT met by my lower bounds on 3GAHA_60 at T=10 (38.3) or T=30 (28.6). At high T, the eps-approximate quantum iteration count, with sigma unmeasured, could be about 1e2-1e4, comparable to SMC's evaluations per particle in raw query count.

Rebuttal:
- A quantum win needs the classical cost per sample to exceed R^2 ≈ 1e9-4e14 evaluations (derivation in `break_even_or_cost_note`), whatever Phi is.
- At T=1, Phi grows at 1.2-1.9 nats/residue (TI: 2.4 to 6.7, super-linear), so QM-11's own cost grows by at least e^{0.6-0.9 L}. The classical cost would have to grow faster than that plus ln R. The G1 multistart census shows p_hit decaying only about e^{-0.05 L}.
- If metastability were real, the quantum remedy is annealed QSA or a walk (QM-01), not one-shot amplification from the prior.

verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Derivation. Let X ≈ KL(pi||q) ± O(sigma), where sigma is the standard deviation of log(dpi/dq) under pi. Costs per posterior sample:
- quantum rejection / amplitude amplification / independence walk: Q ≥ R·e^{X/2};
- classical self-normalised importance sampling (SNIS): about e^X;
- SMC: C_SMC.

Beating SNIS requires e^{X/2} > R, and then Q > R^2. So a quantum window exists only if C_SMC > R^2, up to e^{O(sigma)} factors.

Here R is the wall-clock cost of one coherent full energy relative to one classical energy+gradient evaluation. From T3 at L=60: 1.3e7-8.2e7 Toffolis × 170 us / (1 to 100 factories), against 0.78 ms, which gives R ≈ 3e4-2e7. The required C_SMC is therefore about 1e9-4e14 evaluations per sample, against about 1e2-1e3 measured. The gap is at least 1e6 in the most generous case. The prereg T3 range R = 1e7-1e10 gives a gap of at least 1e11.

Absolute costs:
- L=45, T=1: QM-11 needs at least e^{51} ≈ 1e22 coherent iterations (eps-approximate).
- L=60, T=30 (the most favourable cell): QM-11 needs about 1.6e6-1.9e9 iterations for exact sampling.
- Variant (b): 1+chi^2 > R_gen^2 ≈ 1e10-1e20, given 1e11-1e13 Toffolis per coherent generator call. Classical SMC with generator proposals (SBG) is the competitor.
- Variant (c): at least e^{220} at L=45.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L6 holds only for the generic, non-protein statement that quantum rejection sampling needs Theta(sqrt(M)) queries where classical rejection needs Theta(M) (Ozols-Roetteler-Roland, oracle model). Against the actual classical twin (SMC or non-reversible PT from the same exact product prior), the protein task stays at L0. That comparison is a proven exponential disadvantage whenever Phi = Theta(L): one-shot conditioning costs about exp(Phi_eps/2) coherent evaluations, while annealing pays only the barrier along the path. QSA/QM-01 also dominates QM-11 in every regime, because QSA pays sqrt(barrier cost), not sqrt(exp(whole divergence)).
verdicts.level_practical: L0, and the measurements are negative. The quantum route misses break-even by at least 6.7 orders of magnitude at its most favourable measured point (L=45-60, T=30). verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
1) A better proposal could shrink Phi_eps. Examples: a Laplace mixture over 64 L-BFGS restart minima loaded by QROM, an amortised generator, or a high calibrated temperature. Only the quadratic factor would then remain, and it would sit in the window 2 ln R <= Phi_eps. 2) A golf-course or entropic bottleneck could make every classical annealing path exponential while rejection stays the best option.
Rebuttals:
- On (1): wherever Phi_eps < 2 ln R ≈ 32 nats (R ≈ 1e7), classical rejection or importance sampling with the same proposal is already cheaper than the quantum route. Wherever Phi_eps >= 32 nats, quantum cost per sample is at least R x t_oracle ≈ 1e7 x 2 h ≈ 2,400 years at L=60.
- On (2): QSA/quantum walk (QM-01) pays sqrt(barrier-crossing cost), while QRS pays sqrt(exp(Phi)) over the whole divergence. QM-11 is therefore strictly dominated in that regime as well.
- Caveats on my numbers: the T=1 NRPT pilot made 0 round trips, so its lambda near 1 statistics are non-equilibrium. The KL and Phi values may be off by a factor of about 2 there. The T>=10 figures come from the well-mixed segment near the prior (rung 0 is refreshed by exact prior draws), so they are more reliable. The case for QM-11: one-shot amplitude amplification needs no intermediate-stage mixing. So it sidesteps the unknown (possibly exponential) mixing times that QM-01 depends on, and its quadratic speedup over rejection/IS is provable and tight with no spectral-gap assumption. If a better proposal q brought the divergence down to about 35 nats or less at L>=60 while keeping the pair information, e.g. a coherently simulable flow or generator conditioned on the same ESM features (variant b, Wavefunction Flows), QM-11 would stand on the divergence alone.
