verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
At L=60, T=1, per posterior qsample:
- Coherent calls: at least 3e23 (fidelity-limited 1/BC), about 1e31 (KL scale), at least 5e34 (exact QRS / independence walk).
- Cost per call: about 8e7 Toffolis (T3 central: 2.3e4*L^2), giving about 2e31 Toffolis or more in total.
- Time: at an optimistic 1e6 Toffolis/s, about 1e17 years.

The classical pilot NRPT used 5.6e5 gradient evaluations (about 400 s on this box) at L=45-60 and produced hundreds of correlated posterior samples (post-expected RMSD 2.66 Å at L=45), though with zero round trips, so mixing is not certified. T2 bounds cost at 2.0e4 local steps per round trip or more (95%, model-dependent). Even a classical cost of 1e10 steps per independent sample would beat one-shot QRS by more than 13 orders of magnitude in query count alone. Break-even would need D_1/2 ≤ 2 ln(B_classical * c_cl / (C_coh * t_T)), i.e. D_1/2 of about 20-30 nats at most at L ≥ 60, against 108 nats measured.

Variant (b) break-even: 1+chi^2 of about 1e16 or more, by which point classical SMC with generator proposals is the comparator.

Variant (c): P(realizable) = exp(-Theta(L^2)) by dimension counting (INFERENCE, S29-S33 a≡mu). It is dominated by coordinates.
verdicts.novelty_note:
The mechanism is not new. Prior-qsample-to-posterior amplitude amplification is Ozols et al. 2012 and Low-Yoder-Chuang 2014 (Bayes nets, quadratic in 1/P(evidence)). The multi-stage version is Harrow-Wei 2020. Coherent flow and generator qsamples with quadratic post-processing are Layden et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.08462) and Kodama et al. 2026 (arXiv:2608.21700). A folding-motivated instance already exists in Rattacaso et al. 2026 (arXiv:2603.12334): a lattice compact-polymer qsample reweighted to temperature T by amplitude amplification.

The search found no evidence of a paper applying QRS or amplitude amplification from a learned per-residue (theta,tau) prior, or from a protein structure generator, to a learned ESM-distogram structure posterior at 45-150 aa. Nor did it find one measuring the instance divergences (D_1/2, D_KL, max-ratio Phi) that set the cost. Scope: arXiv API keyword queries ('quantum rejection sampling'; 'wavefunction flows'; quantum + 'Boltzmann generator'; 'amplitude amplification' + 'importance sampling'; quantum + protein + 'amplitude amplification'; quantum + SMC/importance-sampling speedup; quantum + coherent diffusion-model sampling) plus the repo's 448-paper literature map. General web search was unavailable in this session (budget exhausted), so non-arXiv venues were not searched.

The novel content is therefore a negative result. The measured divergences on a learned protein energy (about 108 nats D_1/2 and 142 nats D_KL at L=60; about 2-4 nats per residue, extensive) quantitatively close the one-shot route. They also show it is the degenerate one-stage case of QM-01 on the same path.

Recommended action: record a Section B entry in research/KILLBOOK.md with the reopening condition above, and fold any residual interest into QM-01. I wrote no files to the repo.

title: Rare events and metastability via quantum-walk hitting, search and walk phase estimation vs classical splitting (metastable escape rates, topology-predicate marked sets, ms-s transitions)
merged_from: qalg QM-06 (walk QPE / fast-forwarding for metastable escape), qalg QM-07 (walk search for native-free topology-predicate marked sets), complexity 'Splitting lemma: progress coordinates erase quantum hitting-time speedups', classical 'Rare conformational transitions in >100-residue proteins vs quantum hitting time'
summary: Q: find rare native-like basins, topology classes, or transitions (and estimate slow escape rates) under a learned or physical energy faster than classical methods. Quantum: MNRS / Krovi / AGJK walk search and hitting [A2-A4]; Szegedy-walk QPE from a basin-restricted warm state (slow phase ~sqrt(2 lambda)); quantum fast-forwarding (Apers-Sarlette); Chowdhury-Somma hitting estimation; AE of transition probabilities. Replaces: waiting-time-limited trajectory statistics. Mechanism: interfering reflections about the marked set and pi rotate by ~sqrt(eps delta), giving sqrt(HT) vs HT; walk QPE resolves 1/sqrt(lambda_B) vs 1/lambda_B (scalar readout, so no one-sample-per-anneal penalty). Splitting lemma (I(prog) framing of Cerou-Guyader): with a committor-aligned coordinate, AMS/WE cost ~polylog(1/p)/eps^2, exponentially better than p^-1/2; with n imperfect interfaces classical sum 1/p_i vs quantum sum p_i^-1/2, no asymptotic gain when p_i = Theta(1). Any native-free predicate derived from ESM contacts can be turned into a smooth restraint that removes rarity classically. Quantum advantage therefore requires that NO classically computable coordinate or bias gives Theta(1) interface probabilities, i.e. QM-02's hide-and-seek regime. Speedup: <= quadratic per interface / in 1/lambda_B. Oracle: coherent chain (QM-05) + cheap native-free marking predicate (E < E*, learned-Q > q*, contact-count predicate ~1e5 Toffolis; knot invariants >= 1e8); MNRS needs the stationary state (= QM-01 problem). Competitor: WE, FFS, AMS, TPS, milestoning, MSM/TICA/VAMPnets, metadynamics, flat-bottom restraint sampling. Info vs comp: kinetics lie outside the structure endpoint; predicates carry classical ESM information. S29-S33: matrix M3 WEAK; QX-25 topology traps were avoided by broad random-prior sampling; benchmarking against brute-force waiting time repeats DNR-05's weak-baseline error. Kill: AMS/FFS with learned-Q, energy, TICA or DG-mode distance reaches the lowest PT basin with every interface p >= 0.05 and <= 20 interfaces at 44-120 aa; OR MSM slowest implied timescale <= 1e8 evals at 60 aa with slow modes connecting chain-equivalent basins (Delta RMSD < MDE); OR restrained samplers hit every predicate set in <= 1e6 evals. Support: interface probabilities < 1e-4 for every native-free coordinate. Test: long40 + 3 native-free 100-aa sequences; AMS with 4 coordinates; TICA+MSM on QM-01 trajectories; 3 native-free predicates, mass and restrained vs unbiased hitting; AMS on a Go/learned model for p = 1e-3..1e-12 with good vs degraded RC. <= 1 day. Track: C theory/query. Prior: low.
dead_reason: Matrix M3 is WEAK, not KILLED.

verdicts.level_theoretical: In the generic query model, against the same classical Markov chain run as brute force, this is L6: quantum-walk search and hitting are provably quadratic, sqrt(HT) against HT (MNRS [A2], Krovi et al. [A3], AGJK [A4]), and walk phase estimation gives 1/sqrt(lambda_B) against 1/lambda_B. On the protein-relevant instance family, against the correct classical adversary (splitting and path sampling), it is L0: formulation only. No separation from AMS/FFS/WE/DPS is known, and the one regime where a separation could exist has not been shown for learned pair-distance energies. That regime needs every native-free coordinate to leave an irreducibly rare interface (hide-and-seek, T5 Lemma 1 condition M8), and pair-distance energies disfavour it by construction. Even inside that regime the ceiling is quadratic per interface and in precision (T5 S2 and S5). Rarity itself is not a quantum resource: with a Theta(1)-interface coordinate, classical splitting costs polylog(1/p), which is exponentially better than the quantum p^(-1/2).
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No resource-normalised win exists at any tested L. The T3 fault-tolerant cost per qubitised walk step at L=60 is 1.1e1 s (D3 generous) to 1.4e2 s (D2 central), with 100 CCZ factories at 170 us per Toffoli. The classical energy+gradient evaluation costs 0.36-1 ms. The quantum walk wins a search or hitting task only if the irreducible classical hitting cost after splitting is at least B = (S*t_Q/t_C)^2, which is about 1e9 (most generous: D3 generous, one classical core) and 1e11 to 1e17 in other scenarios. It wins an estimation task (walk QPE or amplitude estimation at eps=0.1) only if the rarest irreducible interface probability is at most q* = (t_C/(S*t_Q*eps))^2. That is about 1e-7 (most generous), 7e-10 (D2 central, S=1) and 1e-13 to 1e-16 against a 1000-core adversary. Both conditions are far beyond the candidate's own support threshold of 1e-4. Example at p=1e-12 and eps=0.1 with an ideal coordinate: AMS needs about 7.6e7 evaluations (about 7.6 core-hours). Walk QPE needs about 1e7 coherent steps (3.5 years D3 generous, 44 years D2 central).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The candidate's precondition could hold in glassy or first-order regimes. PILOT data point that way. In the G1 256-restart census at L=100-120, n_modes/R is 0.95-1.0 on most crops, and p_hit(best) is about 0.004-0.03. The lambda-path NRPT pilot saw 0 round trips in 1200-1500 scans; T5 says this is significant at L=45/60 and not diagnostic at L>=100. Rolland and Simonnet (arXiv:1412.3362, JCP 283:541, 2015) show that AMS statistics deviate badly at phase transitions when the reaction coordinate is not the committor. If the lowest learned-energy basin is separated by a frustrated barrier (strand-register shift, mirror topology, threading) that no native-free coordinate resolves, AMS/WE fall back toward brute force. AGJK's sqrt(HT) then holds for any reversible chain with no reaction coordinate needed. Rebuttal:
- The census used only 200 L-BFGS iterations and 2 A clustering, which inflates mode counts at L=100.
- Pivot, regrowth and SMC moves jump topological barriers that physical kinetics must cross. The learned energy's escape rates are MCMC artefacts with no physical meaning.
- The pair energy leaks the target basin globally (T5 point 4), so learned-Q or E_pair is a natural progress coordinate.
- MNRS/AGJK needs coherent |sqrt(pi)> setup. On exactly this slow landscape that is the QM-01 problem, whose cost can dominate.
- The one PILOT transmission value (census rho(E, RMSD over modes) = 0.20 on 3M3PA_120) and condition C (rho = -0.08) say that finding rare low-E basins faster does not buy accuracy.
- Even granting the regime, the gain is quadratic and must clear B >= 1e9.
verdicts.evidence:
Classical adversary, strongest first. Citations were verified this session via arXiv API or Crossref, or were already in BIBLIOGRAPHY.md.
- **(1) Adaptive multilevel splitting (AMS).**
  - Cérou and Guyader, Stoch. Anal. Appl. 25(2):417-443 (2007), DOI 10.1080/07362990601139628. With the ideal coordinate, relative variance is about log(1/p)/N, so cost is about log^2(1/p)*tau/eps^2.
  - Cérou and Guyader, Ann. Appl. Probab. 26(6) (2016), DOI 10.1214/16-aap1177: adaptive precision equals optimally placed fixed levels.
  - Bréhier, Lelièvre and Rousset, arXiv:1405.1352: unbiased for any k.
  - Bréhier, Gazeau, Goudenège, Lelièvre and Rousset, arXiv:1505.02674: unbiased whatever the importance function, discrete-time setting. An imperfect reaction coordinate costs variance, not correctness.
  - Lopes and Lelièvre, arXiv:1707.00950: AMS on a molecular isomerisation, which also yields the committor.
- **(2) Forward flux sampling (FFS).** Allen, Warren and ten Wolde, PRL 94:018104 (2005), arXiv:q-bio/0406006. Also Allen, Frenkel and ten Wolde efficiency analysis, arXiv:cond-mat/0602269. Rate = flux times the product of interface probabilities.
- **(3) Weighted ensemble (WE).**
  - Huber and Kim 1996 [E61].
  - Zhang, Zuckerman and Jasnow, arXiv:0810.1963: statistically exact for any binning.
  - Adhikari et al., JACS 141:6519 (2019) [E63]: microsecond-to-second atomistic folding times.
  - Also milestoning [E64], MSMs [E65, E66], and MSM kinetics to hours [E67].
- **(4) Rarity-independent kinetics.**
  - Discrete path sampling: Wales, Mol. Phys. 100:3285 (2002), DOI 10.1080/00268970210162691. Graph transformation: Trygubenko and Wales, JCP 124:234110 (2006), DOI 10.1063/1.2198806. Rates on kinetic transition networks at a cost independent of exp(beta*dE).
  - Eyring-Kramers sharp asymptotics: Bovier, Eckhoff, Gayrard and Klein, JEMS 6:399 (2004), DOI 10.4171/jems/14, and CMP 228:219 (2002), DOI 10.1007/s002200200609. lambda_B is approximately cap/pi(B), from saddle searches with polynomial cost. This dequantises the 'walk QPE resolves lambda_B' use-case for energetic barriers.
- **(5) Static rare sets (E<E*, learned-Q>q*).**
  - Nested sampling: Skilling [B67]; Pártay, Bartók and Csányi, arXiv:0906.3544.
  - Superposition-enhanced nested sampling (SENS): Martiniani, Stevenson, Wales and Frenkel, PRX 4:031034, arXiv:1402.6306.
  - Nested sampling applied to protein folding: Burkoff, Várnai, Wells and Wild, Biophys. J. 102(4):878-886 (2012), DOI 10.1016/j.bpj.2011.12.053.
  - Cost is about log(1/X) levels with Theta(1) shrinkage per level. Any cheap native-free predicate becomes a flat-bottom restraint or a metadynamics/OPES bias [E41-E45].
- **(6) Derivations (DERIVED here).**
  - **No cloning.** Splitting's power comes from resampling (cloning) of partial trajectories. A coherent walk cannot clone the level-i state. The best quantum route through levels is QSA-like (Wocjan and Abeyesinghe [A7], Somma et al. [A8]). Its gain is quadratic only in within-level gap and precision. It is not in rarity once interfaces are Theta(1). This confirms the candidate's splitting lemma. With n levels of q each, the step ratio is at most about 1/(sqrt(n*q)*eps).
  - **Break-even.** Search: HT_eff = n*tau/q_min >= B = (S*t_Q/t_C)^2. Estimation: q <= (t_C/(S*t_Q*eps))^2. Numbers from T3's G(L) are in level_practical.
- **(7) Quantum side verified.** MNRS [A2], Krovi [A3], AGJK [A4], Apers and Sarlette [A35], Chowdhury and Somma [A22] are all at most quadratic. The arXiv title search 'quantum AND (rare event | transition path | committor | metastab)' found only generic amplitude-estimation or tail-sampling papers:
  - Guo et al., arXiv:2606.06316: quadratic for heavy tails; the abstract names no splitting comparator.
  - Hernández Vera et al., arXiv:2608.26840: constant-factor gain with belief-propagation state preparation.
  - Tabarraei, arXiv:2607.18996.
- **(8) Repo pilot data (PILOT, indicative).** research/results/PROCESSED/g1_summary.json (census256, nrpt_pilot); research/theory/RESOURCE_MODELS.md (T3); research/theory/NO_GO_RESULTS/T5_quadratic_ceiling.md.
- **Novelty.** The search found no evidence of any quantum hitting-time or rare-event algorithm benchmarked against AMS/FFS/WE on any molecular or protein instance. Scope: arXiv titles, 2026-09-27. The web-search budget was exhausted, so this scope is narrower than a full search.
verdicts.decisive_test:
**Paper part (done here).** The break-even condition is B = (S*t_Q/t_C)^2, which is at least about 1e9 evaluations per irreducible interface crossing, or q* <= about 1e-7 at eps=0.1, in the most generous T3 scenario. The candidate's support threshold of 1e-4 is therefore not sufficient. It must be tightened to 'every native-free coordinate leaves an interface with tau/q >= 1e9'.

**CPU part (~1 day, governor-scheduled; run only when the machine is below the 95% cap).** Pre-register it first in research/experiments/PREREGISTERED/. Run generalised AMS (Bréhier et al. 2015, discrete-time Metropolis/HMC with pivot moves, N=100 replicas, k=10 killed per iteration) on the vendored A80 energy at T=1 and at T_cal.
- **Crops:** 5O37A_45, 3GAHA_60, 5O37A_100, 4LPQA_120, 3S0QA_120.
- **Endpoints:** A is the dominant PT or prior-relaxed basin. B is the lowest minimum from the 2048-restart census, defined native-free: E < E_min + 1 and dRMS < 2 A to that minimum.
- **Four importance functions:**
  - E_pair;
  - learned-Q, the fraction of pairs whose distance lies in the modal distogram bin (native-free);
  - TICA-1 from short unbiased runs;
  - dRMS distance to B.
- **Records:** every level's survival probability q_i, the number of levels, the total energy+gradient evaluations, and the committor estimate.

**Kill (confirming this verdict).** Any importance function reaches B with every q_i >= 0.05 and <= 20 levels (the candidate's criterion), or with total cost <= 1e8 evaluations at L <= 120.

**Survival.** For all four functions, some interface has an irreducible tau/q >= 1e9 evaluations, and B's basin differs from A's by more than the MDE in RMSD (evaluation only, ORACLE-labelled).

**Budget.** About 3e6 evaluations per crop per function, 20 runs, about 20-60 core-hours.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Using T3 (research/theory/RESOURCE_MODELS.md): G(60) = 6.5e6 Toffolis (D3 generous) to 8.2e7 (D2 central). With t_T = 170 us and R = 100 factories, t_Q is 11-139 s per walk step. t_C is 0.36-1 ms per classical energy+gradient evaluation.
- **Search or hitting break-even.** HT_eff* = (S*t_Q/t_C)^2, about 9e8 (D3 generous, S=1) and 1.5e11 (D2 central, S=1), rising to 1e15-1e17 at S=1e3. HT_eff is the classical cost after splitting, n*tau/q_min, not the brute-force waiting time.
- **Estimation break-even (walk QPE or amplitude estimation, eps=0.1).** q* = (t_C/(S*t_Q*eps))^2, about 1.1e-7 (most generous) and 6.7e-10 (D2 central, S=1), falling to 1e-13 to 1e-16 at S=1e3.
- **Ideal-coordinate example.** At p=1e-12: AMS needs 7.6e7 evaluations, about 7.6 core-hours. Walk QPE needs 1e7 steps, 3.5 to 44 years.
- **Physical versus learned energy.** For a physical force field the oracle is far costlier, and WE/MSM already reach microseconds to hours.
- **Scientific value.** Kinetics of the learned energy are non-physical and lie outside the structure endpoint. The marking predicates carry only classical ESM information: information, not computation.
verdicts.novelty_note:
The search found no evidence that any quantum walk hitting, search or phase-estimation method has been compared with classical splitting (AMS/FFS/WE), discrete path sampling or Eyring-Kramers on protein or molecular instances. Scope: arXiv title search, 2026-09-27; the web-search budget was exhausted. Recent generic quantum rare-event papers (arXiv:2606.06316, 2608.26840, 2607.18996) claim at most quadratic or constant-factor gains, and their abstracts name only direct Monte Carlo baselines or none. Framing the candidate as a 'splitting lemma' (classical sum of 1/p_i against quantum sum of p_i^-1/2) is correct but not new: it is the known quadratic-per-stage structure of quantum simulated annealing [A7, A8]. This note adds two things:
1. Explicit break-even interface probabilities, q* of about 1e-7 or less and HT_eff of about 1e9 or more, derived from T3's G(L).
2. The no-cloning argument: resampling gives classical splitting an exponential advantage in log(1/p) over a coherent walk whenever a Theta(1)-interface coordinate exists.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L2, and only against brute-force waiting-time or i.i.d.-trial classical access. MNRS, Krovi and AGJK walk search give sqrt(HT) against HT, and walk QPE gives 1/(r*sqrt(lambda)) against 1/(r^2*lambda) (THEORETICAL [A2-A4, A22, A35]). T3's G(L) supplies the gate-cost ingredient, so an L3 fault-tolerant runtime statement is available, but only against brute force and only conditional on the stationary-state setup and the gap/overlap assumptions (T2 A-delta is UNPROVEN). Against adaptive classical splitting (AMS, WE, FFS) with any coordinate that gives Theta(1) interface probabilities the level is L0: the classical method costs polylog(1/p)/r^2 evaluations against the quantum lambda^-1/2 walk steps, so it is asymptotically exponentially better and no crossover exists at any lambda. The per-interface gain is at most quadratic.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. The quantum side needs a qubitised learned-energy walk step costing 6.5e6 to 5.1e8 Toffolis at L=60-150 (T3), or 11 s to 24 h of wall-clock per step. Even the most generous scenario breaks even only against one classical core and needs escape rates of about 1e-8 per step. Against a parallel classical adversary (S=1e3) the break-even runtime is centuries or longer. No measured classical cost is anywhere near break-even: the G1 pilot lower bound is 2e5 to 4e5 evaluations per round trip. The readout, an escape rate of a Metropolis chain on a learned posterior, has no endpoint value.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
Suppose a learned-energy landscape at 100 aa or more is genuinely hide-and-seek or entropic-golf-course, so that no classically computable coordinate or bias gives large interface probabilities. Then AMS, WE and FFS degrade to about 1/p brute force. Walk QPE on a basin-restricted warm state returns a scalar escape rate with Heisenberg scaling in both precision and timescale, 1/(r*sqrt(lambda)) against 1/(r^2*lambda), and pays no one-sample-per-anneal penalty. In the most generous design (T3 D3-generous, 100 CCZ factories, c_q=1) this breaks even against one core at lambda about 1.4e-8 per step (L=100), with T* about 0.22 yr, which is not astronomical. The counterargument fails on four points:
(i) The classical side parallelises perfectly for exponential escape (parallel-replica dynamics, AMS replicas). At S=1e3 the break-even moves to lambda about 1.4e-14 and T* about 220 yr.
(ii) D3 samples a bond-relaxed target, not the A80 posterior. The design that samples the actual A80 posterior (D2 central, one factory) needs lambda below about 3e-15 and T* about 1e6 yr.
(iii) T5 (INFERENCE; G6 untested) argues that pair-distance energies leak the basin location into every pair term, so the information-local hiding that the quantum regime needs is structurally unlikely. Any ESM-derived predicate can be turned into a smooth restraint.
(iv) The escape rate of the quantised single-angle Metropolis chain on a learned posterior is neither a physical rate nor a structure-accuracy quantity (condition C).
verdicts.evidence:
ORACLE / RESOURCE LEDGER. Every number is DERIVED from repo T3 (research/theory/RESOURCE_MODELS.md) with t_T = 170 us per Toffoli and one CCZ factory [A56 Sanders et al. arXiv:2007.07391; B46 Babbush et al. arXiv:2011.04149]. My calculator is scratchpad/qm12_be.py.

(1) Coherent walk step (QM-05/T3), qubitised LHPST. Szegedy is 57-543x worse and has the same gap.
- G, D2 central (actual A80 target, torsion moves): 8.2e7 (L=60), 2.3e8 (L=100), 5.1e8 (L=150). Wall-clock per step at R=1 is 3.9 h / 10.9 h / 24 h; at R=100 it is 139 s / 391 s / 867 s.
- G, D3 generous (Cartesian, bond-relaxed target): 6.5e6 / 1.1e7 / 1.8e7. Wall-clock is 11 s / 19 s / 31 s at R=100.
- Logical qubits: 5e3 to 6.5e4. Physical qubits: 1e7 to 1.3e8 at d=31. Multi-year runs need d=37-51, which gives t_T = 5.5d us = 204-280 us and multiplies B and T* by 1.4-2.7x.

(2) Controlled-W for QPE: about 1x. Compute/uncompute pairs need no control. This is INFERENCE.

(3) Stationary-state setup |sqrt(pi)> for MNRS/Krovi/AGJK [A2 quant-ph/0608026; A3 arXiv:1002.2419; A4 arXiv:1903.07493]. This is exactly QM-01's QSA problem. It costs at least c_q*sqrt(t_rel)*G, with c_q between about 90 and 1.6e4 (T2). In a metastable chain t_rel >= 1/lambda_B, so the setup alone costs as much as the claimed speedup.
- If the target basin has large mass under pi (the native-like basin of a good posterior), search reduces to sampling and QM-12 reduces to QM-01, whose B(L) is 3.6e8 to 1.5e15 plus the marking cost.
- If the target has small mass under pi, it is a low-posterior state with no endpoint value (condition C).

(4) Basin-restricted warm state for walk QPE. It needs a coherent basin predicate plus a within-basin QSA. Its overlap with the slow eigenvector is sqrt(pi(B)) in a two-well reduction (DERIVED), which adds 1/pi(B) repetitions, or 1/sqrt(pi(B)) with amplitude amplification. QPE cost: the slow phase is theta ~ sqrt(2*lambda), so relative precision r needs about pi*sqrt(2)/(r*sqrt(lambda)) = 4.44/(r*sqrt(lambda)) controlled-W steps. At lambda=1e-10 and r=0.1 that is 4.4e6 steps: 4.9e13 Toffolis (D3 generous) to 1.0e15 (D2 central) per estimate, before repetitions. The QPE register is about 22-26 qubits, which is negligible.

(5) Marking predicates, counted as compute plus uncompute.
- E < E*: 4.1e7 / 1.1e8 / 2.6e8 Toffolis at L = 60/100/150, about 0.5*G_D2.
- Contact count over the top-L ESM contacts: 1.6e5-4.0e5 on a Cartesian register, which confirms the task's ~1e5 only in that case. On a torsion register it is 1.9e6-4.8e6, because the chain build dominates.
- Gauss/writhe topology predicate: about 9e7-5.6e8 (INFERENCE, at >= 5e4 Toffolis per segment pair). That exceeds the D3 step by 14-31x.
- Marking is amortised over 1/sqrt(delta) steps, so it never rescues the speedup; the cheap predicates are also exactly the ones classical restraints exploit.

(6) Data loading: the per-pair spline QROAM is already included in G. ESM-2 inference is classical preprocessing that both sides pay.

BREAK-EVEN, hitting/search. HT_BE = c_q^2*(S*G*t_T/(R*t_C))^2, with t_C = 0.2 ms*(L/45)^2, a placeholder.
- At L=100 (L=60 is similar): D2 central, S=R=1: 1.6e15, T* = 4.9e4 yr. D2 central, R=100: 1.6e11, T* = 4.9 yr. D3 generous, R=100, S=1: 3.6e8, T* = 4 days. D3 generous, R=100, S=1e3: 3.6e14, T* = 11 yr. c_q=10 multiplies all of these by 100.

BREAK-EVEN, walk QPE rate against brute force/ParRep (r=0.1). lambda_BE is the escape probability per step.
- D3 generous, L=100, R=100: 1.4e-8 at S=1 (T* = 0.22 yr) and 1.4e-14 at S=1e3 (T* = 220 yr).
- D2 central, L=100: 3.2e-11 at R=100, S=1 (97 yr) and 3.2e-15 at R=1 (9.7e5 yr).

AGAINST AMS with a good reaction coordinate. The model is N = ln(1/p)/r^2 replicas and about N*ln(1/p) segments of tau_seg steps. At lambda = 1e-12: AMS needs 4.5e7 to 2.8e9 evaluations, 0.5-32 CPU-days on one core. The quantum side needs 26 yr (D3 generous, R=100) to 5.5e4 yr (D2 central, R=1). The classical advantage grows as lambda falls.

PER-INTERFACE QUANTUM SPLITTING. Here X = G*t_T/(R*t_C), which is at least 1.9e4 even for D3 generous at R=100.
- If each trial is a coherent trajectory via a reversible seed register (T4-style), the quantum side wins only if p_i < 1/(c_q*S*X)^2 = 2.9e-9 (most generous, S=1). At S=1e3 the threshold is 2.9e-15. For D2 central at R=1 it is 6.6e-16.
- With QFF-accelerated segments [A35 arXiv:1804.02321] the threshold rises to p_i < tau_seg*2.9e-9, at most 3e-4.
- The task's support threshold, p_i < 1e-4, is therefore too lenient by up to 5 orders of magnitude.
- With p_i >= 0.05 the per-interface gain is at most sqrt(20) = 4.5x, against a coherent overhead X of at least 1.9e4.

PILOT: G1 saw 0 PT round trips in <= 3.9e5 evaluations, so the classical cost per round trip is only lower-bounded at 2e5-4e5. That is at least 1e3x below even the most generous HT_BE.

Classical lifting limits: [A17 arXiv:1705.08253] (lifting cannot beat the 1/Phi conductance bound). The quantum walk keeps its sqrt(delta) edge over lifted chains in metastable regimes, but that edge is again at most quadratic.

The following references are not in the repo bibliography and I did not verify them this session: Cerou & Guyader, Stoch. Anal. Appl. 25:417 (2007); Cerou, Guyader, Lelievre & Pommier, JCP 134:054108 (2011); Voter, PRB 57:R13985 (1998, ParRep); Allen, Warren & ten Wolde, PRL 94:018104 (2005, FFS). Weighted ensemble is in the repo bibliography as [E61, E62].

Repo context: research/theory/PROOFS/T2_sampling_speedup_statement.md (A-delta UNPROVEN; c_q = K*l); T4_amplified_mode_finding.md (coherent-trial overheads); NO_GO_RESULTS/T5_quadratic_ceiling.md (information locality and pair-term leakage).
verdicts.decisive_test:
Pre-register, then run on 8 cores in 1 day or less.
- Method: Cerou-Guyader AMS (N=200 replicas, k=1, 3 seeds) from prior-sampled or unfolded states A to the lowest G1 PT basin B (DEP, native-free).
- Targets: the long40 targets plus the G1 pilot crops at L=60 and 100.
- Coordinates, one AMS run each: E, learned-Q (the fraction of the top-L ESM contacts formed), TICA-1 fitted on G1 trajectories, and DG-mode distance.
- Record, per interface: p_i, tau_seg (evaluations per segment), and the AMS relative variance against the ideal ln(1/p)/N.
- KILL immediately if any coordinate gives <= 20 interfaces with every p_i >= 0.05, which is the task's criterion. On paper, the audit already kills when the measured min p_i exceeds tau_seg*2.9e-9. That threshold is 1/(c_q*S*X)^2 times tau_seg with X = G*t_T/(R*t_C) >= 1.9e4, the most generous QFF case; the threshold is 2.9e-9 without QFF.
- Survive only if every native-free coordinate gives p_i below that threshold and a restrained sampler also fails to hit B within 1e6 evaluations.

Sanity check on paper: substitute the measured t_C (PILOT 0.78-1.46 ms/eval, which lowers B only 2-5x) and the measured tau_seg into the scratchpad calculator.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
The oracle costs erase the speedup.
- The walk step alone is 6.5e6-5.1e8 Toffolis (11 s to 24 h per step), which is 1.9e4 to 3.9e7 classical evaluations of time per coherent step.
- The stationary-state setup needed by MNRS/AGJK is itself the QM-01 sampling problem.
- Walk-QPE rate estimation breaks even against brute force only at lambda <= 1.4e-8 per step with T* of about 0.22 yr, and only in the most generous case (D3 bond-relaxed target, 100 factories, one classical core, c_q = 1).
- Against a 1e3-core parallel-replica adversary the break-even is lambda <= 1.4e-14 with T* of about 220 yr. For the actual A80 target (D2 central, one factory) it is lambda <= 3e-15 with T* of about 1e6 yr.
- Against AMS or WE with any coordinate giving Theta(1) interfaces there is no crossover at any lambda.
- Per-interface quantum splitting needs p_i <= 3e-9 with coherent trials, or <= 3e-4 with fast-forwarded segments (most generous). That is far below the task's 1e-4 support threshold once S > 1.
- Topology predicates (about 1e8-6e8 Toffolis) exceed a D3 step.

Total per estimate at lambda = 1e-10: 5e13-1e15 Toffolis on 1e7-1.8e8 physical qubits.
verdicts.novelty_note:
The literature phase (448 papers) and the repo theory notes T2-T5 contain no fault-tolerant resource estimate for quantum-walk hitting, walk-QPE rate estimation or quantum splitting on a protein or learned energy. The walk-search, QFF and hitting-estimation primitives themselves are known [A2-A4, A22, A35].

Two items are, as far as that search goes, new to this audit:
- the per-interface splitting break-even p_i < tau_seg/(c_q*S*X)^2;
- the two-well warm-start overlap sqrt(pi(B)).

Both are generic applications of known algebra (B46), not new quantum mechanisms. QM-12 adds no capability beyond QM-01 for finding high-mass basins. Its only distinct output, the escape rate of a synthetic Metropolis chain on a learned posterior, is outside the structure endpoint.

verdicts.level_theoretical:
The primitive is L6, but it is quadratic and query-model only. MNRS/Krovi/AGJK hitting costs about sqrt(HT) against HT. Szegedy-walk QPE resolves a reversible chain's slow eigenvalue in about 1/(delta*sqrt(lambda_B)) steps against 1/(delta^2*lambda_B) for direct waiting-time estimation. Amplitude estimation per interface costs 1/(delta*sqrt(p_i)) against 1/(delta^2*p_i). All of these separations hold only against unassisted chains and brute-force waiting times, which is the DNR-05 weak-baseline error.

Against the relevant adversary the task is L0 (formulation only). That adversary is splitting (AMS/FFS/WE) or an MSM with a native-free reaction coordinate. No separation is proved against it, and no protein-energy instance family is exhibited in which every native-free coordinate has p_i -> 0. The candidate's own splitting lemma gives at most quadratic gain per interface, and no asymptotic gain when p_i = Theta(1). T5 (research/theory/NO_GO_RESULTS/T5_quadratic_ceiling.md, S1–S3) caps hide-and-seek families at exactly quadratic, including hitting and dominant-basin finding (S3b: T_Q = Omega(sqrt(M))). T5 §0.4 also notes that pair-distance energies leak the basin location through every pair term, which works against the hide-and-seek premise.
verdicts.level_practical:
L0. There is no simulator run, no hardware run and no matched classical run.

The per-step cost is the problem. research/theory/RESOURCE_MODELS.md gives 1.1e7 (D3 generous) to 1.0e9 (D1) Toffolis per coherent walk step at L=100, even for the coarse learned C-alpha energy. At 170 us per Toffoli per factory, one step takes about 19 s (R=100 factories, D3 generous) up to about 3.9e4 s (D2 central, one factory). A classical evaluation takes about 3 ms at L=100 (0.59 ms at L=45, scaled as L^2). So each quantum step is roughly 6e3 to 1e7 times slower. The break-even B(L) is 1.3e8 to 4.8e9 classical evaluations per independent rare event in the most generous scenario, 1.5e11 for D2 central (S=1, R=100) and 1.5e15 for D2 central (R=1).

A physical all-atom force field, which is where rates actually mean something, would cost more per coherent step. That is inference; it is not estimated in the repository.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The strongest objection is that the quantity QM-12 accelerates has no protein-science value in the only regime where a speedup could exist. Where it does have value, classical methods already compute it.

(1) Kinetics under the learned energy are not physical. The esmprior/A80 energy is a sum of -log p~(d_ij) over pair distances plus a (theta,tau) head, and it has no dynamical meaning. Its escape rates and lambda_B are artefacts of whichever MCMC kernel is chosen. Replica exchange and multistart bypass them, so they are sampler diagnostics, not protein science.

(2) Kinetics under a physical force field are real protein science, but they lie outside the structure endpoint and are limited by force-field accuracy. A 1 kcal/mol barrier error gives a factor exp(1/0.596) = 5.4 in the rate at 300 K. Only about factor-2 relative precision (delta ~ 0.5) is therefore meaningful, so the 1/delta against 1/delta^2 precision gain is worth at most about 2x. Classical WE/TPS/MSM already remove the waiting-time exponential [E60, E62, E63, E67]. Splitting costs O(ln^2(1/p)/delta^2) at fixed p_i.

(3) "Rare native-like basin" discovery has three problems:
- It needs either an ORACLE predicate (leakage) or a native-free predicate: E < E*, learned-Q > q*, or a contact count.
- An energy-threshold predicate consumed by argmin is the H-001/K-002 formulation class.
- A learned-Q or contact predicate carries classical ESM information, and the classical adversary turns it into a restraint that removes the rarity. QM-12 concedes this point itself.

(4) The G1 pilot already shows that finding rarer low-energy basins transmits weakly to accuracy. The median best-mode RMSD is 5.0–8.5 Å across L = 30–120. Within-crop Spearman(E, RMSD) is 0.20, 0.31 and 0.36 at L=120, so the median (0.31) sits just at the K-G1d threshold of 0.3, on only 3 crops. The predecessor's condition C gave rho = -0.08 at 60 aa or less.

(5) Topology traps were already avoided classically: random prior sampling had 0 traps (QX-25), and random prior sampling beat VQE by 1.35x (K-006). Coherent knot invariants would add at least 1e8 Toffolis per predicate call, on top of the per-step cost of 1e7 to 1e9.

The best case in favour, and why it does not rescue QM-12. The NRPT pilot saw zero round trips at L = 45–150, and the 256-restart gmean p_hit falls from 0.10 to 0.008 between L=30 and L=120. This shows only that one lambda-path configuration and plain multistart have a bottleneck. It does not show that splitting fails with a native-free reaction coordinate, which is the regime QM-12 needs.
verdicts.evidence:
A. Repository prior evidence (read 2026-09-27)

Literature-phase verdicts:
- QUANTUM_OPPORTUNITY_MAP.md:137 rates QA-3 (quantum-walk hitting/search) WEAK: "WE, TPS and MSMs already remove the waiting-time exponential [E60–E67]; kinetics are outside the endpoint".
- literature/OPPORTUNITY_MATRIX.md M3 is the same primitive set (MNRS/Krovi/AGJK [A2–A4], Chowdhury–Somma [A22]). It needs a native-free marking predicate plus a coherent chain, and the stationary state, which is the M1 problem.
- CLASSICAL_COUNTERARGUMENTS.md:77,99 and PROTEIN_BOTTLENECKS.md:14 say rare-event kinetics are classically addressed and lie outside the endpoint.
- QM-12 is therefore largely M3/QA-3 restated, with walk QPE and a splitting adversary added.

S29–S33 kills that apply (KILLBOOK.md and sprint29-33/NEGATIVE_RESULTS.md):
- K-002 (H-001): argmin/prefix consumption of a diagonal energy. This covers the E < E* marking predicate.
- K-005/K-006 and QX-25: topology traps were avoided by random prior sampling; random prior sampling beat VQE by 1.35x.
- K-012/DNR-16 and S32 Theorem D-E (sprint32/NEGATIVE_RESULTS.md N-D12) close "metastability, rates, basin populations, dynamic modes" as native-free scalar rankers. The scope is 9–16 aa only.
- DNR-05: a brute-force or unequal-tuning baseline is inadmissible.
- None of these kills applies directly at 60 aa or more, and the splitting census has not been run.

B. G1 pilot data (research/results/PROCESSED/g1_summary.json; PILOT, pre-production)

256-restart census, gmean p_hit by length:

| L | gmean p_hit |
|---|---|
| 30 | 0.101 |
| 45 | 0.070 |
| 60 | 0.047 |
| 80 | 0.041 |
| 100 | 0.016 |
| 120 (7 crops) | 0.0081 |

- The floor is 1/256 = 0.0039, so at L of 100 or more the census is under-resolved.
- Cost is 174–217 gradient evaluations per restart. Hitting the census-lowest basin at L=120 therefore costs about 217/0.0081 = 2.7e4 evaluations, about 7 orders below B_min.
- Median best-mode RMSD is 5.0–8.5 Å.
- Spearman(E, RMSD) at L=120 is 0.20, 0.31 and 0.36 (3 crops).
- The NRPT pilot saw 0 round trips at L=45, 60, 100, 120 and 150. That is a lower bound of 2e5–3.9e5 evaluations per round trip for that configuration only (RESOURCE_MODELS.md §8).

C. Derivations (this audit; order-of-magnitude)

C1. Classical splitting against quantum splitting.
- In FFS/AMS the relative variance is about sum over i of (1-p_i)/(N_i*p_i).
- With optimal allocation, C_cl ≈ delta^-2 * (sum_i sqrt((1-p_i)*tau_i/p_i))^2, which is about n^2*tau/(p_i*delta^2) for equal interfaces.
- With n = ln(1/p)/ln(1/p_i), that is O(ln^2(1/p)/delta^2) at fixed p_i.
- Quantum amplitude estimation per interface, with delta_i = delta/sqrt(n), costs C_q ≈ pi * n^{3/2} * tau_q/(delta*sqrt(p_i)).
- The query ratio is C_cl/C_q ≈ sqrt(n)*(1-p_i)/(pi*delta*sqrt(p_i)) * (tau/tau_q).
- At n=20, delta=0.5, p_i=0.05 and a generous walk-accelerated segment tau/tau_q = sqrt(1e3) ≈ 32, the ratio is about 390. The per-step overhead is 6e3 to 1e7, so this can never pay.
- Break-even needs every native-free reaction coordinate to have p_i below about 2e-4 (most generous) and below about 1e-10 (D2 central).
- QM-12's support threshold of p_i < 1e-4 is therefore adequate only in the most generous resource scenario.
- Hidden cost: quantum amplitude estimation at interface i needs a coherent state for the conditional entrance distribution at that level (a basin- or level-restricted QSAMPLE). Classical AMS gets this for free by resampling. This is the rule that state preparation is not free.

C2. Walk QPE for lambda_B.
- It needs a warm state with Omega(1) overlap on the basin's quasi-stationary eigenvector, which is a QM-01-class preparation problem.
- A classical MSM or Koopman estimate costs about N_traj * tau_lag and does not grow with 1/lambda_B once a good state decomposition exists (MSMs have reached timescales of hours [E67]).

D. Nearest prior art

Verified this session through arXiv API abstracts (and HTML for Kharazi et al.):
- Kharazi, Alkadri, Mandadapu, Whaley, arXiv:2601.15523 (2026). Gaussian-LCHS reactive-flux estimation. It claims an exponential improvement in eta against worst-case bounds for overdamped Langevin simulation. However:
  - the error is ADDITIVE ("O(1/eps) ... independent of the magnitude of the reactive flux");
  - the e^{Omega(eta)} factor comes from a step-size bound driven by a Lipschitz constant, not from rarity;
  - only overdamped Langevin is compared, and the authors write it "should not be interpreted as a speedup over all classical simulation methods";
  - the only demonstration is a 1D double well, with no protein resource estimate.
  - For a rate k, relative precision needs eps ~ delta*k, so the cost is about 1/(delta*k). That is exponentially worse than splitting's polylog(1/k)/delta^2 whenever a reaction coordinate exists (DERIVED here).
- Mazzola, PRA 104, 022431 (2021), arXiv:2108.11410. Rates obtained as ground-state energies through supersymmetric stochastic quantization. Variational, with no classical splitting benchmark.
- Pravatto et al., arXiv:2107.13025 (2021). VQE for the Fokker–Planck–Smoluchowski eigenproblem (rotor-chain rate) on IBMQ.
- Ghamari, Hauke, Covino, Faccioli, Sci. Rep. 12, 16336 (2022), arXiv:2201.11781; and Ghamari, Covino, Faccioli, JCTC (2024), DOI 10.1021/acs.jctc.3c01174, arXiv:2311.15891. D-Wave path sampling of an ms-scale protein transition. The results agree with Anton; no advantage is claimed (repo labels A67/A68).
- Casares et al., QFold, Quantum Sci. Technol. 7, 025013 (2022). Szegedy-walk folding; the advantage is disputed (A65/D9).
- Guo, Huang, Wang, Thompson, Rebentrost, Gu, arXiv:2606.06316 (2026). Generic rare-event discovery with quadratic, optimal scaling in the rarity threshold; no protein application.
- Leng, Jiang, Lin, arXiv:2604.22996 (2026). Walk-free quadratic improvement in gap dependence, with warm starts in metastable regimes (quantum Gibbs).
- Zhao, arXiv:2605.23442 (2026). Ancilla-efficient QSAMPLE preparation, costing about sqrt(1/overlap)*sqrt(1/gap).
- Tabarraei, arXiv:2607.18996 (2026). Amplitude estimation for rare structural-failure probabilities, with a lookup-table oracle.
- Aghamohammadi et al., PRX 8, 011025 (2018). A memory advantage, not a computational one.

Not verified in this session:
- Cérou–Guyader AMS, whose cost is quoted from the task text.
- The WE, TPS and MSM references E60–E67, which were verified in the literature phase.
verdicts.decisive_test:
Run an AMS/FFS interface census on the existing G1 ladder with the vendored A80/esmprior energy. It is classical and fits on the 8-core box in under a day.

Targets and endpoints:
- Crops: 4 crops at L=100 and 4 at L=120 that are already censused, plus 2 long40 targets at 44–60 aa.
- Target basin B: the census-lowest mode, which is native-free.
- Start basin A: the most-populated census mode.

Reaction coordinates, all native-free:
- (i) E_pair;
- (ii) learned-Q, the fraction of ESM-predicted contacts with p > 0.5 that are formed;
- (iii) the contact-map distance to basin B;
- (iv) TICA-1, fitted on the stored NRPT pilot trajectories.

Protocol:
- AMS with N = 200 replicas, killing the lowest replica each iteration, 10 independent runs per crop and coordinate.
- Record the per-level p_i, the number of levels n, the total energy+gradient evaluations, and the relative standard error of P(A->B).
- Control: unbiased hitting, capped at 1e6 evaluations.
- Budget: at most 1e7 evaluations per crop and coordinate. At the census rate of about 170 evaluations per second per core, 8 cores cover it in roughly 1–2 hours per wave.

Kill QM-12 if, for every crop, some coordinate reaches B with all p_i ≥ 0.05, n ≤ 20, and total cost ≤ 1e8 evaluations. That cost is below B_min = 1.3e8.

Support requires, for every coordinate, min p_i ≤ 2e-4 (the most generous resource scenario; about 1e-10 at D2 central), and an extrapolated splitting cost of at least B(L) ≈ 1e11.

Paper pre-check, about one hour: put the measured p_i into C_cl/C_q ≈ sqrt(n)*(1-p_i)/(pi*delta*sqrt(p_i))*(tau/tau_q) and compare the result with the per-step overhead of 6e3 to 1e7.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
From RESOURCE_MODELS.md, one walk step at L=100 costs 1.1e7–1.0e9 Toffolis, which is about 19 s to 3.9e4 s. A classical evaluation takes about 3 ms, so the per-step overhead is 6e3 to 1e7. Break-even B(L) is 1.3e8–4.8e9 classical evaluations per rare event in the most generous case (D3 generous, S=1, R=100) and 1.5e11–1.5e15 at D2 central.

When every interface has p_i = Theta(1), the splitting query gain is at most about 390x, even with a walk-accelerated segment and delta = 0.5. It can never reach break-even. The quantum side also has to pay for coherent preparation of the level-i entrance distribution, which is not free.

The pilot evidence is far below B. The census-lowest basin at L=120 is hit in about 2.7e4 evaluations by plain multistart, and the NRPT round-trip bounds are 2e5–3.9e5.

Precision is capped by the force field. A 1 kcal/mol barrier error is a 5.4x rate error at 300 K, so the Theta(1/eps) against Theta(1/eps^2) precision gain is worth at most about 2x.
verdicts.novelty_note:
Novelty is low for the primitive and moderate for the no-go framing.

Walk hitting, walk QPE and amplitude estimation of transition probabilities are standard [A1–A4, A22, A35]. They are already in the program as M3/QA-3, rated WEAK in Opportunity Map v2.

The arXiv title/abstract search was 14 API queries on 2026-09-27. The web-search budget was exhausted, so Google Scholar and other non-arXiv venues were not covered. Within that scope, it found no evidence of either:
- (i) a quantum analogue of AMS/FFS/WE with amplitude amplification per interface; or
- (ii) any quantum rate or rare-event method benchmarked against WE/AMS/FFS/MSM on a protein.

The nearest works are:
- Kharazi et al. 2026, whose exponential claim is against worst-case Langevin bounds with additive error, and is not robust to splitting;
- Mazzola 2021 and Pravatto et al. 2021, which are variational rate eigenproblems;
- Ghamari et al. 2022/2024, a D-Wave demonstration that shows agreement, not advantage;
- Guo et al. 2026, generic quadratic rare-event discovery.

QM-12's most original and useful content is the adversary-first splitting lemma. Classical cost goes as sum 1/p_i and quantum cost as sum p_i^-1/2, so there is no asymptotic gain at p_i = Theta(1). That is a negative contribution: publishable as a no-go note next to T5, not as an advantage.

Recommendation: do not run QM-12 as a separate lane. Fold the AMS interface census into G1 as the direct test of QM-02's hide-and-seek premise. Record QM-12 as a KILL in KILLBOOK Section B if the census reports p_i ≥ 0.05.

title: Committors and transition rates via quantum linear-system / QSVT solvers on the discretised backward-Kolmogorov generator
merged_from: qalg QM-10 (committor/rate via QLSA), wild 'Committors and folding rates via quantum linear-system solvers'
summary: Q: committor function (transition-state ensemble) and rate k_AB between two metastable conformations of a learned or physical energy. Quantum: QLSA (O(kappa log 1/eps)) or QSVT inversion of a block-encoded sparse finite-difference backward generator on N = m^d grid points, flux functional read by amplitude estimation. Replaces: grid PDE solvers and trajectory Monte Carlo. Mechanism: block encoding costs poly(d b) per query, so N enters logarithmically, an exponential saving over deterministic grid solvers. But kappa ~ h^-2 e^{beta Delta} (the slow rate enters linearly), relative-precision readout of an exponentially small rate still costs ~k_AB^-1/2, and the committor has a positive Feynman-Kac representation q(x) = P[hit B before A], so classical random-walk Monte Carlo is dimension-free and splitting removes the rare-event factor. Linden-Montanaro-Shao (CMP 2022) prove for the heat equation that QLSA is never faster than the best classical method and AE on random walks is at most quadratic; stochastic-unraveling principle (I(prog)): any quantity with a positive stochastic representation stays <= quadratically ahead of Monte Carlo. Speedup: <= quadratic (precision) vs Monte Carlo; exponential only vs grid solvers nobody uses. Oracle: block encoding from coherent E/grad E at grid points (QM-05, ~1e7+ Toffolis per query at L=100), native-free basin indicators from a classical MSM, boundary-flux state prep, AE. Competitor: WE, FFS, AMS, TPS, milestoning, MSMs, neural variational committors, TT/QTT PDE solvers, string method. Info vs comp: pure computation on a classical energy; kinetics are off the structure endpoint. S29-S33: not tested; K-011/DNR-18 (small dense readout programs) do not apply to a sparse exponentially large generator; the relevant new control is random-walk Monte Carlo. Kill: AMS/WE estimate k_AB to 10% at cost polynomial in L and polylog in 1/k_AB between the two slowest metastable sets at 60 aa (<= 1e8 evals); plus a 2-page note that no QLSA kappa-scaling beats splitting. Test: 2D/4D Muller-Brown or esmprior-projected CV toy (exact grid committor vs AMS/FFS vs beta); WE/AMS between two decoder-found basins at mid30/long40 under overdamped Langevin. <= 1 day. Track: C theory/query. Prior: very low.
dead_reason: Not covered by existing kills (M3 WEAK concerns walks; K-011 concerns small dense convex readouts); killed by argument/literature (Linden-Montanaro-Shao), to be recorded as a new kill.

verdicts.level_theoretical: Exponential claim: L0, refuted. The "N enters logarithmically" saving is measured against full-grid PDE solvers, which nobody uses at d≈120. The committor q(x)=P_x[τ_B<τ_A] has a positive Feynman–Kac form, so random-walk Monte Carlo already costs nothing in N and is dimension-free. Linden–Montanaro–Shao prove for the heat equation that the QLSA route is "never faster than the best classical algorithms", and that the only speedup (AE on an accelerated random walk) is "at most quadratic". The backward generator is a reversible M-matrix (stoquastic), so the same positive-unraveling argument applies. This is INFERENCE by analogy, not proved for this exact operator. What survives is ≤quadratic: 1/ε precision via AE, and at best √κ via walk-based or positive-definite QLSA (Orsucci–Dunjko). That is L6 only as a query-model statement of a quadratic gain. On the rare-event factor, the QLSA+AE rate readout is exponentially WORSE than classical splitting: Θ(k^{-1/2}) AE rounds against O(log 1/k) levels for AMS with a good coordinate. So there is no separation to claim against the strongest classical method.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No matched-conditions usefulness (L1) is plausible. At 60 aa, even the best-case quantum variant (a "quantum AMS", i.e. product-of-ratios with AE per level) gains at most ~10x in 1/ε at ε=0.1. Against that stands a coherent-oracle overhead of ≥1e6–1e7 Toffolis per E/∇E query, plus fault-tolerant clock ratios. The plain QLSA+AE design is ~1e17–1e20 Toffolis, against ~1e8–1e9 classical force evaluations.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The best case for the quantum side is that QLSA is reaction-coordinate-free. AMS, WE, FFS and milestoning reach polylog(1/k) cost only with a decent progress coordinate. On a 60-aa learned-energy landscape with no known coordinate, or with entropic or golf-course bottlenecks, their variance can drift back toward brute-force cost ~1/k. A generic "PDE on an exponential grid" is also not automatically dequantisable: Babbush et al. (PRX 13, 041041, 2023) give a BQP-complete, exponential speedup for 2^n coupled classical oscillators.

Rebuttal (why KILL stands):
(i) In that coordinate-free worst case, QLSA+AE costs κ·√(α/k)/ε, against brute-force MC at T/(kε²). That is quadratic, the stochastic-unraveling ceiling.
(ii) The oscillator result relies on conservative (unitary-embeddable) dynamics. The backward Kolmogorov generator is dissipative and non-normal in flat L2. An–Liu–Wang–Zhao (CMP 406:189, 2025) prove worst-case overheads for exactly these "non-quantum" real-part-gap and non-normality features.
(iii) The oracle list requires native-free basin indicators from a classical MSM, because κ picks up e^{βΔ_int} from every intermediate basin not absorbed into A∪B. Once that MSM exists, MSM transition-path theory already gives the committor and k_AB from a small linear system. The quantum input requirement solves the problem classically.
(iv) Coordinate quality is improved adaptively by neural-committor-plus-AMS loops (Pigeon–Stoltz–Lelièvre 2026; Rotskoff–Mitchell–Vanden-Eijnden), and WE is unbiased for any binning.
(v) Information versus computation: overdamped-Langevin rates on the esmprior statistical potential have no kinetic ground truth and sit off the structure endpoint (condition C). A perfect solver would add nothing to the mission metric.
verdicts.evidence:
VERIFIED this pass (arXiv API or abstract page, or Crossref):
- Linden, Montanaro, Shao, "Quantum vs. classical algorithms for solving the heat equation", arXiv:2004.06516 (CMP 2022, journal ref not re-checked). Abstract: "at most quadratic quantum speedup using ... amplitude estimation [on] an accelerated classical random walk ... [QLSA] is never faster than the best classical algorithms."
- Montanaro & Pallister, PRA 93, 032324 (2016), arXiv:1512.05903: FEM speedup is "polynomial".
- Childs, Liu, Ostrander, Quantum 5, 574 (2021), arXiv:2002.07868.

The only exact separation, log N versus N (L6-type under a sparse-access or block-encoding oracle), is against deterministic grid PDE solvers, which nobody uses at d >= 4. So quantum beats direct simulation in query count only when N_trans >> (eps*c*kappa*ln(1/eps))^2. Against AMS, sqrt(N_trans) versus log(N_trans) is an asymptotic loss unless AMS variance blows up exponentially.

(1) Kharazi, Alkadri, Mandadapu, Whaley (arXiv 2601.15523, v2 June 2026) give a different quantum route to reaction rates. It does not compare against FFS, AMS, WE or TPS, and it gives no fault-tolerant resource estimate. (b) Block encoding. In the SQRA symmetric form H = pi^{1/2}(-L)pi^{-1/2}, the off-diagonal entries are a constant, -D/h^2. The diagonal needs e^{-beta(E(y)-E(x))/2} for every neighbour y. One LCU query therefore costs 2 coherent energies plus their uncomputes, so C_BE ~ 4*C_E ~ 8e7 to 4e8 Toffolis. C_E is 2e7 to 1e8 at L = 60, scaled by L^2 from the repo's T2/T4 figures of 1e7 to 6e7 (and 1e8) at L = 45. The normalisation is alpha ~ 2d*D/h^2*(1+e^{beta*delta_cap}). verdicts.decisive_test:
Paper-only, about 2 pages, with a ≤ 1-hour CPU confirmation.

(1) Write the 'barrier-exponential conservation' lemma. For relative precision ε on k_AB ~ e^{-βΔ}, any pipeline of the form 'QLSA/QSVT on the discretised generator, then AE flux readout' pays e^{Θ(βΔ)} in at least one of three places:
- κ (flat BKE: κ ~ N² e^{βΔV}, Kharazi 2026);
- the readout amplitude (π-symmetrised: a ∝ k, so AE costs k^{-1/2}; confirmed numerically in the scratch script);
- the additive-to-relative conversion (O((kε)^{-1})).
AMS pays O(log(1/k)/ε²) under a reasonable reaction coordinate (Cérou–Guyader CLT). The only escape is coherent splitting, which is capped at quadratic in 1/ε for positive Feynman–Kac quantities (Kwas 2004; LMS 2022 analogue), and CA-4 kills that in practice.

(2) CPU confirmation: extend bke_kappa.py with a vectorised AMS (N = 100 replicas, 30 repeats per β, β ∈ {2, 4, 8, 12, 16}, RC = x) on the same double well. Record the energy and gradient evaluations needed to reach 10% relative error on k_AB. Kill confirmed if AMS cost grows ≤ polynomially in βΔ (expected about linearly) while κ_flat·a^{-1/2} grows ≥ e^{0.5βΔ}.

No mid30/long40 WE/AMS run is needed, because the relevance kill (kinetics are off the structure endpoint and unphysical on esmprior) fires first.

Reopen only if both hold:
(a) a classical experiment shows that committor-type information improves the G1 structure-posterior sampler or the soft readout by ≥ 1.0× MDE;
(b) a quantum readout is exhibited that avoids e^{Θ(βΔ)} at relative precision and beats AMS asymptotically in βΔ.
verdicts.novelty_note: The search (arXiv abstract API plus Crossref, 2004–2026; WebSearch unavailable) found no paper that builds a QLSA/QSVT committor solver for a protein or a learned energy. The formulation itself is not new, though. Kharazi et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.15523) name the committor/BKE linear-solve route, derive κ ~ N² e^{βΔV}, and set it aside in favour of a Gaussian-LCHS flux estimator. Quantum rate estimation for Fokker–Planck dynamics was already claimed in Mazzola 2021 (PRA 104, 022431; SUSY rates and currents, protein-folding motivation), Pravatto et al. 2021 (VQE on the FPS eigenproblem for a conformational rate) and Miyamoto–Tada 2025 (QSVT on the adjoint-FP eigenvalue). Protein transition-path sampling on quantum annealers exists as well (Hauke–Mattiotti–Faccioli PRL 2021; Ghamari et al. Sci. Rep. 2022 and JCTC). The only piece nobody has claimed is applying it to a learned structure energy, and that is scientifically empty because learned-energy kinetics have no physical meaning or validation target. Merge QM-13 into M3 (WEAK) and record it in KILLBOOK Section B as dominated within prior art. The one prior-art gap worth noting is that no quantum rate paper, Kharazi included, benchmarks against WE, FFS, AMS, TPS or MSMs.

title: Fold-switching / competing-fold learned posteriors: an information-first test bed for bimodal sampling (sampler, hitting and swap-test/AE variants)
merged_from: learned 'Fold-switching sequences as the physically grounded bimodal learned posterior', classical 'Alternative-state and fold-switch discovery from sequence', wild 'Competing-fold hypothesis testing: quantum distribution testing and swap-test fidelity'
summary: Q: for metamorphic proteins (GA/GB designed switch pair, RfaH-CTD, KaiB, lymphotactin; <= ~100 aa), does the learned-energy posterior represent both folds, what is their relative population, and is estimating it classically hard? Quantum: QSA/QRELD between two macro-basins (sqrt of the barrier factor), walk hitting between folds, AE of a basin projector (~1/sqrt(p_B)) and swap-test fidelity between wild-type and mutant posteriors. Replaces: inter-fold mixing and relative free-energy estimation. Mechanism: if two comparable-free-energy macro-basins are separated by a first-order-like barrier, PT/ST mixing is torpid [E39,E40] and a walk gains a square root. Classical escape once both modes are known: fold-conditioned decodes + bridge sampling/MBAR along a restraint path, and umbrella sampling along Q_A - Q_B, all polynomial; a known competing fold is a legitimate native-free hypothesis (e.g. from AF2 MSA subsampling), which stratifies away the 1/p_B factor. Quantum matters only if one fold has large mass but a tiny basin of attraction (QM-02 regime). Precondition (information): single-sequence learned models mostly predict one fold (AF2 one conformation for 94% of 98 switchers [E94]; 1/7 out-of-training switchers captured from >280k models [E100]); by the data-processing inequality no sampler creates mass the model lacks. The AE/swap-test variant is covered by M4 (see QM-14). Speedup: quadratic in barrier factor, conditional on both folds being represented and one being invisible to restarts. Oracle: as QM-01/QM-05; the fold indicator must be native-free. Competitor: fold-conditioned restarts + bridge sampling/MBAR, umbrella/metadynamics on Q_A - Q_B, PT/REST2, AF-Cluster/subsampled MSA, BioEmu. Info vs comp: whether ESM/esmprior encode fold B is almost certainly the binding constraint. S29-S33: multimodality becomes the scientific object (populations), replacing single-native RMSD condition C; DNR-16/K-012 information logic still governs. Kill: prior mass on fold-B bins at discriminating pairs < 5% (information-limited, stop); OR both folds found in <= 1e3 restarts and bridge-sampling/umbrella DeltaF converges within +-0.5 kT in <= 1e7-1e8 evals; OR posterior mass does not shift between folds with the switching mutation. Test: ~6 switchers, leakage-checked against esmprior <=72-aa training crops (GB1/GA homologue risk); ESM-2 650M on CPU; per-fold bin mass; 1e3 A80 restarts; NRPT + darting; 16-32-window umbrella + MBAR; ORACLE-labelled mass within 3 A of each fold. Hours to 1 day. Track: C/E (B for the sampler). Prior: very low (1-2%).
dead_reason: Sampler variant not covered by an existing kill (information presence untested); only its AE/swap-test variant falls under M4 (QM-14).

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for the protein task as posed. The generic query separations (quadratic walk/QSA hitting in the barrier factor e^{beta*Delta}; Olivucci et al. 2026 Omega(alpha) vs O~(sqrt alpha) on hide-and-seek wells [A45]; AE 1/(eps*sqrt p) vs 1/(eps^2 p)) are L6 only in their own abstract models. They do not transfer, because the relevant classical comparator here never pays the quantity being sped up. (i) Once two fold hypotheses exist, stratified bridge sampling or MBAR along a non-physical restraint path costs O(K*tau_w/eps^2), which does not depend on the inter-fold barrier or on p_B. (ii) A pairwise-factorised learned energy (A80: sum of -log p_ij(d_ij), plus theta/tau and steric terms) cannot hide a well from inspection. Every pair-basin location sits in the explicit factor tables, so the hide-and-seek instance class of [A45] is structurally excluded at the macrostate level. (iii) The swap-test fidelity between wild-type and mutant qsamples is F = BC^2, where BC = Z_{(E_wt+E_mut)/2} / sqrt(Z_wt*Z_mut). That is a ratio of partition functions, so it falls under the H-001/H-009 reduction class and is classically estimable by BAR/MBAR over three Hamiltonians.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. Nothing has been measured, and the paper derivation below says the classical cost falls below the fault-tolerant per-step overhead alone. Take the fold-conditioned stratified quantum variant, the best case for quantum. It beats classical stratification only if in-window mixing satisfies t_w > (R*eps)^2. With the program's T3 ratio R = C_q/C_c of 1e7-1e10 and eps = 0.5 (from ±0.5 kT), that means t_w > 2.5e13 to 2.5e19 steps inside a single fold-restrained window of ≤100 aa. The project's own G1 census minimises each restart in about 220 gradient evaluations at L = 100-120. The unstratified AE variant is worse still: at scientifically relevant populations (p_B ≥ 0.01, i.e. ΔF ≤ 4.6 kT), 1/sqrt(p_B) ≤ 10, and quantum needs sqrt(t_glob) < K*t_w*sqrt(p_B)/(R*pi*eps). With K*t_w ≈ 3e5, p_B = 0.1 and R = 1e7, the right-hand side is ≈ 6e-3. So quantum cannot win even if the global mixing time t_glob is 1.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument: The strongest case for keeping QM-15 comes from the project's own G1 data. The A80/esmprior landscape looks glassy at L ≥ 60. In the 256-restart census, 39-100% of restarts land in distinct minima at L = 60-120, the best-mode hit rate p_hit falls to 0.004-0.03 at L = 80-120 (research/results/PROCESSED/g1_summary.json), and the lambda-path NRPT pilot made 0 round trips at T = 1 with global barrier Lambda ≈ 14-29 over 30-39 rungs. So in-fold window mixing tau_w might itself be very large, and stratification would move the hardness into the windows rather than remove it. A second risk: if fold B were a narrow funnel with high mass (Woodard persistence), restarts and JAMS mode-finding would miss it. Rebuttals: (a) Hardness inside windows is the general G1/H-006 question, already pre-registered with kills K-G1a-d, including the calibrated-temperature kill K-G1c. QM-15 adds no mechanism, instance class or speedup beyond G1 and QM-02. (b) Whether fold B has competitive mass can be certified directly from the factor tables: for a competitive fold B, the sum over discriminating pairs of log[p_ij(d_B)/p_ij(d_A)] must lie within a few kT, give or take the entropy difference between compact folds. That can be read off without sampling. Persistence also has dedicated classical fixes: weight-preserving tempering, QuanTA, and JAMS (find modes by optimisation, then jump between them). (c) The binding constraint is information. AF2 captured one conformation, not both, for 94% of 98 switchers [E94]. It captured only 1 of 7 out-of-training switchers despite more than 280k models [E100]. Even CF-random reports that it works partly by 'sequence association' to training-set landscapes. A 510k-parameter head trained on 600 crops of ≤72 aa almost certainly lacks fold B, and by the data-processing inequality no sampler, quantum or classical, can create mass the model does not contain. (d) Leakage: GB1/protein G and albumin-binding GA-module homologues are likely in the ≤72-aa training crops. With about 6 targets there is almost no statistical power for a general claim.
verdicts.evidence:
CLASSICAL ADVERSARY PORTFOLIO (the full chain has no step that pays a barrier factor):

(1) NATIVE-FREE FOLD-HYPOTHESIS GENERATION (removes the discovery/hitting variant)

- Subsampled AF2 [E96]. Monteiro da Silva et al. [E101, 10.1038/s41467-024-46715-9] predicted changes in relative state populations with >80% accuracy, working best for the qualitative effects of mutations. That is the QM-15 scientific object, obtained classically.

(3) RELATIVE FREE ENERGY BETWEEN KNOWN FOLDS
- MBAR [E69].
- Umbrella sampling along Q_A - Q_B, or a Hamiltonian restraint path from fold-A-restrained to fold-B-restrained, with replica exchange across windows.
- Cost ≈ K*N_eff*tau_w ≈ 16-32 windows × 10-100 effective samples × 1e3-1e4 evaluations, i.e. 1e5 to 3e7 energy+gradient evaluations. At ≈5 ms per evaluation at L = 100-120 (G1 census: 55,950 gradient evaluations in 280 s, batched, so per-evaluation cost is approximate), that is roughly 10 minutes to 2 days on 8 cores.

(4) PRECEDENT: CLASSICAL DUAL-FUNNEL LANDSCAPES OF REAL SWITCHERS ARE ROUTINE (the computational problem is solved; the error is in the model)

- Seifi, Aina, Wallin, BPJ 2021 abstract, 10.1016/j.bpj.2020.11.315.
- Chen et al., 'Aromatic-aromatic interactions drive fold switch of GA95 and GB95 with three residue difference', Chem. Sci. 2025, 10.1039/d4sc04951a. Verified.

(5) INFORMATION LIMIT: [E94] (10.1002/pro.4353), [E100] (10.1038/s41467-024-51801-z).

(6) THE QUANTUM SIDE
- [A44] Leng et al., PNAS 2026, 10.1073/pnas.2512789123.
- [A45] Olivucci et al., arXiv 2608.24527.

(7) DERIVATIONS
- Swap test: F = BC^2 with BC = Z_{(E1+E2)/2} / sqrt(Z1*Z2), a free-energy ratio. Each swap-test shot also consumes two full qsample preparations, and O(1/eps^2) shots are needed.
- AE on the basin projector: π/(eps*sqrt(p_B)) state preparations, versus stratified classical O(K*tau_w/eps^2), which does not depend on p_B.
- Break-even: t_w > (R*eps)^2 ≥ 2.5e13.

All citation checks were done this session through Crossref, arXiv and Europe PMC. The WebSearch budget was exhausted, so no other claims were checked.
verdicts.decisive_test:
One paper step, then a factor-table certificate on the 8-core CPU box. The CPU part takes under an hour, with no sampling.

STEP 0 (paper): write down the inequality t_w > (R*eps)^2. It already kills every stratified quantum variant, unless a single fold-restrained window of ≤100 aa needs more than about 1e13 steps to mix.

STEP 1: pick switchers and a control.
- Switchers: GA95/GB95, GA98/GB98 (one mutation apart), RfaH-CTD (isolated CTD, about 50 aa), KaiB (about 100 aa) and lymphotactin (93 aa).
- Control: one single-fold protein of matched length.
- Screen every sequence against the 600 esmprior training crops (identity ≥ 30% by MMseqs2 or Smith-Waterman), with a specific check for protein G B1 and albumin-binding GA-module homologues. Flag leaked targets and do not drop them silently.

STEP 2: run the certificate.
- Run ESM-2 650M and the esmprior head once per sequence.
- Define fold-discriminating pairs as those whose CA/CB distance differs by more than 4 Å between the two PDB folds. This definition is ORACLE-labelled and used for analysis only; it must never feed decoding.
- Compute three quantities: (a) median factor mass in fold-B-consistent bins; (b) LLR_AB = Σ log[p_ij(d_B)/p_ij(d_A)], plus the A80 theta/tau and steric terms evaluated at the two native coordinate sets relaxed under light restraints; (c) the shift in LLR between members of each GA/GB pair.

KILL QM-15 if any of these holds:
- median fold-B bin mass < 5% (the pre-registered threshold);
- |LLR_AB| > 10 kT on every non-leaked target, so fold B is non-competitive and the problem is information-limited;
- LLR does not change sign or shift by at least 2 kT between GA and GB variants.

Expected outcome: KILL through the information limit, as in [E94, E100].

STEP 3 (only if Step 2 passes): take fold hypotheses from the bimodal-pair clusters (native-free), run 64 fold-restrained A80 decodes per fold, then 16-32-window restraint-path MBAR. Count evaluations to reach ±0.5 kT. Kill if ≤ 1e8. Expected 1e5-1e7, which is at least 4-7 orders of magnitude below the break-even B ≥ 1e12.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Classical cost of the full task (discovery plus ΔF_AB to ±0.5 kT, at ≤100 aa):
- Hypothesis generation: seconds (one factor-table read) to minutes (1e3 seeded decodes × about 220 evaluations ≈ 2e5 evaluations).
- Stratified MBAR: 1e5 to 3e7 evaluations, i.e. 10 minutes to 2 days on 8 cores at about 5 ms per A80 evaluation.

Quantum break-even:
- Unstratified: B ≥ 1e12 classical steps per independent sample. Using R^2 with R = 1e7-1e10, the threshold is 1e14 to 1e20.
- Stratified: t_w > (R*eps)^2 ≥ 2.5e13.
- The margin is at least 5 orders of magnitude, and more once you note that the classical estimator never pays the barrier factor the walk would square-root.
- AE and swap-test variants gain at most 1/sqrt(p_B) ≤ 10 at relevant populations, or 1/eps vs 1/eps^2 = 2× at eps = 0.5. Both are wiped out by R.

Simulator runtime is not physical quantum runtime, and none was used here.
verdicts.novelty_note: Searches covered the 448-paper literature set plus targeted Crossref, arXiv and Europe PMC checks on 2026-09-27. They found no quantum-algorithm paper on fold-switching or metamorphic-protein populations, and no landscape characterisation of a language-model-derived pair-distance energy on metamorphic proteins. The classical side of the question is already well populated: population and mutation-effect prediction with subsampled AF2 [E101], CF-random, AF-Cluster, ConforMix and ConforFold, plus physics-based dual-funnel landscapes (Wales et al. on RfaH; Chen et al. 2025 and Tian & Best 2020 on GA/GB). The only novel part of QM-15 is the classical factor-table information test on esmprior. It is worth running as supporting K3 (information-limit) evidence, or as a bimodality sub-census inside G1, but it is not a quantum contribution. The quantum variants (QSA/QRELD between basins, walk hitting between folds, AE of the basin projector, swap-test fidelity) are all covered by QM-02, QM-14 and M4, or reduce to free-energy ratios. They should be recorded in KILLBOOK as K5/K4/K1 kills: overhead, wrong factor (the classical method does not pay the barrier), and reduction (swap-test fidelity is a ratio of partition functions).

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for QM-15 as posed. No query separation exists against the relevant classical adversary: fold-conditioned decodes plus stratified (umbrella/bridge/MBAR) estimation along a native-free Q_A-Q_B coordinate. The only provable separations that apply are relative to a different comparator: quadratic in the spectral gap / barrier factor e^{dF} of the *unbiased* quantised chain (Szegedy/QSA), quadratic against *i.i.d.* restarts for AE of a basin projector (T4), and Olivucci et al.'s hide-and-seek Theta(sqrt(alpha)) vs Theta(alpha) (T5 Theorem A: exactly quadratic, and it needs information-locality, which a distogram energy violates). T3 supplies the gate-level oracle cost, and it shows no crossover. The swap-test variant sits at L0: fidelity mixes population shift with within-basin distortion and adds nothing beyond per-fold dF/ddF. It is covered by the killed M4.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. At 56 aa the A80-faithful walk step (D2) costs 2.8e7-1.1e8 Toffolis, which is 1.3-5 h per step on one factory, and needs 2.7-3.0e4 logical and about 6e7 physical qubits (d=31). Even under the most generous stack (kappa=c_q=1, 100 factories, one classical core) the quantum is 1.5e3-1.5e4x slower per independent within-window sample than the classical stratified sampler. Break-even requires a residual classical mixing cost that no measured quantity approaches.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
Assume the information precondition passes: esmprior puts at least 5% fold-B bin mass at discriminating pairs. Suppose also that the switch involves a concerted rearrangement, such as a strand-register or topology change, with hidden barriers orthogonal to any native-free Q_A-Q_B coordinate. Then per-window tau_int could be astronomically large, stratification would not remove the barrier, and a walk would still gain sqrt(tau). T3's G(L) is not a lower bound (perhaps 10x more arithmetic savings, which lowers B 100x). An optimised classical kernel raises B rather than lowering it. Prop. C1 (T5) shows there is no universal quadratic ceiling for classical energies. For a novel switcher, no AF-Cluster-style fold-B hypothesis might exist.

Rebuttal:
(i) That regime is exactly the generic H-006/M1 question: glassy within-basin mixing, which G1 is already measuring (census: n_modes ~ R and p_hit ~ 1/256 at L >= 60). QM-15 adds no new quantum mechanism.
(ii) Even at the lowest B found anywhere, the quantum run needs about 8 days per independent sample at break-even and 23 yr against a 1000-core adversary. That B is 2.3e9, from D3 generous, which samples a bond-relaxed target, not A80, and whose kappa is unmeasured.
(iii) The fold-B mass must come from distogram bins. Those bins leak fold-B distances at every discriminating pair, so the QM-02 regime (large mass but a tiny basin of attraction) is self-undermining. A classical adversary can restrain the decoder to the fold-B modes, and restart saturation is 32-64 in the predecessor. This last step is INFERENCE, not proved.
