verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
AGAINST THE CANDIDATE (decisive):

(1) The claimed source of hardness can be removed by classical computation. With per-peak or per-crosslink ambiguity, p(x,a|D) ∝ π(x)·Π_r w_{r,a_r} f_r(x;a_r) sums exactly to p(x|D) ∝ π(x)·Π_r Σ_k w_rk f_r(x;k). That costs Σ_r m_r = 60–400 extra terms per evaluation at 0.5–1 restraint/residue, 2–4 candidates and L=60–100. The 2^30–4^100 assignment combinations are therefore not a computational cost. For Gibbs data augmentation, collapsed/marginalised samplers mix no worse than the joint Gibbs chain (Liu–Wong–Kong 1994); whether that ordering transfers to a quantised or tempered joint chain is my inference, not a proved result. What remains is a continuous multimodal posterior, the same class as QM-01. The T5 quadratic ceiling and BREAK_EVEN §1 therefore apply unchanged. ARIA's r^-6 sum (Nilges 1995) is a deterministic stand-in for this marginal. The only couplings that do not factorise are:
- one-to-one resonance matching, for which weighted matchings have a classical FPRAS (Jerrum–Sinclair–Vigoda 2004), and which is done upstream anyway (ARTINA 91% correct);
- homo-oligomer copy permutations, which are exact symmetries that can be quotiented out.

(2) In practice the bottleneck is information, not computation. CYANA's systematic evaluation finds combined assignment plus structure calculation "remarkably robust" to NOESY-list imperfections. It is "susceptible to lacking or erroneous resonance assignments", which is a data failure. ARTINA reaches 1.44 Å median RMSD on 100 proteins within hours. RASREC-Rosetta is routine up to 40 kDa with sparse data. IMP practitioners name disordered regions, cryo-ET data use and representation choice as the recurrent challenges, and they coarse-grain precisely so that sampling passes the exhaustiveness tests (Viswanath 2017; NestOR 2024). Near the identifiability threshold, where the Woodard persistence regime could make parallel tempering (PT) torpid, competing folds have comparable mass. The data then do not identify the fold, which is the card's own third kill clause. Only the relative mode weights (class K) would remain as a target, and a quantum walk speeds that up only quadratically.

AGAINST MY VERDICT (why not KILL): this is the only card that brings new per-target information, which meets the DNR-16/K-012 reopening condition. The targets are real and large (NMR structures up to ~40 kDa; assemblies of 10–552 subunits). Viswanath's tests are "necessary but not sufficient", so a hidden torpid regime cannot be ruled out without measuring. That is why the verdict is WEAK rather than KILL for the NOE branch.

verdicts.decisive_test:
Step 1, on paper (done above): exact per-restraint marginalisation removes the assignment register at cost Σ m_r per evaluation. The card's mechanism therefore reduces to QM-01 unless a non-factorising coupling is essential.

Step 2, one 8-core CPU day under the governor, pre-registered:
- Setup: SIM-DATA on long40 and on one L=100 ladder crop, labelled SIM/ORACLE-derived and kept apart from DEP results. 0.5 and 1 restraint/residue, m ∈ {2,4} candidates, 10% and 20% outliers, and a Student-t or two-component outlier likelihood.
- Arm A: collapsed-marginal NRPT + HMC on p(x|D) with the exact mixture likelihood (not r^-6).
- Arm B: joint PT + Gibbs assignment flips.
- Arm C: r^-6 anneal with 100 independent restarts.
- Measurements: round trips; integrated autocorrelation of the top-cluster indicator; Viswanath four-test sampling precision from two independent halves; evaluations per independent sample (B_best).
- Identifiability, computed at ORACLE evaluation time only: whether the maximum-mass cluster is native-like, and whether the gap between the top two cluster masses is over 10:1.

Kill (practical) if B_best < 1e9 in every cell. That is ≥10× below the most optimistic B* ≈ 1e10.
Kill (mechanism) if Arm A ≥ Arm B in mixing everywhere, i.e. collapsing removes the discrete hardness.
Kill (identifiability) if every cell where B_best ≥ 1e7 has cluster masses within 3:1 or a top cluster that is not native-like.
Escalate only if collapsed NRPT needs ≥ 1e9 evaluations per sample in a regime where the data do identify the fold, and that cost grows super-polynomially in L or m.

verdicts.novelty_note:
Search scope, 2026-09-27: arXiv API title/abstract queries and Europe PMC title queries, 2019–2026 plus older anchors. General WebSearch was unavailable because the session budget was exhausted, so the search is narrower than a full web search.

The search found no evidence of a paper applying quantum walks, QSA, quantum Langevin or quantum replica exchange to NMR ambiguous-restraint, crosslink or integrative-modelling structure posteriors. It also found none using quantum methods for NOE or resonance assignment, or for cryo-EM/integrative assembly sampling. Nearest prior art:
- Algorithm: Harrow–Wei 2020 already gives QSA for Bayesian inference along an adaptive annealing path; Wocjan–Abeyesinghe 2008 and Somma et al. 2008 precede it.
- Application analogue: quantum multiproposal MCMC for a scientific Bayesian posterior (Lin et al. 2023, phylogenetics).
- Protein-adjacent quantum work: QUBO/annealing docking, which is optimisation, not posterior sampling (Triuzzi 2024, Micucci 2026, Li 2024).
- Classical data-tempering: Habeck–Nilges–Rieping 2005 PRL.

Novelty is therefore application-level pairing only. The mechanism is QM-01's quadratic walk, and the data-tempering path plus QSA is not new. Any write-up must cite Harrow–Wei 2020 and Habeck et al. 2005.

title: Many-body 1H dipolar-network forward model for fast-MAS solid-state NMR / proton spin diffusion of protonated proteins (quantitative 3-8 A distances past dipolar truncation)
merged_from: physics P1 (many-body 1H dipolar forward model for fast-MAS ssNMR), wild 'Quantum simulation of many-body nuclear-spin dynamics as the forward model for protein NMR', priorart (b) NMR many-body dynamics as forward model
summary: Q: RFDR / proton spin-diffusion cross-peaks in fully protonated proteins at >= 100 kHz MAS are reduced to binned upper bounds because strong geminal/vicinal couplings (~20 kHz) truncate weak long-range ones (~1 kHz at 5 A, ~0.2 kHz at 8 A) and transfer is relayed. Could exact many-body simulation turn build-up curves into quantitative 5-8 A distances, i.e. exactly the per-target long-range information S33 found missing? Quantum: Trotterised/qubitised simulation of the (time-dependent MAS or average-Hamiltonian) homonuclear dipolar Hamiltonian on N 1H qubits; high-temperature correlators via DQC1/Hadamard test or typicality; used inside classical Bayesian inversion or to train a classical surrogate. Replaces: rate-matrix/ISPA spin-diffusion models, low-order LCL/CCE, exact <= ~14-spin SIMPSON-class simulation. Mechanism: 2^N-dimensional non-commuting real-time dynamics (BQP-complete in general); classical must store the state or truncate by spin order/Pauli weight; quantum needs poly(N t) gates. Classical copies it whenever transfer is effectively incoherent (low-spin-order z-magnetisation transport): LCL reproduced experimental spin diffusion (Dumez 2010), LR-LCL scales linearly to thousands of spins under MAS (Perras-Pruski 2019), spinDMFT matches static spin diffusion (Graesser-Uhrig-Ernst 2026), Fratus et al. linear-scaling clusters work in typical regimes. Speedup: exponential in coherently treated cluster size, conditional (expected none for standard observables). Oracle: none hidden; couplings computed classically from candidate coordinates (~45 neighbours within 6 A); 30-200-spin patches; 1e2-1e4 multiplier for powder orientations and Trotter slices; ~1e8 T per circuit x 1e4 shots, ~1e11-1e14 T per likelihood; realistic architecture is quantum-generated training data for a classical surrogate. Competitor: LR-LCL, LCL, spinDMFT, sparse Pauli dynamics, TT Liouville propagation, CCE, exact 20-24-spin embedding, ML surrogates; perdeuteration + sparse back-labelling or REDOR isolated pairs (make dynamics classical by design); AF2/ESM priors. Info vs comp: information is new experimental data (DNR-16 satisfied); the quantum part adds only the forward model, valuable only for relayed/truncated coherent transfer on weak long-range couplings. S29-S33: non-diagonal dynamics fall outside H-001/DNR-02 and DNR-09 dimension counting (physical 2^N spins, not a candidate index); condition-C analogue transfers (forward-model precision must transmit to chain accuracy); lit_F P2 rated it a 'WEAK curiosity'. Kill: on protein-derived 1H clusters (N = 12-22 exact, 1UBQ/GB1 with OpenMM hydrogens, ORACLE/analysis use) rate-matrix, weight-<=4-6 Pauli, LCL or CCE-3 reproduce build-ups within 3-5% at mixing times <= 10 ms, error flat in N, and recover 5-8 A distances with bias < noise sigma at SNR 50; OR the exact model's Fisher information on 5-8 A distances exceeds the rate model's by < 10%; OR backbone accuracy saturates with qualitative contacts (restraint-value curve). Test: probe pairs at 3/5/7 A, nested clusters N = 12/16/20, exact 2-qubit-Trotter statevector (2^20-2^22, <= 64 MB) with typicality and 20 orientations vs rate matrix, truncated Pauli and LCL; finite-difference Fisher information. < 1 day, < 2 GB. Track: E hybrid (B at N >= 100). Prior: low (highest mechanism quality in the physics lanes, gated by QM-21).

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0. The claim is only a formulation. The generic BQP-completeness of real-time Hamiltonian simulation covers worst-case engineered Hamiltonians and observables. It does not carry over to this instance family: infinite-temperature two-point z-magnetisation transport in a dense, disordered, dissipative 3D proton network (1UBQ has a median of 35 protons within 6 Å). For that family I know of no hardness result or query separation. The known structural results point toward classical simulability: dissipation-assisted operator evolution (DAOE) for hydrodynamic transport (Rakovszky et al., PRB 105, 075131, 2022), the polynomial-time classical algorithm for noisy dynamics (Schuster–Yin–Gao–Yao, arXiv:2407.12768), and the rigorous error bounds for state-space restriction when relaxation matches the experimental timescale (Karabanov–Kuprov et al., JCP 135, 2011, doi:10.1063/1.3624564). The speedup is "exponential in the coherently treated cluster size", but this applies only to a window that carries no long-range information (see the practical level).
verdicts.level_practical: L0. Usefulness under matched conditions has not been shown. My exploratory pilot (details under evidence) finds that the target quantity, a quantitative 5–8 Å distance, cannot be identified from the RFDR build-up with any forward model, exact or classical. The structural information that does exist is carried by relays of 4 Å or less. Even the crudest classical rate model's gap to the exact result shrinks with cluster size. Classical linear-scaling methods have been validated for spin diffusion: locally restricted LCL (LR-LCL) and spin dynamic mean-field theory (spinDMFT). Experimental routes that make the dynamics few-body also exist (selective recoupling, deuteration, 19F labelling). Finally, the quantum cost is about 1e14 T gates per likelihood.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument: Coherent many-body effects are real, and a naive classical treatment does fail on them. (a) In the repo's own static C1 v2 gate (research/results/RAW/nmr_gate/1UBQ_p19_N10_*), the best classical adversary, sparse Pauli dynamics with eps = 1e-4, fails at about 34 µs even with dephasing gamma = 1000–5000 s^-1. (b) In my pilot, the golden-rule rate matrix is still biased at N = 12: the median |inversion bias|/sd is 1.25, reaching 5.5 sd for one 7 Å pair. Also, 35% of the exact model's Fisher information on a rigid-residue shift is not captured by the rate derivative. So the pilot does NOT show that a rate model reaches the 3–5% criterion. (c) LR-LCL (Perras & Pruski 2019) was validated on rotating small-molecule solids, not on fully protonated proteins under RFDR at 100 kHz or more. spinDMFT (Gräßer, Uhrig & Ernst 2026) was validated only on static solids. The classical adequacy of these two methods for this exact instance family is therefore plausible but unverified. (d) Relayed build-ups do contain structural information (rigid-shift sd of 0.12–0.53 Å at N = 12 and sigma = 0.01), which a better forward model could extract. Why this still does not rescue a quantum advantage: the coherent regime where classical methods fail (tens of µs, strong couplings) holds almost no long-range signal. The 7 Å static coupling accumulates only about 0.1 rad of phase by 34 µs. The exact-versus-classical gap falls by about 2× for every 2 added spins. The remaining need is a better CLASSICAL relay model, not a quantum simulator.

LITERATURE ADVERSARY (verified via Crossref/arXiv/PubMed metadata on 2026-09-27; the web-search budget was exhausted):
(1) Low-order correlations in Liouville space (LCL): Butler, Dumez & Emsley, CPL 2009 (doi:10.1016/j.cplett.2009.07.017); Dumez, Butler & Emsley, JCP 133, 224501 (2010) (doi:10.1063/1.3505455).

(6) Tensor-train NMR at protein size: Savostyanov, Dolgov, Werner & Kuprov, PRB 90, 085139 (2014).
(7) Rate-model structure determination from proton spin diffusion: Suter & Ernst, PRB 32, 5608 (1985); Elena & Emsley, JACS 2005 (doi:10.1021/ja051208t); Elena et al., JACS 2006 (doi:10.1021/ja062353p). Solution-NMR analogue: the full-relaxation-matrix exact NOE (eNOE), Vögeli, PNMRS 78, 1 (2014).
(8) Dipolar truncation: Bayro et al., JCP 130, 114506 (2009).
(9) Experimental bypasses that make the dynamics few-body: Duong, Raran-Kurussi, Nishiyama & Agarwal, JPCL 9, 5948 (2018), quantitative 1H–1H distances in protonated solids by frequency-selective recoupling, and JMR 317, 106777 (2020); Jain et al., JPCL 8, 2399 (2017), selective H–H restraints in fully protonated proteins; Linser et al., JACS 133, 5905 (2011); Roos, Mandala & Hong, JPCB 122, 9302 (2018), long-range 19F–19F RFDR distances.

- Setup: 1UBQ with OpenMM hydrogens; an RFDR-like first-order average-Hamiltonian ZQ flip-flop, J_ij = 0.25·b_ij·sin2β·cosγ/√2; 12 powder orientations; quasi-static 400 Hz offsets standing in for the bath; exact U(1)-sector diagonalisation; closed nested clusters of N = 8/10/12 spins around 6 amide pairs at about 3, 5 and 7 Å; mixing 0–10 ms; noise sigma = 0.01.

  - median |bias|/sd: 3.0, 2.3, 1.25

verdicts.decisive_test:
An identifiability-first nested-cluster test, run on 1 core in about 2 hours with under 1 GB, extending rfdr_pilot2.py.
- Clusters: 1UBQ and GB1 (1PGA_H.pdb) pairs at 5, 6, 7 and 8 Å, with nested clusters of N = 8/10/12/14. N = 16 is done by typicality plus Krylov propagation.
- Hamiltonian: RFDR average Hamiltonian including finite-pulse ZQ terms and methyl-averaged couplings.
- Bath: both the quasi-static bath and a Lindblad bath.
- Quantity 1: the Fisher information from the direct coupling alone, giving sd(r_ab) at sigma = 0.01 and 0.02.
- Quantity 2: the Fisher-information gap and inversion bias between exact dynamics and the best classical panel as a function of N. The panel is LR-LCL at weight 4–6 with relaxation, a ZQ-lineshape rate matrix whose lineshapes come from exact sub-clusters of 6 spins or fewer, and spinDMFT if it is available.
KILL is confirmed if both hold:
- sd(r_ab) is above 1 Å for every r_ab of 5 Å or more. The pilot already gives 0.8–6.3 Å at N = 10, getting worse with N.
- The classical gap and bias/sd decrease monotonically with N. The pilot's crude rate model already shows 90% to 70% to 35% of the Fisher information missed, and bias/sd falling from 3.0 to 2.3 to 1.25.
Resurrection would need all three of the following:
- a regime where the direct 5–8 Å information gives sd below 0.3 Å at SNR 50;
- LR-LCL or spinDMFT bias above sd at N of 16 or more, not shrinking with N;
- a restraint-value curve showing backbone RMSD gains over binned contacts when an ESM prior is present.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note: Quantum cost per likelihood evaluation: a 100-spin patch with 10 ms mixing has λ ≈ 5e6 rad/s, so λt ≈ 5e4. With about 5e3 coupling terms that is about 1e9 T per circuit. Multiplying by 51 mixing times, 20 powder orientations and about 1e2 for Heisenberg-limited estimation to 0.01 gives about 1e14 T per likelihood (about 1e15 with plain shot sampling). At 1e4–1e6 logical T/s this is 1e8–1e10 s, years to centuries, per likelihood. A Bayesian inversion needs 1e4 or more likelihoods, and a quantum-generated surrogate training set of about 1e3 geometries needs about 1e11–1e13 s. On the classical side, LR-LCL scales linearly and the authors project that it reaches thousands of spins (Perras–Pruski 2019; I did not verify their wall-clock numbers). The rate matrix and spinDMFT take seconds to minutes on a CPU. There is no break-even at any accuracy gain. Even the most favourable case fails, because the quantity the quantum model would sharpen (direct 5–8 Å couplings) carries a Fisher information of about 0.03–4 at sigma = 0.01, i.e. sd(r) above about 0.5 Å even with a perfect model.
verdicts.novelty_note: The idea is anticipated by O'Brien et al. (PRX Quantum 2022; see the repo's research/discovery/NOVELTY_MEMOS.md, NM-1). For fast-MAS RFDR or proton spin diffusion in protonated proteins specifically, the search found no evidence of a proposal to use a quantum computer as the forward model. The scope of that search was Crossref, arXiv API and PubMed metadata queries on 2026-09-27; general web search was unavailable because the budget was exhausted. Both the classical NMR community (LCL, LR-LCL, first-principles PDSD, spinDMFT) and the experimental community (selective recoupling, deuteration, 19F labelling) have already attacked the same bottleneck without quantum hardware. The pilot's quantitative observation is new only as a datum, not as a mechanism: on 1UBQ, the direct 5–8 Å coupling contributes 5–14× less than sigma = 0.01 to RFDR build-ups, and falls further with cluster size. This quantifies the known dipolar-truncation and relay effect (Bayro 2009). It is worth recording in KILLBOOK as the reason for the kill: the gap is in information, not computation. Any residual forward-model need belongs to a classical research line.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 (formulation only). Estimating infinite-temperature two-point correlators Tr[Z_a(t)Z_b]/2^N to additive error is DQC1/BQP-hard only in the worst case and only conditionally (Knill-Laflamme 1998, cited from memory). No hardness result exists for secular dipolar dynamics on protein proton geometries under MAS with physical dephasing. Schuster et al., PRX 15, 041018 (2025), arXiv:2407.12768 (repo bibliography #381) gives a poly-time classical algorithm for average-case noisy circuits. It does not transfer directly, but it points the other way. One exact result cuts the claimed mechanism down (derived here and checked numerically on N=6): S_ab(t) = d_ab^2 t^2/4 + O(t^4). The t^2 coefficient was 0.4225 = d_ab^2/4 for 3 random draws of the other couplings at 5x the scale of d_ab. So distance information enters at leading order exactly pairwise (r^-6), and dipolar truncation and relay only appear at O(t^4) and higher. No query separation is stated for the actual task (distance inference).
verdicts.level_practical: L0. There is no hardware, no simulation and no matched-classical evidence. C1 (the static-oriented version of this family) is still running. Its only numbers are v1 pilots that the pre-registration excludes (research/results/PROCESSED/nmr_gate_summary.json). Resource accounting below puts one quantum forward evaluation at months (most optimistic) to 10^4-10^5 years (Babbush/Sanders 170 µs per Toffoli), before multiplying by the 10^3-10^4 evaluations an inversion or surrogate needs.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument: At ultrafast MAS (150 kHz or more) the local dipolar bath is quenched. The scaled long-range recoupled coupling (kappa*b_ab, about 0.06-0.5 kHz for 5-8 Å) can then approach the zero-quantum linewidth. In that regime golden-rule rate models, low-spin-order LCL and weight-truncated Pauli could all fail, with coherent relay through geminal pairs requiring N_coh > 30 coherently treated spins. There, exact classical cost grows as 2^N (at least 1e7-1e9 core-years at N=50 in my model) while quantum cost is poly(N t). Qubit counts are modest: about 1e5-5e5 physical qubits at p=1e-3 and d≈23-31. A surrogate architecture would amortise the cost. The excluded v1 pilot hints that weak adversaries fail early: weight-4 Pauli truncation failed at t_c = 20-100 µs with f_hard 0.8-1.0 at N=12-14. Rebuttal: that pilot is static, strongly coupled and ergodic, which is O'Brien's non-identifiable regime, and weight truncation is the weakest adversary. Even granting hardness, one forward evaluation costs at least about 0.1 QPU-year under the most favourable assumptions. The experiment it interprets takes days. Changing the experiment (perdeuteration plus sparse back-labelling, REDOR, or initial-rate mixing times) makes the dynamics classically exact for weeks of lab time.
verdicts.evidence:
RESOURCE MODEL (DERIVED; scripts in scratchpad qm19_resources.py and qm19_geom.py; geometry from data/instruments/nmr/{1UBQ,1PGA}_H.pdb):
(a) Geometry, measured on the 1UBQ/1PGA OpenMM protons (629 and 419 H). Mean neighbours: 35.6/31.0 within 6 Å, 77.2/66.1 within 8 Å, 135/112 within 10 Å. Resolving 8 Å transfer therefore needs z≈77 coupled partners per spin, not 45. The median per-spin second moment M2 has sqrt(M2) ≈ 27-28 kHz. Partners within 3 Å supply 89% of M2 and partners at 5-8 Å supply 1.5%. So b_ab/sqrt(M2) ≈ 0.008-0.04, the weak-coupling (golden-rule) regime.
(b) Per-shot Toffolis. Assumptions: 100 kHz MAS; Trotter slices per rotor period 10 (optimistic) or 25 (central; finite RFDR pulses); pair gates per step = N*min(z, N-1)/2; 2-3 arbitrary rotations per pair at 15-30 Toffolis each (phase-gradient, b≈30-40 bits for about 1e9 rotations). Results, central: 1.0e9 at N=30, 2.8e9 at N=50, 8.7e9 at N=100 and 1.7e10 at N=200 (10 ms mixing time). Optimistic: 6.5e7-5.4e8. A qubitisation cross-check (lambda*t ≈ 1e5 at N=100 and 5 ms, with about 2L Toffolis per walk step) gives about 2.4e9, the same order.
(c) Shots. For 5-8 Å the cross-peak is at most about 1/N ≈ 0.01-0.03, and the distance signal is about 10% of that, so the estimator needs ε ≈ 1e-3, i.e. 1e6 shots per mixing time. The shot floor is 1e4 even at ε=1e-2 (which carries no 5-8 Å information), or about 3e3 amplitude-estimation queries per correlator per orientation. Three costs are free under a sampling estimator: infinite-temperature state preparation (random basis state), the powder average (random rotor orientation per shot) and all N^2 correlators (one Z readout). Amplitude estimation loses all three, adding a 20-100x orientation multiplier or coherent angle arithmetic. Seven mixing times per build-up curve.
(d) Per forward evaluation (one geometry). Central: 2.8e15-4.9e16 Toffolis, i.e. 880-1.6e4 years at 10 µs per Toffoli and 1.5e4-2.7e5 years at 170 µs (Babbush et al. 2021, arXiv:2011.04149; Sanders et al. 2020, arXiv:2007.07391; both verified in repo bibliography #433/#434). Optimistic (1 µs, 3e4 shot-equivalents, 3 mixing times, 6 Å cutoff): 0.07-0.8 years.
(e) Surface code (p=1e-3, 1 µs cycle, logical failure below 1e-2 per shot): d = 21-31 and about 0.9e5-5.4e5 physical qubits. Qubits are not the binding constraint; time and shots are.
(f) Crossover with brute-force exact classical (typicality statevector, 1 trajectory, 20-50 orientations, 3 ns per amplitude-gate): N* ≈ 25 (optimistic), 32 (central) or 36 (170 µs). At N* the quantum cost is 0.07, 1e3 and 2e4 years per forward evaluation respectively. At the crossover both sides are infeasible, so the real competitor is approximate classical methods costing seconds to hours.
(g) Use multiplier: a Bayesian inversion or surrogate training set needs 1e3-1e4 forward evaluations. That is at least 1e2-8e3 QPU-years optimistic and 1e6-3e9 QPU-years under the Babbush/Sanders assumptions.
The candidate's own estimate (1e8 T per circuit x 1e4 shots) is low by about 2-3 orders: it uses ε=1e-2, z=45 and too few slices.
ORACLE AUDIT. The Hamiltonian angles are classical, O(Nz) per slice per orientation (about 1e8-1e9 angles per shot), so no hidden oracle. The model still needs data the coordinates do not give: every proton (methyl rotation, exchangeable HN/OH fraction, water, intermolecular packing protons), motional order parameters (S≈0.85 scales D by 15%, i.e. about 5% or 0.3 Å at 6 Å) and experimental chemical-shift assignments. These nuisances set a systematic floor at or above the 3-5% rate-model error the quantum model would remove. Condition-C analogue (INFERENCE, unverified): fast-MAS protonated-protein structures already reach about 1-2 Å backbone precision from binned restraints (Andreas et al. 2016). Existence of that paper was confirmed via a Faculty Opinions record; the details are unverified.
CLASSICAL ADVERSARY, verified via Crossref/arXiv today:
- Perras & Pruski, JCP 2019, DOI 10.1063/1.5099146, "Linear-scaling ab initio simulations of spin diffusion in rotating solids".
- Dumez et al., PCCP 2010, DOI 10.1039/c0cp00050g.
- Dumez & Emsley, PCCP 2011, DOI 10.1039/c1cp00004g: a master equation with rates W_ab ∝ b_ab^2 x F_ZQ(0), where the zero-quantum lineshape comes from small-cluster simulation. This is exactly the factorisation implied by (a).
- Halse et al., JMR 2015, DOI 10.1016/j.jmr.2015.02.016: spin diffusion constants of rotating solids.
- Gräßer, Uhrig & Ernst, arXiv:2512.15572: spinDMFT matches experimental zero-quantum lineshapes in static solids.
Suter & Ernst 1985 (PRB 32, 5608) is cited from memory and was not verified (HTTP 429).
verdicts.decisive_test:
Nested-cluster convergence plus golden-rule factorisation, under the fast-MAS effective Hamiltonian. Runtime about 1-2 h on 8 cores, under 1.5 GB, extending src/qapf/nmr/spins.py. It is labelled ORACLE because it uses native coordinates, and it is used only for forward-model physics.
Setup:
- Geometry: 1UBQ and 1PGA OpenMM protons, 12 probe pairs (a,b) at 5, 6, 7 and 8 Å, spread over secondary-structure types.
- Clusters: the N = 12, 16, 20 (and 24 if memory allows) protons nearest to either pair member.
- Hamiltonian: the time-independent first-order RFDR average Hamiltonian, i.e. ZQ flip-flops scaled by kappa ≈ 0.3, zero-quantum dipolar ZZ terms, and random chemical-shift offsets of about ±2 kHz.
- Dynamics: exact build-up S_ab(t) for 0.5-10 ms, by sector-restricted sparse Krylov (dim C(20,10) = 1.8e5), at γ = 0 and with T2' dephasing of 100-300 s^-1 via 20 unravellings at N ≤ 16.
Comparators:
- (i) The exact result at N-4.
- (ii) A Dumez-Emsley master equation with W_ab = kappa^2 b_ab^2 F_ZQ(0), where F_ZQ(0) comes from 8-spin local clusters, or is fitted only on geminal/sequential pairs (known covalent distances; no target distances used).
- (iii) The exact t^2/t^4 moment expansion.
Compute the finite-difference Fisher information on r_ab at σ = max cross-peak/50.
KILL (confirmed) if either holds:
- the exact curve converges, |S_N - S_{N-4}| < σ/3 by N=20 for at least 90% of pairs, so N_coh ≤ 20, far below the quantum/classical-exact crossover N* ≈ 25-36;
- or FI_rate/FI_exact ≥ 0.9 on 5-8 Å distances.
Reopen only if all three hold: no convergence by N=24, rate-model bias > σ with FI gain ≥ 10, and a compiled per-forward-evaluation cost at or below about 1e12 Toffolis (about 1e3 below the central estimate).
On paper the practical kill already holds. Even at 1 µs per Toffoli with Heisenberg-limited shots, a forward evaluation at N ≥ 30 costs at least 0.07 QPU-years, versus days of NMR acquisition and minutes to hours of classical inversion.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
The quantum forward model breaks even only if all three hold:
1. N_coh > N* ≈ 25-36 spins, the crossover with brute-force exact typicality simulation.
2. The best classical approximation is biased > σ/3 on 5-8 Å build-ups at mixing times ≤ 10 ms. The candidates are the Dumez-Emsley zero-quantum-lineshape master equation, Perras-Pruski low-rank LCL, spinDMFT and cluster embedding.
3. The matched-accuracy classical cost exceeds ρ x T_Q per forward evaluation (ρ = cost of one quantum-computer-second in core-seconds).
T_Q per forward evaluation at N=50:
| Scenario | Toffoli time | T_Q | Classical cost to beat (core-s, ρ=1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Optimistic (3e4 shot-equivalents) | 1 µs | 0.2 yr | 6e6 |
| Central (1e6 shots x 7 mixing times) | 10 µs | 2.5e3 yr | 8e10 |
| Babbush/Sanders | 170 µs | 4.2e4 yr | 1.3e12 |
Multiplying by the 1e3-1e4 forward evaluations needed for inversion or surrogate training gives at least 2e2 QPU-years (optimistic) to 4e8 QPU-years. Shots (ε ≈ 1e-3), not qubits, dominate: physical qubits stay at 1e5-5e5.
The leading build-up term, S_ab = d_ab^2 t^2/4, is exactly pairwise and classically free. So the quantum model only prices information in the higher-order (t^4 and beyond) coherent tail. Classical inversion can buy that information back with more scans in the initial-rate window, or with sparse labelling. The gain g is therefore a sample-complexity factor, not an exponential separation.
verdicts.novelty_note: Scope: repo bibliography and NOVELTY_MEMOS NM-1, plus arXiv API and Crossref queries on 2026-09-27; no general web search. Under that scope the search found no evidence of a fault-tolerant resource estimate for a fast-MAS 1H spin-diffusion/RFDR forward model. The static and oriented setting's cost scalings and its ergodicity versus learnability trade-off are due to O'Brien et al., PRX Quantum 3, 030345 (2022), arXiv:2109.02163. The application, the adversaries (Dumez-Emsley master equation, Perras-Pruski LR-LCL, spinDMFT, Pauli propagation) and the golden-rule factorisation are all prior art. At best QM-19 is an incremental MAS variant of O'Brien 2022. The resource audit above (shots dominate; N* ≈ 25-36; at least 0.07 QPU-year per forward evaluation) is new to this program, not a scientific novelty claim.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0. The formulation is sound, but there is no separation at the instance level. Real-time dipolar dynamics is BQP-complete only in the worst case. The observable here is an infinite-temperature 2-point z-magnetisation correlator in ergodic protein 1H networks, at millisecond mixing times. For that observable there is no hardness result, and no query or oracle model in which the quantum forward model provably wins. The one theory result that bears on it points against: O'Brien et al. (PRX Quantum 2022) found parameters become learnable only as the dynamics turn non-ergodic. L6 holds only for the generic worst case, not for the protein instance class.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. Nothing has been measured. The preregistered C1 gate (static, oriented, secular Hamiltonian, 320 us window) has no valid v2 results yet; the only processed file is the excluded N=12, gamma=3000 pilot. C1 also does not probe QM-19's regime (MAS/RFDR, powder, 1-10 ms mixing), which is more Markovian than C1's. A C1 kill carries over to QM-19 all the more; a C1 survival would not carry over.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The 5-8 A couplings sit deep in the perturbative, Markovian regime. The information they carry enters only through golden-rule rates, which are cheap to compute classically.

1. Paper calculation on the repo's OpenMM-protonated structures:
   - 1UBQ_H has 629 1H. The median amide H has 39 protons within 6 A, 81 within 8 A, and 58 in the 5-8 A shell.
   - The local strong-coupling width, sqrt(M2), has a median of 19 kHz; 1PGA gives 18.7 kHz.
   - Define kappa = b_ij / sqrt(M2_i + M2_j) for all 3555 amide-H pairs at 5-8 A (|dres| >= 2). Median kappa is 0.020, 0.012 and 0.008 in the 5-6, 6-7 and 7-8 A bins; the maximum is 0.046. GB1: 2364 pairs, maximum 0.039.
   - RFDR scales strong and weak couplings by the same factor, so kappa survives recoupling to first order. Chemical-shift offsets broaden the zero-quantum (ZQ) line further and only lower kappa.
   - With kappa <= 0.05, direct transfer goes as k_ij ~ b_ij^2 * J_ZQ(0), with corrections of order kappa^2 (about 1e-3 or less).
   - The only non-trivial quantity is J_ZQ(0). It is a local property: the median amide H has 5 protons within 3 A, so the cluster is about 6-16 spins and can be simulated exactly, with CCE-2/3, or with spinDMFT.
   - Relayed transfer is incoherent and fits a rate matrix, LCL or LR-LCL, all of which scale linearly.
   - Expected consequence: the exact model's Fisher information on r_ij exceeds the rate model's by O(kappa^2), about 1%, well under the 10% kill threshold.

2. Sixth-root compression. With k proportional to r^-6, a 20% rate-model error is a 3.3% distance error, about 0.23 A at 7 A. With coherent build-up proportional to b, it is 6.7%.
   - Systematic experimental errors dominate that budget. The ones below are not quantified here and are dynamics, not computation: motional order parameters (S^2 about 0.8-0.9 on couplings, unverified), methyl and ring-flip averaging, T1rho heterogeneity, RF inhomogeneity, peak overlap, and long-range cross-peak SNR often well below 50.
   - Dipolar truncation is physical signal suppression. A perfect forward model cannot recover information that is not in the data.

3. Restraint value likely saturates. Andreas et al. PNAS 2016 solved a fully protonated 28 kDa capsid dimer from binned 1H-1H upper bounds. Sparse or qualitative restraints plus a strong prior already give backbone accuracy (CS-Rosetta, Raman et al. Science 2010; CASP14 NMR/AF2 assessment; both unverified here). This is the condition-C analogue.

4. Cost. The proposal's own figure is about 1e11-1e14 T per likelihood. With 1e4-1e6 shots at 1e-3 absolute precision, 20 powder orientations and 10-20 mixing times, it is about 1e13-1e16 T per patch. At the roughly 1e4-1e5 T/s that Babbush et al. 2021 assume for early fault-tolerant machines, that is 1e8 s or more per patch likelihood. LR-LCL takes CPU-minutes.

5. Experiment-design bypass. Frequency-selective or band-selective recoupling isolates effectively two-spin transfer and makes the dynamics classical by design: Duong-type JPCL 2018, 10.1021/acs.jpclett.8b02189 (title verified); Potnuru JMR 2021.
verdicts.evidence:
Protein relevance: real, but a niche, and only indirectly tied to the mission.
- The target computation is genuine: integrative structure determination from 1H-detected >=100 kHz MAS data on protonated proteins (fibrils, membrane proteins, capsids, systems where deuteration is impractical). Andreas et al. PNAS 2016, 10.1073/pnas.1602248113 (Crossref-verified), used binned RFDR upper bounds. Mustapha et al. J Biomol NMR 2025, 10.1007/s10858-025-00477-8 (verified), measured CO-H contacts to about 6 A at 105 kHz and reported dipolar truncation in CA experiments. Jain et al. JPCL 2017, 10.1021/acs.jpclett.7b00983 (verified), gave selective 1H-1H restraints.
- Sizes are realistic. My neighbour counts on the repo PDBs say a 5-8 A probe pair plus the first shells of both ends needs 80-150 spins. That is far beyond exact classical simulation, far below exact limits for a quantum computer, and it confirms the proposal's 30-200-spin patches.
- The tie to the mission is indirect. The data already exist and are already used as bounds. The quantum part would only turn bounds into values for 5-8 A pairs.

Prior-evidence audit.
- H-001 / DNR-02 does not apply: the dynamics are non-diagonal and not read out by argmin.
- DNR-09 is lifted: the space is 2^N physical spins and grows with protein size.
- DNR-16 / K-012 are satisfied: the information comes from new experimental data.
- The DNR-10 analogue (a measured classical failure is required) is unmet.
- The condition-C analogue is live and unmeasured.
- The T5 quadratic ceiling does not apply; this is one of the few lanes that could be exponential.
- The literature phase rated it P2 "WEAK curiosity" (lit_F_claims.md).
- NM-1 already states that QM-19/20/21 is at most an incremental extension of O'Brien 2022.

Nearest prior art, quantum side:
- O'Brien, Ioffe, Su et al., PRX Quantum 3, 030345 (2022), arXiv:2109.02163 (verified): ubiquitin, static or oriented, 8- and 60-spin clusters, learnability only when non-ergodic.
- Zhang, Cortinas, Karamlou et al., arXiv:2510.19550 (2025) (verified in lit phase): liquid-crystal small molecules; self-declared not beyond classical.
- Seetharam et al., arXiv:2109.13298 (verified).
- Sels, Dashti, Mora, Demler, Demler, Nat. Mach. Intell. (2020), 10.1038/s42256-020-0198-x, arXiv:1910.14221 (verified).

Classical adversaries:
- Butler, Dumez, Emsley, CPL 2009, 10.1016/j.cplett.2009.07.017 (LCL; verified).
- Perras et al., JCP 2019, 10.1063/1.5099146, "Linear-scaling ab initio simulations of spin diffusion in rotating solids" (verified).
- Veshtort and Griffin, JCP 2011, 10.1063/1.3635374 (proton-driven spin diffusion; verified).
- Grasser, Uhrig, Ernst, arXiv:2512.15572 (2026), spinDMFT spin diffusion in static solids (verified); Grasser et al., arXiv:2107.07821 (verified).

- Fratus et al., arXiv:2508.06448 (verified in NM-1).

Unverified this session: Dumez 2010 (experimental reproduction), Suter-Ernst ZQ-lineshape theory (PRB 1985), Bayro et al. 2009 on dipolar truncation, Raman 2010, the CASP14 NMR assessment.

Derivation: the kappa-map (numbers under the counterargument) was computed by a numpy script over data/instruments/nmr/1UBQ_H.pdb and 1PGA_H.pdb. It uses static couplings as a proxy: b = 120.1 kHz * A^3 / r^3, and isotropic geometric factors cancel in the ratio.
verdicts.decisive_test:
This is a two-stage test, all on CPU, in under a day, using under 2 GB.

Stage (a): kill on hardness. The kappa-map predicts rate-model error below 1%; stage (a) confirms that numerically.
- Setup: exact sector-resolved statevector at N = 16/20/22. The Hamiltonian is the RFDR average-Hamiltonian ZQ flip-flop plus isotropic 1H shift offsets, 20 powder orientations, mixing 0.5-10 ms. Probe pairs at 5 and 7 A on 1UBQ_H/1PGA_H (ORACLE/analysis use only).
- Comparator: a rate matrix whose pair rates b_ij^2 * J_ZQ(0) come from exact local clusters of 12 spins or fewer, plus LCL.
- Kill if: the distance bias after inversion is below sigma at SNR 50, and the Fisher information gain of exact over rate is below 10%, and both stay flat in N.

Stage (b): kill on relevance, independent of hardness. Build a restraint-value curve.
- Setup: the vendored A80 decoder with the esmprior_v1 energy, on 1PGA (56 aa) and long40 targets, ORACLE-labelled. Add the observable 5-8 A 1H-1H restraints either as binned upper bounds or as exact distances with 0.3 A noise.
- Kill if: backbone RMSD improves by less than max(0.3 A, S33's MDE).

Stage (b) alone can settle the lane in hours.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Using the proposal's per-circuit figure of about 1e8 T, one patch likelihood costs:

- 1e4-1e6 shots (1e-3 absolute precision on cross-peaks of about 0.05)
- x 20 orientations
- x 10-20 mixing times
- = about 1e13-1e16 T.

At the roughly 1e4-1e5 T/s assumed for early fault tolerance (Babbush et al. 2021), that is 1e8-1e12 s per patch likelihood, and ubiquitin needs about 70 amide probes. LR-LCL or a rate matrix takes CPU-minutes for the whole protein.

For the quantum model to be worth building, classical methods would have to fail at the level of the distance error itself, not merely at the level of the build-up curve. Sixth-root compression means even a 20% rate error is only about 0.23 A at 7 A. The only conceivable role is producing a handful of validation labels for a classical surrogate. Since kappa is 0.05 or less, even that is expected to show the classical rate model already exact to O(kappa^2).
verdicts.novelty_note:
The scope was:
- arXiv API abstract searches: MAS ∧ (quantum computer, quantum algorithm, quantum simulation, qubits); protein ∧ NMR ∧ quantum computing or advantage; spinDMFT and spin diffusion.
- Crossref queries on fast-MAS 1H-1H distances in protonated proteins and on linear-scaling spin-diffusion methods.
- Project notes NM-1 and lit_F.
- General web search was unavailable (the session budget was exhausted).

Under that scope, the search found no evidence of any proposal to use quantum simulation of MAS/RFDR 1H spin-diffusion build-ups in protonated proteins to extract quantitative 5-8 A distances. The MAS, time-dependent, powder-averaged framing is therefore new relative to O'Brien 2022, which covered static or oriented ubiquitin. It is a variant of the same idea, not a new mechanism, and any write-up must credit O'Brien 2022 as the origin.

The classical side is the mature literature: LCL, LR-LCL, spinDMFT, tensor-train, CCE and selective recoupling. It targets exactly this regime, and none of it reports a failure for this observable.

Recommendation: fold QM-19 into Program C as a sub-case with no separate compute, and run stage (b) before any MAS spin-dynamics code is written.

title: Protein-scale many-body echo (OTOC / Loschmidt / multiple-quantum) NMR with a quantum-simulated forward model, and the shot-noise cost of consuming a quantum-estimated likelihood in posterior MCMC
merged_from: physics P2 (OTOC/MQC echo experiments interpreted with a quantum forward model), physics P12 (posterior sampling with a quantum-estimated NMR likelihood: pseudo-marginal / penalty / delayed acceptance cost model)
summary: Q: can time-reversal echo experiments on 13C-labelled oriented, microcrystalline or MAS-recoupled proteins report geometry of protons 6-12 A from a labelled 'butterfly' site (e.g. to discriminate domain packings or rotamer arrangements in 60-150 aa proteins), when the only adequate interpreter is quantum simulation, and can that likelihood be consumed in Bayesian structure inference at acceptable cost? Quantum: forward/backward Hamiltonian simulation estimating F(t) = Tr[W(t) V W(t) V]/2^N (scaling Zhang et al. 2025, Willow, 8 and 14 H, to 50-200 qubits); Hamiltonian-simulation expectation values as a noisy likelihood inside pseudo-marginal / Ceperley-Dewing penalty / delayed-acceptance MCMC. Mechanism: OTOC sensitivity F ~ 1 - ||[W(t),V]||^2/2 amplifies weak distant couplings that pairwise experiments truncate; in the scrambling regime the number of sign-alternating Pauli strings grows exponentially and truncated Pauli propagation and TN-BP fail (Google OTOC(2), Bermejo et al. 2026): the one physics card with established classical hardness for a closely related observable. Tensions: late-time dipolar dynamics is universal and loses microscopic detail (Li et al. Nat. Phys. 2024); learnability improves as ergodicity drops (O'Brien et al. 2022), the classically easier side; protein motions add Lindblad relaxation that makes Pauli propagation easier (Schuster et al. 2025); solution weak alignment is too slow vs T2. Consumption cost (P12): Var(log L-hat) ~ K/(sigma^2 M) must be O(1), so M >~ K/sigma^2 shots per datum per MCMC step (1e7 for K = 1e3, sigma = 0.01; ~sqrt(K)/sigma ~ 3e3 with AE). At ~3e8-1e9 T per circuit and >= 1e3-1e4 steps per effective sample, >= 1e18 T per posterior sample; delayed acceptance with a classical LR-LCL first stage saves only a constant. The only viable form is an offline emulator trained on 1e2-1e3 quantum evaluations ('trainable implies surrogate'). S32's P1 (growing decision space) and P2 (stochastic energy) are both met, but P2 is a cost, not a resource. Speedup: exponential in cluster size if a hard AND identifiable window exists; practically ~1e12-1e14 T per likelihood, usable only to fit <= 10 geometric parameters. Competitor: exact statevector to ~30-35 spins, sparse/average-case Pauli propagation, noisy Pauli-path bounds, spinDMFT; skipping OTOCs for sparse labelling + DARR/PAR/REDOR, PREs, cryo-EM, AF2; classical approximate-likelihood HMC/PT/SMC and neural simulation-based inference. Info vs comp: new per-target echo data; load-bearing only if (i) echoes carry geometry beyond pairwise experiments and (ii) extraction needs operators beyond classical truncation. S29-S33: formally satisfies S32's P1 condition; OLD FAILURE that transfers is 'apparent wins vanish under stronger classical controls' (Zhang et al. logged as F34 'no advantage, self-declared'). Kill: < 10% of Fisher information on long-range parameters lies where weight-<=8 Pauli propagation deviates beyond noise; OR T1rho/T2' of 1-10 ms ends coherence before operator weight ~10-12; OR powder averaging drops structure contrast below SNR 50; OR M_min x circuit cost > 1e12 T per effective sample at K >= 100; OR swapping in a classical approximate likelihood shifts the posterior mean by < 0.1 A or < posterior sd. Test: P1 clusters plus a 13C butterfly and 2-3 remote protons at 6-10 A, one crystal + 20-orientation powder, Lindblad trajectories at T1rho = 1/3/10 ms, Fisher information for a remote distance, 1 A helix shift and chi1 swap, Pauli weights 4/6/8; separately, long40 penalty-method / pseudo-marginal HMC with a synthetic K = 50-500 likelihood and shot-noise grid M = 1e2-1e8 (ORACLE-labelled synthetic data). < 1 day each. Track: E hybrid (B at scale). Prior: low (best card of the physics lane).
dead_reason: Non-diagonal dynamics with new experimental information; outside all existing kills.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 (formulation only). No separation has been shown for secular-dipolar echo dynamics on protein geometries. The only related classical-hardness evidence is Google's off-diagonal OTOC(2) on 2D random circuits (arXiv:2506.10191; 2604.15427). That paper says the first-order OTOC is "sometimes well-approximated by combining exact wave-function evolution and Monte-Carlo simulation that ignores the effects of small interference loops". QM-20's observable F = Tr[W(t)VW(t)V]/2^N is that first-order OTOC. Worst-case BQP-completeness of local Hamiltonian simulation does not transfer to this instance family, which is decoherence-bounded, echo-limited and orientation-averaged. Schuster, Yin, Gao and Yao (arXiv:2407.12768) and Schuster and Yao (arXiv:2208.12272) show that noise and dissipation suppress exactly the high-weight, non-local components that would carry any hardness.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. Nothing reaches L1 under matched conditions on proteins. The only hardware pipeline (Zhang et al., arXiv:2510.19550) used 9 and 15 qubits, checked against exact 2^15 classical simulation, and is self-declared "not yet beyond classical". Its structural precision equalled independent spectroscopy (toluene ortho-meta distance 2.47±0.01 Å vs reference 2.46±0.01 Å). Consuming a quantum likelihood inside MCMC misses the card's own kill threshold by 3–7 orders of magnitude (derivation in break_even_or_cost_note).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
This is the best case for the quantum side, stated honestly.

(1) The forward model really does look hard for naive classical truncation. A dense protonated protein has about 0.055 ¹H/Å³, which is about 50 / 118 / 230 / 398 protons within 6 / 8 / 10 / 12 Å of the labelled site. For the OTOC to see a proton 6–12 Å away, the operator front must cover that ball, so the relevant Pauli weights are about 50–400. That is far beyond exact statevector (about 30–35 spins), weight-8 Pauli propagation or tensor-network belief propagation. This repo's own v1 pilot on 1UBQ (N = 12/14; excluded from C1 for instrument reasons) already shows weight-≤4 Pauli failing at t_c = 20 µs with frac_hard ≈ 1.

(2) The usual cluster adversary is known to break here. Ryan and Lunghi (arXiv:2602.14613, 2026) show that standard generalised CCE is "insufficient for providing even a qualitatively accurate description" of dipolar spin–spin relaxation. So CCE is not a safe adversary for dense homonuclear ¹H baths.

(3) The mean-field adversaries are unvalidated for this observable. spinDMFT, classical-spin and hybrid methods are validated on FIDs, Hahn echoes and spin diffusion, not on site-resolved 4-point OTOCs. A mean-field embedding could wash out exactly the site-specific geometry the experiment targets.

(4) Google's own team estimates that OTOC-based measurements could reach 20–60 Å (arXiv:2510.19550, an estimate, not a demonstration).

(5) An OTOC(2) variant might inherit the large-loop constructive-interference hardness from arXiv:2506.10191.

(6) The OTOC route needs only a ¹³C isotope label and the native ¹H network. The classical bypass experiments need ¹⁹F or paramagnetic tags, which can perturb the structure.

Rebuttal, which is why the verdict is still KILL:
- (a) Hardness is not value. The Loschmidt echo in many-spin dipolar solids decays in a perturbation-independent way with T3 ~ T2, set by the local second moment (Sánchez, Cappellaro, Pastawski et al., arXiv:1902.06628). The reversible window is therefore only a few 1/√M2 long, and a remote coupling's direct imprint within it is scale-invariant at about (r_local/r_remote)³, roughly 0.005–0.09 rad. Remote-geometry contrast must travel through the whole network. That makes it information about coarse network density, the degenerate, ergodic-regime information O'Brien et al. found (PRX Quantum 3, 030345), and exactly what spinDMFT and classical-spin models capture best.
- (b) Tagged, classically interpretable experiments already deliver the target 6–16 Å information with two-spin forward models.
- (c) Consuming the quantum likelihood is unaffordable at any plausible early fault-tolerant T-rate.
verdicts.evidence:
WebSearch budget was exhausted this session. Items were verified through the arXiv API and PubMed E-utilities.

INFORMATION BYPASS (strongest adversary: the target information needs no quantum interpreter)
- Roos et al., J Phys Chem B 2018, doi:10.1021/acs.jpcb.8b00310: ¹⁹F–¹⁹F spin exchange under fast MAS gives distances "up to 1.6 nm".
- Shcherbakov & Hong, J Phys Chem B 2019, doi:10.1021/acs.jpcb.9b03812: ¹H-detected ¹H–¹⁹F HSQC-REDOR "up to ~15 Å".
- Roos et al. 2018, doi:10.1021/acs.jpcb.8b06878: ¹⁹F RFDR to about 1 nm.
- Hong, Acc Chem Res 2013, doi:10.1021/ar300294x: 15–20 Å.
- Shcherbakov et al., Chem Rev 2022, doi:10.1021/acs.chemrev.1c00662: 1–2 nm by solid-state NMR.
- Standard knowledge, not re-verified this session: PRE to about 25 Å; DEER 1.5–8 nm.
- All of these use pairwise or few-spin forward models that are classically trivial.
- Quantum necessity test: FULL (OTOC + quantum interpreter) vs ABLATION (¹⁹F/PRE/DEER restraints + classical interpreter + AF2/cryo-EM). Domain-packing and rotamer discrimination at 60–150 aa survives the ablation, so the quantum component is not load-bearing.

HARDNESS DOES NOT TRANSFER
- Google, arXiv:2506.10191 (Nature 646, 825, 2025). Quote: "For OTOC, we find that it is sometimes well-approximated by combining exact wave-function evolution and Monte-Carlo simulation that ignores the effects of small interference loops." The advantage claim is for off-diagonal OTOC(2); cached Monte Carlo matched experiment at 40 qubits.
- Zhang et al., arXiv:2510.19550 measures first-order OTOC C(t) = Tr[X_C13(t) B X_C13(t) B†] on 9- and 15-spin molecules, all within exact classical reach. They say 50-spin systems need 10^5–10^6 gates.

ECHO WINDOW AND DECOHERENCE BOUND THE USABLE OPERATOR SIZE
- Sánchez et al., arXiv:1902.06628: "LE decay rate only depends on the interactions themselves, T3 ~ T2, and not on the perturbation."
- Domínguez & Álvarez, PRA 104, 062406 (2021), arXiv:2107.03870: decoherence induces a localization cluster size for observable scrambling; a classical model fits more than 10^4-spin NMR data quantitatively.
- Lozano-Negro et al., arXiv:2407.03273: local OTOCs determine global ones.
- Schuster & Yao, arXiv:2208.12272 and Schuster, Yin, Gao & Yao, arXiv:2407.12768: noise damps non-local correlations, giving polynomial-time classical simulation on average.

CLASSICAL FORWARD-MODEL ADVERSARIES (strongest in dense, high-coordination networks, which is the protein ¹H case)
- spinDMFT: Gräßer et al., arXiv:2107.07821.
- nl-spinDMFT, arXiv:2403.10465: the adamantane Hahn echo "agrees excellently … without further fitting".
- arXiv:2512.15572: static-solid spin diffusion shows an "excellent match with published experimental data". Its only prerequisite is that "each spin interacts with a large number of other spins".
- Cluster spinDMFT (CspinDMFT), arXiv:2307.14188.
- Elsayed & Fine, PRB 91, 094424 (2015): classical spins are quantitative for many 3D lattices.
- Starkov & Fine, PRB 98, 214421 (2018): hybrid quantum core embedded in classical spins, accurate in 1D, 2D and 3D, with a built-in error estimate from varying the core size.
- Navez, Starkov & Fine, arXiv:1812.02155: classical spins degrade only below about 4 interacting neighbours. A protonated protein has about 27 protons within 4.9 Å.
- Begušić & Chan, arXiv:2409.03097: sparse Pauli dynamics in 3D.
- Fratus et al., arXiv:2508.06448: cluster approximation with linear scaling for NMR spectra.
- Gap, stated explicitly: none of these has been validated on site-resolved OTOCs. This is an unverified adversary.

IDENTIFIABILITY
- O'Brien et al., PRX Quantum 3, 030345 (2022), arXiv:2109.02163: in the ergodic, classically hard regime the Hessian of the ubiquitin learning cost is degenerate; the Hamiltonian becomes learnable only in the non-ergodic regime.

DERIVATION (dipolar constants 120.1 kHz·Å³ for ¹H–¹H and 30.2 kHz·Å³ for ¹³C–¹H)

| Distance | ¹³C–¹H | ¹H–¹H |
|---|---|---|
| 6 Å | 140 Hz | 556 Hz |
| 8 Å | 59 Hz | 235 Hz |
| 10 Å | 30 Hz | 120 Hz |
| 12 Å | 17 Hz | 70 Hz |

- Local ¹H couplings are 15–20 kHz at about 2 Å.
- Phase imprinted by the direct remote coupling in a 50–100 µs reversible window: ¹³C–¹H 0.044–0.088 rad at 6 Å and 0.005–0.011 rad at 12 Å; ¹H–¹H 0.02–0.35 rad over the same range. These values are comparable to σ = 0.01.
- Scaling the couplings (MAS, recoupling) does not help, because T3 tracks T2.

CONSUMPTION
- Pseudo-marginal and penalty methods need Var(log L̂) = O(1) (Doucet et al., arXiv:1210.1871; the optimum SD of about 1.0–1.7 is quoted from memory and not re-verified).
- Walch et al., arXiv:2609.20406 find that shot counts grow only weakly with molecule size. That concerns spectrum accuracy, not MCMC consumption, so it does not rescue this card.

NOT VERIFIED THIS SESSION
- Li et al., Nat Phys 2024 (universality).
- Any spinDMFT or hybrid-method OTOC paper.
- Any classical rebuttal of arXiv:2510.19550. The arXiv-API search for "quantum echoes", OTOC ∧ Pauli path/propagation, and OTOC ∧ molecular geometry returned only Google-affiliated papers.
verdicts.decisive_test:
The derivation below already decides the practical question: the card's own kill criterion 4 fires on paper (see break_even_or_cost_note).

For the remaining forward-model value question, the cheapest decisive computation (about 2–3 h on 6 cores under the governor, reusing src/qapf/nmr/spins.py) is a FULL-vs-ABLATION posterior-shift test.

Setup
- Protein and site: 1UBQ with OpenMM hydrogens. Put a ¹³C label on a buried Ile/Leu/Val methyl or on Cα.
- Cluster: N = 18–20 spins, meaning the ¹³C plus its nearest ¹H, forcibly including 2–3 protons at 6–10 Å.
- Hamiltonian: static secular dipolar, dt = 1 µs.
- Observable: first-order OTOC F(t) with the butterfly V on each remote proton. Forward and backward evolution to 100–200 µs.
- Decay: a non-reverted perturbation (5–20% of H) calibrated so that T3 ≈ T2, which is the perturbation-independent-decay mechanism and not just Lindblad damping. Add T1ρ ∈ {1, 3, 10} ms.
- Orientations: one crystal orientation plus a 20-orientation powder.
- Parameters: remote distance r, a 1 Å helix shift, and a χ1 swap.
- Data: synthetic ORACLE-labelled, σ = 0.01, K = 100.

Likelihoods
- FULL: exact 2^20 statevector with typicality, about 2–3 min per trajectory, about 300 trajectories.
- ABLATION: the best of four classical adversaries:
  1. Starkov–Fine hybrid (a 10–12-spin quantum core embedded in classical spins; not yet implemented in the repo; the novelty memo lists it as an open adversary);
  2. classical-spin decorrelator;
  3. sparse Pauli dynamics at ε = 1e-4 with dissipation;
  4. weight-≤8 Pauli propagation.

Readout: posterior under each likelihood (Laplace approximation or HMC).

KILL (confirming) if either holds:
- |Δ posterior mean| < max(0.1 Å, posterior sd) for all three parameters; or
- the OTOC's Fisher information for r inside t ≤ 3·T3 is below that of a two-spin ¹H–¹⁹F REDOR model for the same distance at matched data count.

ESCALATE only if both hold:
- the ablation shifts the posterior by more than 1 sd; and
- the OTOC's Fisher information exceeds the REDOR model's.

Even then, the consumption cost below applies.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
DERIVED; the T-gate throughput is an assumption.

Circuit cost for N = 100, which is the ¹³C plus about 99 ¹H inside about 7.5 Å:
- z ≈ 27 couplings per spin above 1 kHz (r < 4.9 Å), so N·z/2 = 1,350 pair terms.
- dt ≈ 0.8 µs for first-order Trotter against 20 kHz couplings, giving 125 steps forward and 125 backward.
- About 100 T per pair gate from rotation synthesis.
- Total about 3.4e7 T per OTOC circuit, so the card's 3e8–1e9 is pessimistic by about 10×.

One likelihood evaluation (K = 100, σ = 0.01):
- Direct sampling: 1e6 circuits, about 3.4e13 T.
- Amplitude estimation: about 1.6e4 circuit-equivalents, about 5e11 T.

Pseudo-marginal MCMC (per-datum precision σ/√K):
- Sampling: 3.4e15 T per evaluation.
- Amplitude estimation: 5e12 T per evaluation.
- At ≥1e3–1e4 steps per effective sample: ≥5e15–5e16 T (amplitude estimation) to 3e18–3e19 T (sampling). That is 3.7–7.5 orders of magnitude over the card's 1e12 T kill threshold. Delayed acceptance saves only a constant.

The only surviving form is an offline emulator or importance reweighting that uses 1e2–1e3 quantum evaluations:
- Cost: 5e13–5e14 T.
- At an assumed early fault-tolerant throughput of 1e5 T/s, that is about 17–170 years; at 1e7 T/s, about 0.2–1.7 years.
- The classical comparators (spinDMFT, classical-spin or hybrid runs, and two-spin REDOR/¹⁹F models) cost CPU-minutes to hours per structure, a gap of at least 1e6 in wall-clock.

At that point the quantum output is at most 1e3 scalars feeding a ≤10-parameter emulator: "trainable implies surrogate", the same pattern as a≡mu in S29–S33.
verdicts.novelty_note:
Both the idea and the pipeline predate this card: O'Brien et al. 2022 (PRX Quantum 3, 030345), protein ¹H dipolar learning on ubiquitin, and Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.19550), NMR OTOCs interpreted on Willow.

The search found no paper that does either of the following:
- prices pseudo-marginal or penalty-method consumption of a quantum-estimated NMR likelihood for structure inference; or
- tests site-resolved OTOCs against spinDMFT or hybrid quantum-classical adversaries.

Search scope: arXiv API title/abstract queries plus PubMed E-utilities on 2026-09-27; general WebSearch was unavailable (budget exhausted). verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The emulator route escapes the MCMC-consumption kill because its cost is a one-off design cost, not a per-step cost. Suppose protein 1H OTOCs at N >= 50 spins have an identifiable window in which every classical approximation fails (weight-w Pauli propagation, sparse Pauli dynamics, sub-cluster/CCE, classical spins with and without the Fine two-spin correction, spinDMFT). Then the forward-model separation is exponential, not quadratic. That is the only card in the programme where this is conceivable, and exact classical simulation stops near N ~ 45 (a 2^45 statevector is about 0.56 PB).

At the forward-model level the break-even is not astronomical. One forward evaluation (N=100, t=1 ms, K=100, eps=sigma/2) costs about 4.2e12 Toffoli: 48 QPU-days at 1 us/Toffoli, or 22.5 QPU-years at 170 us. A weight-10 or larger Pauli propagation over 100 spins could plausibly cost more than that. If the hard window is also the only source of some structurally relevant parameter (singular easy-window Fisher matrix), a quantum forward model would be load-bearing in principle. A fleet of about 100 fast (1 us) fault-tolerant machines would finish a 10-parameter local fit in weeks.

Why this does not rescue the card:
1. Hardness and identifiability squeeze each other. Direct 13C-1H couplings at 6/8/10/12 A are only 140/59/30/17 Hz, while the measured 1H local-field rms is 9.5-12.8 kHz, so 1H flip-flops self-decouple the distant protons. Exposing those couplings requires 1H-1H decoupling (LG/FSLG), which leaves a commuting ZZ central-spin model that is classically solvable in closed form. Keeping the flip-flops means scrambling, which by O'Brien et al. 2022 and Li et al. 2024 means degenerate, universal information.
2. The forward model assumes a free, validated Hamiltonian. It needs all 3N coordinates plus the nuisance terms: 1H shift offsets of 0.6-6 kHz (larger than the target couplings), methyl/aromatic motional scaling (S^2 0.3-0.9), and 1-3% errors in the echo-reversal sequence. The OTOC amplifies nuisance errors exactly as it amplifies signal.
3. The same <= 10 geometric parameters are available from experiments with classical interpreters: PRE (10-25 A), CHHC/PAR/REDOR (6-8 A), RDCs, sparse labelling and AF2.

title: Hardness-identifiability trade-off theorem for spin-dynamics structure learning (the physics-lane analogue of H-001) - gate for the whole quantum-NMR family
merged_from: physics P3 (hardness-identifiability trade-off theorem)
summary: Q: does any NMR observable of a protein-like dipolar network have a classically hard exact forward simulation whose hard component carries Fisher information about geometry beyond classically simulable observables? Decides QM-19, QM-20 and the spin variants of QM-22 together. Quantum: none built; the object is BQP Hamiltonian simulation / DQC1 traces vs classical truncated Pauli/Liouville propagation under dissipation. Mechanism: dO(t)/dD_ij = i * integral_0^t Tr(rho [h_ij(s), O(t)]) ds, so sensitivity to a distant coupling is itself an OTOC-type commutator, non-zero only once the Heisenberg operator has spread onto the pair. Claims to prove or refute: (C3-a) with per-spin-order relaxation gamma, weight > w components are damped ~exp(-gamma w t), so FI_hard <= FI_total exp(-2 gamma w t) + truncation error (cf. Schuster et al. noisy Pauli paths); (C3-b) in the ergodic regime sensitivity to any single coupling self-averages over exponentially many paths (universality); (C3-c) Fisher information concentrates near the ergodic edge, where localisation makes classical simulation easier. If all hold, the quantum-unlockable Fisher information is bounded by f(gamma/J, graph) x classical Fisher information: a structural negative result for the family. Speedup: none (gate); a positive region would imply exponential simulation. Oracle: not applicable (explicit Hamiltonians, high-temperature state). Competitor: noisy Pauli-path simulation, average-case Pauli propagation, LR-LCL, spinDMFT, exact small clusters + cluster-expansion corrections. Info vs comp: Fisher information measures whether information exists in the data; operator weight / retained Pauli strings measure the classical cost of extracting it; quantum adds value only on their product. S29-S33: H-001 says nothing about non-commuting dynamics; this extends the generalised reduction theorem (QM-06) to the physics lane. Kill (family): FI_hard/FI_total < 0.1 for all realistic gamma/J (T1rho/T2' 1-10 ms vs 0.2-20 kHz couplings) on protein 1H networks; equivalently FI_w >= 0.9 FI_exact at w <= 6. Promote QM-20 if FI_hard/FI_total > 0.3 at weight > 12 with > 1e7 retained strings. Test: 50 random 12-20-spin clusters from 1UBQ/GB1 (OpenMM hydrogens); exact Heisenberg evolution with typicality for autocorrelation, cross-transfer and OTOC at gamma/J in {0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1}; Fisher information for ~10 geometric parameters and FI_w from Pauli propagation truncated at w = 2-10 with string counts. <= 1 day. Track: C theory/query. Prior: low for a positive region; very high decision value, cheapest decisive gate in the physics lanes.

- Static or dilute-probe spin diffusion and FID: spinDMFT and nl-spinDMFT, plus hybrid quantum-cluster and classical-spin methods.
- Ensemble FID late times: a few moments plus a universal Lanczos growth rate.

The one corner that no classical method has been shown to cover is site-resolved coherent 1H-1H transfer or OTOC in a dense, static, protonated protein. That observable cannot be measured today, and it sits in the ergodic regime, where O'Brien et al. (2022) found the learning Hessian degenerate. The formal gate theorem is also weaker than proposed: C3-a is vacuous at realistic gamma/J (see evidence), so the kill rests on the empirical and physical arguments, not on the dissipation bound.

The C1 instrument as built cannot decide the question either way:
- A survival would come from isolated-cluster artefacts.
- The kill it already produced comes from sparse Pauli dynamics at N=10, a size so small that the method is close to brute force.

Re-instrument it with the nested and embedded test below before citing C1 in either direction.
verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 (formulation only). No hardness evidence exists for this instance family. BQP-completeness of generic 2-local Hamiltonian simulation says nothing about 3D 1/r^3 dipolar protein networks with z_eff ~ 3. No result shows that the classically hard component carries identifiable geometric Fisher information. The proposed bound C3-a is vacuous at realistic gamma/J ~ 1e-3 to 1e-2. C3-b (universality and self-averaging) has indirect support: the universal operator growth hypothesis was verified experimentally in 19F NMR FIDs (arXiv:2604.09362), and O'Brien et al. (2022) found the learning Hessian degenerate in the ergodic regime. C3-b is not proven for this system.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No protein experiment measures the observable that would be needed (site-resolved static 1H-1H transfer or OTOC). The quantum forward-model cost is 1e14 to 1e17 T gates per likelihood-gradient evaluation (see the cost note). The classical twins run in minutes to seconds. The one production C1 point, probed at a size too small to test scaling, already shows the best classical adversary with a hard-window Fisher-information fraction of 0.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
1. The adversary's local win is not evidence about scaling. At N=10, sparse Pauli dynamics with |c| >= 1e-4 matched the exact result, but it kept up to 54,450 strings. That is 5.2% of 4^10 and about 29% of the dimension of the Sz-conserving operator space, C(20,10) = 184,756, so it is close to brute force. At N >= 20 the same accuracy could need about 1e10 strings or more.

2. Weight truncation fails early even at N=10: w=5 fails at 80 us, classical spins at 40 us, and the exact 8-spin sub-cluster at 60 us.

3. Protein 1H networks fall in the few-strong-neighbour regime, which is where classical spins (Elsayed and Fine) and single-site spinDMFT are least reliable; Gräßer et al. state that spinDMFT needs each spin to interact with many others. Measured here: z_eff = (sum of d^2)^2 / (sum of d^4) has median 3.2, and the strongest partner carries 49% of the second moment M2.

4. With 1/r^3 couplings in 3D (alpha = d), there is no finite Lieb-Robinson velocity, so light-cone truncation arguments are weak.

5. The Google OTOC work (arXiv:2510.19550) shows that echoes refocus near-field dynamics and make the signal sensitive to distant couplings. This is the explicit mechanism, dO/dD_ij = i * integral of Tr(rho [h_ij(s), O(t)]) ds.

6. The corner that survives is an OTOC in an oriented, partially deuterated protein, with a few strong neighbours and time reversal. No classical method has been shown to reproduce such an observable to sigma = 0.01 beyond about 60 us at N >= 20.

Rebuttal to point 6: dilution pushes the network toward non-ergodic dynamics, where cluster expansions converge (C3-c) and the O'Brien Hessian becomes learnable but easy. Imperfect dipolar time reversal also adds decoherence that grows with cluster size. This rebuttal is not quantified here.
verdicts.evidence:
LOCAL (repo data; no new jobs were launched because CPU was at 98% from running G1 jobs; only numpy post-processing).

(E1) research/results/RAW/nmr_gate/1UBQ_p19_N10_o0_g1000.json, the only production C1 v2 point:
- Sparse Pauli |c| >= 1e-4 reproduces the sector-exact S_ab(t) at all 17 time points up to 320 us. Its maximum bias is 0.0025, below sigma = 0.01. The best-adversary hard-window fraction is 0 for all 4 parameters, so K-C1a fires under the stricter pre-registered rule.

(E2) Where the Fisher information sits. For radial_HA/GLU16 (FI_total = 485), 95% of the FI accumulates at t >= 60 us, with the median near 110 us. By about 100 us, S_ab has reached finite-cluster plateaus of 0.03 to 0.125, close to 1/N.

(E3) Embedding attack, computed from data/instruments/nmr/1UBQ_H.pdb (629 H, 73 amide probes):
- The 3 farthest cluster protons carry C1's long-range parameters. For N = 10 to 30 they get a median 58 to 65% of their dipolar M2 from protons outside the cluster, with sqrt(M2_out) = 5.3 to 5.8e4 rad/s.

- The physical plateau is about 1/629 = 0.0016, which is below sigma.
- Conclusion: the isolated-cluster "hard" FI at t >= 60 us is mostly a finite-size artefact.

(E4) Why C3-a is vacuous:
- Median sqrt(M2) per proton is 7.1e4 rad/s (11.3 kHz). With T1rho/T2' of 1 to 10 ms, gamma/J = 1.4e-3 to 1.4e-2.
- The damping factor exp(-2*gamma*w*t) at w=12 and t=100 us is 0.09 at gamma = 1000 s^-1 and 0.79 at gamma = 100 s^-1.
- For the Schuster et al. noisy-circuit bound, the noise per Trotter step is gamma*dt = 2e-3, so the exponent is about 500.
- The operative mechanism is therefore unitary operator backflow into the protein bath, not dissipation.
