verdicts.decisive_test:
Nested and embedded Fisher-information convergence test. It uses the existing scripts/nmr_gate.py plus a small hybrid bath; runtime is 1 day or less on 8 cores, under the governor.

Setup:
- 6 amide probes of 1UBQ, one per secondary-structure element.
- A fixed B0 direction and gamma = 1000 s^-1.
- The same long-range parameters in every run: protons 3.5 to 4 Å from the probe that are present in all clusters.

Steps:
(i) Compute sector-exact S_ab(t) and FI(t) in nested isolated clusters at N = 10, 12 and 14.
(ii) Repeat at N = 14 with the next 30 protons added as a classical-spin bath coupled by mean field (Starkov-Fine hybrid, the open adversary in NM-1). A cheaper proxy is per-spin dephasing at gamma_i = sqrt(M2_out,i) of about 5e4 rad/s.
(iii) At each N, record the minimum sparse-Pauli string count needed to keep the bias below sigma/3 up to t_c.

The family is KILLED if any of these holds:
(a) The FI at t >= t_c (best adversary) changes by more than 2x between N = 10, 12 and 14, or the bath removes more than 90% of it. Either result means the hard-window FI is a finite-size artefact.
(b) The hybrid or sparse-Pauli result matches exact within sigma until the embedded S_ab falls below sigma.
(c) The generalised-eigenvalue gain g = max_v v'F_total v / v'F_easy v is below 2.

Promote QM-20 only if all of these hold:
- The late-window FI converges in N.
- More than 30% of the late-window FI survives the bath.
- The sparse-Pauli string count grows faster than 3^N.

Paper-level pre-check (no compute): the embedded late-time plateau of about 1/629 = 0.0016 is already below sigma = 0.01.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
This is a rough derivation, not a citation. A fault-tolerant forward model for the 629 protons of ubiquitin:
- 629 logical qubits.
- About 11,000 dipolar pair terms per Trotter step (median 35 protons within 6 Å).
- 160 steps, giving about 5.3e6 rotations or about 2.6e8 T gates per circuit.
- 1e5 shots to reach ±0.003, times 17 time points, times about 600 parameter settings for a finite-difference gradient over about 300 geometric parameters. That is about 1e9 circuits, or about 3e17 T per likelihood gradient.
- Amplitude estimation plus a quantum gradient (Jordan / Gilyén-type) could bring this to about 1e14 T, which is years at 1e6 T/s.

The classical twins:
- spinDMFT: about 5 min on 4 laptop cores per substance.
- Full-relaxation-matrix NOE: a 629-dimensional linear ODE, seconds.
- Sparse Pauli at N=10: 233 s.

Break-even would require the classical cost at matched accuracy to grow exponentially in the regime where the Fisher information lives. That growth is not demonstrated, and E3 suggests the FI there is mostly an artefact of isolated clusters.
verdicts.novelty_note:
QM-21's hardness-identifiability trade-off was anticipated, qualitatively, by O'Brien et al. (2022): the same protein (ubiquitin), with the learning Hessian degenerate in the ergodic regime. C3-a has a liquid-state precedent in Kuprov's state-space restriction, which drops rapidly relaxing states and correlations between distant spins, at more than 1000 spins (2007/2014). C3-b corresponds to the universal operator growth hypothesis and to DAOE/backflow suppression.

The only possibly new element is a quantitative split of the Fisher information against an explicit, embedded panel of classical adversaries. Search scope: arXiv API only, because the WebSearch budget was exhausted, plus research/discovery/NOVELTY_MEMOS.md NM-1. Under that scope, the search found no evidence of a study that measures structural Fisher information beyond the classical-adversary failure time for protein 1H dipolar networks. It also found no evidence that spinDMFT or the hybrid methods have been applied to protein 1H networks.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0. No separation exists for this instance family: infinite-temperature 2-point or OTOC correlators of a secular dipolar Hamiltonian on protein 1H geometries, with T2-type dephasing and σ = 0.01 readout. Generic BQP-completeness of local Hamiltonian simulation does not carry over to it. As stated, C3-a is false for the instrument's own noise model. Pure dephasing damps only the X/Y factors of a Pauli string, and Z-strings are undamped. Total Z is conserved, so high-weight Z-strings are the slow hydrodynamic modes. The bound has to count X/Y factors, not weight. Even when corrected, it is weak at realistic noise. With γ = 100–1000 s⁻¹ and t = 320 µs, γt is 0.03–0.32, so the w = 12 damping factor e^{-2γwt} is between 0.46 and 5e-4. Dephasing alone cannot enforce the family kill. C3-b is the load-bearing claim, and the weak-coupling reduction in `evidence` supports it.
verdicts.level_practical:
L0. No run has shown any classical failure. The only valid pre-registered v2 row is N = 10 at γ = 1000 s⁻¹. There, sparse Pauli dynamics at ε = 1e-4 reproduces the exact signal over the whole 320 µs window with max bias ≤ 0.0025 (σ = 0.01) and at most 5.4e4 strings. frac_hard_best = 0 for all 4 parameters and the gain spectrum is 1.0. The sector-exact solver (35.6 s) was cheaper than every adversary (up to 268 s). An end-to-end inference would take 10²–10⁴ years at 170 µs per Toffoli (see break_even). Two data or model oracles also erase the premise:
- The Hamiltonian is treated as known apart from geometry. In reality it has order parameters, methyl and ring averaging, chemical-shift offsets and couplings to water and neighbouring molecules.
- The instrument assumes site-resolved static 1H transfer data. Real experiments get site resolution by MAS, dilution or recoupling, and those make the dynamics few-body.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
1. The hardness side is plausible and not yet refuted. Operator growth in dense 3D dipolar networks is ballistic. At 320 µs the light cone holds about 240 protons (radius about 14 Å, computed from 1UBQ). The sparse-Pauli string count at fixed accuracy may well grow exponentially with N. The N = 10 success says nothing about the scaling.
2. The forward model is modest by FTQC standards: about 80–1300 logical qubits and 3e6–6e7 Toffolis per shot. Any speedup would be exponential (simulation), not quadratic, so the Babbush/Sanders quadratic-overhead argument does not apply.
3. Brute-force exact classical simulation loses to the quantum forward model from about N* = 30–48 spins (see break_even). That crossover is not astronomical in N.
4. Beyond-classical echo experiments exist: Google's OTOC(2) on random circuits, and the NMR geometry demo of Zhang et al. (arXiv:2510.19550). A time-reversal (magic-echo) design might concentrate geometric information in the high-weight component and so reverse C3-b.

Why it still fails:
- (a) The information that S33 lacked is long-range: 5–6 Å H–H couplings of 271 Hz median against an 11.4 kHz local field. In that regime the sensitivity is perturbative and Markovian, so it is classically reducible.
- (b) The run is limited by shots × forward models × inference iterations, not by one circuit.
- (c) The data and Hamiltonian oracles are unrealistic.
- (d) O'Brien et al. (2022) already found that ergodic dynamics degenerate learnability.
verdicts.evidence:
**Repo data**
- `research/results/RAW/nmr_gate/1UBQ_p19_N10_o0_g1000.json`, the only valid v2 row. Weight-truncated Pauli at w = 2–5 fails at 40–80 µs (frac_hard 0.95–0.9999). Weight is therefore the wrong complexity measure, and the task's kill test phrased as "FI_w ≥ 0.9 FI_exact at w ≤ 6" is miscalibrated.
  - Sparse Pauli at ε = 1e-4 is exact over the window: 5.4e4 peak strings, 233 s.
  - The 4e-14 eigenvalue that appears in both F_total and F_easy is an instrument artefact. radial_HA/GLU16 and rigid_res16 are the same parameter (n_moved = 1).
  - All perturbed protons sit at 3.25–3.80 Å, which is not structurally long-range.
- The v1 pilots (excluded per the deviation log) show the same weight-truncation failure at 20 µs.

**My computation** (scratchpad script `qm21_audit.py`, using `qapf.nmr.spins` on `data/instruments/nmr/1UBQ_H.pdb` and `1PGA_H.pdb`)
- 1UBQ has 629 H. Mean neighbour counts are 21.6, 35.6 and 77.2 within 5, 6 and 8 Å.
- Per-spin local field: sqrt(Σd²)/2π has median 11.4 kHz. The largest |d|/2π is 26.5 kHz.
- For pairs at 5–6 Å, |d|/2π has median 271 Hz and 90th percentile 505 Hz. Couplings beyond 5 Å carry 2.4% of Σd².
- Hamiltonian 1-norm: λ = 1.04e8 s⁻¹ over all pairs, so λt = 3.3e4 at 320 µs. There are 11,205 pairs within 6 Å.
- The nearest-N cluster radius is 3.85 Å at N = 10 and 4.6 Å at N = 14. The gate as instrumented therefore cannot see distances ≥ 5 Å.
- 1PGA (419 H) gives similar values.

**Derivation (inference, not proof): weak-coupling reduction behind C3-b**
- For a pair a, b with ε = d_ab/Δ_loc ≈ 0.024–0.044 (5–6 Å), the leading sensitivity of the transfer signal S_ab to d_ab is d_ab² times a 4-point function of the unperturbed dynamics.
- That function is supported on the union of the ~4 Å neighbourhoods of a and b (≤ about 25–30 spins), so it is classically exact at 2^30 or less. Higher orders are suppressed by ε² ≈ 6e-4 to 2e-3.
- Under the independent-bath approximation it factorises into the Suter–Ernst overlap-integral rate W_ab = (d_ab²/2)∫G_a G_b dτ, which is a classical rate matrix.
- Numerically: W ≈ 18 s⁻¹, so the direct transfer is W·t ≈ 0.006–0.012 at 320 µs, about σ. The predicted frac_hard for long-range parameters is ≲ 0.01–0.05.
- Chemical-shift dispersion (kHz) is much larger than 270 Hz. It further pushes long-range flip-flops into this overlap-integral (classical) regime.

**Citations**
- Repo-verified: O'Brien et al., PRX Quantum 3, 030345 (2022), arXiv:2109.02163 (ergodic implies degenerate learnability). Zhang et al., arXiv:2510.19550. Begušić & Chan, arXiv:2306.16372. Elsayed & Fine, PRB 91, 094424 (2015), arXiv:1409.8564. Walch et al., arXiv:2609.20406.
- Not re-verified this session: Babbush et al., PRX Quantum 2, 010103 (2021), arXiv:2011.04149. Sanders et al., PRX Quantum 1, 020312 (2020), arXiv:2007.07391. Gidney & Fowler, Quantum 3, 135 (2019), arXiv:1812.01238 (170 µs ≈ 5.5·d cycles at d = 31, 1 µs cycle).
- Unverified: Schuster–Yin–Gao–Yao, arXiv:2407.12768. Rakovszky–von Keyserlingk–Pollmann DAOE, PRB 105, 075131 (2022), arXiv:2004.05177. Suter & Ernst, PRB 32, 5608 (1985).
verdicts.decisive_test:
**Paper pre-check (already done above).** The golden-rule and cluster reduction predicts frac_hard ≲ 0.05 for 5–6 Å parameters.

**Cheapest run (≤ 1 day on the 8-core box).** Re-run nmr_gate v2 with these changes:
- Move the perturbations to protons at 4.5–6.5 Å from the probe. Remove duplicate parameters. Add chemical-shift offsets as nuisance parameters.
- Add two adversaries:
  - (i) a golden-rule rate-matrix model: W_ab from overlap integrals of classical-spin or sub-cluster FIDs, O(N³);
  - (ii) exact simulation on the union of the 4 Å neighbourhoods of a and b (≤ 22 spins).
- Record the sparse-Pauli string count S*(N) at max bias ≤ σ/3.
- Run on 8 probes of 1UBQ with N ∈ {10, 14, 18, 22}, plus 3 probes at N = 24.
- Use γ = 0, the conservative case for hardness. The reference is statevector typicality with one vector, so its error is ~2^{-N/2} ≤ 2e-4. Memory is ≤ 0.3 GB per vector, and one forward model at N = 24 takes about 15 min.

**Kill the family** if any of these holds:
- median FI_total for the long-range parameters < 1 Å⁻² at σ = 0.01 (nothing to unlock);
- median frac_hard against the best adversary (including i and ii) < 0.1;
- a log-linear fit of S*(N) extrapolates to fewer than 3e9 strings at N = 60 (below the 1 µs-Toffoli break-even).

**Promote QM-20** to N = 30–60 scaling and FT costing only if all of these hold:
- FI_total ≥ 1 Å⁻² for at least a third of the long-range parameters;
- frac_hard_best ≥ 0.3 at N = 22–24;
- S* grows by ≥ 0.46 bits per added spin, so that S*(60) ≥ 5e11.

The task's current promotion threshold (> 1e7 retained strings) is 2.5–4.7 orders of magnitude below break-even and should be replaced.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Per-geometry forward model with a first-order Trotter circuit identical to the instrument's: dt = 2 µs, 160–640 steps, 1H cutoff 6 Å. Each XXZ pair gate costs about 32 Toffolis (2 distinct rotation angles × 16 Toffolis using a phase-gradient register). Toffolis per step = number of pairs × 32.

**Resource counts at 160 steps (640 steps is 4× the Toffolis)**

| N | Logical qubits | Pairs within 6 Å | Toffoli per step | Toffoli per shot | One shot at 170 µs | One shot at 1 µs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14 | ~34 | 77 | 2.5e3 | 3.9e5 | 67 s | 0.4 s |
| 60 | ~80 | 656 | 2.1e4 | 3.4e6 | 9.5 min | 3.4 s |
| 240 (320 µs light cone) | ~260 | 3,942 | 1.26e5 | 2.0e7 | 57 min | 20 s |
| 629 (all of ubiquitin) | ~650 | 11,205 | 3.6e5 | 5.7e7 | 2.7 h | 57 s |

- Logical qubits are N plus about 20 for the phase-gradient register and ancillas. Amplitude estimation would need a purified maximally mixed state, which doubles this to about 2N + 25.
- Qubitization is worse for the full protein: λt = 3.3e4 queries at about 3.4e4 Toffolis each is about 1e9 Toffolis per shot.
- Surface-code distance is about 23–27 at p = 1e-3. That is about 1e5 physical qubits at N = 60 and about 1e6 for the full protein, plus factories.

**Shots**
- One forward model needs about 1e4 shots per time point for σ = 0.01. A single shot from a random computational-basis input yields every S_ab at once.
- Across 16 time points the cost is about 8.5 full-circuit equivalents.
- Amplitude estimation (~500–1600 circuits per individual correlator) does not beat sampling once there are 10 or more observables.
- If the model's own noise must be σ/3, multiply by 9.
- Finite-difference gradients at h = 0.05 Å need about 2e6 shots per point for 10% precision.

**Wall-clock per forward model** (1e4 shots per time point)

| N | At 170 µs per Toffoli | At 1 µs per Toffoli |
|---|---|---|
| 60 | 1.5–6 years | 3–13 days |
| 629 | 26–105 years | 56–226 days |

**Inference.** One inference with P = 10 parameters and 20 Gauss–Newton iterations is about 420 forward models:
- About 650 years at 170 µs per Toffoli, or about 4 years at 1 µs, before the shot inflation for gradients.
- That is ~1e2–1e4 years under the Sanders/Babbush-style assumptions.

**Break-even against exact statevector**
- Classical exact simulation of one forward model costs about pairs × 160 × 2^N × 24 flops. That is 1.8e18 flops at N = 40, and needs 4.5 PB of memory at N = 48.
- Crossover N* with ρ = 1 (a quantum-computer second priced as one CPU core): about 38 at 170 µs per Toffoli and about 30 at 1 µs.
- With ρ = 1e3 the crossover is about 48, which is also the memory wall.

**Break-even against the best approximate adversary (N = 60, ρ = 1)**
- The quantum forward model wins only if the classical method needs more than B_fwd ≈ 3e15 flops (1 µs per Toffoli) to 5e17 flops (170 µs) per forward model.
- In sparse-Pauli strings that is S*(60) > 3e9 to 5e11.
- The measured value is S*(10) = 5.4e4. Break-even requires growth of at least 0.31–0.46 bits per added spin, which has not been measured.

**Against more data acquisition.** A classical inversion can buy information with more spectrometer time or classically friendly experiments (dilution, MAS recoupling).
- The quantum route needs a gain g ≳ 1e3.
- The measured gain is g = 1.0 (N = 10).

**Bottom line.** Even if a hardness window exists, the oracles (a known Hamiltonian, site-resolved static 1H data) and the multiplicative cost of shots × forward models × iterations erase it. Default: KILL.
verdicts.novelty_note:
Under the repo's literature scope (arXiv API plus the literature-phase F notes, no general web search), the search found no evidence of a study that measures, for protein 1H dipolar networks, how much structural Fisher information lies beyond the failure time of the best classical adversary. That makes QM-21 at most an incremental, quantitative extension of O'Brien et al. (2022), which must be cited as the origin of the idea (NM-1).

This audit adds three things:
1. The promotion threshold is recalibrated to the break-even string count, S*(60) ≈ 3e9–5e11. The earlier threshold was 1e7.
2. A constructive reduction (derivation sketch, unverified): the leading sensitivity to weak long-range couplings is a local 4-point function, or equivalently a Suter–Ernst overlap-integral rate. It is classically exact on ≤ 30 spins, with ε² ≈ 1e-3 corrections.
3. A correction to C3-a: the damping should count X/Y factors, not weight.

The search found no evidence, within the same limited scope, that item 2 has been stated for protein 1H networks.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 (formulation only). No theorem is proved. C3-a follows almost directly from known noisy Pauli-path and open-system operator-growth results. It is a no-go-style bound, not an advantage claim. As stated, C3-b and C3-c are contradicted or anticipated by 2025–2026 prior art for time-reversed (echo/OTOC) observables. A positive region would need evidence of exponential classical simulation hardness, and none exists for protein 1H networks.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No quantum component has been built. In-house C1 v2 on 1UBQ H/ILE3, N=10: sparse Pauli dynamics at eps=1e-4 reproduces the transfer signal over the full 320 us window at gamma = 0, 1000 and 5000 s^-1. That gives FI_hard(best adversary) = 0 for all 4 parameters, with gain spectrum = 1. At gamma=0 this takes 1.66e5 strings, 90% of the C(20,10)=1.85e5 sector, so N=10 is effectively exact enumeration and says nothing about hardness. OTOC observables at gamma=0 keep frac_hard = 0.85–0.97 even against eps=1e-4, but only at N=10, where exact simulation is trivial. Practical relevance to protein structure is indirect (see counterargument).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
(1) PROTEIN RELEVANCE IS INDIRECT. No protein-structure pipeline reads coherent many-body 1H dynamics. Solution NOESY is a classical N×N rate matrix (full relaxation-matrix analysis), and RDCs are first-order splittings. Solid-state MAS uses restraints between dilute 13C/15N spins plus rate-equation or spinDMFT spin diffusion. Static oriented membrane-protein NMR uses isolated 15N–1H pairs under 1H decoupling. The static, rigid, fully protonated oriented-protein setting (O'Brien 2022's ubiquitin case) matches no experiment actually run on proteins.
Measured on data/instruments/nmr/1UBQ_H.pdb (629 H; GB1 419 H):
- Clusters of 12–20 spins have median radius 3.9–4.8 Å (GB1 4.1–5.0 Å). They see only local covalent and rotamer geometry, which is already known.
- Fold-informative couplings (r ≥ 5 Å, D ≤ 0.96 kHz) contribute only 1.9% of the local second moment. The nearest-neighbour D is 21.5 kHz and the rms local field is 28 kHz.
- In a protonated protein, a 12–20-spin cluster is not isolated. The other ~600 protons act on each boundary spin at rates ~1e5 s^-1 (gamma/J ~ O(1)), far above the proposed grid of {0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1}. Isolated-cluster runs at gamma/J ≤ 0.1 overstate the hard-window information.
- The gamma/J the candidate itself calls realistic (T 1–10 ms against 0.2–20 kHz couplings) spans 8e-4 to 0.8. For the weak, fold-informative couplings (0.2–1 kHz) it is 0.02–0.8, mostly outside the grid.
(2) IT CANNOT GATE THE WHOLE FAMILY AS STATED. A universal C3-b ("sensitivity self-averages in the ergodic regime") is contradicted for echo observables:
- Google, arXiv:2506.10191 / Nature 646, 825 (2025) [F30]: OTOC(2) "remain sensitive to the underlying dynamics at long time scales" in ergodic dynamics. It shows Hamiltonian learning via OTOC(2) beyond known classical algorithms, at the ergodic *edge*, the very regime C3-c assumes is classically easy.
- Gjonbalaj, Kokail, Yelin, Choi, arXiv:2603.04486 (2026): "ergodicity and chaos improve the robustness of Hamiltonian learning".
- Scrambling-enhanced metrology: Li et al., Science 380, 1381 (2023), arXiv:2212.13880; an 18 dB gain in solid-state nuclear spins, Li…Suter, Peng, arXiv:2606.31827 (2026).
NMR can time-reverse dipolar dynamics, and F34 uses exactly those echoes. A theorem restricted to forward 2-point correlators would therefore not decide QM-20. The live question becomes empirical and sample-specific: how fast real-sample irreversibility damps the echo. Pastawski's group reports perturbation-independent Loschmidt-echo decay on the intrinsic dipolar timescale in dense dipolar solids (Sánchez et al., PRL 124, 030601 (2020), arXiv:1902.06628). Domínguez et al. (PRA 104, 012402 (2021), arXiv:2005.12361) find that decoherence grows as a power law in correlated-cluster size. Both point toward kill in real samples. I recalled their exact exponents and ratios from the abstracts and did not verify them.
(3) WRONG CLASSICAL TWIN. The comparator is 'classically simulable observables of the same experiment'. The real competitor is the best classically interpretable experiment at equal spectrometer time: NOESY/RFDR/REDOR, deuteration dilution, or selective two-spin sequences. Hard-window Fisher information only has value if it exceeds the Fisher information that alternative delivers per unit instrument time. The candidate does not model this.
(4) S29–S33 META-LESSON. Protein structure accuracy is information-limited (K-012/DNR-16). The information here comes from the NMR experiment. The quantum computer would only be an interpreter, and it has to beat classical interpreters (spinDMFT, sparse Pauli, cluster expansions) on the same data.
Steelman: the gate is cheap and has high decision value. The one protein-relevant regime not yet covered is perdeuterated, amide-back-exchanged proteins (~1 H/residue, sparse HN network, cross-strand HN–HN ~3–4.5 Å). There, weak couplings encode sheet topology, which is fold-level information. That regime should be added rather than claimed.

verdicts.decisive_test:
Do not launch the new 50-cluster campaign. It duplicates C1 and C2 (research/experiments/PREREGISTERED/PREREG_G1_C1_Q4.md) and is infeasible for gamma>0 at N≥16. Instead, extend the running C2 M*(N) scaling (1UBQ probes 19 and 245, N = 8–14 sector-exact, 16–20 against the converged eps reference) with three changes:
(i) Use the OTOC observable, the only one with any hard-window Fisher information, as the primary statistic.
(ii) Apply per-spin-order dephasing at gamma/J_rms ∈ {0.03, 0.1, 0.3}, with J_rms = 28 kHz. This covers the fold-informative couplings, where gamma/J is 0.02–0.8. Also add a rest-of-protein bath term, either as spinDMFT mean-field noise or as classical spins around an exact core, instead of treating the cluster as isolated.
(iii) Add one perdeuterated amide-only HN network of N ≈ 12–20 spins from 1PGA (a beta sheet with cross-strand HN–HN pairs).
Kill the family if, at gamma/J_rms ≥ 0.1, the median FI_hard(best adversary)/FI_total < 0.1 for OTOC. Also kill it if ln M*(N) fits N^k better than exp(kappa N) (dBIC > 10), or if M*(60) < 1e9. About 1–2 days on 8 cores.
On paper, first: the bound FI_hard ≤ FI_total·exp(−2·gamma_eff·w_c·t50) with t50 ≈ 1.2e-4 s and w_c ≈ 6 gives 0.24 at gamma_eff = 1e3 s^-1 and 6e-7 at 1e4 s^-1. The whole family therefore turns on whether the effective per-order damping in a real protein sample is below about 2e3 s^-1. For protonated proteins it is not (bath field ~1e5 s^-1). Only the dilute-HN regime can plausibly stay open.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
The gate itself is cheap: about 1–2 CPU-days if trimmed to N ≤ 14 exact plus sparse-Pauli references to N=20. If the family survived, C2's promotion criterion would require M*(60) > 1e12 strings, exponential in N.
The quantum side at N=60 (O'Brien's cluster, 7.3 Å radius in 1UBQ):
- Circuit: an all-to-all secular dipolar Trotter step has about 1,770 pair terms, roughly 5e3 two-qubit gates. 160 steps (320 us at dt = 2 us) give about 8e5 two-qubit gates per forward pass, and about 1.6e6 for an OTOC.
- Shots: at sigma = 0.01, about 1e4 shots per time point × 17 time points × about 21 finite-difference points, roughly 3.6e6 circuit executions.
- Total: about 5e12 two-qubit gate applications. That is fault-tolerant only, since NISQ fidelity at 1e-3 error per gate is about e^-1600.
- Against: spinDMFT or sparse Pauli at 1e5–1e6 strings in CPU-minutes for N=10. Even a positive gate implies at best a sample-specific interpretation advantage, and it must also beat the best classically interpretable NMR experiment at equal spectrometer time.
verdicts.novelty_note:
Search scope: arXiv API title and abstract searches plus id_list verification on 2026-09-27, plus literature-phase records F30–F39 and NM-1. General WebSearch was unavailable because the budget was exhausted, so non-arXiv journal-only work may be missed. Under that scope, the search found no paper that bounds the parameter Fisher information carried by weight>w Heisenberg components under per-order dissipation for dipolar NMR networks. It also found none that tests that bound on protein 1H networks against an explicit classical-adversary panel.
The components are prior art:
- C3-a ≈ Schuster–Yao 2022 / Schuster–Yin–Gao–Yao 2024–25 / DAOE / Mele 2024, specialised to Fisher information
- C3-b ≈ Holmes 2021 + O'Brien 2022, and it is qualified or contradicted for echo observables by F30 (2025), Gjonbalaj et al. 2026 and scrambling-metrology results (2023, 2026)
- C3-c ≈ F30's 'edge of ergodicity' and the Pastawski/Álvarez–Suter localisation and echo work
Net: at most an incremental, quantitative extension of O'Brien et al. 2022, as NM-1 already concluded. Any write-up must cite O'Brien 2022 as the origin, and must restrict the no-go to forward (non-time-reversed) correlators, or model real-sample echo irreversibility explicitly.

title: Other spectroscopic and scattering forward models whose exact simulation is classically polynomial or whose hard part is fold-uninformative (liquid-state NMR/QABC, ZULF, EPR/DEER and bath decoherence, radical-pair cryptochromes, optical/vibrational spectra, diffraction/multislice)
merged_from: physics P4 (liquid-state NMR + QABC), physics P5 (ZULF NMR), physics P7 (EPR/DEER and electron-spin decoherence), physics P10 (IR/2D-IR/ROA/ECD/VCD/2DES), physics P11 (MicroED/XFEL/SAXS/neutron), wild 'Radical-pair spin dynamics in cryptochromes'
summary: Q: does quantum simulation of any other experimental forward model add fold-level structural information? Quantum: Hamiltonian/Liouvillian simulation (QABC, Sels et al. 2020; digital NMR spectra, 34-spin and 21-spin hardware demos validated against classical references), qubitised ZULF simulation (Elenewski et al.), central-spin electron/bath simulation, open-system radical-pair dynamics, vibrational/excitonic simulation, first-quantised wave propagation. Mechanism and why classical copies it, per modality: liquid high-field NMR: secular weak coupling commutes with every I_z (first-order multiplets), Solomon/Redfield NOE closes in the N-dim longitudinal subspace (full relaxation matrix), RDC/PCS are closed forms, shifts are closed-shell electronic structure; Spinach simulated 1000+-spin ubiquitin with full Redfield (Edwards 2014). ZULF: hard Heisenberg J-graph dynamics, but protein J graphs are quasi-1D (MPS/TT), content is local 3J dihedrals already in the (theta,tau) head, and slow-tumbling linewidths (10-100 Hz) wash out the J spread. DEER: product kernel exact for multi-spin clusters, bath echo converged by CCE (2000 protons) and TN; fold uncertainty comes from label rotamer ensembles (classical sampling). Radical pair: exponential in hyperfine nuclei (~20-30), but central-spin structure favours semiclassical/spin-coherent sampling and typicality; a few scalar yields weakly constrain geometry. Optical: one-/two-exciton manifolds (N, N^2/2), DichroCalc, HEOM; information content is a few SS fractions (SESCA). Diffraction: single-particle linear Schroedinger equation (multislice O(grid log grid)), no many-body entanglement; readout of Omega(grid) intensities erases polylog gains. Speedup: none-known at protein scale (exponential only for small strongly coupled molecules or many-nucleus radical pairs if approximations fail). Info vs comp: most are new-information sources (DNR-16) but low-information or already classically interpretable; residual hard parts (ensemble averaging, label ensembles) reduce to QM-01 sampling. S29-S33: no new computational mechanism; condition-C analogue applies. Kill (confirmation): full-relaxation-matrix/first-order NOESY within 10-20% of exact Liouville on <= 10-spin 1UBQ clusters; ZULF linewidth > J spread at 60 aa or only 3J dihedrals identifiable; CCE-2/4 match exact 20-proton + nitroxide echo and echo Fisher information on a distant 1 A helix shift ~0; semiclassical/top-k truncation reproduces singlet-yield anisotropy within 5% at n = 6-20 nuclei; exciton amide-I + matrix-method CD native-vs-decoy AUC < 0.6 at SNR 100; multislice 512^2 x 200 slices in minutes. Tests: minutes to < 1 day each on this CPU. Track: C theory/query (kill cards). Prior: very low to nil.
dead_reason: No existing program kill applies (non-diagonal physics outside H-001); each variant is killed by literature/argument and should be recorded as a new kill after its cheap confirmation.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 (formulation only). No query or complexity separation exists for any QM-22 forward model at protein scale. In the dominant regimes, classical simulability is structural. (a) High-field liquid NMR under the secular, weak-coupling truncation has H = sum_i w_i I_zi + 2pi sum_ij J_ij I_zi I_zj, which is diagonal in the Zeeman product basis, so spectra have closed forms. NOE is linear Solomon/Redfield dynamics in the N-dimensional longitudinal subspace. (b) Optical/vibrational exciton spectra conserve excitation number: the 1-exciton manifold has dimension N and the 2-exciton manifold N(N+1)/2, both polynomial. (c) Diffraction/multislice is a single-particle linear Schroedinger equation, O(G log G) per slice by FFT. (d) The DEER dipolar kernel is closed-form, and the multi-spin product kernel is exact under the secular approximation. The only genuinely many-body parts are ZULF J-networks, radical pairs and electron-nuclear baths. In each of them, the fold-informative parameters enter as weak, perturbative couplings, where cluster/CCE/restricted-state/tensor-network expansions are controlled.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No matched-conditions usefulness (L1) exists for any modality on any protein. Hardware demonstrations are 4-qubit acetonitrile ZULF (Seetharam et al. 2021) and few-spin radical-pair toys (Zhang/Kais 2022; Tolunay 2022; Alvarez 2024), and all of them are classically trivial. Classical codes already run at or beyond protein scale: >1000-spin ubiquitin (Edwards 2014), an exact tensor-train 15N ubiquitin spectrum (Savostyanov 2014), a converged exact 47-spin radical pair (Lindoy 2020), and MPS/MPDO radical pairs with 30–60 nuclei (Hino 2025). Measured here: one multislice step on a 512^2 grid takes 0.135 s single-threaded at idle priority while the machine was at 91% background load, so 200 slices take about 27 s.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
1) Walch, Fratus, Reiner & Lesanovsky (arXiv:2609.20406, 2026) find that shot-noise cost grows only weakly with molecular size. Readout therefore does not by itself kill quantum NMR-spectrum simulation, and I concede that point. 2) The Fratus et al. cluster approximation (arXiv:2508.06448) is benchmarked for typical liquid-state regimes. Strongly coupled regimes (ZULF, low field, oriented media) are less covered, and radical-pair tensor networks stop at about 30 explicit nuclei (60 in benchmarks) under non-Markovian hopping. 3) Dense 1H dipolar networks in solids or oriented media, such as MAS proton-driven spin diffusion, really are ergodic and classically hard, and they carry contact information.

Rebuttal: (1) and (2) concern the cost of simulating spectra, not fold information. ZULF measures the same isotropic {J_ij} that high-field weak-coupling experiments give in closed form, so it only encodes those parameters more expensively. The fold-informative couplings are the weak ones: trans-H-bond 3hJ_NC' is about 0.2–0.9 Hz [recalled, Cordier & Grzesiek 1999, unverified this session]. Estimated ZULF linewidths for a 7 kDa protein (tau_c about 4 ns) are about 5–20 Hz from J(0)-dominated 13C–1H and 1H–1H dipolar relaxation (d_CH = 23 kHz), so 3hJ is invisible and 3J is marginal. Radical-pair anisotropy averages away under isotropic tumbling. What remains is a MARY curve, a handful of scalars about one cofactor pair, and it applies only to flavoproteins. Point (3) belongs to QM-19/20/21 (Program C, pre-registered C1). O'Brien et al. 2022 (arXiv:2109.02163) found there that learnability degrades exactly as dynamics become ergodic. It does not rescue QM-22.
verdicts.evidence:
Classical adversary per modality (arXiv ids verified this session via the arXiv API; WebSearch budget was exhausted):

LIQUID HIGH-FIELD NMR/QABC:
- Quantum proposal: Sels, Dashti, Mora, O. Demler, E. Demler, arXiv:1910.14221 (QABC, small molecules).
- Classical: Kuprov, Wagner-Rundell & Hore, physics/0701294 (restricted state space, O(n^2 k), linear for protein topologies). Edwards, Savostyanov, Welderufael, Lee & Kuprov, arXiv:1402.6139 (ubiquitin, >1000 spins, with relaxation). Savostyanov, Dolgov, Werner & Kuprov, arXiv:1402.4516 (exact tensor-train 15N ubiquitin spectrum, several hundred spins). Fratus et al., arXiv:2508.06448 (cluster approximation, linear in spin count, accurate 'throughout, and even somewhat beyond' typical regimes).
- Full relaxation-matrix NOE for about 400 protons at 60 aa is one 400x400 matrix exponential, about 1e8 flops.
- Locality: sigma_ij scales as r^-6. d_HH is about 120 kHz*A^3/r^3, i.e. about 1 kHz at 5 A, and long-range NOEs are about 460x weaker than 1.8 A geminal pairs.

ZULF:
- Quantum: Seetharam et al., arXiv:2109.13298 (4 qubits, acetonitrile). Burov & Javerzac, arXiv:2608.20250 (Heisenberg-NMR compilation). The 'Elenewski qubitised ZULF' work was not found on arXiv and is unverified.
- Parameter-identity argument: H = 2pi sum J_ij I_i.I_j carries no parameter that high-field first-order J spectroscopy lacks.
- The residue clustering (1J_CH/NH 90–140 Hz and 1J_CC 35–55 Hz inside residues, versus about 11–15 Hz 1J_NCa/1J_C'N between them) gives a quasi-1D chain of ~15-spin clusters with perturbative links, which is TT/DMRG-tractable.

DEER/EPR:
- The dipolar kernel is closed-form.
- The bath is solved by CCE (PyCCE, Onizhuk & Galli, arXiv:2107.05843; many CCE molecular-radical papers, e.g. arXiv:2504.18254 and 2609.16851). Canarie, Jahn & Stoll, JPCL 2020, report about 2000 protons for nitroxides [recalled, unverified].
- The e–1H coupling is about 79 MHz*A^3/r^3 (79 kHz at 10 A, 3 kHz at 30 A). Bath pair contributions fall steeply with distance, so the echo senses only local proton density within about 1–1.5 nm.
- Fold uncertainty comes from label rotamer ensembles, which is a classical sampling problem (QM-01).

RADICAL PAIR:
- Lindoy, Fay & Manolopoulos, arXiv:2004.11261, JCP 152, 164107 (2020): converged exact 47-spin simulation; 'the best semiclassical approximation does capture essentially all of the relevant physics'.
- Hino, Frantzov, Kurashige & Antill, arXiv:2509.22104 (MPS/MPDO flavin–Trp, 30–60 nuclei).
- Lewis, Manolopoulos & Hore, arXiv:1407.2162 (semiclassical). Fay, Lindoy & Manolopoulos, arXiv:1910.09870 (beyond Redfield).
- Quantum toys: arXiv:2211.15427, 2208.10107, 2406.12986.

OPTICAL/VIBRATIONAL:
- Frenkel exciton matrix method: N = 60 amides x 2 transitions gives a 120x120 diagonalisation, and 2-exciton about 7e3 states, which takes seconds.
- Recalled and unverified: CD carries about 3–5 independent components (Hennessey & Johnson 1981; SESCA, Nagy et al. JCTC 2019; DichroCalc, Bulheller & Hirst 2009; NISE, Jansen).
- Quantum ECD work (arXiv:2602.03710) only matches classical references.

DIFFRACTION:
- Multislice cost is O(G log G) per slice; measured here at 0.135 s per 512^2 slice single-threaded under 91% load.
- A quantum first-quantised propagator needs Omega(G) samples to compare against a G-pixel micrograph, and amplitude-loading the data needs QRAM (no free state prep). Any polylog gain is erased.
- A 7 kDa target is also below the practical single-particle cryo-EM size limit [recalled: Henderson 1995 about 38 kDa theoretical; unverified].

INFORMATION VERSUS COMPUTATION:
- All structural information comes from the experiment. The quantum device would only replace a forward model that is already classical.
- The structure has about 174 DOF (3n-6 at 60 aa, consistent with a≡mu). Fold-level information per modality: CD about 3–5 numbers; DEER about 1–3 numbers per label pair; radical pair about 0 fold DOF; ZULF gives local dihedrals, which the (theta,tau) head already models.
- The condition-C analogue holds: forward-model fidelity beyond the classical approximation does not transmit to fold accuracy.
verdicts.decisive_test:
Paper test, zero CPU (decides QM-22 by itself): a parameter-identity and locality audit.

For each modality, write H(theta) or L(theta) and tag every parameter that depends on sequence-distant geometry (|i-j| > 5 contacts, helix packing). Show that each tagged parameter enters in one of three ways:
- (i) a commuting or first-order term (high-field J, NOE rate matrix, DEER kernel);
- (ii) a single-particle or fixed-low-excitation term (excitons, multislice);
- (iii) a weak perturbation with epsilon = (tagged coupling)/(local coupling) < 0.1, which applies to ZULF 3hJ (<1 Hz) against 1J (90–140 Hz) and to bath hyperfine at >15 A against <10 A.

Also show that ZULF shares its parameter set {J_ij} with high-field first-order spectroscopy. If all tagged parameters fall in (i)–(iii), KILL is confirmed.

CPU confirmation (under 1 h, 22-spin state vector about 64 MB): place a nitroxide electron and 20 protons from an ESM-predicted 60-aa structure (DEP path) and compute the exact Hahn echo by Krylov propagation against CCE-2 and CCE-4. Compute the Fisher information of the exact echo about a rigid 1 A shift of a helix at >= 15 A from the label.

KILL if both hold:
- |F_exact - F_CCE2|/F_exact < 1%, or the CCE-2 echo matches within noise at SNR 100;
- the Cramer-Rao sigma for the shift at SNR 100 exceeds 1 A.

Run the CPU test only when the governor reports CPU below 85%. The machine was at 91% during this review.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
No break-even exists: the classical cost is polynomial and the information gain from a quantum forward model is about zero.

Classical costs at 60 aa:
- NOE full relaxation matrix: about 1e8 flops (milliseconds).
- 1H/15N spectra: restricted-state-space or tensor-train codes already handle ubiquitin (76 aa, >1000 spins).
- Exciton CD/IR: 1-exciton 120x120, 2-exciton about 7e3x7e3, seconds.
- Multislice 512^2 x 200 slices: about 27 s single-threaded under 91% background load (measured).
- Radical pair: exact converged at 47 spins (Lindoy 2020); tensor networks at 30–60 nuclei.
- DEER bath: CCE with about 2000 protons [recalled].

Quantum side:
- Even granting a zero-cost fault-tolerant Hamiltonian simulator, and accepting that shot noise grows only weakly (Walch 2026), the output is the same experimental observables that classical models already invert. It adds no fold-level parameters.
- Any residual hard part reduces to classical ensemble or label-rotamer sampling. That is QM-01 territory, INTERESTING-conditional at best and bounded by the quadratic ceiling (T5).
verdicts.novelty_note:
Scope: arXiv API title/abstract queries run on 2026-09-27, plus the literature-phase records; general web search was unavailable because the budget was exhausted. Within that scope, the search found no evidence of any study that claims or demonstrates fold-level protein structural information from quantum simulation of ZULF, EPR/DEER, radical-pair, optical/vibrational or diffraction forward models.

Nearest prior art:
- Quantum proposals: QABC (Sels et al. 2019, small molecules); trapped-ion ZULF (Seetharam et al. 2021, acetonitrile); few-spin radical-pair quantum algorithms (2022–2025); Google arXiv:2510.19550 (small molecules in liquid crystal, 'not yet beyond classical').
- Classical rebuttals: Kuprov 2007/2014, Savostyanov 2014, Fratus 2025, Lindoy 2020, Hino 2025.

The one modality with protein-scale many-body hardness and contact information is dense 1H dipolar networks in solids or oriented media. It belongs to QM-19/20/21 and is anticipated by O'Brien et al. 2022 (arXiv:2109.02163). It should not be credited to QM-22.

Recommend recording QM-22 in KILLBOOK with this rule: fold information lives in weak couplings, and weak couplings are classically perturbative.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 (formulation only). None of the six modalities has a separation at protein scale, even under a query model. The only known exponential-cost regimes are small, strongly coupled molecules, radical pairs with 40 or more significantly coupled nuclei if semiclassical and typicality methods fail, and hard ZULF J-graph dynamics. The first two are not protein-fold problems. For ZULF, relaxation limits the observable window to a short light cone (see evidence), which makes it classically tractable (INFERENCE, test below). For fold-level structure, the value term is about zero in every modality, so no information-theoretic advantage exists to prove.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. Using Babbush 2021 / Sanders 2020 assumptions (170 µs per Toffoli, one factory), every quantum forward evaluation takes months to millennia. The best classical method takes 0.5 s to hours, or the output carries no tertiary-fold information. No hardware advantage: the NMR/EPR/EM sample is already the physical analog simulator, and it measures about 1e17 spins per shot where a qubit register gives one ±1 outcome.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
ZULF is the one place where hardness is credible. At zero field there is no secular truncation, so every isotropic J coupling is 'strong'. A uniformly 13C/15N-labelled protein has a connected J graph. Elenewski, Camara and Kalev (arXiv:2406.09340; PRR 8, 013315, 2026) call ZULF spectra 'taxing for classical computation' and a promising early-fault-tolerant target, and they mention protein spectroscopy. Long-lived singlet-order states could extend the observation window past the T2 light cone. Radical pairs with 40 or more anisotropically coupled nuclei may defeat Schulten-Wolynes-type semiclassics.

Rebuttal:
(i) Even with an exact oracle for free, the isotropic ZULF Hamiltonian contains only through-bond J couplings. Tertiary contacts appear only as H-bond couplings of 0.2-0.9 Hz. The dihedral information in 3J(HN,Hα) is 2-10 Hz and Karplus-ambiguous. Both are already measured at high field with first-order, closed-form analysis (HNHA, h-bond HNCO), and they duplicate the (θ,τ) head. My linewidth estimate is 67-89 Hz (INFERENCE), which buries both.
(ii) Long-lived states are pair or few-spin by construction, so they are classically exact.
(iii) Radical-pair yields report FAD/Trp hyperfine tensors, not the backbone fold.
(iv) Every quantum forward evaluation costs about 1e10-1e14 Toffolis, and an inference loop needs at least 1e2-1e4 evaluations.

Honest residual: I did not read the Elenewski full text, so its resource numbers are unchecked. The ZULF classical-tractability claim is INFERENCE until the decisive test runs.
verdicts.evidence:
RESOURCE AUDIT
Scope: logical-level Toffoli counts. Rotations are about 25 Toffoli-equivalents each. Amplitude estimation (AE) is at ε = 1e-3, i.e. about 1e3 coherent repetitions (shot sampling would be 1e6). Timing is 170 µs per Toffoli [#433 Sanders 2020, arXiv:2007.07391; #434 Babbush 2021, arXiv:2011.04149], with 1 µs as an optimistic bound. Script: C:\Users\abena\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-abena-quantum-advantage-protein-folding\deded8ee-ac50-420b-a8f2-b349dc3a4fdc\scratchpad\qm22_audit.py (DERIVED arithmetic, plus classical timings MEASURED on one core of this machine under about 78% background load).

(1) ZULF, 60 aa, uniformly 13C/15N-labelled
- Size: about 830 spins, so about 830 system qubits plus about 15 SELECT ancillas plus coefficient registers, about 900 logical. At d ≈ 27 that is about 1.5-2e6 physical qubits.
- Hamiltonian: about 8e3 J terms, i.e. about 2.4e4 Paulis. λ ≈ 5e5 rad/s.
- Window: t ≈ 30 ms, so about 1.5e4 qubitisation steps at about 7.5e4 Toffolis each.
- Per (time point, geometry) with AE: 1.1e12 Toffolis, i.e. 6.1 yr at 170 µs or 13 days at 1 µs. A 30-point FID is 3.4e13 Toffolis: 182 yr at 170 µs, 1.07 yr at 1 µs.
- Oracle and state-preparation issues: the high-temperature mixed initial state needs typicality or DQC1-style estimators. Signal-to-variance scales poorly with the number of spins.
- Zero-field relaxation (INFERENCE; extreme narrowing, τc = 3-4 ns): b_HH/2π = 21.3 kHz and b_CH/2π = 23.3 kHz, giving a CH2 linewidth of about 67-89 Hz. That is far above 3J = 2-10 Hz and above 3hJ = 0.2-0.9 Hz.
- Observable window: t ≤ 1/(πΔν) ≈ 4 ms. J·t is 3.5 rad for the local 1J(CH) pair, 1.4 rad for 1J(CC), and 0.3-0.4 rad across the peptide-bond links (1J(C'N) ≈ 15 Hz, 1J(NCα) ≈ 11 Hz). Operator spreading therefore stops within about one residue. A residue-cluster expansion with 2^≤21-dimensional clusters should be accurate (INFERENCE).
- Homonuclear 1H alone gives no zero-field signal, because total I_z commutes with isotropic J.

(2) DEER / bath decoherence
- 2000 1H plus the electron is about 2001 logical qubits (about 4e6 physical).
- Echo over 50 times with AE: 1.5e14 Toffolis, i.e. 808 yr at 170 µs or 4.75 yr at 1 µs.
- CCE-2/4 [Yang & Liu PRB 78, 085315 (2008), not re-verified this session] runs about 6e4 pairs, or up to about 1e7 clusters of 64 dimensions, in seconds to hours on a CPU.
- The dipolar kernel is closed-form. Fold uncertainty comes from label rotamer ensembles (MMM/chiLife), which is classical sampling and reduces to QM-01, already killed at practical level: B* ≥ 1e10-1e11 evaluations per sample (research/theory/BREAK_EVEN.md §1).
- The Hahn-echo T_m has 1-2 parameters and is dominated by protons within about 6-10 Å, so the Fisher information about a distant helix shift is about 0.

(3) Radical pair (FAD-Trp)
- 30 nuclei is about 50-100 logical qubits (about 1e5 physical).
- 1 µs of evolution at 1 ns steps, times 30 nuclei × 9 anisotropic terms, AE, 10 field orientations: 6.8e10 Toffolis, i.e. 0.36 yr at 170 µs.
- Classical exact treatment is feasible up to n = 20-24 nuclei (state vector 67 MB-1.1 GB, Krylov plus typicality; one random state suffices because the trace-estimator variance is about 1/dim). At n = 30 it needs a node with about 350 GB, for hours. Semiclassical methods take seconds.
- Output: a few scalar yields that report chromophore hyperfine tensors, not backbone fold.
- Break-even would need n ≳ 40 significantly coupled nuclei and semiclassical failure. The fold value is nil either way.

(4) Multislice diffraction
- Measured: 512² grid × 200 slices takes 7.4 s in single-core numpy.
- First-quantised version: about 18 grid qubits. The cost is dominated by the projected-potential oracle, Ω(N_atoms) per slice: about 1e3 atoms × 1e3 Toffolis × 200 slices is 2e8 Toffolis, i.e. 9.4 h at 170 µs per propagation.
- Image readout to ε = 1e-2 needs about 512²/ε² shots: 5e17 Toffolis, 2.8e6 yr at 170 µs. Readout of Ω(grid) intensities erases any polylog gain.
- Single-particle linear Schrödinger dynamics has no many-body entanglement.

(5) Liquid high-field NMR
- Measured: the full-relaxation-matrix NOESY (450 protons, expm at 10 mixing times) takes 0.53 s.
- Weak-coupling secular H = Σ ω_i I_iz + Σ 2πJ_ij I_iz I_jz is diagonal, so spectra are first-order multiplets. Strong-coupling clusters have at most about 8-10 spins, which is exact classically.
- Classical rebuttals: Fratus et al. arXiv:2508.06448 (cluster approximation, linear in N; in NOVELTY_MEMOS); Edwards, Savostyanov, Welderufael, Lee, Kuprov, J. Magn. Reson. 243, 107-113 (2014), DOI 10.1016/j.jmr.2014.04.002 (title verified via Crossref; the '1000+-spin ubiquitin, Redfield' detail is from the task text, not re-verified).
- QABC: Sels, Dashti, Mora, Demler, Demler, arXiv:1910.14221, Nat. Mach. Intell. 2, 529-537 (2020) (verified via arXiv API). It targets small metabolite mixtures, not proteins.

(6) Optical, CD and IR
- Exciton manifolds are N = 60 (one-exciton) and 1830 (two-exciton), each a diagonalisation of about 1 s.
- Information content is 3-4 secondary-structure fractions (SESCA/DichroCalc, not re-verified this session), so native versus decoys with the same secondary structure should be indistinguishable (INFERENCE).

Cross-cutting
- All fold-level information in these modalities (NOE, RDC/PCS, DEER P(r), 3J, SS fractions) is extracted with classically polynomial forward models. That is information, not computation.
- The residual hard parts (conformer and label-ensemble averaging) are QM-01 sampling.
- The condition-C analogue holds: forward-model fidelity beyond the classical approximation does not transmit to structure accuracy.
- The oriented/solid dipolar case is excluded from QM-22 and handled in QM-19/20/21 (BREAK_EVEN.md §4, O'Brien 2022, arXiv:2109.02163).
verdicts.decisive_test:
Relaxation-enforced light-cone plus Fisher-information test for ZULF. ZULF is the only QM-22 modality where classical hardness at protein scale is credible. Run time is minutes to about 1 h on this CPU, under the governor.

Setup: uniformly 13C/15N-labelled Gly-Ala-Gly (about 21 spins), with literature J values: 1J(CαHα) 140, 1J(NH) -92, 1J(CαC') 55, 1J(CαCβ) 35, 1J(C'N) -15, 1J(NCα) -11 Hz, plus 2J/3J with Karplus 3J(HN,Hα)(φ), and an optional 3hJ(NC') of 0.2-0.9 Hz.

(a) Compute the exact zero-field FID, with sector-exact or Krylov propagation on a 2^21-dimensional state (about 32 MB) and one to four random typicality states. Compare it with a residue-cluster expansion (each residue exact, peptide-bond couplings included to second order) up to t_max = 1/(πΔν), for Δν ∈ {10, 30, 70, 90} Hz. The zero-field linewidth is estimated from dipolar Redfield rates at τc = 3-4 ns.

(b) Compute the Fisher information, at SNR 100 per acquisition, of the broadened spectrum with respect to φ (via 3J) and to the H-bond coupling. Compare it with the Fisher information of a first-order high-field HNHA analysis.

Kill is confirmed if both hold:
- the cluster-expansion error is below 1% of the signal over the whole window at Δν ≥ 30 Hz;
- the H-bond Fisher information is effectively 0 and the φ Fisher information is at most that of HNHA.

If the cluster error exceeds 5% at Δν ≤ 30 Hz and the extra information is non-zero, reopen ZULF only, as a QM-19-style information-gain problem.

The remaining modalities are already decided on paper by the resource table in the evidence field: classical cost 0.5 s to hours against 0.36-808 yr quantum, or fold value about 0.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Break-even condition: C_Q < C_C and ΔI_fold > 0, where ΔI_fold is the fold-coordinate Fisher information of the exact forward model minus that of the best classical approximation. Every modality fails at least one side.

| Modality | Quantum cost | Best classical | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZULF, 60 aa | ~1.1e12 Toffolis per (time point, geometry): 6 yr at 170 µs, 13 days at 1 µs; 30-point FID 182 yr / 1.1 yr; ~900 logical and ~2e6 physical qubits; inference needs ≥ 1e2-1e4 such evaluations, so ≥ 1e3 yr | Residue-cluster expansion, minutes (INFERENCE) | Both sides fail: hardness unlikely under the ~80 Hz relaxation-limited window, and ΔI_fold ≈ 0 because couplings are through-bond only |
| DEER bath, 2000 1H | 1.5e14 Toffolis, 808 yr | CCE, seconds to hours | Both sides fail; ΔI_fold ≈ 0 |
| Radical pair, 30 nuclei | 6.8e10 Toffolis, 0.36 yr | Exact on a 350 GB node for hours, or semiclassical in seconds | Crossover needs n ≳ 40 nuclei plus semiclassical failure, and the fold value is nil anyway |
| Multislice | 2e8 Toffolis (9.4 h) per propagation; 5e17 Toffolis (2.8e6 yr) with readout | 7.4 s measured | Fails on cost; no crossover asymptotically, since readout is Ω(grid) against classical O(grid log grid) |
| NOESY full relaxation matrix | No quantum target needed | 0.53 s measured | Classical is complete |
| Exciton CD/IR | No quantum target needed | About 1 s | Classical is complete |

Conclusion: the crossover is infinite because the value term is zero for fold-level structure, and it is astronomically large even for the physics observables alone. The oracle and readout (potential loading, image readout, mixed-state estimation) erase any gain where one exists.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 (formulation only). No protein-relevant separation exists for any modality in QM-22. Generic BQP-hardness of spin time evolution does not carry over, because in each modality the fold-informative observables sit in classically closed-form sectors: the first-order multiplets, the N-dim NOE relaxation matrix, the RDC/DEER kernels, the one-exciton manifold and linear-wave multislice. The sectors that are genuinely hard carry almost no fold information: ZULF J-graphs (covalent topology), bath echo envelopes (local proton density) and radical-pair hyperfine dynamics (a few scalar yields).
verdicts.level_practical: L0 for proteins. All hardware NMR demos are small molecules validated against classical references: Burov et al. arXiv:2512.14513 (34 spins, IBM/IonQ), Stadler et al. arXiv:2609.17102 (21-spin effective model, H2) and Seetharam et al. Sci. Adv. 2023 (4 qubits). At most L1 for small molecules; none reaches a protein or a fold-level observable.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
(1) Elenewski, Camara and Kalev (arXiv:2406.09340 v2, 2025) estimate resources for 211 protein spin networks: ubiquitin, VDAC, P7, MBP. They conclude that ZULF protein spectra form one molecule-spanning, classically hard cluster, simulable with a few hundred logical qubits and fewer than 1e12 T-gates ("days"). With weak alignment the fold-informative RDCs enter the coherent Hamiltonian.

Rebuttals:
- (a) They set t_max = T2 = 1 s "as a compromise across molecular scales". My zero-field extreme-narrowing dipolar estimate on the 629 protons of 1UBQ_H (tau_c 4.1 ns) gives a median 1H R2 of about 193 s^-1: T2 ≈ 5 ms, linewidth ≈ 60 Hz (10–90% range 77–332 s^-1). Internal-motion order parameters or deuteration might recover about 2–10x. That is still 20–200x short of 1 s.
- (b) Given that, fold information is lost. In an 8-spin 13C/15N backbone fragment with an exact ZULF propagator, switching a trans-H-bond coupling hJ(N–C') from 0 to -0.6 Hz (tertiary information) changes the oscillating signal by 4.4e-2 at T2 = 1 s, 4.6e-4 at 50 ms and 8e-6 at 5 ms. A helix-to-strand phi change through 3J(HN,HA) gives 0.13, 2.6e-2 and 1.5e-3 at the same T2 values. At a realistic T2, detecting the tertiary coupling needs per-trace SNR of about 1e5.
- (c) Short T2 also means J_max × t_max ≈ 140 Hz × 15 ms ≈ 2 cycles. Light cones stay small, and classical cluster methods converge (Fratus et al. arXiv:2508.06448: linear-scaling cluster solver valid "throughout, and even somewhat beyond" typical regimes).
- (d) The RDC information is obtained classically, in closed form, from high-field IPAP-type experiments. ZULF plus quantum would only substitute one instrument for another; it adds no computational advantage.

(2) A second counterargument: these modalities are new information sources, which satisfies DNR-16 for information. True, but that information is already extracted by classical closed forms. What is left is conformational and label-ensemble averaging, which reduces to QM-01 sampling, already killed at the practical level (T2/T3/T5, break-even of at least 1e12 classical steps).

(3) What survives: the one spin setting where through-space, fold-informative couplings are also the strong coherent (hard) couplings is static or oriented 1H dipolar networks. That is H-C1 / Program C (O'Brien et al. PRX Quantum 2022), which is outside QM-22. Quantum-enhanced measurement in low-dose EM (Okamoto arXiv:2604.11303) is sensing, not forward-model computation, and is also out of scope.

IN-SESSION DERIVATIONS (single-thread, idle priority, <15 s CPU total; scripts in the scratchpad: qm22_checks.py, zulf_toy.py)

- **Zero-field 1H dipolar R2 on 1UBQ_H (629 H):**
  - 60 aa (tau_c 3.3 ns): about 155 s^-1, linewidth about 49 Hz.
  - 76 aa (tau_c 4.1 ns): about 193 s^-1, about 61 Hz.
  - 150 aa (tau_c 8 ns): about 376 s^-1, about 120 Hz.
- **ZULF fold sensitivity:** 8-spin toy with exact propagation, results as in the counterargument.
- **Full-relaxation-matrix NOESY:** all 629 protons, one expm, 172 ms CPU.
- **Multislice:** 512^2 grid × 200 slices, 7.9 s CPU on one thread.
- **Amide-I excitons:** two-exciton eigh at n = 60 (dim 1830) takes 2.4 s. The one-exciton problem at n = 300 is trivial.

STRUCTURAL REASON

In isotropic solution the coherent (hard) couplings are through-bond J couplings. These are fixed by covalent topology and are fold-invariant, except 3J (local dihedrals, already in the (theta,tau) head) and sub-Hz hJ. The through-space, fold-informative couplings enter only through tumbling-averaged relaxation (N-dim, closed form) or as about 1e-3 RDCs. So "hard" and "fold-informative" are separated by the physics, not by accident. The same pattern holds per modality: DEER (hard bath vs closed-form distance kernel), radical pairs (hard hyperfine dynamics vs a few scalar yields over about 6 geometric DOF), optical (at most about 2–6 SS components per SESCA), and diffraction (linear single-particle propagation).

PRIOR-EVIDENCE MAPPING

- DNR-16 is satisfied on information, but that information is classically interpretable.
- The condition-C analogue (DNR-08) fails by construction: fitting the hard sector does not transmit to structure accuracy.
- The residual ensemble averaging reduces to QM-01 (practically killed).
- Chemical shifts rest on closed-shell electronic structure, which the literature phase rated WEAK.
verdicts.decisive_test:
ZULF fold-information and cluster-truncation test on 1UBQ. ZULF is the only modality in QM-22 with a published protein-scale quantum resource claim. The test takes minutes on one core.

1. **Inputs.** For 13C/15N-labelled backbone fragments of 12–16 spins, take all 1J, 2J and 3J couplings (standard values; Karplus 3J from 1UBQ phi) plus hJ(N,C') for every backbone H-bond in 1UBQ. Take per-nucleus T2 from the zero-field dipolar estimate (median about 5 ms; also run 2x and 10x for motion or deuteration).
2. **Signal.** Compute the exact ZULF signal with Krylov or sector evolution out to 3 T2.
3. **Fisher information.** Compute it per shot at SNR 100 for (a) the tertiary parameters (the hJ on/off pattern, i.e. which H-bonds exist) and (b) the local phi, relative to (c) the 1J nuisance parameters.
4. **Cluster adversary.** Compare against a Fratus-style cluster approximation (clusters of at most 6–8 spins, couplings under 5 Hz cut).
5. **Kill confirmed if** tertiary FI is below 1e-4 of total FI and the cluster error is below the noise floor at physical T2.
6. **Reopen QM-22's ZULF branch only if** tertiary FI exceeds 1e-2 and the cluster error exceeds noise at a T2 achievable by deuteration.

The on-paper 8-spin version already gives a tertiary signal change of 8e-6 at 5 ms. All other modalities are already closed by published classical methods and need no new experiment. Record QM-22 in the KILLBOOK and route the only live spin sub-branch (static or oriented dipolar networks) to H-C1.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Elenewski et al. put the quantum cost at a few hundred logical qubits and fewer than 1e12 T-gates (days) at t_max = 1 s. At physical T2 of about 5 ms the qubitised cost (which scales with lambda × t) drops by about 200x. The classical cost collapses as well: J_max × t_max ≈ 2 cycles, so cluster or Pauli light cones stay small and linear-scaling solvers converge. The quantum run becomes cheap, but the classical one is cheaper, and the fold-level output is about 1e-5 relative. Fold-informative classical forward models are also cheap on this CPU:
- full-matrix NOESY for 629 protons: 0.17 s
- multislice 512^2 × 200 slices: 8 s
- two-exciton amide-I at 60 aa: 2.4 s

None of this sets a break-even in the protein regime. Simulator runtimes here are not quantum runtimes.
verdicts.novelty_note:
Low novelty. The nearest prior art is:
- Elenewski et al. 2024/25: protein ZULF resource estimates, with no analysis of how much structural information the spectra carry.
- O'Brien et al. 2022: ubiquitin dipolar learnability, now Program C.
- Sels et al. 2020: QABC, small molecules.
- Fratus et al. 2025: classical rebuttal for liquid NMR.
- Lam & dos Reis 2026: the quantum-multislice authors concede there is no full-image advantage.

Scope of my search: arXiv API abstract searches (2019–2026) plus Crossref. No general web search was possible (budget exhausted). Under that scope, the search found no evidence of any work testing whether the classically hard sector of protein ZULF, DEER-bath, radical-pair, optical or diffraction forward models carries fold-level (tertiary) structural information.

QM-22's defensible contributions are therefore:
- (i) a negative consolidation: in isotropic solution, hardness and fold information are separated by the physics, not by accident;
- (ii) one specific, checkable critique: protein ZULF estimates assume T2 = 1 s against a dipolar estimate of about 5 ms, which cuts the tertiary signal by about 5000x in the toy model.

Point (ii) is worth writing up as a short note if the 1UBQ decisive test confirms it. It is not a quantum-advantage candidate.

title: Genuinely quantum-mechanical structural subproblems: strongly correlated metal cofactors (FT QPE for active-site protonation/ligand structure) and nuclear quantum effects in H-bond networks (digital Gibbs or analog emulation)
merged_from: physics P8 (metal cofactors: FT QPE energies/properties for active-site structure), physics P9 (nuclear quantum effects in H-bond networks), wild 'Analog quantum simulation of nuclear quantum effects in protein H-bond networks (and analog polymer emulators)'
summary: Q: (a) which protonation, ligand and oxidation-state structure of multi-metal sites (FeMoco E-states, P-cluster, OEC S-states, Fe-S, P450 Cpd I) matches crystallographic and EPR/ENDOR/Moessbauer data? (b) do proton delocalisation / low-barrier H-bonds (KSI, GFP pockets, proton wires) change stable H-bond geometry, tautomer or protonation state? Quantum: (a) qubitised QPE with THC block encoding for low-lying energies and properties; (b) thermal-state preparation of the quantum nuclear Hamiltonian, or analog simulators/annealers as emulators. Mechanism: (a) dense near-degenerate spin ladders of up to 8 antiferromagnetically coupled centres; QPE cost poly(orbitals)/eps given overlap, a polynomial precision advantage with no generic exponential (Lee et al. 2023); FeMoco 76-orbital model solved classically in ~23 h on Frontier vs ~8.6 h quantum estimate (Zhai et al. 2026); DMRG mapped the P-cluster. (b) Equilibrium structure of distinguishable nuclei is a positive-weight imaginary-time path integral, so no sign problem: PIMD/PIGLET costs ~P = 6-32 x classical MD; real-time coherent tunnelling decoheres in fs-ps and is kinetic; effect sizes ~0.01-0.05 A. Speedup: (a) polynomial precision; (b) none-known. Oracle: (a) ~1e9-1e10 Toffoli per QPE at FeMoco scale, ~4M physical qubits, overlap is the crux, active space chosen classically; (b) needs a PES oracle that duplicates classical inputs; analog mapping uncontrolled, temperature uncontrolled. Competitor: DMRG/DMRG-NEVPT2, SHCI, AFQMC, BS-DFT, QM/MM quantum refinement (Ryde group); PIMD/RPMD/instantons with ML potentials (i-PI, OpenMM RPMDIntegrator), grid diagonalisation, PERM/Wang-Landau for polymer emulators. Info vs comp: both are sub-0.1 A chemistry below the built-chain RMSD endpoint's resolution; DE-7 measured energy accuracy is not the fold bottleneck (AMBER in-band rho 0.000). S29-S33: matrix M14 WEAK / out of scope for (a); M8 KILLED covers the analog-emulator branch of (b); digital NQE Gibbs sampling reduces to the M1 family. Kill: (a) DMRG/AFQMC energy differences between candidate states converge to < 1-2 kcal/mol vs the gap, or BS-DFT and DMRG geometries differ by < 0.05 A; (b) sign-free path integral (true by construction) and PIMD-classical heavy-atom shifts << 0.1 A, cost polynomial in beads and protons. Test: PySCF + block2 DMRG-CASCI on [2Fe-2S](SCH3)4 (~(30e,20o), M = 500-2000) for two protonation variants; audit FeMoco E4 / OEC S3 claims; OpenMM RPMD (16 beads) vs classical MD on a beta-hairpin or KSI fragment; double-well proton grid vs PIMC P = 4-64. < 1 day each. Track: B fault-tolerant (a) / D (b). Prior: low for protein structure; low-medium for metal-site chemistry (out of the fold endpoint).
dead_reason: M14 is WEAK/out of scope, not KILLED; only the analog-emulator sub-branch of (b) falls under M8 KILLED.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for the protein-structure endpoint. Branch (a), metal-site energies: L1 at most. Qubitised QPE with THC or spectrum amplification has a rigorous cost of O(lambda/eps) block-encoding calls given an overlap, but there is no proven separation from DMRG/CC/AFQMC. Lee et al. 2023 (Nat. Commun. 14, 1952, DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-37587-6) find no evidence of a generic exponential advantage. The only provable separation is against exact diagonalisation, which is the wrong comparator. Branch (b), nuclear quantum effects (NQE) in H-bonds: L0, because there is no mechanism. The equilibrium density of distinguishable nuclei is a positive-weight imaginary-time path integral with no sign problem. The P-bead discretisation error falls as O((beta*hbar*omega)^2/P^2), so classical PIMC/PIMD is polynomial in beads and protons. The best a digital quantum Gibbs sampler could offer is the generic quadratic mixing speedup (M1 family, already covered by T5's quadratic ceiling), and that needs PES oracle calls at least equal to the classical ones.
verdicts.level_practical: L0 for both branches. (a) At the largest biological instance (FeMoco, 7Fe+Mo, 113e/76o), classical methods have already reached the target: a CCSDTQ + DMRG composite with extrapolation reaches chemical accuracy (Zhai et al. 2026, preprint), and the quantum estimate is the same order of magnitude or slower (numbers in the break-even note). (b) Classical PIMD already "exactly include[s] nuclear quantum effects" for the flagship protein case, ketosteroid isomerase (KSI). My grid check shows P=32 reproduces the exact quantum proton density to 4e-4 Angstrom. Both effects are sub-0.1 Angstrom chemistry, far below the resolution of the built-chain RMSD endpoint (DE-7: energy accuracy is not the fold bottleneck).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The cheap classical workhorse for (a) is broken-symmetry DFT inside QM/MM, and it is unreliable. For the FeMoco E4 protonation isomers, TPSS and B3LYP relative energies differ by more than 300 kJ/mol (Cao, Caldararu, Ryde 2018). Sharma et al. 2014 showed that the Heisenberg double-exchange model undercounts Fe-S low-lying states by one to two orders of magnitude, and that same-spin levels are "dense on the scale of vibrational fluctuations". The multireference composite has only been converged on a dimer model (Zhai et al. 2023: B3LYP MAD 10 kJ/mol, max 13 kJ/mol) and on the FeMoco resting state. Hydride-bearing E4 and OEC S3/S4 could push DMRG past reach: variational DMRG at chemical accuracy already needs D~393,000 and ~4e9 core-hours at FeMoco scale, and the classical result depends on a heuristic extrapolation. QPE gives certified energies at the Heisenberg limit, and the overlap is good (dominant-determinant weight 0.447). So a constant-factor or polynomial fault-tolerant advantage for a few metal-site spin-ladder energetics stays plausible.

Rebuttal: (i) This is not protein structure computation. (ii) The instance family is bounded in size: biology stops at about 8 coupled metals and 76-120 valence orbitals, so no asymptotic regime exists for a polynomial speedup to pay off. (iii) The spin isomers are degenerate to within chemical accuracy (BS7/BS8 at +/-0.3-1.3 kcal/mol). The residual model error from active-space truncation, basis, dynamic correlation and protein geometry is about 1-3 kcal/mol, and QPE on a fixed active space does not remove it. (iv) What actually discriminates the structures is experiment (crystallographic density, EPR/ENDOR/Moessbauer), used through classical quantum refinement. That is information, not computation.

verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
(a) Break-even at the largest biological instance (FeMoco, 76 active orbitals):
- Quantum: 8.6 h per energy (spectrum amplification) on a fault-tolerant machine with about 1e6 physical qubits (older THC estimates: about 4M physical qubits and about 1e9-1e10 Toffolis).
- Classical, the practical route: CCSDTQ + DMRG extrapolation to chemical accuracy at 2.8e6 core-hours. That is about 46 s at ideal Frontier scaling, or days on 1e4 cores.
- Classical, a fully variational D=393k DMRG: 4.08e9 core-hours, i.e. 22.9 h on Frontier.
- So the quantum speedup is at most about 2.7x against the most expensive classical route and a slowdown against the practical one.

Biology caps cluster size at about 8 metals (76-120 valence orbitals, about 400 orbitals with dynamic correlation). So no asymptotic regime exists for a polynomial or precision speedup to pay off, and the constant factor is all there is. Studying a mechanism needs about 1e2-1e4 QM/MM geometries. At 8.6 h each, that is about 1 machine-year of fault-tolerant time per mechanism, and the classical CC composite scales the same way.

(b) Classical cost is P = 6 (PIGLET) to 32 (primitive) x classical MD, polynomial in beads and protons, with about 1e-3 Angstrom accuracy at P=32. A quantum thermal-state preparation for the nuclear Hamiltonian must query the same PES, so it cannot be cheaper per sample. Analog emulators or annealers were already killed under M8 (temperature and mapping are uncontrolled).
verdicts.novelty_note: Under the scope of arXiv plus Europe PMC fetches and the repo's 448-paper literature map (web search budget exhausted), the search found no evidence of a protein-structure question whose answer is limited by the classical cost of simulating metal-site electronic structure or nuclear quantum effects. It also found no quantum proposal for protein NQE that goes beyond sign-free path-integral sampling. Branch (a) duplicates the existing AA-3/M14 entry (WEAK / out of scope), and the 2026 FeMoco preprint weakens it further. Branch (b) reduces to M1 (digital Gibbs) and M8 (analog, KILLED). The KILLBOOK entry should record that NQE equilibrium structure is sign-free, so it has no mechanism for more than a quadratic speedup. Metal-cluster QPE should stay filed as a legitimate long-horizon chemistry lane outside this program's structure endpoint, not as a protein-structure advantage.

verdicts.level_theoretical: (a) Metal-cofactor fault-tolerant QPE. The only L6 support is generic, not tied to these instances. The guided local-Hamiltonian problem at 1/poly precision is BQP-complete (Gharibian & Le Gall, SIAM J. Comput. 52, 2023; repo bibliography #397). That result assumes a guiding state with 1/poly overlap supplied from outside and says nothing specific about FeMoco, P-cluster, OEC or P450. For the actual instances the supportable level is L3: published fault-tolerant resource estimates exist, and the speedup is a polynomial precision gain over exact diagonalisation. Lee et al. 2023 found no evidence of generic exponential advantage over heuristics. For the protein-structure endpoint the level is L0, because no mechanism carries a sub-1 kcal/mol active-space energy to backbone or built-chain structure (the brief's DE-7 result: energy accuracy is not the fold bottleneck). (b) Nuclear quantum effects: L0. I found no quantum speedup mechanism. The equilibrium path integral for distinguishable nuclei has positive weights, and the proton exchange correction is negligible at 300 K (derived below), so classical PIMD/PIGLET is polynomial.
verdicts.level_practical: (a) At best L1, and only for the electronic energy of one fixed candidate state. At FeMoco-LLDUC scale the per-state cost is about equal to classical when the classical side has S = 1e3 cores and the quantum side has one factory. Classical methods have already delivered this benchmark (Zhai et al. 2026, preprint). For assigning structures (protonation or ligand isomers times broken-symmetry spin isomers), the quantum cost at R = 1 factory is 3 to 9,400 years, so L0 for protein structure. (b) L0, KILL: the quantum machine cannot finish even one coherent evaluation of the potential-energy surface in the time a converged classical PIMD run takes.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The strongest pro-quantum case is branch (a):
- For one fixed state at FeMoco-LLDUC scale (76 orbitals, 113 electrons), the break-even is only about 1x, not astronomical. The quantum estimate is 8.6 h (spectrum-amplified QPE, assuming O(1) overlap). Classically, UCCSDTQ takes about 4e4 core-hours, which is about 40 h on 1e3 cores, and variational UDMRG takes 22.9 h on Frontier.
- The broken-symmetry initial-state overlap is good (up to about 0.45), so state preparation is not the crux.
- Scaling favours quantum as active spaces grow. UCCSDTQ costs about N^10; THC or spectrum-amplified QPE Toffolis grow roughly as N^2.5 to N^3 (my inference). Doubling the orbitals therefore moves the ratio about 100x toward quantum.
- With R = 10 to 100 factories, quantum would be about 10 to 80x faster per state.
- Goings et al. 2022 explicitly call large P450 Compound I active spaces a "potential quantum advantage problem".
- Where the protons and ligands sit on a metal cluster is genuine atomic structure.

Why this does not rescue the candidate:
1. Zhai et al. 2026 report that the difficulty "lies not in the description of intrinsically multi-configurational effects, but the correct ranking of many competing, but largely single-configuration, states". That is the regime where cheap single-reference classical methods work. QPE gives no speedup in enumerating the candidates: each candidate needs its own run, so cost is linear in K.
2. Structural assignment is limited by model error, not by active-space error. Truncating the active space, the QM/MM environment, zero-point and thermal corrections, and empirical calibration of Mössbauer and hyperfine data each contribute 1 kcal/mol or more (Zhai's own error bar is ±1.25 kcal/mol, with several spin isomers degenerate inside it). So sharper model energies do not carry through to the assignment, the same pattern as the within-target rho of -0.08 in the predecessor work.
3. Adding classical dynamic correlation on top of QPE (for example NEVPT2) needs the 3-RDM or a contracted 4-RDM read out of the quantum computer. That readout costs 7e2 to 7e4 years even with R = 1000.
4. The best case needs about 1.5e7 extra physical qubits for 100 factories, on top of 4 to 4.6 million.
5. None of this reaches the backbone or built-chain endpoint.

verdicts.level_theoretical: Protein-structure endpoint: L0 (a formulation only). There is no mechanism linking a better correlated-site energy or a nuclear-quantum ensemble to fold or backbone accuracy, and DE-7 measured energy accuracy as not the bottleneck (AMBER in-band rho 0.000). Sub-question (a), metal-site electronic structure taken as chemistry: resource-normalised fault-tolerant estimates against DMRG exist on paper (Goings et al. 2022 for P450; Zhai et al. 2026 for FeMoco), which is about L3 on paper. There is no L6 separation: QPE is efficient only given an inverse-poly overlap, and Lee et al. 2023 find no generic exponential advantage. Any advantage is polynomial (precision or runtime), and on the flagship instance the estimate is about 2.7x in wall-clock (8.6 h hypothetical fault-tolerant vs 22.9 h on Frontier). Sub-question (b), nuclear quantum effects on H-bond geometry and protonation: none. The equilibrium ensemble of distinguishable nuclei is a sign-free imaginary-time path integral, so classical PIMD costs P (6 to 32 beads) times the PES cost, which is polynomial. The only quantum lever left in (b) is the accuracy of the PES, and that collapses into (a).
verdicts.level_practical: Protein structure: L0. Chemistry sub-question (a): at most L1. Hardware demonstrations on exactly the proposed systems are classically matched: Sycamore on nitrogenase Fe-S cluster models (Tazhigulov et al. 2022), and IBM SQD on [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] with up to 77 qubits and 10,570 gates (Robledo-Moreno et al. 2024). Neither shows a load-bearing quantum component against DMRG. Fault-tolerant estimates are falling: about 1e10 T gates for FeMoco QPE; 89k noisy superconducting qubits for under a month on a 108-spin-orbital FeMoco model (Low et al. 2026); about 1e5 physical qubits and days to weeks for 20–50 orbitals (Kanasugi et al. 2026). No such machine exists. Sub-question (b): L0, and KILL. Analog emulators are already KILLED under M8, digital Gibbs sampling reduces to the M1 family, and classical ab initio PIMD already answers the headline question (KSI).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
(1) Sub-question (a) is limited by the model and by information, not by computation, the same failure mode as S29–S33. Zhai et al. (arXiv 2601.04621v2) find several spin-isomer candidates degenerate to chemical accuracy inside the FeMoco model. Their QM/MM protein environment leaves the low-energy landscape "qualitatively unchanged". Choosing among near-degenerate states is limited by errors in active-space truncation, basis, geometry and environment (at least about 1 kcal/mol). An exact QPE eigenvalue of a truncated Hamiltonian therefore cannot decide "which protonation or oxidation state matches EPR/ENDOR/Mossbauer". Classical DMRG plus high-order CC extrapolation already ranks the states. Per the paper's Frontier-throughput estimates, extrapolation costs about 46 s and a two-sweep variational UDMRG (D=393,000) about 22.9 h, against a cited 8.6 h fault-tolerant QPE estimate. That is a polynomial gap of at most about 2.7x, on hardware that does not exist.
(2) The candidate brief says sub-question (b)'s effects are only about 0.01–0.05 Å. That undersells them: in KSI, nuclear quantum effects lower the Tyr57 pKa by 3.8 +/- 0.5 units (6.3 vs about 10.1 for classical nuclei), which is a discrete protonation-state change. But classical ab initio PIMD (B3LYP-D3/6-31G*, 6 beads, 47–68 QM atoms, >52k MM atoms, 1.1 ps/day on 6 GPUs) got this right. It matched the experimental excess isotope effect (0.50 simulated vs 0.57 +/- 0.16 measured). That removes any role for a quantum sampler.
(3) Neither sub-question moves the program's endpoint. Heavy-atom shifts outside the metal's first shell sit below crystallographic coordinate error (about 0.1–0.2 Å). Single-structure fold accuracy at 9–60 aa is information-limited, not energy-limited (DE-7).
Best case for the candidate: correlated active sites are the one place in protein science where electronic structure is plausibly beyond classical methods (Goings et al. 2022 call larger P450 models a "potential" advantage problem). X-ray diffraction is nearly blind to hydrogen positions and prone to photoreduction. So it is a legitimate quantum-chemistry lane, but not a protein-structure one.
