verdicts.decisive_test:
A paper audit of the value of a perfect oracle, followed by one 8-core confirmation run.

Step 1: grant sub-question (a) a free, exact electronic-structure oracle (active-space FCI) for the K candidate states of one real question, for example the FeMoco E4 hydride and protonation placements or the OEC S3 water insertion. Take the model-error budget from Zhai 2026 and Goings 2022: active-space truncation, basis, geometry and QM/MM environment. Then answer two questions.
(i) Does the top-2 candidate gap exceed the model error (at least about 1–3 kcal/mol)?
(ii) Does choosing among the candidates move any heavy atom outside the first coordination shell by more than about 0.1–0.2 Å (the crystallographic coordinate error), or any Calpha by more than 0.1 Å?
If (i) fails, even a perfect QPE cannot adjudicate the spectroscopy. If (ii) fails, the question is irrelevant to protein structure computation. The expected outcome is that both fail.

Step 2, confirmation within the 95% ceiling (about 2 GB RAM): run PySCF + block2 DMRG-CASCI (30e,20o) on [2Fe-2S](SCH3)4 in two protonation variants (bridging S-H vs terminal thiol) at BS-DFT-relaxed geometries. Use M = 500, 1000 and 2000 with a truncation-error extrapolation, and in parallel measure the BS-DFT heavy-atom displacements between the variants.
KILL (a) for this program if the extrapolated gap converges to within 0.5 kcal/mol in under about 1 day, or if displacements beyond the first shell are below 0.1 Å.

For (b), about 10 minutes in NumPy: compare 1-D proton double-well grid diagonalisation with PIMC at P = 4–64, at O-O distances of 2.45–2.65 Å. This shows convergence of <x^2> and of the transfer probability that is polynomial in P and sign-free.
KILL (b) formally, citing Wang et al. 2014 (the KSI pKa shift was reproduced by classical AI-PIMD at 6 beads).
verdicts.novelty_note: This is not new relative to the program: it is M14 (WEAK / out of scope) plus M8 (KILLED) and the M1 family. It is also not new in the literature. Correlated-cofactor QPE with THC or double-factorised block encodings: Reiher 2017, J. Lee 2021, Goings 2022, Oumarou 2022, Rocca 2024, Low 2026, Kanasugi 2026, Khinevich 2026. Fe-S clusters on quantum hardware: Tazhigulov 2022, Robledo-Moreno 2024. Classical rebuttals: Lee 2023, Zhai 2026. Nuclear quantum effects on quantum computers via NEO: Kovyrshin 2023, Nykanen 2023, Cabral/Pavosevic/Hammes-Schiffer 2025. Classical PIMD of enzyme H-bond networks: Wang et al. 2014; Kapil group 2025. Within the arXiv API, PMC and repository-bibliography queries done this session, the search found no paper that connects correlated-cofactor QPE or quantum nuclear-quantum-effect sampling to a protein-structure (fold or backbone) endpoint. Coverage is partial because the web-search budget was exhausted, and the absence is itself consistent with DE-7. One correction to the candidate brief: nuclear quantum effects are not only sub-0.1 Å effects. They can flip protonation states (4 pKa units in KSI). That makes them relevant to active-site chemistry, but they remain classically tractable.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note: (a) Flagship instance: classical variational UDMRG (D=393,000) takes about 22.9 h on Frontier, a machine that exists, and the classical extrapolation protocol about 46 s. The hypothetical fault-tolerant QPE estimate (sum-of-squares spectral amplification, 1 kcal/mol) is 8.6 h on a machine that does not exist. That is at best about a 2.7x polynomial wall-clock gain. The physical-qubit requirement fell from about 4M (THC, 2021) to 89k over less than a month (2026 dense surface code), still at about 1e10 T gates. The model-error floor is at least about 1 kcal/mol, and the spin isomers are degenerate within it, so extra precision buys nothing. The effect on protein-structure RMSD is 0 (DE-7). (b) Classical PIMD costs about P = 6–32 times the PES cost, or less with ring-polymer contraction or PIGLET (unverified this session). The quantum cost would add state preparation for a thermal state of a PES that must itself come from classical inputs. There is no break-even because there is no speedup mechanism.

title: Quantum sensing and metrology as a new per-target information source: quantum-memory / Heisenberg-limited single-molecule NV-NMR, and multi-pass / interaction-free electron microscopy
merged_from: physics P6 (quantum-memory learning from nuclear-spin quantum data, NV sensing), wild 'Quantum-memory learning from single-molecule spin sensors', wild 'Interaction-free and multi-pass quantum electron microscopy to lift the dose limit', priorart (g) metrology branch (Kruit QEM, interaction-free measurement)
summary: Q: since the endpoint is information-limited, can quantum measurement physics acquire more structural information per experiment or per unit radiation damage? (a) Determine one molecule's conformational state or a few inter-nuclear distances (e.g. which fold a metamorphic protein adopts) by nanoscale NV-diamond NMR with far fewer repetitions; (b) single-particle structures and heterogeneity below the ~40-50 kDa cryo-EM limit. Quantum: (a) quantum-memory learning with joint multi-copy measurements (Huang et al. Science 2022), Heisenberg-limited Hamiltonian learning (Huang-Tong-Fang-Su 2023), quantum-logic readout with a nuclear memory (Lovchinsky 2016), collective hypothesis testing; (b) coherent multi-pass phase accumulation and quantum-Zeno interaction-free detection (Kruit et al. QEM design; Juffmann multi-pass). Replaces: repeated single-copy readout + classical Bayesian estimation; single-pass phase-contrast TEM. Mechanism: (a) coherent accumulation gives error ~1/T_total (capped by T2) instead of 1/sqrt(reps); for nonlinear/non-commuting properties, learners that store copies and measure jointly need exponentially fewer experiments (information-theoretic), because single-copy measurement destroys the information before any computer sees it. But geometry learning is local, commuting zz-coupling Hamiltonian learning, already efficient with single copies + classical processing, so the exponential separation likely does not apply; sequential 'copies' of one molecule require static heterogeneity. (b) N passes accumulate N*phi at fixed damage, so SNR ~ sqrt(N) phi sqrt(D), and information per dose grows ~N until per-pass loss caps N_eff ~ 1/l (electron-optics N_eff UNVERIFIED; optical multi-pass shows 26 dB). Speedup: sample-complexity (a) / precision per dose (b); metrology, not computation. Oracle: none; physical requirements are coherent sensor-to-memory transfer with memory coherence >> experiment time (unrealised for biomolecules), and low-loss electron mirrors/cavities. Competitor: conventional NV-NMR with Bayesian inference (27-13C cluster imaging, Abobeih 2019), ensemble NMR, smFRET, DEER; phase plates, detector DQE, scaffolds/fiducials, microED, cryo-ET, AF2 + NMR/X-ray for small monomers. Info vs comp: pure information acquisition, consistent with H-002 (only new information moves the endpoint); claim category is quantum sensing, not computational advantage. S29-S33: meets DNR-16 by construction; SA/random-prior twins are meaningless, the twin is the optimal single-copy classical-processing protocol with equal experiments. Kill: classical Fisher information of the best single-copy measurement >= 0.5x the sensor state's QFI for geometric parameters and the task is local-Hamiltonian learning; two-copy vs single-copy Chernoff exponent ratio < 2x; restraint-value curve saturates at ~1 A noise; multi-pass N_eff < ~3, or even G = 10x information per dose fails to lift 20-30 kDa particles above the alignment threshold, or benefiting targets are already solved by prediction/NMR. Test: restraint-value curve on mid30/long40 (K in {5..50} ORACLE-labelled synthetic restraints, sigma 0.1-2 A, flat-bottom terms, 32 restarts); NV + 12-16-spin 1UBQ surface cluster QFI vs projective CFI and Bayesian experiment counts; quantum Chernoff single- vs two-copy; Henderson-style alignment-SNR simulation at 15/30/60 kDa, doses 10-60 e/A^2, G in {1..30} with loss model. < 1 day. Track: D hardware-realistic (+ C theory). Prior: low.
dead_reason: Information-acquisition mechanism outside all computational kills; satisfies DNR-16.

verdicts.level_theoretical: (a) Quantum-memory / collective NV learning: L0, formulation only. The claimed exponential sample-complexity separation provably does not apply to this task class. For one geometric parameter, a single-copy measurement reaches the full QFI (Braunstein–Caves). For two-hypothesis fold discrimination, the collective-to-single-copy Chernoff-exponent ratio is at most 2 for any pair of states. For the NV pure-dephasing states actually produced, the ratio is exactly 1.000, because the states commute. (b) Multi-pass / interaction-free TEM: L1 as a metrology claim under an idealised model. Information per dose gains about N up to N of about 1/(loss per pass), about 10x at 300 keV in 20 nm ice. It is not a computational advantage and not an entanglement advantage: Koppell & Kasevich 2022 saturate the dose-limited bound without entanglement, and the optical multi-pass analogue uses classical light. None of the charter's quantum-computational categories 1–6 is reached. At most this is a sensing/hardware claim.
verdicts.level_practical: L0 for both. (a) No single-protein structure or fold assignment by NV-NMR exists. In my toy model the cost is set by NV–nucleus distance (signal falls as r^-6 in the exponent), sensor T2 and readout efficiency, not by the measurement strategy. (b) No electron multi-pass microscope has been demonstrated (Juffmann et al.: 'a multi-pass TEM still has to be demonstrated'). The only published design runs at 10 keV and re-images to within 4 nm. At 10 keV in 20 nm vitreous ice the gain is G_max ≈ 1.3. That meets the candidate's own kill criterion N_eff < ~3.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument: Part (b) at 300 keV (or 100 keV) is a real order-of-magnitude gain in information per dose that no single-pass classical trick can reach. Zernike phase contrast is the single-pass optimum for weak phase objects, and Koppell et al. 2022 argue the quantum limit is at least 10x beyond aberration-free Zernike. With G ≈ 10, the Henderson-type alignment threshold (~38 kDa) would fall roughly as 1/G, to ~4 kDa. That would allow per-molecule heterogeneity analysis of unscaffolded 10–40 kDa particles. Ensemble NMR (averaged), smFRET (a few distances), scaffolds (perturbing) and AF2 (single structure) cannot fully replace this. So the kill of (b) rests on engineering (no 300 keV gated, aberration-compensating electron mirrors) and on scope (it is information acquisition, not computation, and the project's 1–7 kDa targets are already solved classically), not on physics. For (a), a memory advantage could reappear only if the quantity of interest were itself a non-commuting quantum property (for example nuclear-spin correlations or entanglement). Classical backbone geometry is not such a property.
verdicts.evidence:
ADVERSARY RESULTS (derivations run in scratchpad: ...\scratchpad\chernoff_check.py and ...\scratchpad\nv_cpmg.py).

(a1) Collective vs single-copy discrimination. The fidelity-achieving measurement gives Bhattacharyya coefficient = F, so the classical exponent xi_C ≥ -log F. Log-convexity of s ↦ Tr ρ^s σ^(1-s) together with Q ≥ F² gives xi_Q ≤ 2 xi_C. Numerically, xi_Q/(-log F) peaked at exactly 2.0000 over 450 random pairs (d = 2..16); the maximum occurs for pure states, where the true ratio is 1. Over 200 random mixed qubit pairs, the maximum xi_Q / xi_C(best projective) was 1.53. So the candidate's kill criterion (ratio < 2x) holds for every pair of states, whatever the hardware.

(a2) NV toy: 12 thermal protons, B0 = 0.05 T, CPMG resonant with the 1H Larmor frequency, 4 protons moved by 2–5 Å between fold A and fold B, T2_DD = 500 us, room-temperature readout efficiency 0.03 (assumed). The symmetric DD signal on an unpolarised bath is real, so both hypotheses' sensor states lie on one Bloch axis and commute. The collective/single-copy ratio is 1.000 in every configuration. Shots to 1e-3 error: 4e5 (~26 s) at 3 nm depth, 7.7e6–1.1e7 (~0.5–0.7 h) at 4 nm, 7.5e8 (~8 days) at 5 nm. The bottleneck is distance, T2 and readout, not quantum memory.

(a3) Heisenberg-limited scaling needs neither quantum memory nor entanglement:
- Higgins et al., Nature 450:393 (2007), arXiv 0709.2996 [verified]
- Huang–Tong–Fang, PRL 130:200403 (2023), arXiv 2210.03030: O(1/ε) total evolution time from single experiments [verified]
- Dutkiewicz–O'Brien–Schuster, Quantum 8:1537 (2024), arXiv 2304.07172: needs quantum control, advantage only quadratic, SQL→HL [verified]
- Duan–Feng–Ying, PRL 98:100503 (2007): perfect unitary discrimination by sequential use without entanglement [verified]
- Acín–Bagan–Baig, PRA 71:032338 (2005): adaptive individual measurements reach the collective error exactly for two pure states [verified]
- Calsamiglia et al., PRA 77:032311 (2008) [verified]

(a4) Where the memory separations actually hold. Huang et al., Science 2022, arXiv 2112.00778 [verified]. Chen–Cotler–Huang, arXiv 2111.05881 [verified]: Pauli estimation needs Ω(2^((n-k)/3)) samples without memory. These are shadow tomography, Pauli-magnitude and symmetry tasks, not few-parameter commuting-coupling estimation. Even if one applied, at n = 16 it bounds the gain at 2^(16/3) ≈ 40x, which is polynomial and below the memory-decoherence overhead. Nuclear-memory NV sensing is already standard single-copy practice. Abobeih et al., Nature 576:411 (2019), arXiv 1905.02095 [verified]: 27 13C spins, <80 mHz resolution, lattice spins at cryogenic temperature, not a molecule. Lovchinsky et al., Science 351:836 (2016) [not re-verified this session].

(b1) Juffmann, Koppell, Klopfer, Ophus, Glaeser, Kasevich, arXiv 1612.04931 [full text read]:
- 300 keV, 20 nm vitreous ice, λ_in = 350 nm, ~5.5% loss per pass
- best SNR at 12–16 passes (small protein), 4–8 passes along the thick axis because of phase wrapping
- idealised lossless, aberration-compensating mirrors
- 'a multi-pass TEM still has to be demonstrated'; the design re-images at 10 keV 'to within 4 nm'
- Koppell et al., arXiv 1904.11064: 10 keV design [verified]

(b2) My loss model. Information/damage = m² e^{-ml}(1-e^{-l})/(1-e^{-ml}). λ_in is scaled with an Egerton-type formula (approximate, from memory) and λ_el with 1/β². G_max:
- 300 keV: 10.6 (20 nm ice), 20.9 (10 nm ice)
- 100 keV: 6.0 (20 nm)
- 30 keV: 2.5 (20 nm)
- 10 keV: 1.31 (20 nm), 2.16 (10 nm)
These figures exclude mirror loss, aberrations and phase wrapping, all of which lower G.

(b3) Koppell et al., APL 2022, DOI 10.1063/5.0086148, arXiv 2201.09183: quantum limit ≥10x beyond Zernike [verified]. Koppell & Kasevich, arXiv 2203.10137: bound saturated without entanglement [verified]. Arxiv search (author Kasevich/Koppell; abstract 'multi-pass' AND electron) found no experimental electron multi-pass demonstration through 2026-09.

(c) Classical adversaries that already cover the targets:
- bulk NMR, X-ray and AF2/ESMFold for 9–60 aa and ≤30 kDa monomers
- smFRET and DEER for fold identity and distance distributions
- scaffolds/fiducials and microED below ~40 kDa
Henderson QRB 1995 (~38 kDa) and MINFLUX Å-distance work (Sahl et al., Science 2024) were NOT verified this session because the web-search budget was exhausted. Braunstein–Caves PRL 72:3439 (1994) is cited from memory.
verdicts.decisive_test:
Already run on paper and CPU, under 5 minutes; it decides the quantum question.

1. Bound the collective/single-copy discrimination exponent. The ratio is ≤ 2 for all states. For the NV symmetric-DD sensor states it is exactly 1, because the states commute. This triggers the candidate's own kill criteria (ratio < 2x; single-copy CFI = QFI).
2. Compute G_max(E, t_ice) from per-pass loss. The only designed MPTEM (10 keV) gives G ≤ 1.3–2.2, i.e. N_eff < 3.

Anything that remains is not a quantum-computation question:
- (i) The ORACLE-labelled restraint-value curve on mid30/long40 (K ∈ {5..50} synthetic distances, σ 0.1–2 Å, 32 restarts, a few CPU-hours) shows whether per-target information from any source moves the endpoint. Even a steep curve would be satisfied by classical NOE, DEER or smFRET restraints.
- (ii) For (b), the only thing that could reopen it is a physical demonstration: ≥100 keV gated mirrors with ≤10% loss per pass and Å-level re-imaging. That is out of scope for this repository.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note: (a) No break-even exists. A collective measurement saves 1.00x on commuting NV sensor states and at most 2x in exponent in general. A nuclear memory's real benefit is repetitive readout, up to about 1/η ≈ 30x at room temperature, and that is already a single-copy classical-processing technique. Single-copy fold discrimination costs about 4e5 shots (~26 s) at 3 nm depth, about 1e7 (under 1 h) at 4 nm, and about 7e8 (~8 days) at 5 nm. The protein must stay static on the surface throughout, which is the real practical limit. (b) The ideal G is ~10 at 300 keV in 20 nm ice, which would move the ~38 kDa alignment threshold to ~4 kDa (unverified Henderson scaling ∝ 1/G). The only designed instrument (10 keV) gives G ≈ 1.3, which would move it only to ~29 kDa. The project's targets are 1–7 kDa and are already solved classically.
verdicts.novelty_note: Literature coverage is limited: the web-search budget was exhausted, so only the arXiv API was checked. Within that scope the search found no evidence of: an experimental electron multi-pass microscope; quantum-memory (multi-copy) learning applied to biomolecular structure; or a collective-measurement advantage for estimating commuting dipolar couplings. The ≤2x Chernoff bound and the commuting-state argument are standard quantum-information facts applied here, not new results. The G(E, t_ice) table is my own rough estimate, not a published figure.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 as a quantum-over-classical advantage. (a) Quantum-memory NV-NMR: there is a derived no-go. The gain from joint or multi-copy measurement is exactly 1 in the unpolarized-nucleus regime, at most 1.39x in the polarized regime, and there is no Heisenberg scaling beyond T2. (b) Multi-pass or QEM TEM: the gain is a real metrology result. Information per damage event scales as G(N,l) = N^2 s^(N-1) l/(1-s^N) with s = 1-l, and the maximum is about 0.65/l. That puts it at roughly L1 as a sensing and instrument claim. It is coherent phase accumulation of a single particle, which has a classical-wave analogue (cavity-enhanced phase), so it is not a quantum-computational advantage and not an advantage from entanglement. None of CLAUDE.md claim categories 1-4 or 6 apply, and category 5 applies only in a stretched sense, because the device is a sensor, not a quantum computer.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. (a) Memory-assisted joint measurements on a biomolecule near a shallow NV have never been realised. Coherent sensor-to-memory transfer with i.i.d. "copies" of one molecule is a hidden oracle, and even if it were free it would buy at most 1.39x. (b) Multi-pass electron microscopy is at the design or prototype stage; I could not verify its current status this session. At the proposed ~10 keV operating energy, per-pass inelastic loss in vitreous ice alone is 0.36-0.60 for 10-20 nm of ice, which gives N_eff of 2-4 and G_max of 1.1-1.8. Even at the ideal G, the program's targets (9-60 aa, 1-7 kDa) are routinely solved by solution NMR and by AF2-class prediction, so the quantum necessity test gives "nothing disappears".
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
(1) Multi-pass TEM is physically sound. At 300 keV, with 10 nm ice and about 1% optics loss per pass, G_max is roughly 20-60 by my loss model. By Henderson-type scaling (M_min ~ 38 kDa / G), that would push the single-particle alignment floor to about 1-2 kDa and make single-molecule conformational heterogeneity of small, metamorphic or disordered proteins observable. That is information no ensemble method gives. It is the one element of QM-24 that is not bounded by a small constant.

Rebuttal: the gain is metrological and classical-wave in nature, not computational, and the idea is not original (Kasevich/Juffmann/Koppell multi-pass; Kruit QEM, about 2016-2019; citations recalled, not verified). The loss inputs (optics l, mirror aberrations, inelastic loss at the design energy) are unverified, and at 10 keV the ice alone caps G at 1.8 or less. Scaffold and fiducial methods and microED compete, and none of it moves the program's endpoint: the average structure of 9-60 aa chains, which classical NMR already provides.

(2) If the target nuclei are hyperpolarized (DNP, or NV-driven polarization) and several geometric parameters are estimated at once on the qubit sensor, collective measurement can in principle beat any single-copy measurement by the Gill-Massar factor P/(d-1), which is at most 3 for a qubit, and by the Holevo/SLD factor of at most 2. This is still a bounded constant, not a scaling. It is below the 2x Chernoff kill threshold for binary fold discrimination: at most 1.39 on my grid, and 1.0 with adaptive single-copy measurement for pure states (Brody-Meister). It is further eroded by memory-transfer fidelity: the net gain is ratio x F^(2k), which is 1.13 or less at F = 0.95, k = 2.
verdicts.evidence:
DERIVATIONS (script: C:\Users\abena\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-abena-quantum-advantage-protein-folding\deded8ee-ac50-420b-a8f2-b349dc3a4fdc\scratchpad\qm24_audit.py; it runs in about 1 minute on one core)

**(a1) Commuting-family no-go.** At room temperature, or with unpolarized nuclei (every biomolecular NV-NMR experiment to date), the nuclear projection is random in each round. The NV state after a secular A_zz coupling is rho = (I + cos(2 pi A T) X)/2, and it lies on one Bloch axis for every geometry. So states for different geometries commute. The quantum Chernoff exponent then equals the classical one for an X measurement, and QFI = CFI. The gain from quantum memory or joint measurement is exactly 1, and the kill criteria "CFI >= 0.5 QFI" and "Chernoff ratio < 2" are met by construction.

**(a2) Polarized, non-commuting case.** I computed the quantum Chernoff exponent xi_Q against the best fixed single-copy projective measurement over a grid: Bloch length r in {1, 0.9, 0.5, 0.2} and phase difference in {0.05, 0.3, 1, pi/2}.
- r = 1: ratio 1.20-1.25
- r = 0.9: ratio 1.28-1.39 (the maximum)
- r = 0.5: ratio 1.04-1.07
- r = 0.2: ratio 1.01

Adaptive single-copy measurement reaches the Helstrom optimum for pure states (Brody & Meister, PRL 76, 1 (1996)). Single-parameter CFI = QFI (Braunstein & Caves, PRL 72, 3439 (1994)). The multi-parameter gap is bounded by Gill & Massar (PRA 61, 042312 (2000)): for single-copy measurements, Tr(F_Q^-1 F_C) <= d-1. The Holevo bound is at most 2x the SLD bound (Albarelli, Tsang & Datta, arXiv:1911.11036). The exponential memory separations of Huang et al. (Science 2022, arXiv:2112.00778) and Chen, Cotler, Huang & Li (arXiv:2111.05881) need exponentially many non-commuting properties of a high-dimensional state. Here there is one sensor qubit and a few local, commuting geometric parameters. Local Hamiltonians are learnable efficiently from single copies (Haah, Kothari & Tang, arXiv:2108.04842).

**(a3) No Heisenberg scaling beyond T2.** The NV signal (a Z term) is parallel to its dominant dephasing (Z noise), so the Hamiltonian-not-in-Lindblad-span condition fails. Ancillas, memory and QEC then cannot restore 1/T_total scaling (Zhou, Zhang, Preskill & Jiang, Nat Commun 9, 78 (2018); Demkowicz-Dobrzanski, Kolodynski & Guta, Nat Commun 3, 1063 (2012)). Conventional repeated Ramsey or dynamical decoupling already reaches Var ~ 2/(T_total T2). The Heisenberg-limited learning of Huang, Tong, Fang & Su (PRL 130, 200403 (2023)) assumes coherence over T_total.

**(a4) Coupling and cost scale.**
- NV electron to 1H or 19F: 2.9 kHz at 3 nm, 0.63 kHz at 5 nm, 0.15 kHz at 8 nm.
- Intra-protein 1H-1H: 961 Hz at 5 Å, 120 Hz at 10 Å. 13C-13C: 61 Hz at 5 Å.
- Resolving intra-protein couplings needs the target's own T2 to be at least 1-10 ms. Densely protonated protein spins are dipolar-broadened, so only sparse labels work, which puts NV-NMR in the regime DEER and smFRET already cover.
- One NV-to-label distance at 1 Å precision at 5 nm (SNR about 17 on A), with T2 = 100 µs: 8.3e5 shots or about 85 s without memory; 1.9e4 shots or about 20 s with nuclear-memory repetitive readout; about 0.2 s at the projection limit.
- The memory's real benefit is about 44x fewer shots from lower readout noise (sigma_R 20 to 3). That technique is already the conventional twin (Jiang et al., Science 326, 267 (2009); Lovchinsky et al., Science 351, 836 (2016); Aslam et al., Science 357, 67 (2017)).

**(b) Multi-pass TEM.** Information per protein-damage event relative to single pass, with per-pass loss l:
- l = 0.01: G_max 64.8 at N = 159
- l = 0.03: G_max 21.6 at N = 52
- l = 0.10: G_max 6.5 at N = 15
- l = 0.30: G_max 2.2 at N = 4
- l = 0.50: G_max 1.33 at N = 2

Ice-only loss, scaling the inelastic mean free path as beta^2 from an anchor of about 350 nm at 300 keV (anchor unverified):

| Energy | 10 nm ice | 20 nm ice | 40 nm ice |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 keV | G_max 1.8 | G_max 1.2 | G_max 1.0 |
| 30 keV | 4.4 | 2.4 | 1.4 |
| 100 keV | 11.6 | 6.0 | 3.2 |
| 300 keV | 23 | 11.7 | 6.0 |

Adding 5% optics loss per pass gives G_max 1.0-1.7 at 10 keV and 4.2-8.4 at 300 keV.

Henderson-type floor M_min ~ 38 kDa / G (ideal) or 50 kDa / G (practical): 12.7-16.7 kDa at G = 3 and 3.8-5.0 kDa at G = 10. So the kill criterion "G = 10 fails to lift 20-30 kDa" is not met on paper. The kill criterion "N_eff < 3" is met at 10 keV. The program's targets are 1.0-6.6 kDa.

**Resource accounting (oracle, qubit and gate audit).**
- (a) needs 1 sensor qubit plus k = 2 memory qubits, 2k sensor-memory CNOTs per round and one Bell measurement. It needs no Toffoli or T factory and no fault tolerance, and classical Bayesian inversion takes under 1 CPU-second per restraint.
- The hidden oracles are:
  - free coherent sensor-to-memory transfer with memory T2 much longer than k times the round time;
  - i.i.d. copies of one molecule's state, which needs static heterogeneity and polarized nuclei;
  - free placement of the molecule within 5 nm of a shallow NV with T2 of at least 100 µs.

**Citations.** Babbush et al. 2021 (#434) and Sanders et al. 2020 (#433) are verified in the repository bibliography. Every sensing, metrology and TEM citation above is recalled from memory and was not verified this session (the web-search budget is exhausted, and these papers are not in the repository's 448-paper corpus). Henderson, Q Rev Biophys 28, 171 (1995); Abobeih et al., Nature 576, 411 (2019); Kruit et al., Ultramicroscopy 164, 31 (2016); Koppell et al., Ultramicroscopy (2019), 10 keV multi-pass TEM design; Juffmann et al., multi-pass microscopy, Nat Commun (2016 or 2017); and Putnam & Yanik, PRA 80, 040902 (2009) are all UNVERIFIED.
verdicts.decisive_test:
One test on paper and one CPU run of about 10 minutes, no pre-registration needed because it is a derivation.

**(1) Commutator test for (a).** Use the existing sector-exact code in src/qapf/nmr/spins.py on the NV plus a 12-16 spin 1UBQ surface cluster. Compute the NV reduced states rho_theta for geometries theta (distances perturbed by ±1 Å, and the two alternative folds of a metamorphic pair) under three nuclear initial states: (i) unpolarized, (ii) 10% polarized, (iii) fully polarized. Report:
- max ||[rho_theta, rho_theta']|| / ||rho||;
- QFI against the best adaptive single-copy CFI;
- two-copy and asymptotic quantum Chernoff against the single-copy classical Chernoff exponent.

KILL (a) permanently if the commutator is below 1e-3 in the unpolarized case, and the Chernoff ratio is below 2x and CFI/QFI is at least 0.5 in every case. The analytic results above predict ratios of 1.0 (unpolarized) and at most 1.4 (polarized).

**(2) Loss-limited G for (b).** Recompute G_max(E, ice thickness, optics loss) with a published inelastic mean free path for vitreous ice at 10, 100 and 300 keV, replacing my unverified 350 nm beta^2-scaled anchor. Then run a Henderson-style alignment-SNR simulation at 15, 30 and 60 kDa. This only decides whether (b) remains an out-of-scope instrument note; it cannot revive a computational claim.

The restraint-value curve on mid30/long40 (synthetic restraints K = 5-50, sigma = 0.1-2 Å) measures the value of new information. It is worth running for H-002, but it does not test quantum necessity, because NMR, DEER, smFRET and crosslinking can supply the same restraints classically.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
No fault-tolerant computation is involved, so the Babbush/Sanders Toffoli break-even model (170 µs per Toffoli) does not apply. The coherent processing is about 10 gates, and the whole cost sits in physical transduction and measurement count. The break-even quantity is the number of experiments, or the dose, per unit of information.

- **(a) Break-even for the joint-measurement protocol:** it beats adaptive single-copy measurement only if Chernoff ratio x F^(2k) > 1.
  - Unpolarized, commuting regime: the ratio is 1, so there is never a break-even.
  - Polarized regime: at a ratio of 1.39 or less, with k = 2, this needs F > 0.92. The maximum net gain is 1.13x at F = 0.95 and about 1.3x at F = 0.99.
  - This is against about 20-85 s per NV-to-label distance restraint with conventional methods, and those give only NV-to-label distances, not intra-protein ones.
- **(b) Break-even in dose:** G_max is about 0.65/l. Getting 3x or more needs per-pass loss l of about 0.2 or less, which requires 100 keV or more with ice of 20 nm or less and optics loss per pass of 5% or less (unverified). The 10 keV designs give G of 1.8 or less.
- **Endpoint relevance:** the program's 1-7 kDa targets need G of about 6-40 (ideal) to cross the alignment floor, and classical NMR already solves them. The component is not load-bearing under the quantum necessity test.
verdicts.novelty_note: Neither mechanism is original. Memory-assisted NV-NMR (repetitive readout 2009, single-protein detection 2016, nuclear-memory spectroscopy 2017) and multi-pass or interaction-free QEM electron microscopy (about 2009-2019) are established proposals. These citations are recalled, not verified this session. The repository's 448-paper corpus contains no sensing literature, and no web search was possible this session. So the only supportable statement is: the search, limited to the in-repo corpus, found no evidence of the commuting-family no-go being stated for biomolecular NV-NMR. That no-go says that for unpolarized nuclear targets, quantum-memory and joint-measurement learning gives exactly zero gain in Chernoff exponent or Fisher information. It is a direct corollary of standard estimation theory, so it is a useful kill note for KILLBOOK, not a result. Suggested KILLBOOK entry: QM-24(a) KILLED (derived; gain of 1.0 if unpolarized, 1.39 or less if polarized, no Heisenberg scaling past T2 by HNLS). QM-24(b): WEAK, out of scope as an instrument, not a computation; revisit only if a verified multi-pass electron microscope reports per-pass loss of 0.1 or less on vitreous specimens.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for any computational claim. (a) is refuted on paper. The candidate's claimed mechanism is exponential savings from quantum memory or joint multi-copy measurement. That does not apply to protein geometry, for two reasons. First, the target has a polynomial description: S29-S33 found a≡mu, about 3n-6 numbers per target, and local Hamiltonians are learnable with poly(n) single-copy samples (Anshu et al., arXiv:2004.07266). The proven exponential separations (Chen-Cotler-Huang-Li arXiv:2111.05881; Huang et al. Science 2022 arXiv:2112.00778; King-Wan-McClean arXiv:2403.03469) need property families of size about 2^n, as in shadow tomography, purity testing or Pauli-channel spectra. Second, for sparse-label or heteronuclear zz couplings the generators commute, so Im<d_i psi|d_j psi> = t^2 Im<G_i G_j> = 0. The Matsumoto/Ragy compatibility condition then holds, and single-copy measurements attain the QFI matrix, giving CFI/QFI = 1 (the kill threshold is 0.5). Two known folds are unitaries, and those can be discriminated perfectly by finitely many sequential single-probe runs without entanglement (Duan-Feng-Ying, quant-ph/0601150), so collective hypothesis testing gains at most a constant. What remains is Heisenberg (1/T) versus SQL (1/sqrt(reps)). That gap is only quadratic (Dutkiewicz-O'Brien-Schuster arXiv:2304.07172) and capped by T2. It is also already used by the classical twin, since conventional NV correlation spectroscopy with a nuclear memory reaches 13 Hz linewidths (Pfender arXiv:1610.05675) and single-Hz frequency estimates (Spohn arXiv:2503.18930). The dense-1H case with non-commuting flip-flops is not new: it is Program C (NM-1, O'Brien et al. PRX Quantum 2022), which is already being tested by C1. (b) There is a real sensing-category bound: the quantum limit on information per dose is at least 10x beyond aberration-free Zernike phase contrast (Koppell et al. arXiv:2201.09183), and simulations give about 10x less damage for single proteins (Juffmann et al. arXiv:1612.04931). That is prior-art metrology, a hardware/sensing claim outside this program's computation mission, not computational advantage.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. (b) The arXiv search found no experimental multi-pass TEM image and no electron interaction-free measurement; there are only designs and simulations (Kruit et al. arXiv:1510.05946; Juffmann 2016/17; Koppell et al. 10 keV design arXiv:1904.11064; Agarwal-Berggren-Goyal arXiv:1901.09702). N_eff for electron optics is unmeasured. (a) No single-protein structure (distances or fold state) from NV-NMR was found. The most advanced biomolecular results are the single-ubiquitin 2H/13C signal detected with quantum logic (Lovchinsky et al. Science 351:836, 2016, doi:10.1126/science.aad8022; signal only, no structure) and "a few molecules" of fluorinated DNA (Janitz et al. arXiv:2609.05570, Sept 2026). Three-dimensional spin maps exist only for 13C clusters inside diamond (27 spins, Abobeih arXiv:1905.02095; 50 spins, van de Stolpe arXiv:2307.06939), not for a protein on a surface. Coherent sensor-to-memory joint measurement across copies of a biomolecule has not been realised.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument: The best case for QM-24 is (b). H-002 says only new per-target information moves the endpoint, and (b) is the one component with real physics beyond the standard quantum limit per dose. Its ceiling is at least 10x (Koppell 2022), and phase plates cannot reach that because they only approach the Zernike SQL. A shot-noise alignment model, M_min proportional to (G*D)^(-3/4 to -1), puts the unscaffolded threshold at about 40 kDa for G=1, 13-18 kDa for G=3 and 4-7 kDa for G=10. That would open sub-40-kDa heterogeneous drug targets, a real protein-science bottleneck that today needs scaffolds (26 kDa with a scaffold, Chiu et al. Biochemistry 2021; sub-100 kDa reviews by Wentinck 2022, Harrison 2023 and Singh 2026). Rebuttal: (1) this is a microscope, not a computation, and falls outside the program's claim categories. (2) It is not original: Juffmann 2017 already claims single-protein imaging at about 10x less damage. (3) Nothing on this 8-core box can decide it. (4) Multi-pass scales the phase from ice and the protein alike, so vitreous-ice structural noise and beam-induced motion, which are not shot noise, probably bind before G reaches 10. (5) The program's instruments are 9-60 aa (about 1-7 kDa) and would need an ideal G of about 10-60, while no electron multi-pass has been demonstrated even at N=2. For (a) the best defence is fold-state identification of single metamorphic molecules. Sequential single-probe discrimination already achieves it in principle, and smFRET, DEER and ensemble NMR chemical shifts classify folds routinely.
verdicts.evidence:
Checks against inherited evidence and the literature phase:
- DNR-16/K-012 are satisfied by construction, since this is a new information source. No DNR-01..18 entry applies because no computation is involved. The quantum-necessity test fails for (a): with memory and joint measurement removed, single-copy NV plus Bayesian processing keeps the full QFI (derivation above).
- The literature phase's "at most quadratic" finding has an exact learning-theory analogue: Heisenberg vs SQL is quadratic (Dutkiewicz-O'Brien-Schuster 2024, verified arXiv:2304.07172; Huang-Tong-Fang-Su verified arXiv:2210.03030).
- (a) collapses into the running Program C for dense 1H (NM-1).

Physical numbers (computed):
- The 1H-1H dipolar coupling is 120.1 kHz*A^3/r^3: 15.0 kHz at 2 A, 4.45 kHz at 3 A, 0.96 kHz at 5 A.
- The NV-1H coupling is 79.1 kHz*nm^3/r^3: 9.9 kHz at 2 nm, 2.9 kHz at 3 nm, 0.63 kHz at 5 nm.
- Intra-protein 1H flip-flop couplings are therefore at least as large as NV hyperfine contrast at 2-5 nm depth. Individual proton positions are washed out unless the protein is deuterated and sparsely labelled, and at that point the model is commuting, the kill applies, and classical labelling methods (NMR, EPR/DEER) compete.
- 1H polarisation at 1 T and 300 K is 6.8e-6, so the nuclear state is effectively classical and mixed.
- Distance goes as D^(-1/3), so a 1 A error at r = 5 A needs only 60% coupling precision (38% at 8 A), and 10% precision gives 0.17 A. Precision is not the limiting factor; detection and assignment are. A quantum precision gain acts on a factor that does not limit the result.

Verified citations (arXiv API or PubMed E-utilities, 2026-09-27):
- Proposals for NV single-molecule or protein structure: Cai-Jelezko-Plenio-Retzker arXiv:1112.5502; Ajoy et al. arXiv:1407.3134; Kost-Cai-Plenio arXiv:1407.6262; Ma-Liu arXiv:1510.04081.
- NV experiments: Lovchinsky 2016 (PMID 26847544); Shi et al. Science 2015 single-protein ESR (PMID 25745170); Zopes et al. arXiv:1807.04559; Yang et al. arXiv:1902.05676; Cujia et al. arXiv:2103.10669; SiC single-molecule-scale NMR, Chen et al. arXiv:2512.10278.
- Quantum-computing-enhanced sensing with NV feasibility: Allen-Machado-Chuang-Huang-Choi arXiv:2501.07625 (Grover-Heisenberg limit for unknown-frequency weak signals, a quadratic gain), realised experimentally by Xu et al. arXiv:2609.07613 (Sept 2026).
- Quantum electron microscopy: Okamoto arXiv:2209.04819 proposes a quantum electron microscope running Grover search over candidate structures, with "provable" damage (query) advantage. It is the nearest prior art to "quantum measurement + structure hypothesis selection".
- Theory: Matsumoto quant-ph/9711008; Ragy-Jarzyna-Demkowicz-Dobrzanski arXiv:1608.02634.
- Cryo-EM: Herzik et al. Nat Commun 2019 (PMID 30833564).

Not re-verified this session (from memory): Henderson Q Rev Biophys 1995, about 38 kDa theoretical threshold; smallest unscaffolded structures about 40-64 kDa (SAM-IV riboswitch 40 kDa, streptavidin 52 kDa, haemoglobin 64 kDa); Brody-Meister 1996 on adaptive local measurement attaining Helstrom for pure states; Putnam-Yanik PRA 2009; laser phase plate (Schwartz et al. 2019). General WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted), so the novelty scope is arXiv plus PubMed only.
verdicts.decisive_test: A paper derivation of under an hour, already carried out above in outline. (i) For the NV plus sparse-label model H = sum_k A_k S_z I_z^k (+ heteronuclear zz), show that the generators commute, so the Matsumoto condition holds and the QFI matrix is attainable single-copy (CFI/QFI = 1). Two-fold discrimination is perfect with finitely many sequential single-probe runs (Duan-Feng-Ying), so the two-copy/single-copy Chernoff ratio is below 2x. This meets both of the candidate's own kill rules for (a). (ii) Propagate r proportional to D^(-1/3) to show that 1 A needs only 38-100% coupling precision at 3-8 A, so Heisenberg precision gains do not reach the limiting factor. (iii) Put (b) through the alignment-threshold scaling M_min = 40 kDa * G^(-3/4 to -1): the 9-60-aa instruments need an ideal G of about 10-60, against an unmeasured N_eff and an ice/motion noise floor that G does not reduce. If a CPU number is still wanted, run only the sigma arm of the ORACLE-labelled restraint-value curve on mid30/long40 (K=20, sigma in {0.1, 0.3, 1, 2} A, flat-bottom, 32 restarts, a few CPU-hours). If RMSD(sigma=1 A) - RMSD(sigma=0.1 A) < 1 MDE, no precision-type quantum sensor can move the endpoint. File that run as an H-002 information-value diagnostic, not as a QM-24 quantum test.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note: (a) Nothing to break even against: the quantum-memory component gives 1.0x Fisher information over single-copy processing for commuting geometric parameters. What remains is 1/T versus 1/sqrt(reps), bounded by T2 (shallow NVs are typically 10-100 us; 13C/15N memories run ms to s). The twin, conventional NV correlation spectroscopy, already exploits it. (b) Under an ideal shot-noise model, lifting a particle from 40 kDa to M needs G = (40/M)^(4/3 to 1). That is 3 for 13-18 kDa, 10 for 4-7 kDa and about 30-60 for the program's 1-7 kDa instruments. N_eff is capped at about 1/(per-pass loss) and is unmeasured for electron mirrors; the stated ceiling is at least 10x (Koppell 2022). Any gain is per-dose metrology, not compute. Simulator or CPU runtime here says nothing about the physical instrument. Program cost if pursued: under one day of CPU for simulations that reproduce Juffmann 2017 and Koppell 2022 without a decision-relevant outcome.
verdicts.novelty_note:
Scope: arXiv API and PubMed E-utilities, 2026-09-27; general web search unavailable. The search found no evidence of a work that (i) quantifies single-copy versus multi-copy (quantum-memory) Fisher or Chernoff information for protein geometric parameters or fold identity with an NV sensor, or (ii) ties a multi-pass or quantum electron microscope gain G to the sub-40-kDa alignment threshold with an explicit G-sweep. Both would be incremental syntheses. Every physical mechanism is prior art:
- NV single-molecule structure: Cai 2013; Ajoy 2015; Kost 2015; Lovchinsky 2016; Pfender 2017.
- Quantum-memory learning: Chen-Cotler-Huang-Li 2021; Huang 2022.
- Heisenberg Hamiltonian learning: Huang-Tong-Fang-Su 2023; Dutkiewicz 2024.
- Quantum-computing-enhanced NV sensing: Allen et al. 2025; Xu et al. 2026.
- Multi-pass/IFM TEM: Kruit 2016; Juffmann 2017; Koppell 2019/2022.
- Quantum electron microscope with Grover search over candidate structures: Okamoto 2022, the closest prior art to the whole idea.
Part (a) with dense 1H is already this repo's Program C (NM-1, O'Brien et al. 2022). Recommendation: record QM-24(a) in KILLBOOK as mechanism-refuted, cross-referenced to NM-1/C1. Park QM-24(b) as external quantum metrology (sensing category, prior art owned by the Kasevich/Kruit/Okamoto lines), with no program experiment.

title: Quantum topological invariants: Jones/Khovanov knot invariants of protein chains (AJL, DQC1) and quantum topological data analysis (LGZ Betti numbers, hole persistence, Mayer homology) of structures and ensembles
merged_from: wild 'Protein knot invariants by quantum Jones-polynomial approximation (AJL / one-clean-qubit)', priorart (d) knot invariants / topology of protein chains, wild 'Quantum topological data analysis of conformational ensembles', priorart (e) quantum TDA (persistent / Mayer homology) and its dequantisation
summary: Q: (a) knot type / entanglement (knots, slipknots, lassos) of protein chains, predicted models and ensembles; (b) topology of conformational landscapes and atomic point clouds (basins beta_0, cyclic pathways beta_1, cavities/tunnels), and whether a hole persists across scales. Quantum: (a) additive Jones approximation at roots of unity via Temperley-Lieb/Fibonacci braid representations (BQP-complete plat, DQC1-complete trace closure; Quantinuum end-to-end H2 pipeline, PRX Quantum 2026), quantum Khovanov homology; (b) LGZ phase estimation on the clique-complex combinatorial Laplacian for beta_k/|S_k|, guided persistence testing (BQP1-hard, Gyurik et al. 2026), quantum Mayer homology (Nghiem et al. 2026). Mechanism: exponentially large representations or Laplacians applied/phase-estimated directly; genuine non-diagonal mechanisms outside H-001. Why classical copies it: (a) protein knots have <= ~7 minimal crossings after KMT reduction (6_3/7_1 in AF models); Alexander/HOMFLY-PT/Jones computed exactly in < 1 s (Topoly, KnotProt, AlphaKnot); the additive error is exponentially coarse for small knots; hard instances need large high-treewidth braids with no natural source. (b) exponential advantage needs clique-dense high-order complexes with exponentially large beta_k; biomolecular TDA uses k <= 2 with small Betti numbers (Ripser/GUDHI in seconds); LGZ is only quadratic in almost all cases (Schmidhuber-Lloyd); the Apers et al. classical estimator matches it at constant gap. Open protein questions (knotting probability, knotted-folding pathways, basin topology) are sampling problems with cheap per-sample invariants, i.e. they reduce to QM-01. Speedup: none-known at protein scale (exponential only in regimes disjoint from protein data). Oracle: chain -> closure -> braid, or RMSD-graph construction, classical polynomial; no oracle problem; readout ~1/eps^2 shots. Competitor: Topoly, KnotProt 2.0, AlphaKnot, tensor-network Jones; Ripser/GUDHI, element-specific persistent homology and persistent Mayer Laplacians (Wei group), classical Monte Carlo Betti estimators, MSM/PCCA+, cavity finders. Info vs comp: invariants are deterministic functions of given coordinates; no information added. S29-S33: materially different primitives, but killed by instance size / regime mismatch, not by S29-S33 mechanisms. Kill: reduced crossing number <= ~20 and exact invariants <= 1 s for all PDB/AFDB chains and compact random ensembles to L = 1000; beta_k/|S_k| < 1e-3 wherever |S_k| is classically intractable, and k <= 2 features saturate basin-classification AUC. Test: KMT + Alexander on ~50 knotted entries (incl. Q9PR55 7_1) and A80/random CA traces at L = 100-1000; exact beta_0..beta_3 and |S_k| (k <= 6) on RMSD-graph clique complexes of 1e3-1e4 mid30 conformers at 5-10 radii, Mayer Betti numbers where feasible. Hours. Track: C theory/query (A NISQ for the DQC1 variant). Prior: very low.
dead_reason: No existing program kill covers knot or TDA primitives; killed by argument (instance size / regime mismatch), to be recorded as a new kill after the cheap timing confirmation.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 on protein-derived instances: a formulation only. Complexity results exist, but on the wrong instances. AJL/Shor-Jordan show additive Jones approximation is BQP-/DQC1-complete. Gyurik et al. 2024 show guided persistence is BQP1-hard. Nghiem et al. 2026 prove an exponential separation for Mayer homology, but only against enumeration and only on a synthetic cone family of order k=Theta(n). All of these hold on instance families disjoint from protein data. On protein-derived families (derivations D1-D4 in evidence), exact classical algorithms run in polynomial time, often near-linear. The possible separation there is at best polynomial (at most quadratic, per Schmidhuber-Lloyd), and for R^3 atomic data it is plausibly negative: exact classical near-linear versus Omega(|S_k|) for exact quantum Betti numbers.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. There is no instance where a quantum topological-invariant computation is useful under matched conditions for protein structure. Protein knot diagrams sit more than 400x below the quantum-Jones crossover in crossing number. Protein persistent homology has k<=2 and is computed exactly classically in seconds.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The best case for the quantum side is Nghiem, Babbush, Zalcman, Berry, Phan, Wei, Hayakawa, arXiv:2609.28058 (posted 2026-09-23, not yet peer-reviewed). It claims that Mayer Betti numbers (d^N=0, xi=e^{2 pi i/N}) of dense high-order complexes can be exponentially large, which removes the normalisation bottleneck of LGZ. It also argues that dequantisation guarantees (Apers et al.) break down there, and estimates about a few hundred logical qubits and 6e7 Toffolis beyond known classical methods. Protein heavy-atom Rips complexes at 10-12 A really are dense: cliques hold about 54-93 atoms, so C(90,45) ~ 1e26 simplices per neighbourhood, which enumeration cannot reach. Mayer Laplacians have been used on biomolecular data (Wei group). So a protein-derived family with a real exponential gap over enumeration is conceivable.

Rebuttal:
(i) The exponent sits in the cutoff volume rho*r^3, which is a physical constant, not in protein length L. |S_k| grows linearly in the number of atoms for fixed r (D3).
(ii) It is a descriptor of coordinates already given. It adds no structural information and addresses none of bottleneck classes A-Y.
(iii) In the dense regime, Mayer Betti numbers count clique combinatorics and local or sample density rather than geometry. They are not homotopy invariant, and I know of no stability theorem for them (my own belief, not checked this session). For conformer ensembles they scale with the number of samples, so they are not landscape properties.
(iv) The claimed separation is only against enumeration. Classical methods that exploit locality or structure have not been ruled out.
(v) No evidence exists that high-order Mayer features predict anything beyond cheap classical descriptors. That is an information question, and it must be tested first at classically feasible orders.

Weaker counterargument: random compact globules at L~1000 are heavily knotted and may have hundreds of reduced crossings, which would make exact HOMFLY or Jones costly. But they are not proteins (the most complex known protein knot is 7_1). The polynomial-time Alexander determinant already answers 'knotted / how complex'. And the AJL output, with error eps*phi^{n-2}, cannot identify specific knots in that regime (Kuperberg).
verdicts.evidence:
VERIFIED this session via the arXiv API, Europe PMC or abstract pages:
- Aharonov-Jones-Landau, quant-ph/0511096 (STOC 2006).
- Shor & Jordan, 0707.2831, QIC 8:681 (2008): Jones estimation is DQC1-complete.
- Kuperberg, 0908.0512, Theory Comput. 11:183 (2015): 'any value-dependent approximation of the Jones polynomial at these non-lattice roots of unity is #P-hard'.
- Laakkonen, Rinaldi, Self, ..., Meichanetzidis, 2503.05625, PRX Quantum 7:020355 (2026):
  - Markov-closure additive error is eps*phi^{n-2}.
  - The classical mpo-proj algorithm on Frontier becomes slower than the quantum algorithm only for c>=2800 crossings, at a two-qubit error rate of 1e-4 and about 40% relative error.
  - Classical methods hit memory limits first.
  - The H2 demo used 16 qubits, 340 two-qubit gates and 4000 shots.
- Maria, 1910.00477: Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants in O(N^{3/2 cw} poly(n)), so exact computation is fixed-parameter tractable in cutwidth.
- Schmidhuber & Lloyd, 2209.14286, PRX Quantum 4:040349 (2023): exact Betti numbers are #P-hard and multiplicative approximation is NP-hard. LGZ is quadratic 'in asymptotically almost all cases'. Exponential advantage needs simplices given explicitly, not a vertex/edge list.
- Berry, Su, Gyurik, ..., Babbush, 2209.13581, PRX Quantum 5:010319 (2024): super-quadratic speedup needs multiplicative error and growing Betti numbers. Exponentially large dimension and Betti number are 'necessary, but insufficient'. Seemingly intractable instances need 'tens of billions of Toffoli gates'.
- Apers, Gribling, Sen, Szabo, 2211.09618, Quantum 7:1202 (2023): classical estimation in n^{O(log(1/eps)/sqrt(gamma))}.
- Gyurik, Cade, Dunjko, 2005.02607, Quantum 6:855 (2022).
- Gyurik, Schmidhuber, King, Dunjko, Hayakawa, 2410.21258: guided persistence is BQP1-hard, with the guiding state built from a harmonic representative.
- Crichigno & Kohler, 2209.11793, and King & Kohler, 2311.17234: clique homology is QMA1-hard. These are worst-case constructions.

DERIVATIONS:
- D1 (R^3 truncation): by the nerve lemma, Cech_r(X) is homotopy equivalent to the union of balls, an open subset of R^3, so H_k=0 for all k>=3. The alpha complex has the same homotopy type and is a subcomplex of Delaunay: O(n^2) in the worst case, about O(n) for atom-spaced points. So all geometrically faithful persistent homology of atomic clouds is beta_0..beta_2 and exactly computable in near-linear time. Cavities and tunnels therefore need no quantum computer.
- D2 (exact-integer barrier): LGZ returns beta_k/|S_k| +/- eps. Certifying the integer beta_k needs eps<1/(2|S_k|), which costs Omega(|S_k|) even with amplitude estimation. That is no better than near-linear classical exact computation whenever |S_k| is polynomial.
- D3 (locality):
  - Heavy-atom density is about 1.35 g/cm^3 divided by 14.5 Da per heavy atom, about 0.056 per A^3.
  - By Jung's theorem a Rips clique at scale r lies in a ball of radius 0.612r.
  - Maximum clique size is therefore about 12 (r=6 A), 54 (r=10 A) or 93 (r=12 A) for heavy atoms, and about 2, 7 or 12 for CA atoms.
  - Simplex order is bounded by a constant, and |S_k| <= n*C(K_nbr,k) is linear in protein size.
- D4 (knot gap): proteins reach at most 7 minimal crossings and a few tens after KMT reduction, against a quantum crossover of c>=2800. The quantum error eps*phi^{n-2} is value-independent, so it cannot discriminate small knots, which classical exact methods handle instantly.
- D5 (reduction to sampling): knotting probability, knotted-pathway fractions and basin topology are all E_pi[f] for a cheap classical f. The bottleneck is drawing samples from pi, which is QM-01 / the A45 lead. Amplitude estimation on f is at most quadratic, and that lane is already in the Killbook.

NOT RUN: no computation was done. At check time the machine was at 94.4% CPU from another job, so running it would have broken the 95% ceiling.

verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Knots:
- Protein diagrams have c <= ~7 minimal crossings and a few tens after reduction. Classical exact Jones/HOMFLY/Khovanov runs in well under a second (fixed-parameter tractable in width).
- The quantum Jones advantage needs c >= 2800 at a two-qubit error of 1e-4, with about 40% relative error (Laakkonen et al. 2026).
- Break-even is never reached for any known protein or AFDB chain: the gap is more than 400x in crossing number before reduction.

Ordinary TDA:
- Exact integer Betti numbers need eps < 1/(2|S_k|), so quantum cost is Omega(|S_k|). Classical alpha-complex persistence in R^3 is near-linear, so quantum cannot break even even in the query model.
- LGZ's generic speedup is quadratic (Schmidhuber-Lloyd), and quadratic speedups do not pay on early fault-tolerant hardware (Babbush et al. 2021, from the project literature).
- For the non-protein instances Berry et al. call seemingly intractable, the cost is tens of billions of Toffolis.

Mayer:
- The only claimed near-term crossover (about a few hundred logical qubits and 6e7 Toffolis) computes a quantity with no demonstrated use for protein structure. On protein complexes its 'exponential' lives in the constant rho*r^3, not in chain length.
verdicts.novelty_note: Scope of the check: arXiv API title searches and abstract fetches this session, plus the project's 448-paper literature phase, which did not cover TDA or knots. The WebSearch budget was used up, so this is a limited-scope check. Within it, I found no evidence of any paper applying quantum knot-invariant algorithms (AJL, DQC1, Khovanov) or quantum TDA (LGZ, persistence, Mayer) to protein structures or ensembles, or benchmarking them against Topoly, KnotProt, Ripser or GUDHI. The closest is Nghiem et al. 2026 (arXiv:2609.28058, posted 4 days ago, with Guo-Wei Wei as a co-author), which lists drug discovery as an application but, as far as I extracted, gives no protein-structure instance family. The gap is not an opportunity: D1-D4 explain why no one has shown advantage here. Suggested Killbook entry: 'QM-25 killed by instance-size/regime mismatch and R^3 dimensional truncation; reopen only if (a) protein-derived diagrams with reduced c >= ~2800 are shown to matter scientifically, or (b) high-order (k >= 10) Mayer or clique-homology features show held-out predictive value for a structure task beyond classical descriptors at feasible orders.'

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for the protein formulation. The abstract results are L6 for their own problems: additive Jones approximation at the 5th root of unity is BQP-complete for plat closure and DQC1-complete for trace closure, and LGZ-type Betti estimation has query-model guarantees. None of these carries over to protein data. The quantum algorithms only guarantee an additive window of eps*phi^(n-2) (Markov closure) or eps*phi^(n/2-3/2) (plat closure) on V, or eps*|S_k| on beta_k. When the answer is O(1), as for every protein knot (|V(7_1)| <= 7) and for every Betti number measured on learned-energy ensembles (beta_k <= 29), reaching useful accuracy costs the quantum side phi^Theta(n) or sqrt(|S_k|/beta_k) repetitions. The separation from exact classical transfer-matrix evaluation (cost phi^(2n) for Markov closure, phi^n for plat closure) is then at most QUADRATIC (derived below). Exponential separations need |V| >~ phi^Theta(n) (large irreducible knots) or beta_k/|S_k| >= 1/poly with |S_k| exponential. That regime does not overlap with protein data. Schmidhuber and Lloyd 2023 independently show LGZ is quadratic in almost all cases. Berry et al. 2024 show a super-quadratic speedup needs multiplicative error and asymptotically growing Betti numbers.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. At protein scale the classical side wins by 7-8 orders of magnitude in wall-clock. Example: 7_1 on Q9PR55 costs about 1e-7 s on a classical transfer matrix, versus 2-4 s of fault-tolerant runtime at 170 us per Toffoli, and classical returns the whole polynomial, not one additive value. The fault-tolerant break-even lies at irreducible diagrams with >= 24-43 Seifert circles/strands, costing 0.46-16 years per crossing at 170 us per Toffoli. The NISQ DQC1 break-even from the Quantinuum pipeline is >= 2800 crossings. Proteins give <= 8 crossings and <= 3 Seifert circles. Betti estimation on RMSD complexes of 1e4 conformers would take 94-936 years of fault-tolerant time at 170 us per Toffoli, for a quantity (beta_3) that no protein-structure question uses.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
1. The complexity theory is real. AJL and Shor-Jordan are BQP- and DQC1-complete, and Laakkonen et al. (PRX Quantum 2026) built an end-to-end pipeline that runs on H2 hardware and quotes a crossover. For some input source, the DQC1 Jones problem could be a legitimate NISQ-era advantage. Very long knotted polymers such as DNA, chromatin or polymer melts might produce high-crossing, high-braid-index diagrams with large |V|.
2. Schmidhuber et al. 2025 give a quantum Khovanov algorithm with pre-thermalization, which claims to avoid the small-Betti-fraction problem. Guided persistence testing (Gyurik et al. 2026, cited in the task and not verified here) is BQP1-hard, so a persistence question with good guiding states might escape the LGZ limits.
3. Exact dense transfer matrices are not the best classical method. The fair comparison is Alexander/HOMFLY + tensor-network MPO, which makes the quantum case worse, not better.
Rebuttal for the protein-structure mission:
(i) The largest knot in any protein (AF/PDB) is 7_1, with braid index 2. Every real protein knot reduces to <= ~8 crossings. Knot identification is solved exactly in milliseconds by the polynomial-time Alexander determinant, backed up by HOMFLY.
(ii) Learned-energy posterior samples at L = 45-150 are all unknots after KMT reduction (0 crossings).
(iii) Even non-protein compact random chains at L = 1000 reach only c <= 75 and s <= 22, far below the break-evens.
(iv) The open protein questions (knotting probability, knotted folding pathways, basin topology) are SAMPLING questions with per-sample invariant cost of 6-50 ms. They reduce to QM-01/QM-14, which are already killed at the practical level.
(v) Invariants are deterministic functions of given coordinates and add no structural information. The S29-S33 bottleneck is lack of information, not computation. The DNA/chromatin route is outside protein scope and would need its own audit.
