verdicts.novelty_note:
The search found no evidence of any study applying quantum knot-invariant algorithms (AJL, DQC1 Jones, quantum Khovanov) or quantum topological data analysis (LGZ, Berry et al., NISQ-TDA, Mayer homology) to protein chains or conformational ensembles. The scope was arXiv/Crossref/Europe PMC metadata checks of the papers listed; no general web search was possible because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted. This absence reflects a regime mismatch, not an open opportunity.

Two parts are new within this project but carry little weight:
- the pilot measurements: learned-energy posterior samples are unknots, and Betti numbers are tiny on posterior RMSD complexes;
- the explicit window/cost-duality break-even (n* = 24-43 strands).
The underlying observation, that additive-error Jones and Betti estimates are informative only when the answer is exponentially large, is implicit in Schmidhuber-Lloyd 2023, Berry et al. 2024 and Laakkonen et al. 2026. It should not be claimed as original.

Suggested KILLBOOK entry: QM-25 killed by instance size, the additive window and the information-vs-computation separation, not by the S29-S33 mechanisms. Re-open only with a source of irreducible diagrams with >= 2800 crossings or >= 24 strands and |V| >> 1, which lies outside protein structure.

verdicts.level_theoretical: Generic complexity separations exist, but none on protein inputs. They are L6 (worst-case/complexity-theoretic) in their own input models: AJL plat-closure Jones approximation is BQP-complete, trace-closure is DQC1-complete (Shor-Jordan), guided hole-persistence is BQP1-hard (Gyurik et al.), and Khovanov-rank approximation is DQC1/BQP-hard (Schmidhuber et al.). Every one of these needs large, high-treewidth braids or clique-dense complexes with non-negligible normalized Betti numbers, and protein data supplies neither. For protein chains and protein point clouds and ensembles the level is L0: a formulation with no separation. The Mayer-homology variant (Nghiem et al. 2026) claims an exponential regime for dense high-order complexes, but that is the other authors' L6-style argument, and the only protein complexes I measured fall outside it (see evidence).
verdicts.level_practical: L0. The search found no quantum evaluation of a protein chain's or ensemble's topological invariant on any hardware or simulator. The Quantinuum H2-2 Jones pipeline works on generic links and says quantum advantage needs 'a candidate set of links' to be supplied. On every protein instance I looked at, classical exact computation is trivial (under 1 s for knots; seconds to minutes for k<=2 homology).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The best case for keeping it: protein heavy-atom Vietoris-Rips complexes ARE a natural source of clique-dense, high-order complexes, which the quantum-TDA literature says is missing. Steric packing sets the clique number omega(r) independently of chain length, and it is large. On 1UBQ (602 heavy atoms), omega is 8, 18 and 29 at 4, 6 and 8 A. The exact number of simplices at 6 A is 8.66e6 (peak 1.63e6 at k=7), and at 8 A it is about 1e10, which makes exact high-k homology classically intractable at 8 A or more. Nghiem et al. (2026) argue that Mayer Betti numbers, unlike ordinary ones, are large in exactly this dense high-order regime, that dequantizers lose their guarantees there, and that a few hundred logical qubits and about 6e7 Toffolis would reach it. Wei-group Mayer and persistent-homology features are already used in protein-ligand ML.

Why it fails anyway:
(i) It is prior art. Nghiem, Babbush, Zalcman, Berry, Phan, Wei and Hayakawa (arXiv 2609.28058, Sept 2026) already propose it and name drug discovery as an application.
(ii) It is a descriptor computation, not a structure computation. It adds no information, and nobody has shown that high-k (k>=3) features predict anything about proteins.
(iii) The measured normalized Betti numbers vanish exactly where |S_k| is large. Ordinary homology is zero for k>=2 (heavy atoms, 4 A) and for k>=3 (CA, 6-10 A). Mayer N=3 on CA at 10 A is zero for k>=5 and at most 0.016 of |S_k| at k=4.
(iv) The cost does not pay. One FT run gives one scalar feature at additive error; ML descriptor sets need about 1e5-1e7 feature evaluations, against seconds for classical k<=2 features.
verdicts.evidence:
PRIOR-EVIDENCE AND RELEVANCE

(a) Knots. Brems, Runkel, Yeates and Virnau, 'AlphaFold predicts the most complex protein knot and composite protein knots', Protein Sci 2022, DOI 10.1002/pro.4380: the most complex knot ever found in a protein is 7_1, plus six-crossing composite knots and the first 5_1. AlphaKnot 2.0 (Rubach et al., NAR 2024, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkae443) covers more than 680,000 knotted models from AFDB v4, all detected classically. The other classical tools are Topoly (Dabrowski-Tumanski et al., Brief Bioinform 2021, DOI 10.1093/bib/bbaa196) and KnotProt 2.0 (NAR 2019, DOI 10.1093/nar/gky1140). Classical Jones for open chains also exists: Panagiotou and Kauffman, arXiv 2001.01303 (RSPA 2020); Barkataki and Panagiotou, arXiv 2205.03474; Musfeldt, arXiv 2410.22652, near-linear runtime on protein test cases; persistent/multiscale Jones, Song ... Wei, AIMS Math 2025, DOI 10.3934/math.2025068. So protein knots have 7 or fewer minimal crossings after reduction, and the candidate's kill criterion (a) is met from the literature alone. Knot identification needs only the Alexander polynomial, a determinant computed in polynomial time. Both the ~1% knotted fraction of the PDB and the AFDB total size are unverified in this session.

Quantum knot works: AJL, quant-ph/0511096 (STOC 2006). Shor and Jordan, arXiv 0707.2831 (QIC 8:681, 2008). Laakkonen ... Meichanetzidis, arXiv 2503.05625 (PRX Quantum 7:020355, 2026): demonstrated on H2-2 against tensor-network classical baselines, and advantage requires supplied candidate links. Schmidhuber, Reilly, Zanardi, Lloyd and Lauda, arXiv 2501.12378 (Khovanov; efficient only if the Hodge Laplacian thermalizes quickly and has a large gap).

(b) Quantum TDA. LGZ, arXiv 1408.3106. Berry et al., arXiv 2209.13581 (PRX Quantum 5:010319, 2024): super-quadratic speedup only for multiplicative error with asymptotically growing Betti numbers; the claimed intractable instances need tens of billions of Toffolis. Schmidhuber and Lloyd, arXiv 2209.14286 (PRX Quantum 4:040349, 2023): polynomial advantage in the worst case. Apers, Gribling, Sen and Szabo, arXiv 2211.09618 (Quantum 7:1202, 2023): a classical Monte Carlo estimator that matches the quantum one at constant gap. Gyurik, Cade and Dunjko, arXiv 2005.02607 (Quantum 6:855, 2022). Gyurik, Schmidhuber, King, Dunjko and Hayakawa, arXiv 2410.21258 (PRX Quantum 7:020361, 2026): BQP1-hard guided persistence, with no realistic datasets. Nghiem et al., arXiv 2609.28058 (2026, Mayer). All identifiers were checked via the arXiv API, arXiv abstract pages or Europe PMC in this session.

NOVELTY. The search found no evidence of a quantum algorithm or quantum hardware computing knot or Jones invariants or Betti or persistence of protein chains, protein point clouds or conformational ensembles. The scope was the arXiv API ('topological data analysis' AND quantum AND protein gave 0 hits; knot/entanglement AND protein AND quantum computer/algorithm gave 0 relevant hits) and Europe PMC title searches. The one protein-adjacent quantum proposal, Mayer homology for drug discovery, is already preempted by Nghiem et al. 2026. The literature phase (448 papers) had no quantum-TDA or knot entries, so this audit is the first coverage.

S29-S33 / DNR REGISTRY. No S29-S33 mechanism applies directly: these are non-diagonal primitives, not argmin or CVaR readouts. The binding constraint is the S33 finding that single-structure accuracy is limited by information, not computation. Invariants are deterministic functions of given coordinates and supply no missing per-target information. Ensemble questions (knotting probability, knotted-folding pathways, basin topology) are expectations over samples with invariants that are cheap to evaluate per sample, so they reduce to QM-01 sampling and the already-killed lane of amplitude estimation for ensembles.

NEW MEASUREMENTS (this audit, 1UBQ, exact; scripts in scratchpad cliq.py, mayer.py, mayer2.py):
- CA Vietoris-Rips clique number is 4, 6, 9 and 12 at 6, 8, 10 and 12 A.
- Exact |S_k| for CA at 10 A: {76, 550, 1496, 2097, 1698, 814, 223, 32, 2}.
- Heavy-atom totals: 2.2e4 simplices at 4 A, 2.76e5 at 5 A, 8.66e6 at 6 A.
- Ordinary Betti numbers: CA 6 A gives b0=1, b1=8. CA 8 A gives b0=1, b1=4. CA 10 A gives b0=1, b2=1. Heavy atoms at 4 A give b0=1, b1=56, and bk=0 for k>=2. Every Betti number is zero for k>=3; the largest bk/|S_k| is 0.017.
- Mayer N=3 on CA at 10 A: the largest beta/|S_k| is 0.058 (k=3), at most 0.016 at k=4, and 0 for k>=5.
- Large Mayer ratios for N=5 at CA 6-8 A (up to 1.0) occur only at k<=4 with |S_k|<=485, and are partly truncation artefacts.
So on real protein complexes the normalized invariants vanish where |S_k| becomes large. Part (b)'s kill criterion is supported for ordinary homology at these scales and is suggestive, not yet shown, for Mayer.
verdicts.decisive_test:
One test is left, and only for the Mayer residue; parts (a) and (b) are already decided by the literature plus the 1UBQ numbers above. It runs on the 8-core box in about 2-4 h under the 95% CPU/RAM limit.

(1) Regime check. On 6 mid30 and 6 long40 natives, plus 50 A80 decoys each, build CA Rips complexes at 8, 10 and 12 A and heavy-atom Rips complexes at 4, 5 and 6 A. Compute exact Mayer beta_{k,q}/|S_k| for N=3 and N=5 at every k where the rank fits in memory, using sparse modular rank over GF(p) with p = 1 mod 15 rather than dense SVD. Fit the trend in k and in r. Kill if the ratio falls below 1e-3 for every k where |S_k| is above 1e6, or extrapolates to that.

(2) Information check (DEP-only, natives used just to label decoys). Build decoy-vs-near-native classification on long40 A80 decoys. Compare classical k<=2 persistent features (plus the A80 energy) against the same features plus exact Mayer features with k>=3 at the largest tractable scale. Use a train/dev split with the test set held out. Kill if the AUC gain is below 0.01 or its 95% CI includes 0.

Passing both would only raise the Mayer residue to WEAK-conditional, as a descriptor computation. A quantum advantage there would still belong to Nghiem et al.'s proposal, not this program. Optional check for (a), not decisive: pip-install Topoly and run KMT reduction plus Alexander/HOMFLY-PT on the 7_1 AlphaFold model and about 50 KnotProt entries, confirming under 1 s each and 7 or fewer reduced crossings.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note:
Knots: no break-even exists. Instances have 7 or fewer crossings after reduction. The exact Jones or HOMFLY-PT evaluation (under 1 s) is cheaper than compiling a single braid circuit, and additive-error AJL/DQC1 estimates are coarser than the exact value at these sizes.

Standard TDA: Berry et al. put claimed-intractable instances at about 1e10 or more Toffolis. Protein complexes have bk/|S_k| of 0 for k>=3 (measured), so the 1/(eps^2 * normalized Betti) shot cost diverges.

Mayer: about 6e7 Toffolis and a few hundred logical qubits per estimate (Nghiem et al.; unverified whether that count includes the estimation repetitions). Assumed logical Toffoli rates of 1e4-1e6 per second (an assumption, not verified) give about 1 min to 1.7 h per scalar feature. A protein-ligand descriptor pipeline needs roughly 1e2-1e3 features across 1e3-1e4 complexes, so 1e5-1e7 runs, or FT-machine-years. Classical k<=2 persistent/Mayer features cost seconds per complex. For comparison, exact classical computation for heavy-atom Rips at 6 A on a 76-aa protein involves about 8.7e6 simplices and is tractable with sparse methods. Intractability starts near 8 A (about 1e10 simplices), and there the measured trends say the normalized invariants are already zero.
verdicts.novelty_note: The search found no evidence of any quantum topological-invariant computation (Jones/Khovanov via AJL/DQC1; Betti/persistence via LGZ, guided persistence or Mayer) applied to protein chains, structures or conformational ensembles. Scope: arXiv API and Europe PMC queries, Sept 2026, with the web-search budget exhausted, so publisher-only venues are not covered. On the topology side the nearest prior art is classical: AlphaKnot 2.0, Topoly, KnotProt 2.0, Panagiotou-Kauffman open-chain Jones, and Wei-group persistent Jones and Mayer homology. On the quantum side it is generic TDA and knot algorithms, plus Nghiem et al. 2026, which already proposes quantum Mayer homology with drug discovery as an application. So the only protein-adjacent quantum angle is preempted, and a 'first quantum knot invariant of a protein' demo would be novel in an empty way: a small, classically trivial instance. The one new datum from this audit is that on a real protein (1UBQ) the ordinary and Mayer normalized Betti numbers go to zero exactly where clique counts become large. That is worth recording in the KILLBOOK as regime evidence.

title: Exponential quantum simulation of coupled classical oscillators (Babbush et al.), quantum elastic network models and Koopman-von Neumann MD for protein mechanics
merged_from: classical 'Exponential-dimension simulation of protein mechanics (coupled-oscillator and Carleman quantum ODE solvers)', wild 'Exponential simulation of coupled classical oscillators for vibrational energy flow in macroscopic protein assemblies', priorart (i) quantum elastic network models / KvN molecular dynamics
summary: Q: global dynamical observables of elastic-network or MD models of very large protein assemblies (capsids, fibril networks, defected protein crystals): energy transfer between domains, response to a local perturbation, kinetic energy of a residue subset at time t, Green-Kubo correlators. Quantum: Babbush-Berry-Kothari-Somma-Wiebe mapping of 2^n harmonic oscillators to Schroedinger evolution (BQP-complete, 2^{Omega(n)} classical queries); QENM (graphene only); KvN MD with QPE/AE readout (H2 only); Carleman linearisation for dissipative nonlinear ODEs. Replaces: sparse Verlet/Krylov propagation and Lanczos normal modes. Mechanism: amplitudes encode sqrt(M) x-dot and B^dagger x; with efficiently computable masses and springs (formula-defined from the index) and an efficiently preparable initial state, cost is poly(n) and readout limited to a few global scalars. Conservative wave dynamics has no positive stochastic unraveling, so unlike QM-13 the exponential survives in principle. Why it fails for proteins: every protein object has <= ~1e6-1e8 EXPLICIT coordinates (spring oracle requires Omega(N) QROM loading, erasing the exponential), or is periodic (Bloch reduction), or macroscopic and homogenisable (continuum elasticity); the 2^n regime needs procedurally generated non-periodic structure that proteins do not supply. Anharmonic chaotic MD: any algorithm outputting the normalised solution state costs exponentially in time with positive Lyapunov exponents (Lewis-Eidenbenz-Nadiga 2024); Carleman needs dissipation-dominated R < 1. Speedup: exponential only for 2^n oracle-structured oscillators; none for explicit protein ENMs. Competitor: sparse Lanczos ANM/GNM, analytic harmonic propagation from modes, GPU/Anton MD, kernel polynomial methods, disorder averaging. Info vs comp: the harmonic model carries little information about large conformational change and none for structure prediction. S29-S33: new mechanism outside H-001, but outside the structure-accuracy endpoint; killed by data loading and input size. Kill: exact classical computation of the target observable at the largest biologically meaningful N (1e6, extrapolated to 1e8) in <= CPU-hours; no protein-science question needs 2^n >> 1e9 non-periodic, succinctly described oscillators. Test: symmetry-tile a CA trace to 1e3-1e6 nodes with random defects (8-15 A cutoff); lowest 200 modes by sparse Lanczos and analytic propagation of a local perturbation, plus sparse Verlet; record wall-clock/RAM under the 95% ceiling and extrapolate. Hours. Track: C theory/query (B). Prior: ~0 for proteins.
dead_reason: No existing program kill covers this exponential-simulation primitive; it dies on instance class and data loading, to be recorded as a new kill.

verdicts.level_theoretical: L0 for the protein instance family. L6 holds only for the non-geometric oracle family: glued trees and the BQP-complete circuit construction, where Babbush et al. themselves note that the "interactions between oscillators are not spatially local". For elastic networks embedded in 3D space with a distance cutoff and a minimum node spacing, the graph has polynomial growth, so the separation is provably at most polynomial. A local observable costs classically O((w_max*t)^4*d) (Chebyshev/Verlet on the light-cone ball) against quantum Omega(w_max*t) (no fast-forwarding). A global intensive observable costs classically O((w_max*t)^4/eps^2) by sampling random light-cone patches against quantum O(w_max*t/eps). So the gain is cubic in time plus quadratic in precision, which is "super-quadratic" in Babbush's own words, and never exponential. For explicit (non-procedural) protein coordinates, loading the data into the oracle adds a factor of at least Omega(sqrt(P*b)) Toffolis and a comparable number of ancilla qubits per query (QROAM), or Omega(P) without ancillas. That erases the log-N benefit.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. The measured classical cost of exact propagation, with every observable available at once, is about 1.3 CPU-hours at 1e6 nodes for a full crossing of the assembly. Extrapolated to 1e8 nodes it is about 600 core-hours (about 10-20 core-hours after 60-fold icosahedral symmetry or rigid-block reduction). The quantum cost of one scalar at 1% precision is about 1.3e11 Toffolis at 1e6 nodes and 6e12 at 1e8. That is 1.5 d and 70 d at an optimistic 1 us per Toffoli, or 0.7 yr and 33 yr at 170 us per Toffoli (one factory). No protein-structure endpoint is served. The elastic network needs the native structure as input, so it adds zero information to structure computation, which is the project's endpoint.
verdicts.strongest_counterargument:
The strongest case for quantum is the procedural sub-regime: a perfect capsid or crystal lattice (symmetry makes the coordinate oracle cheap) plus defects drawn from a pseudorandom hash. There the quantum walk keeps a real speedup of about the light-cone volume (T^3 in 3D, so classical ~T^4 against quantum ~T). That is "quartic" in the sense of Babbush et al. (PRX Quantum 2021), which they call far more practical than quadratic. My break-even model, using the measured light-cone front v ~1.5-2.5 Å/unit and 0.55 us per node-step, puts crossover at light cones of 5.7e6 nodes (855 Å radius, ~6 h single core) with 1 us Toffolis and one classical core. With 8 cores it is 4.6e7 nodes. At 170 us Toffolis it is 1e9-8e9 nodes, and 1e12 against a 1000-core classical machine. The QENM graphene paper (arXiv:2601.05161) makes the analogous 2D claim: cm-scale sheets with ~160 logical qubits. So an exact, realization-specific harmonic response of a micron-scale defected protein crystal or fibril network could in principle favour quantum.

Rebuttal:
(i) The defect configuration of a real crystal is unknown. A realization-specific answer therefore has no scientific meaning, and the meaningful disorder-averaged observable is self-averaging. It can be computed from representative-volume samples, finite-size scaling or effective-medium/phonon-transport theory.
(ii) Stronger classical algorithms cut the classical constant by 10-1000x: perfect-lattice Bloch Green's functions with a defect T-matrix (cost ~ defect density times light-cone volume), rigid-block or coarse-grained far fields (228 to 6 DOF per molecule here), and symmetry.
(iii) The harmonic model is qualitatively wrong for long-time transport: harmonic crystals have no normal Fourier heat conduction (Rieder-Lebowitz-Lieb 1967). The model error of a one-parameter network dwarfs any integration error the quantum computer removes.
(iv) The output is a few scalars at a cost of 1/eps.
(v) None of this is structure computation.
verdicts.evidence:
VERIFIED LITERATURE (arXiv API / Crossref / full-text grep this session):
- Babbush, Berry, Kothari, Somma, Wiebe, PRX 13, 041041 (2023), arXiv:2303.13012. Abstract: the speedup requires that "individual masses and spring constants can be efficiently queried, and ... the initial state can be efficiently prepared".
  - Conclusion (verbatim, from the full text): "only efficient for computing particularly large or global properties and when masses and spring constants can be computed in time polylogarithmic in system size ... complexity is (almost) linear in the evolution time t ... This would discourage applications where ... N = poly(t) ... expected to arise when simulating physical systems with geometrically-local interactions, and for initial states that are locally supported ... light cone, whose size in D spatial dimensions would scale as N ∝ t^D. Nevertheless ... significant quantum speedups (e.g., super-quadratic)."
  - Sec. VI: its hard instances "may seem artificial (e.g., resulting interactions between oscillators are not spatially local)".
- Cramer, Serafini, Eisert, arXiv:0803.0890; Nachtergaele, Raz, Schlein, Sims, CMP 286, 1073 (2009), arXiv:0712.3820. Lieb-Robinson bounds for harmonic lattices.
- Danz et al., arXiv:2405.08694. QPE response functions; query complexity O(s||H||max/(delta^2 eps)). Its exponential example is the random glued trees.
- Kolotouros et al., arXiv:2601.05161 (QENM, graphene, ~160 logical qubits; comments say it was extended to defects). Its runtime was not checked.
- Lewis, Eidenbenz, Nadiga, Subasi, Quantum 8, 1509 (2024), arXiv:2307.09593. Complexity is at least exponential in integration time for chaotic systems.
- Liu et al., PNAS 118, e2026805118 (2021), arXiv:2011.03185. Requires R<1. For conservative MD Re(lambda_1)=0, so R=inf and the guarantee is void.
- Weisse et al., RMP 78, 275 (2006) (KPM, linear in dimension).
- Tama & Brooks, JMB 345, 299 (2005), doi:10.1016/j.jmb.2004.10.054 (capsid ENM normal modes).
- Dykeman & Sankey, PRL 100, 028101 (2008) and PRE 81, 021918 (2010) (atomistic capsid low-frequency modes).
- Kadau, Germann, Lomdahl, IJMPC 17, 1755 (2006) (3.2e11-atom MD); Germann & Kadau, IJMPC 19, 1315 (2008) (trillion-atom MD).
- Jung et al., JCC 40, 1919 (2019) (MD beyond 1e5 cores, large biophysical systems).
- Rieder, Lebowitz, Lieb (1967), doi:10.1007/978-3-662-10018-9_21 (reprint; the original is J. Math. Phys. 8, 1073, which was not verified).
- The QROAM cost form is taken from the repo's T3_resource_model (Berry et al. 2019).

MEASURED THIS SESSION (single core at idle/below-normal priority on a box already at 76-100% load from other jobs, so classical timings are pessimistic):
- Setup: 1UBQ CA tiled on an orthorhombic lattice, with 3% vacancies, 5% random reorientations and 0.5 Å cell jitter (non-periodic). Anisotropic network model, rc = 10 Å, about 16.2 contacts per node. K = B^T B, the same factorisation Babbush encodes in amplitudes.
- Verlet cost per step, linear at 0.41-0.67 us per node-step:
  - N=912: 0.10 ms
  - 2,888: 0.40 ms
  - 9,880: 4.1 ms
  - 29,944: 14 ms
  - 99,408: 62.5 ms
  - 299,516: 201 ms
  - 999,400 (3.0e6 DOF, 8.14e6 springs): 553 ms
- At N=999,400: build 6.3 s, Lanczos w_max 56 s, peak RSS 1.46 GB, energy drift 8e-4.
- Lowest 200 modes by shift-invert Lanczos: 0.8 / 5.1 / 38.7 / 252 s for 912 / 2.9e3 / 9.9e3 / 3.0e4 nodes (0.77 GB). Scaling is about N^1.7. At 1e6 this needs rigid-block reduction or symmetry, which is the standard practice.
- Exact Krylov propagation of the Babbush first-order system z = (v, Bx), checked against Verlet at dt = 0.2/w_max: KE of the kicked molecule agrees to 0.4%, velocity-vector error is 1% at 1e4 nodes, and the exact method costs about 3x Verlet.
- Light-cone truncation at 3e4 nodes, t = 18.7 (400 steps): a 100 Å sphere (10,507 nodes) reproduces the kicked-molecule KE to 1.5e-6 relative error; 80 Å to 1.8e-4. The far-molecule KE is 1e-93 to 1e-47 (in the 1e5 run the far molecule's KE is still ~4e-31 at t≈95).
- Energy front enclosing all but 1e-6 of the KE: 42 Å at t=2.7, 95 Å at t=9.2, 220 Å at t=94.7.

DERIVATION: a Chebyshev degree of D ≈ e*w_max*t/2 + log(1/eps) is exact to eps and has support within graph distance D of the initial support. A polynomial-growth Euclidean graph then gives classical cost ≤ D * d * rho * (4pi/3)(D*rc)^3. The physical Lieb-Robinson radius v*t is far smaller than D*rc.

verdicts.novelty_note:
The weakness this analysis turns on is not new. Babbush et al. (2023) state in their conclusion that geometrically local systems with local initial states give only light-cone-limited (N ∝ t^D), super-quadratic speedups, and that the oracles must be polylog-computable. What this session adds is the protein-specific quantification: a measured classical cost for a defected protein-lattice network up to 1e6 nodes, measured light-cone and front radii, and a break-even against an FT resource model.

The search found no evidence of an application of the Babbush oscillator algorithm to protein elastic networks or protein mechanics. Scope: the literature-phase corpus (448 papers), an arXiv title search for "quantum elastic network" (which returned only QENM graphene, arXiv:2601.05161), and the arXiv records for Danz et al. 2405.08694 and Babbush 2303.13012. The web-search budget was exhausted this session, so this is not exhaustive.

Unverified items:
- QENM's runtime and T-count
- van Vlijmen & Karplus 2005 (capsid symmetry NMA)
- The J. Math. Phys. citation for Rieder-Lebowitz-Lieb (only the reprint DOI was verified)
- Protein Lyapunov times

Relation to H-001: this is a new mechanism outside H-001 (coherent wave dynamics, not argmin over a diagonal energy). But it sits outside the structure-accuracy endpoint, because the elastic network needs the structure as input and carries no structure-prediction information. It should go to KILLBOOK with reason "classical light-cone/linear-scaling propagation + data loading; protein ENMs are Euclidean polynomial-growth graphs, exponential separation impossible; polynomial residual only for procedurally generated, non-protein-science instances".

verdicts.level_theoretical: L6 holds only for the abstract, non-protein problem: Babbush-Berry-Kothari-Somma-Wiebe (BBKSW) oscillator dynamics with 2^n oscillators and oracle couplings, a 2^{Omega(n)} classical query lower bound, BQP-complete. For any protein-instantiated task the level is L0, and I derived two no-go results. (1) Explicit elastic-network (ENM) data: loading the spring and neighbour data costs Theta(E) Toffolis per query with QROM (linear-cost lookup table), or Theta(sqrt(E*M)) Toffolis plus Theta(sqrt(E*M)) logical ancillas with QROAM (qubit-for-Toffoli trade-off variant). The query count Theta(omega_max*t) equals the classical Verlet step count, so no exponential remains, and at best a qubit-paid sqrt(N) factor. (2) Procedurally defined networks embedded in 3D with finite-range springs: cos(t*sqrt(A)) and sin(t*sqrt(A))/sqrt(A) are entire in A. Up to error eps they are polynomials of degree K ~ omega_max*t/2 + O(log 1/eps), and A^k has graph range k, so the dynamics has an exact light cone. Classical cost is O(rho*K^4*d) for a local perturbation, against quantum O(K*polylog(N)/eps) per scalar. The exponential collapses to at most a degree-(D+1)=4 polynomial separation in the light-cone radius K. No classical lower bound is proven, so this is not L6 for proteins. BBKSW hard instances need exponential-growth graphs (glued trees, hypercube-like index graphs). Physical 3D protein objects have polynomial ball growth, so they cannot supply them.
verdicts.level_practical: L0. For explicit ENMs, quantum loses at every protein-relevant size by 10^2-10^6x. For the procedural residual the model is physically invalid for proteins, and damping destroys the encoding (see the break-even note).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument: A procedurally defined, defected, macroscopic protein microcrystal has an explicit N far beyond classical memory. A 1 mm^3 lysozyme crystal holds ~10^18 CA nodes (INFERENCE from unit-cell volume). Defects given by a hash of the index make the spring oracle poly(n) (my uncompiled estimate: G ~ 1e4-1e5 Toffolis per query), with no QROM. For 'energy fraction in a macroscopic region at time t after a local perturbation', quantum cost is ~ (pi/eps)*2K*G, while brute-force classical light-cone simulation is ~ rho*K^4*t_node. This quartic-in-K gap is beyond quadratic ('Focus beyond quadratic' does not rule it out), and the break-even is finite. With G=3e4, eps=0.01, 1 classical core and 170 us per Toffoli, it is K* ~ 3.9e3 hops (~1.7e9 light-cone nodes), at 145 days per scalar. With 1e3 cores and 1.7 us effective Toffolis (R=100 factories) it is K* ~ 8.5e3 hops, at 3.1 days per scalar. This is the only non-astronomical corner. It fails on four counts. (a) The question is not protein science. Undamped harmonic energy transport over 10^3-10^4 hops (~0.3-2 um) of a Calpha ENM has no physical meaning. ENM springs are fitted to equilibrium B-factors, not dynamics, and hydrated protein crystals have overdamped low-frequency modes with nm-scale phonon mean free paths (INFERENCE). (b) Adding the needed damping gamma makes the evolution non-unitary. The encoded norm decays as e^{-gamma t}, so post-selection or amplification costs ~ e^{gamma t}, with gamma*t ~ 2K*gamma/omega_max >> 1 at K ~ 1e3. Damping meanwhile shrinks the classical light cone. (c) Real defect realisations are unknown per node. The physically meaningful answer is an ensemble average, which is self-averaging and can be sampled classically by light-cone Monte Carlo, or handled by homogenisation or phonon transport theory. Neither is tested here. (d) Classical output is the whole field; quantum output is one eps-accurate scalar per ~1e10-1e11 Toffolis. Those Toffolis need a per-gate error of ~1e-12, which pushes the code distance above 31 and raises t_T above 170 us.

verdicts.decisive_test: The main test is done: sparse Verlet across a 1e6-node defected tiled crystal took 55 s (GNM) and ~10 min extrapolated (ANM) on one core, well inside the kill criterion. The paper derivation also closes the exponential regime for anything physically embedded in 3D: a degree-K polynomial in A implies a light cone, so classical cost is poly(K) and the separation is <= K^4 vs K/eps. The single cheapest remaining experiment addresses the procedural residual and runs in hours on this 8-core box: (i) in a 1e6-1e7-node defected 13 A ANM crystal, apply a local velocity kick; (ii) compute the exact light-cone energy fraction E_S(t) crossing a plane at K = 100-600 hops; (iii) compare it with a homogenised continuum or phonon-radiative-transfer prediction fitted on a separate crystal realisation; (iv) repeat with Langevin damping gamma/omega_max in {0, 0.01, 0.1}. Kill the residual permanently if either condition holds: the transport or continuum model reaches |error| < 0.01 for K >= 300 (the classical cost becomes K-independent and the quartic gap vanishes), or gamma/omega_max >= 0.01 confines the energy within <= 1e2 hops (quantum norm-decay penalty e^{gamma t} >= e^{2}, with a trivial classical light cone).
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note: Explicit protein ENM, the only data-faithful protein instance. With linear QROM, quantum is 5.9e3x slower per step (170 us Toffolis vs 0.93 us per node-step classically, N-independent) and 1.8e6x slower after pi/eps readout, so it never breaks even. With QROAM, break-even is N* ~ 6e13 nodes (1 core, 170 us, eps = 0.01) with ~5e8 logical qubits, rising to 6e19 against 1e3 cores. Every protein assembly is <= 1e8-1e9 nodes, and 1e8 nodes costs 78 core-hours classically. Procedural 3D networks: the finite corner (K* ~ 4e3 hops, months per scalar at 170 us; ~8e3 hops, ~3 days per scalar only with 100 parallel factories against 1e3 cores) rests on an undamped harmonic model that has no protein-science meaning, and damping adds an e^{gamma t} penalty. The oracle erases the exponential in the explicit case, and Euclidean locality caps it at polynomial in the procedural case. The prior stays ~0 for proteins.
verdicts.novelty_note: Using BBKSW-type oscillator simulation for protein ENMs or crystals is not protein-relevant, and the search found no evidence (448-paper map, T5 notes, this audit) of any protein-specific BBKSW application. The light-cone no-go (3D embedding plus finite-range springs caps the separation at a polynomial of degree D+1 in the propagation radius K, using Chebyshev locality) is a short derivation from standard facts; it is probably known in spirit, since BBKSW hard instances rely on exponential-growth graphs, but I have not verified that it is written down. It is worth recording in research/theory/NO_GO_RESULTS as a per-family closure of escape route (v) in ADVANTAGE_CONDITIONS A4. The candidate is outside the H-001 structure-accuracy endpoint and carries no structure information, so it cannot touch the information-limited bottleneck found in S29-S33.

verdicts.level_theoretical: For protein instances: L0, with published no-go results that rule out an exponential advantage. L6 (exponential query separation, BQP-complete) holds only for the non-protein family of 2^n oscillators whose springs are defined by an oracle or circuit (Babbush et al. 2023). Two published results block the transfer to proteins. (a) Liu et al. 2024 (arXiv 2411.03972), Thm S1.10 as reported by the fetch summary: an efficient connectivity oracle exists only when the Kirchhoff/Hessian matrix K has a polylog(N)-bit description, and the paper states that the K matrix for protein MD "does not satisfy the polylog(N)-bit condition". Its own loader is a QROM with O(N log N) gates. (b) Schade, Simon, Wiebe et al. 2026 (arXiv 2609.20721): a Lieb-Robinson-like bound means locally coupled D-dimensional networks give at most an O(t^D) speedup for local observables, which is quartic in 3-D. The paper says a super-polynomial gain needs "a non-local generator or a combination of a globally driven system with a non-local observable". Protein ENMs are 3-D local (8-15 Å cutoff), and every protein structure is explicit data of Omega(N) bits. What remains in principle is polynomial only: about sqrt(N) from QROAM loading for non-local observables, and t^3 for local ones. For anharmonic chaotic MD the output-state route is exponential in t (Lewis et al. 2024).
verdicts.level_practical: L0. No L1 evidence exists for any protein task. The one protein paper (Liu et al. 2024) has no runtime comparison with a classical method; its numerics use Crambin (1360 atoms) and Chignolin. QENM (Kolotouros et al. 2026) covers graphene only, and the KvN Green-Kubo and Langevin papers (Watanabe et al. 2026) cover H2 only. The break-even model below puts crossover at or above the largest CA-level protein assemblies (about 1e5-1e7 nodes; this size range is approximate and was not verified this session), except against a single-core adversary under optimistic hardware. The observables the candidate names, such as the response to a local perturbation and the kinetic energy of a residue subset at time t, cost the classical side an amount independent of N (light-cone check below).
verdicts.strongest_counterargument: For NON-local observables (energy transfer between macroscopic capsid domains, or a Green-Kubo correlator summed over a whole assembly), the Lieb-Robinson no-go does not apply. With QROAM loading (about 2*sqrt(M*N) Toffolis per query, M ≈ 60 coordinate bits), quantum cost grows as sqrt(N)*t/eps while classical Verlet grows as N*t. That is a real polynomial gap. Against my measured single-core rate (7.8e-7 s per node-step), with 100 parallel Toffoli factories (170 µs/R) and eps = 1e-2, the break-even is N* ≈ 1.4e6, inside the CA size range of giant capsids. A proponent could also say that a procedurally generated assembly (an icosahedral template plus seeded random defects) has a polylog(N)-bit description, which would restore the Babbush et al. exponential. Rebuttal, in five parts. (1) One core is too weak an adversary. Against 8 cores N* ≈ 8.5e7 (R=100, eps=1e-2) or 8.5e11 (R=1). Against one GPU sparse matrix-vector product (about 2e-9 s per node-step) N* ≈ 2e11-2e15. These N* also need 7e4-4e8 logical QROAM ancilla qubits. (2) The plain O(log N)-qubit QROM that Liu et al. use gives no asymptotic gain: quantum is about 2.4e3 times slower than 8 cores and about 1.2e5 times slower than a GPU at every N (R=100, eps=1e-2). (3) The quantum run returns one eps-additive scalar. Classical returns every observable at every time step. (4) Real defect positions come from experimental data, so they cost Omega(N) bits. A seeded procedural model is a modelling assumption, and protein science wants disorder-averaged quantities, which self-average and can be computed on sub-volumes classically. Icosahedral symmetry block-diagonalises capsid NMA (Tama and Brooks 2005; van Vlijmen and Karplus 2005). (5) The harmonic ENM carries no structure-prediction information and misses anharmonic large conformational change. Anharmonic chaotic MD is blocked by Lewis et al. 2024, and Carleman needs R < 1.

O(N log N) gates"; "we need to load O(N) bits"; efficient construction "only possible when the minimal number of bits to describe the K matrix is polylog(N) ... the K matrix for protein molecular dynamics simulation does not satisfy" this; no classical runtime baseline.
- Kolotouros et al., arXiv 2601.05161 (2026). QENM for graphene only; about 160 logical qubits for cm-scale graphene.
- Schade, Simon, Wiebe, Keating, Bösch, Fichtner, arXiv 2609.20721 (17 Sep 2026). Damped non-Markovian oscillators, BQP-complete in the worst case; "infeasibility of exponential quantum advantages in locally coupled topologies" and "quartic speedups ... in three dimensions". [fetch] classical cost O(t^{D+1}) for local observables.
- Luangsirapornchai et al., arXiv 2501.06100 (2025). Heterogeneous spring-mass systems need O(N log2 N log(1/eps)) gates, an independent confirmation that loading explicit springs erases the exponential.
- Watanabe et al., arXiv 2605.30142 and 2605.30143 (2026). KvN MD for Green-Kubo coefficients and Langevin NVT; H2 only; the Nose-Hoover block costs O(n_xi n_p 2^{n_p}).

- Muraleedharan and Wiebe, arXiv 2505.17170 (2025): weakly nonlinear oscillators. Krovi, arXiv 2404.07303 (2024): damped oscillators, BQP-hard. Zschetzsche et al., arXiv 2512.03681 (2025): continuous-time quantum walks are equivalent to oscillator dynamics. MICRO-CHECK (this session; scratch, not a project result). Script: C:\Users\abena\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-abena-quantum-advantage-protein-folding\deded8ee-ac50-420b-a8f2-b349dc3a4fdc\scratchpad\enm_lightcone.py; output enm_lightcone.json in the same folder.
- Setup: randomly rotated 1UBQ CA copies on a 32 Å lattice with 10% vacancies; ANM, 10 Å cutoff; single thread at below-normal priority on a machine at about 92% CPU from other jobs, so the timings are pessimistic.
- Verlet cost: N = 8,892 / 34,276 / 90,592 nodes gave 6.6 / 28 / 71 ms per step (nnz 1.3e6 / 5.0e6 / 1.33e7; RSS ≤ 226 MB). That is linear, about 7.8e-7 s per node-step. Extrapolated: about 0.8 s per step at 1e6 nodes on one core; 1e8 nodes needs about 180 GB of CSR, so memory is the binding constraint there, not time.
- Light cone: I kicked a central residue and measured the kinetic energy of the 10 residues within 8 Å of a site 25 Å away, over 400 steps (t = 20). A 90 Å ball (5,909 of 90,592 nodes) reproduced the full-network observable to a relative error of 1.4e-4 at 22x lower cost. A 70 Å ball (2,631 nodes) gave 2.3e-3 at 91x lower cost. The ball size is set by t, not N, which confirms the Schade et al. locality for a protein-derived network.

BREAK-EVEN (derivation). Queries Q ≈ omega_max*t/eps ≈ 0.35*S/eps, where S is the number of Verlet steps. Cost per query ≈ 2*sqrt(60*N) Toffolis (QROAM). Setting N*c_node*S = Q*C_q*t_T/R gives sqrt(N*) = 0.35*2*sqrt(60)*t_T/(R*eps*c_node). The resulting N* values are in the break-even field.
verdicts.decisive_test: The paper derivation is already decisive, and I ran it this session. N* = [0.35 * 2*sqrt(M) * t_T / (R * eps * c_node)]^2 with M = 60 bits, t_T = 170 µs and c_node measured at 7.8e-7 s per node-step on one core. Only one combination breaks even inside the protein range: a single-core adversary with 100 Toffoli factories and eps = 1e-2 (N* ≈ 1.4e6). Every stronger adversary, or R = 1, puts N* at 8.5e7 to 2e15, above the largest CA-level assemblies (≤ about 1e7, approximate). For every observable driven by a local perturbation, classical cost is independent of N (the light-cone ball matched the full network to 1.4e-4 using 6.5% of the nodes). One confirmation run remains optional and cheap, to go under the governor only when it is idle, since RAM headroom today is about 3 GB. It is a single 8-thread run at N = 1e6 GNM/ANM (about 2.5 GB) measuring Verlet per-step cost and a Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM) density of states with 1000 moments and 10 random vectors. The kill stands if the cost stays linear with c_node ≤ 1e-7 s on 8 threads, which puts N* at or above 8.5e7 even at R = 100. A result that would reopen the candidate is the discovery of a protein-science observable that is non-local, not disorder-averaged, and defined on a succinctly described non-periodic assembly with more than 1e8 nodes. The search found none.
verdicts.break_even_or_cost_note: Plain QROM, the O(log N)-qubit loader Liu et al. use, has no crossover at any N: quantum is about 2.4e3 times slower than an 8-core CPU and about 1.2e5 times slower than a GPU (R = 100, eps = 1e-2). With QROAM (sqrt(N) scaling), N* is as follows. Against 1 core: 1.4e6 (R=100, eps=1e-2), 1.4e8 (eps=1e-3), 1.4e10 (R=1). Against 8 cores: 8.5e7 (R=100, eps=1e-2), 8.5e11 (R=1). Against a GPU: 2e11-2e15. The QROAM ancilla needed at those sizes is about 9e3-4e8 logical qubits, roughly 2e3 physical qubits per logical qubit at d = 31. These estimates ignore distance and inverse-sqrt arithmetic per query (about 1e3-1e4 Toffolis), multiple observables and the cost of preparing the initial state, all of which raise N*. For observables driven by a local perturbation, classical cost scales as O((v*t)^3 * t) and does not depend on N, so N* is effectively infinite unless t exceeds the time for a wave to cross the whole assembly. Simulator runtime is not relevant here, since no quantum circuit was simulated.
verdicts.novelty_note: Not novel. Four pieces of prior art cover it. (1) The protein application of Babbush-type oscillator simulation, meaning quantum GNM/NMA dynamics for proteins with DOS, mode and correlation readouts, is Liu, Li, Wang and Liu, arXiv 2411.03972 (2024), which is already in the project literature as B58/D69. (2) QENM is Kolotouros et al., arXiv 2601.05161 (2026), graphene only. KvN MD with QPE/AE readout of Green-Kubo coefficients is Watanabe et al., arXiv 2605.30142 and 2605.30143 (2026), H2 only. (3) QM-26's own kill arguments are also prior art: the data-loading no-go is Liu et al.'s Thm S1.10; the locality no-go is Schade et al., arXiv 2609.20721 (Sep 2026); the chaos no-go is Lewis et al., Quantum 2024. (4) The project already recorded "no advantage (QM-26)" in research/theory/COMPLEXITY.md. What QM-26 adds is only project-specific: the explicit N* break-even envelope and a light-cone check on a protein-derived ENM. Scope caveat: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the novelty search used the arXiv API (7 queries, 2019-2026) plus Crossref and the project's 448-paper literature base. Under that scope, the search found no evidence of any protein assembly whose ENM or Hessian admits a polylog(N)-bit description, and no protein-science observable that meets the Babbush et al. conditions. Journal-only ENM or capsid work after 2019 was not searched.

title: Precision-type quantum estimation of posterior functionals: basin masses, DeltaF, Z, entropy/mutual information, expected information gain, convergence/property testing, DQC1 traces and Lee-Yang characteristic functions
merged_from: qalg QM-09 (partition-function ratios for competing topology hypotheses), qalg QM-14 (quantum property testing for ensemble convergence), classical 'Free energies of large conformational changes (>200 aa)', wild 'Quantum-accelerated Bayesian experimental design (EIG)', wild 'Allosteric coupling and conformational entropy via quantum distribution-functional estimators', wild 'Normalised-trace and characteristic-function estimators (DQC1, Lee-Yang/Fisher zeros)', priorart (f) quantum distribution property testing
summary: Q: estimate posterior masses of topology/fold hypotheses, DeltaG between functional states, Z, conformational entropy and allosteric MI, EIG of candidate experiments, cross-chain closeness (convergence), or folding-transition order (Fisher zeros) with fewer samples. Quantum: QAE / quantum mean estimation; quantum partition-function estimation (Montanaro, Harrow-Wei, Cornelissen-Hamoudi); nested AE / quantum MLMC; BHH / Gilyen-Li closeness and entropy testing with purified access; DQC1 normalised traces and probe-qubit Z(beta + i tau)/Z(beta). Mechanism: interference gives O(sigma/eps) vs Theta(sigma^2/eps^2), and sqrt(N) support-size gains for unstructured distributions; any mixing gain is exactly QM-01's sqrt(delta). Why classical copies it: every functional here is an expectation (or ratio of expectations) of a diagonal-energy distribution; with a known energy, TI/MBAR remove support-size dependence (S = beta(<E> - F)); DQC1-diagonal lemma (I(prog)): Tr f(E)/2^n and <e^{-i tau E}> are classical Monte Carlo expectations with identical additive error; the leading Fisher zero sits where the characteristic function is O(1) and Wang-Landau DOS gives all zeros; no tester sees mass its sampler never reaches (bias, Woodard et al.); qsample entanglement carries no information beyond the classical distribution (Holevo). The binding errors are force-field/learned-energy bias, calibration (condition M) and hysteresis from slow orthogonal modes, not variance; break-even needs sigma/eps >= ~1e4 while decisions need 10-100. Oracle: coherent Gibbs states per window (M1 cost), coherent log arithmetic, purified access (unavailable from classical sample streams without QRAM). Competitor: MBAR/BAR, restrained PT, AIS/SMC, Wang-Landau, string+umbrella, Laplace basin free energies, KSG/kNN, ensemble-reuse EIG with greedy submodular selection, two-sample tests on coarse basin labels. S29-S33: matrix M4 KILLED (practical: bias- and mixing-limited), H-005 retired, M5 WEAK (only sqrt(delta) matters), M13 KILLED for entanglement-as-resource claims; H-001 covers the linear-functional readouts. Residual (not dead, kept elsewhere): the mixing part -> QM-01; hidden modes -> QM-02; the classical restraint-value curve and design-ranking stability test are worth running as infrastructure for QM-18/QM-24. Kill (confirmation): bootstrap sigma_stat < 0.2 x method-to-method systematic spread; decisions stable at <= 1e3-1e4 samples; EIG top-10 ranking Kendall tau > 0.9 at M <= 1e4. Track: C theory/query. Prior: very low.
dead_reason: Opportunity-matrix M4 KILLED (practical): ensemble estimation is bias/mixing-limited, not variance-limited, with break-even sigma/eps >= 1e4; H-005 retired; M5 WEAK reduces to M1's sqrt(delta); DQC1/characteristic-function readouts are linear functionals of diagonal-energy distributions (H-001/M4); purified-access testing requires the M1 sampler and cannot see bias; entropy/entanglement claims fall to M13. No materially different mechanism beyond the mixing part already carried by QM-01/QM-02.

title: Quantum solvers inside experimental-inversion pipelines: Grover pose search / AE marginalisation / QLSA tomography for cryo-EM heterogeneity and phasing, and quantum convex solvers for IDP ensemble reweighting
merged_from: classical 'Cryo-EM heterogeneity inference: pose and state marginalisation over 1e5-1e7 particles', priorart (g) quantum computing for cryo-EM / crystallographic inverse problems (computational branch), classical 'IDP ensemble inference against SAXS / NMR / smFRET data'
summary: Q: accelerate cryo-EM pose/state inference (1e5-1e7 particles x 1e5-1e6 pose grid x K states), tomographic reconstruction or phasing, and max-entropy/Bayesian reweighting of IDP ensembles against SAXS/PRE/smFRET. Quantum: Grover / Durr-Hoyer maximum finding over each particle's pose x state grid; AE of per-particle marginal likelihoods (E-step); QLSA/QSVT or QUBO tomography (Lee & Jun 2025, X-ray/CT); quantum convex/QSVT solvers for the reweighting dual. Mechanism: sqrt(N_pose K) coherent likelihood calls per particle; polylog-dimension linear solves. Why classical copies or erases it: each particle's D^2 ~ 1e4-1e5 pixels must be loaded per query (QRAM/re-encoding Omega(D^2), matching the classical per-pose FFT cost); pose grids are enumerable and already pruned by branch-and-bound (cryoSPARC) or amortised (cryoDRGN); the E-step needs marginals (exact grid sums leave no variance for AE) and posteriors are sharp at high resolution; tomographic low-rank structure is dequantised (Chia et al. 2020); IDP reweighting is a convex program in m = 10-1000 dual variables solved in seconds (BME, metainference). The real limits are SNR/dose, particle count, forward-model misspecification, underdetermination and prior coverage: information. Speedup: none-known. Competitor: RELION Bayesian EM, cryoSPARC SGD + B&B, 3DFlex, cryoDRGN, RECOVAR, MD-ensemble image reweighting (BioEM); CALVADOS + BME/EOM/metainference, idpGAN. S29-S33: primitives map onto killed rows: M9 (Grover/AA search, KILLED), M4 (AE of ensemble expectations, KILLED), M15 (QSVT/HHL for readout programs, KILLED, dequantised, QRAM-bound), K-011/DNR-18 (quantum solvers for classical convex readout programs), DNR-03 (quantum search over enumerable registers). The search found no quantum cryo-EM algorithm in scope (no evidence under repo bibliography + one web search). Residual non-computational branch (quantum metrology) is carried by QM-24; the only super-quadratic cryo-EM route is QM-17(c). Kill (confirmation): exhaustive-grid marginalisation gives no class/pose accuracy gain over B&B heuristics at SNR 0.1-0.01 while all degrade with SNR; BME solve < 1 min with a broad chi^2-fitting weight family. Test: 2e4 simulated 64^2 particles from two conformations; 1e4-member CG IDR pool with synthetic SAXS + PRE. < 1 day. Track: C theory/query. Prior: very low.
dead_reason: Every quantum primitive proposed maps onto an existing KILLED row with no materially different mechanism: Grover pose search -> M9 (KILLED) / DNR-03; AE marginalisation -> M4 (KILLED); QLSA/QSVT tomography and quantum convex reweighting -> M15 (KILLED, dequantised, QRAM-bound) and K-011/DNR-18. Data loading (CA-5) erases any residual gain; the limits are information (SNR, dose, underdetermination).

title: Multistate negative design as a zero-sum game solved by quantum Gibbs-sampling LP/game solvers
merged_from: wild 'Multistate negative design as a zero-sum game solved by quantum Gibbs-sampling game/LP solvers'
summary: Q: which sequence stabilises a target fold while destabilising competing decoy folds (misfolds, alternative states, wrong oligomers), maximising the worst-case or soft-min energy gap (fold specificity, switch design)? Quantum: van Apeldoorn-Gilyen quantum zero-sum-game/LP solver using quantum Gibbs sampling inside multiplicative weights, O~(sqrt(n+m)/eps^3) vs classical Grigoriadis-Khachiyan O~((n+m)/eps^2) (UNVERIFIED this session).
